1057576_1057576.article_context: Tens of thousands of Russians are planning major protests against President Vladimir Putin, marking the largest opposition movement since he came to power twelve years ago. The protesters are demanding new elections and the annulment of a recent parliamentary vote marred by widespread allegations of fraud and voting violations. Authorities have responded with heightened security measures, deploying thousands of police and troops across Moscow and other cities, and moving the main protest site away from the Kremlin. The demonstrations, organized through social media, highlight growing discontent among Russia's middle class over a lack of democracy and freedom under Putin, while organizers promise a peaceful protest despite fears of police crackdowns and attempts by officials to disrupt participation.

934961_934961.caption: Protesters take part in the Britain Needs a Pay Rise march in London
934961_934961.article_context: Tens of thousands of union members marched through central London, Glasgow, and Belfast to demand pay rises and highlight the financial struggles faced by public sector workers, including nurses, midwives, and civil servants. Organized by the TUC, the Britain Needs a Pay Rise demonstration drew up to 90,000 participants and featured strong criticism of government pay policies, cuts to public services, and growing income inequality. Union leaders called on the Labour party to offer stronger support for workers, citing persistent wage suppression, job losses, and the privatization of public services as key concerns.

1224276_1224276.caption: Unicef estimates that 7 of Guatemalan girls are married by the age of 15 and 30 by 18
1224276_1224276.article_context: Guatemala has raised the minimum age for marriage to 18 in an effort to curb child marriage and its associated risks, though exceptions still exist for 16-year-old girls with judicial approval. Women’s rights activists praise the law but warn that enforcing it will be difficult, especially among rural and indigenous communities where child marriage is prevalent. Campaigners hope the new law will help reduce teenage pregnancies and improve girls’ educational opportunities, but note that substantial cultural change and judicial training are needed for full implementation.

286724_286724.caption: Midland police fire and sheriffs respond to an accident where a trailer carrying wounded veterans in a parade was struck by a train in Midland Texas on Thursday
286724_286724.article_context: A freight train struck a parade float carrying wounded veterans in Midland, Texas, killing four people and injuring 17 others during an event organized to honor veterans. The crash occurred when the float became stuck on a railroad crossing as the train approached, despite working crossing gates and warning lights. Federal investigators and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the incident, which led to the cancellation of related veterans’ events. The tragedy has prompted expressions of sympathy from officials, including the Secretary of Defense.

321144_321144.caption: Smoke rises from a fire at the Country Club Plaza in Kansas City Mo
321144_321144.article_context: A major explosion and fire destroyed J.J.'s Restaurant in Kansas City after a cable TV crew accidentally punctured a marked natural gas main while extending a fiber-optic line. Gas leaked for over an hour before igniting, leading to a deadly blast that killed at least one person and injured 15 others. Search teams later found a body believed to be missing employee Megan Cramer. Six victims remain hospitalized, with three in critical condition. Emergency crews worked quickly to remove debris and investigate the incident, which occurred shortly before a winter storm was expected. The exact ignition source is still unclear, but multiple utility workers were among the injured.

570795_570795.caption: High school students demonstrate on in Bordeaux against France s government pensions reform
570795_570795.article_context: In cities across France, high school students and workers staged widespread protests against the government's proposed retirement reforms. Demonstrations included blocking school entrances, fuel depots, and oil refineries, leading to clashes with police and disruptions to fuel supplies. Protesters voiced their opposition through marches, placards, and barricades, while union representatives and local officials publicly supported the movement.

311612_311612.caption: A bulldozer clears a makeshift refugee camp during a police operation at the GreekMacedonian border near the northern Greek village of Idomeni on May 24 2016
311612_311612.article_context: Greek authorities began evacuating the Idomeni refugee camp near the Macedonian border, deploying hundreds of riot police and sealing the area as they moved thousands of refugees to new facilities, mostly industrial sites near Thessaloniki. The operation follows the closure of the Balkans migration route and the camp's overcrowding and poor living conditions, with many refugees reluctant to leave and hoping the border will reopen. The situation is further complicated by an EU-Turkey agreement that enables the deportation of new arrivals to Turkey, leaving refugees in limbo and uncertain about their future in Greece or further passage to Europe.

1510406_1510406.caption: The new nuclear plant will be built next to two existing facilities at Hinkley Point in Somerset
1510406_1510406.article_context: Rolls-Royce has been awarded major contracts worth £100m to supply heat exchangers and nuclear waste treatment systems for the new Hinkley Point C nuclear power plant, in partnership with Nuvia. The contracts are pending a final investment decision from EDF, the French company leading the project. Construction of the plant has been delayed, and a new timetable will be provided once the investment decision is finalized.

1556594_1556594.caption: People mourn after a Christian man mistaken for a Muslim was killed by antibalaka militiamen
1556594_1556594.article_context: Intense violence in Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, has resulted in 43 deaths and 71 injuries over four days, according to the Red Cross. The conflict, which began after Seleka rebels overthrew the president last March, has shifted from ethnic to religious violence, with Christian anti-balaka militias targeting Muslims in reprisal attacks. Despite the inauguration of a new interim leader and deployments of French and African troops, the situation remains dire, with calls for a larger UN peacekeeping force amid reports that neither the current forces nor diplomatic efforts are sufficient to protect civilians or stop the violence.

1645944_1645944.caption: US special forces have paired up with local troops and Ugandan soldiers to seek out the LRA in the CAR
1645944_1645944.article_context: Dominic Ongwen, a senior commander in Uganda's Lord's Resistance Army (LRA), is set to be transferred to the International Criminal Court (ICC) for trial, following his recent surrender in the Central African Republic. Ongwen, accused of crimes against humanity for his role in the abduction of thousands of children for fighting and sex slavery, was taken into US custody after defecting from the LRA. While Uganda initially wanted to try Ongwen in its own courts, the decision was made to send him to the ICC due to the LRA's transnational crimes. Ongwen is one of several top LRA figures indicted by the ICC, with most now captured or deceased except leader Joseph Kony.

1652498_1652498.caption: Two US marines were killed and a number of British soldiers were injured in the Taliban attack
1652498_1652498.article_context: Photographs have surfaced showing at least one UK serviceman from the RAF Regiment posing with the body of a dead Taliban fighter following a 2012 attack on Camp Bastion in Afghanistan. The images, which appeared online, have prompted a military police investigation and led to two RAF members being withdrawn from frontline duties. The Ministry of Defence condemned the actions, citing a zero-tolerance policy on the mistreatment of enemy dead, and stated the individuals could face serious consequences for breaching military rules. The incident has sparked embarrassment for the UK military and raised concerns over appropriate conduct in conflict zones.

47888_47888.caption: The Iranian flag flies in front of a UN building where closeddoor nuclear talks take place at the International Center in Vienna Austria Wednesday June 18 2014
47888_47888.article_context: As the July 20 deadline for negotiating a comprehensive agreement on Iran’s nuclear program approaches, U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry emphasizes that Iran faces a critical choice: to prove its nuclear program is entirely peaceful or risk continued isolation and sanctions. While Iran has complied with several interim measures and negotiations have demonstrated some progress, significant gaps remain between Iran's commitments and necessary actions to ensure nuclear nonproliferation. Kerry warns that without tangible, verifiable steps from Iran, no extension of talks will be granted, and the opportunity for a breakthrough that could benefit Iran's economy and security may be missed.

1551659_1551659.caption: China has been criticised for failing to distinguish between religious extremists and peaceful Muslims
1551659_1551659.article_context: The article describes heightened security and intense surveillance in Kashgar, Xinjiang, as China faces ongoing violence linked to tensions with the region's Muslim Uighur minority. Following recent deadly attacks, the government has escalated its crackdown, imposing strict restrictions on religious practices and monitoring citizens for signs of dissent, which human rights groups say fuels further unrest. While China blames foreign influences and militant Islam for the violence, many Uighurs attribute their frustration to state repression, economic marginalization, and erosion of their culture. Despite claims of controlling terrorism, the author saw limited evidence of an imminent militant threat but observed extensive restrictions on Uighur freedoms, perpetuating a cycle of alienation and occasional violence.

1549953_1549953.caption: A South African court ruling has made a landmark ruling that Zimbabwean officials
1549953_1549953.article_context: A South African high court has ordered authorities to investigate Zimbabwean officials accused of torturing opposition members in 2007, following a case brought by human rights groups representing exiles. The judge ruled that, under international law, South Africa is obliged to investigate crimes against humanity, despite previous refusals by prosecutors due to political concerns. Zimbabwe’s justice minister dismissed the ruling, claiming South Africa has no jurisdiction over such cases. The decision has been welcomed by human rights advocates as a significant step towards accountability for alleged abuses.

1624744_1624744.caption: Mosul Dam in northern Iraq is one of the places targeted by US air strikes over the past month
1624744_1624744.article_context: UK Prime Minister David Cameron condemned the beheading of a second US hostage by Islamic State (IS) militants, calling the act barbaric and reaffirming Britain's commitment to combating terrorism. IS threatened to kill a British hostage unless US airstrikes in Iraq ceased, but Cameron and ministers pledged to consider every possible option to protect the man while maintaining the UK's policy against paying ransoms. The UK government is considering military involvement, such as potential airstrikes, and is working internationally to build a united front against IS. Political leaders across parties expressed support for strong action, while new measures to address national security and the return of terror suspects are being discussed. The acts have been widely condemned by figures across British society.

405892_405892.caption: A member of the MesoAmerican Migrant Movement hangs a banner in front of the US Embassy in Mexico City
405892_405892.article_context: During a three-day trip to Latin America, President Obama emphasized the importance of strengthening U.S. trade and economic ties with countries in the region to remain competitive in the global economy. He highlighted the benefits of increased integration, education, and renewable energy cooperation. Obama also discussed the need to reform immigration laws, offering a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants, and acknowledged ongoing challenges with drug-related violence, stressing that economic growth is key to addressing these issues. Overall, the visit aimed to reinforce economic and social partnerships while addressing concerns important to both Latin American nations and the Hispanic population in the U.S.

1648960_1648960.caption: The US Navy s 5th Fleet is based in Bahrain and serves as the US s main maritime counterbalance to Iran
1648960_1648960.article_context: Several Gulf leaders, including Saudi Arabia's King Salman, announced they would not attend a summit with US and Arab officials at Camp David, instead sending junior representatives. While Saudi officials cited pressing regional matters like overseeing the Yemen ceasefire as the official reason, analysts interpret their absence as a sign of dissatisfaction with President Obama's negotiations with Iran over its nuclear program. The summit aims to reassure Arab allies of US support, but the lack of senior Gulf representation highlights ongoing tensions over US policy in the region.

1605331_1605331.caption: Calls for a ceasefire have heightened since Israel began a ground operation in Gaza last Thursday
1605331_1605331.article_context: Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict in Gaza have escalated, with US Secretary of State John Kerry meeting with UN chief Ban Ki-moon in Cairo, as the death toll reaches nearly 600 Palestinians and 29 Israelis. Kerry expressed concern over civilian casualties but supported Israel's military actions, while announcing $47 million in US aid for Gaza. The US and UN, joined by the Arab League, are urging for an immediate ceasefire, but Hamas has rejected existing proposals, calling them a surrender. The UN reports a humanitarian crisis with over 100,000 people seeking shelter, and an Israeli airstrike on a Gaza hospital has further heightened concerns about rising civilian deaths.

819463_819463.caption: Strong waves caused by Hurricane Norbert hit Mazatlan in Sinaloa Mexico on Thursday
819463_819463.article_context: Hurricane Norbert brought heavy rains and prompted mass evacuations along Mexico’s Baja California peninsula, with local authorities closing schools and government services and urging residents in vulnerable areas to seek shelter. The storm toppled trees, caused power outages, and led to rescue operations in flooded streets, while ports popular with tourists were closed and police guarded evacuated neighborhoods. With Norbert's winds reaching 120mph, forecasters noted the hurricane could also bring much-needed rainfall to the drought-stricken US Southwest by pushing moisture from Tropical Storm Dolly into the region.

457843_457843.caption: RAF Tornado aircraft are already stationed within striking distance of Isis targets with air strikes expected to commence soon
457843_457843.article_context: The UK Parliament has overwhelmingly approved military air strikes against Islamic State (Isis) targets in Iraq, marking Britain's renewed involvement in Middle East conflict and paving the way for operations to begin within 48 hours. The decision also involves sending military advisers to help the Iraqi army, though officials signaled the campaign may expand to Syria in the future. The government stressed this will be a prolonged campaign lasting months or even years, with the possibility of future parliamentary approval required for action in Syria. The move aligns the UK with US-led coalition efforts, following similar commitments from Belgium and Denmark, as global leaders warn that Isis must be confronted across borders.

52756_52756.caption: A Taliban fighter talks with residents at the main square of Kunduz
52756_52756.article_context: U.S. Special Operations troops and military advisers from NATO joined Afghan forces in a major effort to retake Kunduz after the city was captured by the Taliban, marking the first time a provincial capital has fallen to the group since 2001. Coalition personnel came under fire and called in airstrikes near Kunduz airport, where Afghan troops had retreated due to being surrounded and low on supplies. The situation in the city remained dire, with Afghan forces struggling to resist Taliban advances, hundreds of casualties among civilians, and thousands fleeing. Afghan leadership admitted they had monitored the threat but failed to act in time, while coalition troops continued to provide training, advice, and combat assistance.

329368_329368.caption: Vintage WWII planes fly past the Washington Monument Friday during a historic flyover commemorating the 70th anniversary of Victory in Europe Day
329368_329368.article_context: On Victory in Europe Day, 56 WWII fighter and bomber planes participated in the 'Arsenal of Democracy' flyover over Washington, D.C.'s National Mall, traversing one of the nation’s most restricted airspaces since post-9/11 security enhancements. The event required extensive planning and coordination with multiple federal agencies to ensure safety and compliance with strict regulations. As a precaution, aircraft and flight routes were closely managed, and one plane made a safe emergency landing without injuries. The flyover commemorated the 70th anniversary of Germany's surrender, marking the end of WWII in Europe.

1081099_1081099.caption: A police officer peppersprays students at an Occupy protest at University of California Davis
1081099_1081099.article_context: After campus police employed pepper spray at close range against peaceful students protesting at UC Davis, Chancellor Linda Katehi faced calls to resign and condemnation from the faculty association for a failure of leadership. Two police officers involved, including Lt. John Pike, were placed on administrative leave pending investigation. The incident, widely publicized and criticized, was part of broader 'Occupy' protests against tuition increases and police force on other UC campuses. Despite taking responsibility and pledging reforms, Katehi announced she would not resign, and promised to ensure such events do not happen again.

1519816_1519816.caption: France has stepped up antiterrorist patrols in face of the crisis in Syria and Iraq
1519816_1519816.article_context: French authorities faced criticism after a security blunder led to three suspected jihadists—linked to infamous Islamist attacks and believed to be part of a recruiting network—arriving in Marseille instead of Paris due to a mix-up with Turkish police. The suspects, originally detained by Turkey after trying to return from Syria, slipped into France unnoticed when communication between Turkish and French officials failed. Although the men later surrendered to French police, the incident sparked concern over gaps in international cooperation and heightened anxiety given France’s recent escalated terrorist threats and involvement in military action against Islamic State.

1578628_1578628.caption: The presence of Russia has been welcomed by many of Crimea s ethnic Russians
1578628_1578628.article_context: US President Barack Obama urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to withdraw troops from Crimea, stating that Russia's military intervention in Ukraine violates international law and Ukrainian sovereignty. Putin defended Russia's actions, claiming the right to protect Russian interests and citizens in Ukraine. The crisis led Ukraine to put its army on combat alert, while Canada recalled its ambassador and suspended participation in the upcoming G8 summit. The UN and NATO called for de-escalation, and emergency diplomatic talks were convened. Meanwhile, pro-Russian rallies and clashes erupted in several Ukrainian cities, and reports indicated a significant Russian military presence in Crimea.

1267544_1267544.caption: A young Syrian migrant waits in a holding centre for immigrants in the Spanish enclave of Melilla in north Africa
1267544_1267544.article_context: Central and eastern European leaders have resisted efforts by Brussels and Berlin to impose mandatory refugee quotas, highlighting deep divisions within the EU over how to respond to the migration crisis. Ahead of emergency summits in Brussels, countries like Hungary, Poland, and the Czech Republic have opposed the quotas, citing concerns about sovereignty and legality, with Hungary enacting new laws allowing the army to use non-lethal force against migrants. While Germany and the European Commission push for a quota-based system modeled on Germany's own refugee distribution, consensus remains elusive, raising the possibility of a qualified majority vote that could further fracture the union. The upcoming summits will also focus on external measures to reduce migrant inflows, such as funding neighboring countries and reinforcing border controls, but so far, EU governments have failed to agree on a coherent strategy or deliver adequate support to frontline agencies like Frontex.

133478_133478.caption: A runner embraces another woman on the marathon route near Kenmore Square after two bombs exploded during the 117th Boston Marathon
133478_133478.article_context: After the Boston Marathon bombings, investigators identified the explosive devices as pressure cookers filled with nails and ball bearings, resulting in three deaths and injuring 176 people. Authorities, with no suspects or claims of responsibility, are combing thousands of images and video footage for clues, considering both domestic and foreign terrorism as possible motives. The investigation is ongoing and in its early stages, with evidence sent to FBI labs for analysis. President Obama condemned the attack as an act of terrorism and will attend an interfaith service for victims. The city responded with acts of bravery and solidarity, while officials continue to search for the perpetrators.

1684029_1684029.caption: US officials fear European extremists could try to enter the country to launch an attack
1684029_1684029.article_context: The US House of Representatives has overwhelmingly voted to tighten the visa-free travel program following the Paris terror attacks, aiming to prevent potential extremists from entering the country. The new measures would require people who have traveled to Iraq, Syria, Iran, or Sudan since 2011 to obtain a visa, rather than using the existing visa waiver program. The bill, supported by the White House, also mandates electronic passports with biometric data for travelers and calls for increased information sharing between the US and participating countries. The move comes amid heightened security concerns and was widely approved in the House, though proposals for even stricter restrictions have been debated.

476607_476607.caption: Stacey Addison Police seized methamphetamines from her shared taxi and told her not to leave TimorLeste
476607_476607.article_context: American veterinarian Stacey Addison was detained in Timor Leste on suspicion of drug trafficking after methamphetamines were found in a taxi she was sharing. Despite claiming she was unaware of the drugs and was simply sharing a ride with other passengers, Addison was arrested and has not been formally charged, but is prohibited from leaving the country while the investigation continues. Timorese police, citing heavy workloads and backlogs, may take up to a year to investigate. Addison maintains her innocence and is seeking assistance from US officials while awaiting resolution.

803388_803388.caption: Alabama protesters take part in a demonstration infront of the federal courthouse in Birmingham
803388_803388.article_context: A federal appeals court delivered a partial ruling on Alabama’s stringent new immigration law, allowing police to detain suspected undocumented immigrants but blocking sections that required schools to check students’ immigration status and made it a crime to lack proper documentation. The decision followed a challenge by the Justice Department, which criticized the law for fostering a hostile environment and for potentially straining diplomatic relations. While law supporters celebrated that key provisions remain, civil rights groups and the federal government expressed hope that more of the law will be overturned, citing fears over its impact on Hispanic communities, labor markets, and school attendance.

1549825_1549825.caption: Egyptian troops have reportedly begun flooding tunnels under the border with Gaza
1549825_1549825.article_context: Human Rights Watch reports that Egypt has demolished over 3,255 homes and other buildings in the Sinai peninsula, primarily along the Gaza border, in an effort to create a buffer zone to combat militant activity and smuggling. These demolitions, which began in 2013, were carried out with little warning, inadequate compensation, and no temporary housing for displaced residents, allegedly violating international law. The Egyptian government maintains the actions were necessary for national security and claims local support, but HRW questions the justification and evidence for the operation, noting it may have breached international conventions and failed to use less destructive methods.

443510_443510.caption: Spanish police found 300kg of cocaine in a raid on a laboratory near Madrid
443510_443510.article_context: Spanish police have arrested 25 people and dismantled the largest and most advanced cocaine laboratory ever discovered in Europe, near Madrid. Authorities seized 300 kilograms of cocaine, 33 tonnes of chemicals, 470 mobile phones, and €2 million in cash. The arrests include Spanish and Colombian nationals, as well as several Spanish lawyers suspected of money laundering. The operation was the result of a two-year investigation that began in December.

1284845_1284845.caption: A baby born in Recife Brazil earlier this year suffering from microcephaly
1284845_1284845.article_context: Spain's health ministry has confirmed the country's first case of the Zika virus in a pregnant woman who had traveled to Colombia, marking Europe's first known Zika infection after the World Health Organization declared a global health emergency. The ministry reported seven total cases in Spain, all imported and not posing a risk of local transmission. Zika, which originated in Brazil, is suspected of causing severe birth defects and has the potential to spread worldwide. Spanish authorities emphasize that there are currently no domestic cases.

469714_469714.caption: An Indian army rescue operation in Uttarakhand
469714_469714.article_context: Severe floods and landslides in Uttarakhand, India, have left as many as 4,000 people, mostly Hindu pilgrims, stranded near the Kedarnath shrine, with over 100 confirmed dead and many more feared missing. Rescue operations are ongoing, with helicopters ferrying aid to the affected areas, but many villages remain inaccessible and entire roads, bridges, and homes have been destroyed. Authorities warn the final death toll could be much higher. While natural causes such as torrential rains and glacier collapse contributed to the disaster, experts and environmentalists also blame unchecked development and deforestation for exacerbating the devastation.

1515365_1515365.caption: Gazprombank Russia s third largest bank has less access to Western capital due to sanctions
1515365_1515365.article_context: EU member states have agreed in principle to extend economic sanctions against Russia for six more months in response to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine and Russia's annexation of Crimea. The sanctions target Russia's energy, defense, and financial sectors, and their extension is expected to be formally approved by EU foreign ministers. Alongside this, the EU also agreed to prolong a ban on investment in Crimea. These measures reflect continued concerns over Russia's support for separatists in eastern Ukraine and the lack of progress in fully implementing the Minsk ceasefire agreement. The sanctions are part of coordinated Western efforts, with the US also imposing similar restrictions, while Russia has retaliated with its own bans on Western food imports.

805666_805666.caption: Tactical movements a convoy of Ukrainian forces drives towards Debaltseve part of heavy troop concentrations around the city
805666_805666.article_context: In eastern Ukraine, intense fighting continues between government forces and rebel groups, with heavy artillery and troop movements around key cities like Debaltseve and Donetsk. Despite an agreed ceasefire, shelling persists, causing damage to civilian infrastructure and leaving residents at risk. Ukrainian troops remain positioned and prepared for further conflict, while signs of fatigue and disruption to daily life are evident among both military personnel and civilians.

100272_100272.caption: Laidoff CNN reporter gives final signoff in style
100272_100272.article_context: CNN is reducing its congressional coverage as part of broader cost-cutting measures, resulting in the departure of Capitol Hill reporter Lisa Desjardins and the elimination of several positions on the digital politics team. The network is shifting its focus toward social mobile video content, although it promises continued coverage of key Congressional races, especially during the upcoming election season.

1561647_1561647.caption: Tomahawk Cruise missiles launched from ship were involved in the attack on Khorasan
1561647_1561647.article_context: The US launched air strikes in Syria targeting the Khorasan group, a cell of al-Qaeda veterans believed to be plotting imminent attacks against the US and Western countries. The strikes in Aleppo province were conducted solely by the US and focused on disrupting the group's preparations for major attacks, possibly involving aircraft. The operations coincided with broader US and Arab ally attacks against Islamic State militants in Syria. Officials say Khorasan had established a safe haven in Syria to develop external attacks and recruit Westerners. The strikes reportedly killed dozens of militants, many of whom were foreign fighters, and several civilians, though the exact impact remains unclear.

239166_239166.caption: Police use a water canon as right wing demonstrators protest at a memorial site at the Place de la Bourse in Brussels on March 27 2016
239166_239166.article_context: Belgian authorities have banned an anti-Islam demonstration planned by the far-right youth group Generation Identitaire in Brussels’ Muslim-majority neighborhood of Molenbeek, following recent disruptions by far-right protesters and fears of violence. Despite the prohibition, community leaders and locals remain concerned that protesters might attempt to defy the ban, potentially leading to clashes with the neighborhood’s youth, who are mistrustful of police. The situation is heightened by Molenbeek’s association with recent terrorist attacks and ongoing tensions following last week’s Brussels bombings.

329001_329001.caption: Debris from the Germanwings Airbus A320 at the crash site in the French Alps Tuesday
329001_329001.article_context: A Germanwings Airbus A320 crashed in the French Alps after a sudden, eight-minute descent, killing all 150 people on board, including 16 German students and two babies. No distress call was sent by the pilots, and the cause of the crash remains unclear, though investigators have found no evidence of terrorism so far. The crash site is described as one of complete destruction, and recovery operations are expected to last for a week. National leaders from Germany, France, Spain, and the U.S. expressed condolences, and authorities have begun an investigation into the incident.

1119370_1119370.caption: Skype worked with intelligence agencies last year to allow Prism to collect video and audio conversations
1119370_1119370.article_context: Top-secret documents leaked by Edward Snowden and obtained by the Guardian reveal that Microsoft has closely collaborated with US intelligence agencies, including the NSA and FBI, to enable interception of user communications. The documents detail how Microsoft helped the NSA bypass its own encryption on services like Outlook.com, gave the agency pre-encryption access to emails, and assisted the FBI in providing easier access to cloud storage service SkyDrive. Microsoft also worked to increase NSA access to Skype communications. These revelations highlight broad cooperation between tech companies and US intelligence under the secret Prism program, raising concerns about user privacy and transparency. In response, Microsoft and other involved companies insist they only comply with lawful government requests.

1618430_1618430.caption: The UK s extra test for EU migrants is seen as proportionate in the new legal opinion
1618430_1618430.article_context: A senior EU legal adviser has supported the UK in its dispute with the European Commission over the UK's 'right to reside' test for EU migrants seeking social benefits. The adviser deemed the UK's approach of imposing additional checks to protect its state budget as justified, despite claims of discrimination against EU migrants. This opinion is significant for the UK government, particularly as it seeks changes to EU rules on migrant benefits in advance of the UK's EU membership referendum. The final decision will be made by the European Court of Justice, but the adviser's view typically influences the outcome.

1492419_1492419.caption: The raid on Wprost s offices by a prosecutor was broadcast live by several TV channels in Poland last week
1492419_1492419.article_context: A Polish news magazine, Wprost, published excerpts from secretly recorded conversations in which Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski criticized Poland’s alliance with the US, calling it 'worthless' and made disparaging remarks about the Polish government's approach to international relations. Sikorski also attacked UK Prime Minister David Cameron’s handling of EU affairs. The leaks have caused a crisis for the Polish government, with officials accusing an 'organized crime group' of being behind the recordings, and prompting discussions of potential snap elections. The scandal escalated after prosecutors raided Wprost’s offices over the leaks, which also involved allegations of improper political discussions between Poland’s central banker and government ministers.

1471316_1471316.caption: The Turkish invasion of Cyprus in 1974 led to the island s partition
1471316_1471316.article_context: The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Turkey to pay 90 million euros in damages for its 1974 invasion of Cyprus, one of the largest awards ever made by the court. The compensation covers suffering experienced by relatives of missing persons and Greek Cypriots living in the Karpas peninsula. The court held Turkey responsible for the ongoing consequences of the invasion and division of Cyprus, despite the time that has passed. The decision comes as Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders are in new talks to resolve the longstanding division of the island.

171444_171444.caption: Migrants and refugees arrived on the Greek island of Lesbos on Tuesday
171444_171444.article_context: NATO has deployed warships to the Aegean Sea to target migrant-smuggling networks operating between Turkey and Greece, marking the alliance’s most direct involvement yet in Europe’s ongoing migrant crisis. The mission, quickly assembled after proposals from Germany, Turkey, and Greece, aims to monitor and disrupt criminal smuggling routes and is supported by the US, Canadian, and Italian vessels, working alongside EU border forces. While NATO stresses its goal is to counter criminals and not push back refugees, critics argue the move could militarize the crisis and hinder legitimate asylum seekers. The operation comes amid political pressure in Germany and continued disagreements among European nations over handling the influx, with many details about NATO’s role and responsibilities still unclear.

156898_156898.caption: A European Union flag under British flags
156898_156898.article_context: Homophobic attacks in the UK have risen by 147 percent since the Brexit vote, according to a report by anti-violence charity Galop. The report, based on a survey of LGBT individuals, highlights a significant spike in homophobia, biphobia, and transphobia-related hate crimes in the three months following Brexit. In addition to homophobic attacks, Britain has seen a surge in racist incidents and hostility toward immigrants after the referendum, prompting concerns about the social consequences of the vote to leave the European Union.

194966_194966.caption: People pass a kiosk center that is used as a clinic where girls are circumcised by a barber in the Imbaba area of Giza Egypt in 2012
194966_194966.article_context: Egyptian lawmaker Elhamy Agina sparked outrage after arguing that female genital mutilation (FGM) was necessary due to Egyptian men's supposed 'sexual weakness,' claiming it would 'reduce women's sexual desires.' Despite FGM being banned in Egypt since 2008, it remains widespread, with millions of women affected. The Egyptian cabinet has approved draft legislation to increase penalties for practicing FGM, following high-profile cases and international criticism. After facing backlash, Agina attempted to walk back his comments, saying they were meant as a jest.

472326_472326.caption: A member of the Association for the Recovery of Historical Memory looks for evidence during the exhumation of a grave at Guadalajara s cemetery
472326_472326.article_context: Spanish campaigners have begun exhuming a mass grave near Madrid to recover the remains of civil war victims, following pressure from an Argentinian court urging Spain to address crimes committed during the 1936-1939 civil war and the Franco dictatorship. This marks the first exhumation mandated by a Spanish court at the request of Argentinian investigators, as families hope for justice and proper burials for relatives lost decades ago. The case, spurred by 90-year-old Ascension Mendieta’s search for her father, highlights ongoing struggles to overcome Spain’s 1977 amnesty law and the continuing debate over how to confront the country’s troubled past.

1629185_1629185.caption: Raids were conducted on the site in Marshfield near Newport on Monday
1629185_1629185.article_context: Police have arrested four individuals in raids across Cardiff, Monmouthshire, and Marshfield as part of 'Operation Imperial,' an investigation into alleged slavery and servitude. The inquiry began after a missing man was discovered living in poor conditions at a Marshfield site, reportedly forced to work without pay. Authorities are also investigating claims that a body may be buried on the property. A man of Eastern European origin was found at the site and taken to hospital for assessment. The operation, involving multiple agencies and over 100 officers, is probing whether these incidents are part of a wider criminal conspiracy.

54485_54485.caption: Kenyan LGBT supporters chant slogans against Uganda s antigay bill in front of the Ugandan High Commission in Nairobi Kenya on Feb 10 2014
54485_54485.article_context: A Kenyan court has ruled that the use of anal examinations to determine a suspect’s sexual orientation is legal, upholding the practice despite widespread criticism from human rights advocates and the United Nations, which consider it a form of torture and medically invalid. The ruling came after two men, arrested on suspicion of gay sex in 2015, challenged the use of such examinations and related mandatory medical testing as degrading and abusive, but their petition was dismissed. Homosexual acts remain a crime in Kenya, and similar examination practices are reported in several other countries.

1541670_1541670.caption: Support for Catalan independence has been fuelled by Madrid s perceived neglect of the region
1541670_1541670.article_context: Catalonia's recent regional elections resulted in a record voter turnout and an absolute majority for pro-independence parties, intensifying tensions over the region's future within Spain. The results, interpreted differently across Spanish society and media, have led Catalan President Artur Mas to pledge steps toward independence, though Madrid emphasizes legal and constitutional barriers. The election highlights broader political trends in Europe, with rising populism and demands for transparency. Spain's government, focused on the upcoming general election, may consider granting Catalonia greater fiscal autonomy, as regional economic grievances persist. The independence issue remains largely a domestic matter, with limited attention from European institutions.

782265_782265.caption: Children in the Karakalpakstan region of Uzbekistan Residents in the area around the Aral Sea suffer with a higher incidence of tuberculosis
782265_782265.article_context: Karakalpakstan, a depressed region in northern Uzbekistan, suffers severe environmental and health problems due to the drying of the Aral Sea and legacy of Soviet-era weapon testing. Despite significant international funding for improvement, locals report worsening conditions and widespread out-migration for economic reasons, leading to threats to Karakalpak ethnic identity. A small online separatist movement, 'Alga Karakalpakstan,' led by Aman Sagidullaev from abroad, calls for independence but lacks widespread support and clear policies. The movement gained attention after Russia's annexation of Crimea but faces opposition from Uzbek authorities and risks further repression of Karakalpaks both at home and in diaspora communities. There are concerns that continued political agitation could endanger the future existence of the Karakalpak people.

503891_503891.caption: The Sinalei resort in Samoa after it was struck by the tsunami
503891_503891.article_context: A powerful tsunami struck Samoa and American Samoa, causing widespread devastation across villages such as Leone and Lalomanu. The disaster resulted in loss of life, destruction of infrastructure, and displacement of residents, with authorities and search teams working to recover victims and assess damage. New Zealand and other international forces provided support, while local officials addressed the aftermath and coordinated relief efforts.

588170_588170.caption: Twitter updates have become an alternative to the Iranian government s official version of events during the unrest
588170_588170.article_context: An anonymous Oxfordshire resident known as Oxfordgirl has become a key figure in sharing information and aiding protest coordination during Iran's political unrest, primarily through Twitter. Despite living far from Iran, she has used her platform to direct protester movements and counter official narratives, often warning of potential dangers. Her social media activity has helped circumvent government censorship and is seen as a threat by Iranian authorities, who have attempted to undermine her credibility online. Despite risks to her safety and family, Oxfordgirl remains committed to supporting resistance against the Iranian regime.

1567475_1567475.caption: Tens of thousands of families travel mostly from the state of Orissa to work in the brick kilns of Andhra Pradesh
1567475_1567475.article_context: In the brick kilns near Hyderabad, India, thousands of migrant families—including children—work in hazardous conditions, facing long hours, poverty, exploitation, and health hazards. Despite laws prohibiting bonded labor and child labor, abuses such as withheld wages, physical abuse, and denial of safety equipment remain widespread. Recent international attention—including guidelines from the United Nations and the OECD—now requires multinational companies to ensure their supply chains are free from human rights violations. Labour activists and trade unions are campaigning to hold companies accountable, while the Indian government claims to be addressing the issues, though activists and evidence suggest abuses persist. The new regulations shift responsibility to corporations to investigate and take action on labor violations tied to their products.

337671_337671.caption: Jefferson County sheriff s deputies converge Aug 29 2016 outside a home in Conifer Colo were a pair of pitbull terrier mixes mauled their owner killing her
337671_337671.article_context: A woman in Conifer, Colorado, died after being attacked by her two pit-bull terrier mixes at home. Her son was also injured but survived. Authorities struggled to restrain the aggressive dogs, which are now under animal control as the investigation continues. The victims' identities and the cause of the attack have not yet been released.

406442_406442.caption: Protestors clash with riot police near Taksim Square in Istanbul Turkey during a demonstration against the demolition of the park
406442_406442.article_context: Turkey's Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan issued a final warning to protesters occupying Gezi Park in Istanbul, demanding they end their two-week sit-in that sparked the largest political crisis of his decade-long rule. Despite threats of police intervention, Erdogan agreed to meet with selected protest representatives, though many demonstrators remained defiant. The protests, initially triggered by a police crackdown on a small environmental protest, have grown into a nationwide movement against Erdogan's government and its increasingly authoritarian tendencies. The European Parliament condemned Turkey for its excessive use of force, but Erdogan dismissed the criticism and indicated his determination to end the unrest.

206784_206784.caption: A US Navy boat conducts an exercise in the Arabian Sea on June 12 2012
206784_206784.article_context: Ten U.S. sailors were briefly detained by Iran after their boats accidentally entered Iranian waters near Farsi Island due to mechanical or navigational problems. The sailors were held overnight, questioned, and then released unharmed after diplomatic conversations between U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry and Iranian officials. U.S. officials thanked Iran for the swift resolution, denying any apology was made. The incident, handled peacefully, was seen as a demonstration of improved U.S.-Iran relations following the recent nuclear agreement, though underlying tensions remain between the two countries.

568963_568963.caption: An Italian coastguard ship carrying migrants arrives at Pozzallo s harbour near Ragusa Sicily on 19 May
568963_568963.article_context: The European Union's proposed plan to impose mandatory migrant quotas on member states is in jeopardy after France and Spain withdrew their support, following the UK's earlier decision to opt out. The quotas, designed to distribute refugees more evenly across the EU to address the Mediterranean migrant crisis, faced further opposition from several Eastern European countries. Leaders such as France's President Hollande and Spain's Foreign Minister García-Margallo cited national border policies, economic concerns, and high unemployment as reasons for rejecting the plan. The setback has cast doubt on the future of the quota system and highlighted deep divisions within the EU on how to manage the ongoing migrant crisis.

1625040_1625040.caption: Thousands of Yazidis have been stranded on Mount Sinjar since the IS advance
1625040_1625040.article_context: President Barack Obama praised US forces for their role in breaking the siege on Mount Sinjar in northern Iraq, which allowed tens of thousands of displaced people to escape. Obama stated the humanitarian situation had improved, reducing the need for further rescue operations, but confirmed continued US airstrikes and support for Iraqi and Kurdish forces against Islamic State militants. Meanwhile, the political situation in Iraq saw progress, with Prime Minister Nouri Maliki reportedly agreeing to step aside for Haider al-Abadi to form a new, more inclusive government, amidst ongoing concerns related to political stability and the humanitarian crisis caused by IS advances.

1636306_1636306.caption: Dozens of police officers were later seen inside Zaman s main office in Istanbul
1636306_1636306.article_context: Turkish police raided the offices of Zaman, the country's largest newspaper, after a court placed it under state control due to alleged ties with the Hizmet movement, which the government labels as a terrorist organization. The state takeover was met with protests, which police dispersed using tear gas and water cannons. The move has sparked international criticism and is seen as part of a wider crackdown on press freedom under President Erdogan's government, following similar actions against other media outlets and arrests of journalists. The US State Department and press advocates have expressed concern over the erosion of democracy and media independence in Turkey.

99610_99610.caption: Central American immigrants wait to be transported after turning themselves in to Border Patrol agents near Rio Grande City
99610_99610.article_context: The Department of Homeland Security is planning a series of large-scale raids to deport hundreds of Central American families who crossed into the U.S. since last year and have been ordered removed by immigration judges. The operation, which could begin as early as January, marks the first major effort to target families for deportation amid a surge of illegal border crossings and renewed violence in Central America. The plan has sparked controversy, with immigrant advocates condemning it as harsh and inhumane, while groups favoring stricter immigration controls view the move as overdue. The raids come amid legal and political pressures, including a court order to release families from detention centers and increased scrutiny of immigration policies during the 2016 presidential campaign.

1174956_1174956.caption: Maarten Verwey s team will hold the Greek government to the economic and social changes demanded in return for an 86bn bailout
1174956_1174956.article_context: Ahead of Greece’s upcoming election, both major parties have little control over the country’s future, as real power now lies with EU-appointed officials in Brussels, especially Dutch economist Maarten Verwey, who leads an unprecedented EU taskforce overseeing Greece’s bailout. Under the conditions of its third €86bn rescue package, Greece’s government must consult with EU institutions before enacting policy, surrendering significant economic and social decision-making in exchange for continued financial support. This arrangement mandates numerous austerity measures and sweeping reforms, including strict targets for tax, pensions, welfare, and public administration, with legislation largely drafted by Verwey’s team. Many Greeks express disillusionment, believing their votes will not affect these predetermined policies.

76980_76980.caption: Iranian protesters set fire to the Saudi Embassy in Tehran during a demonstration Saturday
76980_76980.article_context: Iran claimed that a Saudi-led airstrike hit its embassy in Yemen, a charge for which no visible evidence was found, but which further heightened tensions between the regional rivals. This accusation came shortly after Saudi Arabia and several Sunni-majority countries cut diplomatic ties with Iran, following the execution of a prominent Shiite cleric and subsequent attacks on Saudi diplomatic compounds in Iran. The diplomatic crisis has fueled concerns about intensifying proxy conflicts in Yemen and Syria, and raised doubts about upcoming peace negotiations in the region. Both nations’ officials have called for continued diplomacy, but aggressive rhetoric and trade bans highlight the deepening rift.

255975_255975.caption: People dig out their cars on Jones Street in Sioux City
255975_255975.article_context: A massive winter storm swept across the central and eastern United States, affecting 20 states and 60 million people, with heavy snow, sleet, and freezing rain causing dangerous conditions. Nebraska, Oklahoma, and Kansas received up to 17 inches of snow, leading to widespread travel disruptions, airport closures, and shut down highways. Schools, government offices, and legislatures in several states closed, and Missouri declared a state of emergency. The storm was forecast to weaken as it moved east, but still threatened additional snow and ice across the Great Lakes and Northeast, with potential record snowfall in Boston. Despite the hardships, the moisture brought some relief to drought-stricken farm areas.

506942_506942.caption: PRIDE JA was the first public gay pride celebration in the Englishspeaking Caribbean after a similar event had to be canceled due to security concerns in the Bahamas last year
506942_506942.article_context: Jamaica hosted its first public gay pride celebration, PRIDE JA, marking a significant moment for the country's LGBT community in a society often described as highly homophobic. Organized by JFLAG, the week-long events provided a rare safe space for LGBT Jamaicans to express themselves openly and with pride. The celebration comes amid ongoing challenges, including legal discrimination and frequent homophobic violence, but was seen as a step toward greater visibility and acceptance. While the event drew both support and criticism, it highlighted the ongoing struggle for broader social and legal change in Jamaica.

704784_704784.caption: Google data shows a significant growth in internet content collection from its products by the NSA
704784_704784.article_context: Major tech companies, including Microsoft, Google, Facebook, and Yahoo, disclosed for the first time that tens of thousands of user accounts have had data handed over to U.S. government authorities every six months due to secret court orders as part of the NSA’s Prism surveillance program. This transparency was allowed after a deal with the Justice Department, although the companies can only release data in broad ranges and must wait six months before disclosing recent requests. The disclosures revealed significant growth in government requests over recent years, but lack detailed information that advocates and the companies themselves argue is necessary for proper accountability. The tech firms called for greater transparency about the types and impacts of these government data requests, expressing ongoing concern about communication intercepted outside legal processes.

1212088_1212088.caption: Hundreds gather for a protest rally against the Confederate flag in Columbia South Carolina on 20 June
1212088_1212088.article_context: Following the Charleston church massacre by a young white man with white supremacist motives, protests and rallies emphasized the need for white Americans to take active responsibility in combating racism and supporting black communities. Activists and organizers called for white participants to move beyond passive allyship and become engaged co-conspirators in the fight against racial injustice. Key figures highlighted the importance of white people acknowledging their privilege, addressing racism within their own circles, and supporting black-led movements. The ongoing conversation also included calls for white individuals to confront discomfort and take direct action, rather than merely expressing sympathy.

125165_125165.caption: A USmade Reaper drone part of Operation Barkhane s aerial detachment flies over a Nigerian military airport in Niamey in January 2015
125165_125165.article_context: The U.S. has secretly expanded its global drone operations by establishing a base in Tunisia to conduct surveillance missions over neighboring Libya, targeting Islamic State militants. The deployment, which began in June, involves unarmed Reaper drones and about 70 U.S. military personnel, and is part of a broader strategy to enhance intelligence gathering and support counterterrorism efforts in North Africa. The move follows difficulties using existing drone bases in Europe and Africa due to logistical challenges and seeks to close a key intelligence gap in the region, especially around the Islamic State stronghold in Sirte. The agreement with Tunisia remains sensitive due to concerns over Tunisian public opinion and the country's political stability, but it allows for intelligence sharing and possible future arming of drones, contingent on Tunisian approval.

1636194_1636194.caption: Melilla s formidable border barrier does not deter migrants desperate to get into Europe
1636194_1636194.article_context: Over 200 migrants from sub-Saharan Africa forcefully entered Spain's North African enclave of Melilla by scaling the border fence, marking one of the largest such incidents in recent years. The break-in involved clashes with police and resulted in injuries among the migrants. Similar mass entries have recently occurred in both Melilla and Ceuta, as these Spanish territories have become key destinations for migrants seeking entry into Europe. The migrant reception centre in Melilla is now severely overcrowded, and authorities expect the new arrivals to be expelled.

267442_267442.caption: Typhoon victims wait for an evacuation flight at the airport in Tacloban Leyte island Philippines
267442_267442.article_context: Following the devastation caused by Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines, the U.S. government, through USAID and support from the Defense Department, began deploying emergency aid and resources, including search-and-rescue teams and supplies for health care, clean water, and shelter. Humanitarian organizations such as the American Red Cross activated family tracing services and private aid groups called for essential supplies. Tools like Google Person Finder were set up to assist in locating missing persons, while officials urged donations to reputable organizations to support relief efforts.

1092889_1092889.caption: A US soldier looks through the material found after the Palomares crash
1092889_1092889.article_context: Nearly 50 years after a US B-52 bomber carrying nuclear weapons crashed in Palomares, Spain, and contaminated the area with radioactive plutonium, the US and Spain have signed an agreement to clean up the site. US Secretary of State John Kerry and Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel García-Margallo announced that the contaminated earth will be shipped to the US for safe storage, likely in Nevada. The clean-up deal comes as the US increases its military presence in Spain, and follows renewed concerns about lingering radioactive pollution. The agreement is seen as part of broader negotiations around military and diplomatic cooperation between the two countries.

1224711_1224711.caption: Refugees making their way to MacedoniaGreece border crossing from Eidomeni Greece
1224711_1224711.article_context: Thousands of mainly Syrian refugees were stranded at Budapest railway station after the Hungarian government cancelled all international train services. Faced with increasing hardship and overcrowding, some refugees attempted to walk to Austria, while others faced hostility from locals. Hungarian authorities eventually chartered buses to transport the refugees to Austria after days of uncertainty. The article also documents refugees' journeys through border crossings in Greece, Macedonia, and Serbia, highlighting the challenges, chaos, and resilience experienced as they sought safe passage across Europe.

539832_539832.caption: Six Canadian CF18 fighter jets are still conducting sorties in Iraq and Syria
539832_539832.article_context: Canada's Conservative opposition has criticized Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's government for its 'incoherent' approach to the fight against ISIS, pointing to Canada's exclusion from a key meeting of US-led coalition allies in Paris. The Conservatives argue that Trudeau's decision to withdraw Canadian fighter jets from combat missions while increasing training and humanitarian roles has diminished Canada's standing among allies. Although Canadian forces remain involved in reconnaissance and support roles, the absence from the Paris talks is seen by critics as evidence of reduced influence in the anti-ISIS campaign. Government officials downplayed the exclusion, maintaining ongoing cooperation with coalition partners.

1027837_1027837.caption: Egyptian armoured vehicles patrol the town of Sheikh Zuweid Sinai earlier this month after four soldiers were killed by a roadside bomb
1027837_1027837.article_context: The United States is set to deliver eight F-16 fighter jets to Egypt within the next two days as part of a recently unfrozen military aid package, with four more jets scheduled for delivery in the autumn. This move follows President Barack Obama’s decision in March to reauthorize over $1.3 billion in weapons supplies to Egypt, including fighter jets, missiles, and tank kits. Despite concerns among US lawmakers about Egypt’s progress on democratic reforms, military ties between the two countries have strengthened since Abdel Fatah al-Sisi’s rise to power. US Secretary of State John Kerry is scheduled to visit Egypt soon to renew strategic dialogue between the nations.

896576_896576.caption: Syrian migrants cross under a fence as they enter Hungary at the border with Serbia
896576_896576.article_context: Germany’s foreign minister Frank-Walter Steinmeier warned that Germany may pursue legal action against EU member states, such as Slovakia and Hungary, that refuse to accept refugees according to the EU quota system. He emphasized that European solidarity requires shared responsibility and access to open borders. Slovakia and Hungary have resisted the quota and threatened legal challenges themselves. The EU faces continued tensions over the distribution of 160,000 refugees across its members, with leaders seeking agreement on new border controls and accelerating aid to Turkey to manage migration.

1609502_1609502.caption: Iraqi forces are being supported by Iranianbacked Shia militiamen in the offensive against Islamic State
1609502_1609502.article_context: Iraqi government forces, supported by Shia militias and local tribesmen, have made significant advances against Islamic State militants in the city of Tikrit, reportedly recapturing around 75% of the city, including key government sites. The operation marks a major step in the broader campaign to retake territory held by IS, with the recapture of Tikrit considered vital for future efforts to liberate Mosul. Ongoing fighting persists in some areas, but officials express optimism that the city will be fully retaken soon.

1533337_1533337.caption: Ukraine relies on gas imports from western Europe but storage is low ahead of the winter season
1533337_1533337.article_context: Ukraine and Russia have reached a consensus on resolving their ongoing gas dispute, with Ukraine agreeing to settle part of its debts and both sides establishing a price for winter gas supplies. Despite this progress, a key issue remains unresolved, as Ukraine seeks a binding six-month agreement that Russia's Gazprom has not yet accepted. Tensions stem from Russia's previous price hike and its halt of gas supplies to Ukraine over unpaid bills, following deteriorated relations after Ukraine's political upheaval. While negotiations continue alongside European Commission mediation, Ukraine's Naftogaz accuses Gazprom of trying to provoke a new crisis, and denies allegations of diverting gas intended for Europe.

854462_854462.caption: A woman takes shelter with her child in the basement of the 21st hospital of Donetsk s Oktyabrsk district
854462_854462.article_context: Donetsk, once the main city of eastern Ukraine's Donbass region, is now at the center of ongoing conflict as the capital of the self-proclaimed Donetsk People’s Republic. Despite intermittent shelling, daily life remains perilous, with many residents forced to live in basements and shelters due to destroyed homes and constant bombardment. The city faces severe shortages of food, water, and medicine, while humanitarian aid is distributed unevenly and sometimes sold on local markets. Volunteer groups like Responsible Citizens work to help civilians, but the coming winter poses a dire threat to those living in difficult conditions. Amid growing fears and uncertainty, residents express anxiety over political developments, the potential for renewed fighting, and their ability to survive the harsh environment.

1570352_1570352.caption: Afghanistan s national airline suffered under the Taliban
1570352_1570352.article_context: The article reflects on the changes in Kabul since the fall of the Taliban in 2001, highlighting the city's rapid modernization alongside lingering signs of conflict. As Afghanistan approaches a pivotal presidential election, the city is abuzz with political activity and debate, with numerous candidates from both traditional and modern backgrounds vying for power. Amid concerns over security, electoral legitimacy, and possible delays, the outcome of the election is seen as critical to determining whether Afghanistan will progress toward stability or risk returning to instability.

982786_982786.caption: Routes from North Korea to Seoul and Bejing do nt display
982786_982786.article_context: Google Maps has expanded its coverage in North Korea, providing satellite navigation, mapping of roads and landmarks, and route calculation features via its web and mobile applications. Despite North Korea’s restrictions on internal movement and limited vehicle and internet access, the map data is now available to outside users, displaying major roads, buildings, and even notable sites like the Yodok concentration camp. However, Google Maps lacks border crossing information and public transport schedules, and South Korean security regulations prevent mapping within the DMZ. The project reflects Google’s ongoing collaboration with global users to improve map quality for the secretive country.

693270_693270.caption: Tuvalu a series of lowlying islands in the Pacific has declared a state of emergency due to water shortages
693270_693270.article_context: Tuvalu has declared a state of emergency due to a severe fresh water shortage, with some areas facing only a two-day supply. New Zealand responded by sending aid workers, desalination units, and water containers to help address the crisis, and officials have expressed concern that nearby Pacific islands like Tokelau may also be at risk. The situation follows six months of low rainfall, and aid agencies are working on both immediate relief and long-term solutions.

332652_332652.caption: A family of five drowned after their SUV plunged into Tempe Town Lake
332652_332652.article_context: Tempe police have ruled a tragic incident at Tempe Town Lake as a murder-suicide, in which Glenn Edward Baxter, who was separated from his wife, intentionally drove his estranged wife's SUV into the lake, killing himself, his wife Danica Baxter, and their three young children. Surveillance footage showed Baxter scouting the location before driving into the water shortly after midnight. The family was in the process of separating, and Danica Baxter had begun divorce proceedings. Despite rescue attempts, all victims died, and the event has deeply affected the community.

622263_622263.caption: Demonstrators hold signs during a silent march in New York to end the NYPD s stopandfrisk program last summer
622263_622263.article_context: In a landmark class action lawsuit challenging New York City's stop-and-frisk program, two NYPD officers testified that a high-pressure quota system drives the controversial policing practice, leading to widespread and disproportionate stops of minorities. Plaintiffs allege systemic, unconstitutional harassment of Black and Latino communities, supported by secretly recorded conversations implicating supervisors in promoting quota-driven and racially biased stops. City officials, including Mayor Bloomberg and Police Commissioner Kelly, defend the program as vital for crime reduction and deny the existence of quotas or racial targeting. The case raises significant questions about civil rights, police accountability, and the future of NYPD policies.

188957_188957.caption: An Afghan National Army soldier keeps watch near the Provincial Reconstruction Team as a NATO helicopter flies over the site of an attack in Jalalabad province April 15 2012
188957_188957.article_context: As the U.S. military presence in Afghanistan rapidly decreases, American diplomats and civilian aid workers are now largely confined to Kabul, making direct oversight of billions of dollars in U.S.-funded development projects throughout the country nearly impossible. To continue monitoring these projects, the State Department plans to rely on private contractors and remote methods such as aerial imagery and phone surveys. The transition is a result of heightened security risks and the loss of military support, leading to a drastic reduction in personnel stationed outside the capital. Critics question the effectiveness of these new strategies and the overall impact of previous civilian initiatives, amid ongoing concerns about corruption, waste, and the ability of Afghans to sustain development progress as U.S. involvement diminishes.

333838_333838.caption: A plume of smoke rises after an airstrike in eastern Kobani Syria
333838_333838.article_context: The United States has begun expanded airstrikes in Iraq against Islamic State militants, marking a shift from prior operations that focused on protecting American interests and humanitarian missions. These latest strikes, supporting Iraqi forces near Baghdad and Sinjar, follow President Obama's announcement of a campaign to 'degrade and ultimately destroy' ISIS. While the U.S. seeks international cooperation, including talks with Iran, Iran has rejected joining the coalition against the Islamic State due to distrust of American intentions. Secretary of State John Kerry met with global leaders in Paris to rally support, as the U.S. reports having conducted 162 airstrikes in Iraq since August, and the CIA estimates that ISIS has up to 31,500 fighters.

1483224_1483224.caption: Syrian rebel positions around Damascus were heavily bombarded on Friday
1483224_1483224.article_context: A major temporary truce in Syria’s five-year civil war, brokered by the United States and Russia, came into effect at midnight, aiming to halt hostilities between the Syrian government and rebel factions, though it excludes ISIS and al-Qaeda-linked groups. Initial reports indicated a general reduction in violence, with Russia suspending airstrikes against groups participating in the truce. However, isolated attacks and accusations of violations were reported on both sides, including government shelling and rebel claims of attacks. The US-led coalition continued to target ISIS, who launched assaults on Kurdish-held areas. The ceasefire is seen as a critical step to resume peace talks and allow humanitarian aid into besieged areas, but concerns remain over attempts to undermine the agreement, especially amidst ongoing tensions between international backers of opposing sides.

54948_54948.caption: Demonstrators march against amnesty for immigrants in the US illegally during a July 15 rally against the immigration reform bill in Washington
54948_54948.article_context: A new Washington Post-ABC News poll reveals broad support among Americans for both increased border security and a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants, but deep partisan and demographic divides hinder comprehensive immigration reform. While most Hispanics and half of Americans would be disappointed if citizenship provisions are omitted, the majority of Republicans oppose such measures, putting pressure on GOP leaders and complicating their efforts to appeal to Hispanic voters ahead of future elections. The poll also highlights internal dissatisfaction among Republicans with their party's direction, while Democrats remain more united despite lingering concerns over President Obama's healthcare law and approval ratings. Overall, the poll underscores the political challenges facing both parties as immigration policy moves to the forefront in Congress.

414956_414956.caption: Evidence markers line the parking lot of a mass shooting at Club Blu in Fort Myers
414956_414956.article_context: An early morning shooting at Club Blu Bar and Grill in Fort Myers, Florida, during a teen event resulted in more than a dozen people being shot, with at least two fatalities – 14-year-old Sean Archilles and 18-year-old high school basketball player Ste'fan Strawder. Police responded to related incidents nearby and have detained several individuals for questioning. Authorities have stated the shooting was not connected to terrorism. The victims ranged in age from 12 to 27, and the most seriously injured required surgery. The club, which was hosting a ‘swimsuit glow party’ for teens, expressed condolences following the tragedy.

46863_46863.caption: Russian humanitarian aid convoy sets out for Ukraine
46863_46863.article_context: A large convoy of Russian aid trucks departed for eastern Ukraine, raising concerns among Ukrainian and Western officials that the effort could be a cover for supporting pro-Russian rebels amid ongoing conflict. Ukraine warned that any unauthorized entry by the convoy would be considered an invasion and insisted that all aid should be delivered according to its rules, with inspection and distribution managed by the International Red Cross. While Russia agreed to some conditions, including allowing observers and using Ukrainian-held border crossings, logistical and security issues remained unresolved. Western leaders called for coordination with the Ukrainian government to prevent misuse of humanitarian aid, reflecting ongoing distrust and tension between Russia and Ukraine.

167836_167836.caption: Israeli leftwing activists demonstrate against a new law that bans boycotts of West Bank products
167836_167836.article_context: Israel's parliament has passed a controversial law penalizing individuals and organizations that publicly call for boycotts of Israeli settlement products in the West Bank. The law allows affected businesses to sue boycott advocates for damages and denies state benefits to those promoting boycotts. This legislation has sparked significant public debate and defiance, with critics arguing that it infringes on free speech and planning to challenge its constitutionality in the Supreme Court. Settlement businesses, like the Psagot Winery, have experienced mixed reactions, with some customers supporting and others avoiding their products due to the law.

790597_790597.caption: In 2010 the Stuxnet computer virus was discovered to have knocked out centrifuges at Iran s Bushehr nuclear enrichment plant
790597_790597.article_context: Junaid Hussain, a British hacker once dismissed as a prankster, later joined ISIS in Syria, becoming a key figure in their online operations. ISIS has increasingly recruited tech-savvy individuals to support propaganda and cyber activities, highlighted by the embarrassing hack of the US Central Command’s Twitter and YouTube accounts. Although these attacks have focused largely on publicity rather than serious damage, experts warn ISIS and similar groups possess growing capabilities to exploit technological vulnerabilities, with potential future risks to critical infrastructure. The group’s cyber efforts are currently constrained by military pressures, but the threat of more sophisticated attacks remains as the digital landscape evolves and security protections lag behind hackers’ abilities.

1614111_1614111.caption: Saturday s agreement was signed in the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur
1614111_1614111.article_context: The Philippines has finalized the last section of a peace agreement with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), a major Muslim rebel group in the south. The deal, which follows a framework set out in 2012, outlines the rebels surrendering their weapons in exchange for self-rule in southern regions. Reached in Kuala Lumpur, this accord paves the way for a comprehensive peace treaty and marks the end of formal negotiations after decades of violence that have killed tens of thousands. Both sides acknowledge that implementing the agreement will be a significant challenge moving forward.

1055612_1055612.caption: Afghan security personnel attempt to enter the British Council building
1055612_1055612.article_context: A suicide attack targeted the British Council building in Kabul, Afghanistan, resulting in casualties and prompting an extensive response from Afghan security forces and emergency personnel. The assault involved explosions and gunfire, causing significant damage and wounding both Afghan police officers and embassy staff. Security forces eventually gained control of the scene after a lengthy confrontation with the assailants.

1273574_1273574.caption: A member of the Occupy Wall Street movement demonstrates in Zuccotti Park during the first snow fall of winter in New York October 29 2011
1273574_1273574.article_context: Occupy Wall Street protesters in New York City faced a severe October snowstorm, testing their resolve and ability to endure harsh winter conditions. Despite tents collapsing and freezing temperatures, a core group of activists remained determined to continue their occupation of Zuccotti Park, viewing this weather challenge as a pivotal test of the movement's strength and commitment. Organizers emphasized the importance of maintaining a physical presence in the financial district, believing their ongoing occupation to be essential for their cause and visibility.

1682836_1682836.caption: Whitenose syndrome has now been confirmed in 28 US state and five Canadian provinces
1682836_1682836.article_context: Wildlife officials have raised alarms after white-nose syndrome, a deadly fungal disease that has killed millions of bats in eastern North America, was discovered on the US Pacific coast for the first time, in Washington state. First identified in New York in 2006, the disease has now spread to 28 states and five Canadian provinces, making it one of the worst wildlife health crises in recent US history. The fungus, Pseudogymnoascus destructans, threatens hibernating bats and can wipe out entire populations, posing significant ecological and economic risks due to bats' role in pest control. Authorities are ramping up surveillance and collaborative efforts to combat the spread, while studies suggest some bat species might eventually develop resistance to the disease.

56990_56990.caption: Soldiers patrol along a fence seen from a migrant camp near the border with Hungary in Horgos Serbia on July 25 2016
56990_56990.article_context: Hungarian authorities have implemented a new tactic to deter migrants from crossing into the country by placing makeshift scarecrows along the border with Serbia. This comes amid ongoing efforts by Hungary's right-wing government to keep out Syrian refugees and others seeking passage to Western Europe, including the construction of a border fence. Photos of these scarecrows—made partially from carved sugar beet root—were shared on social media by supporters of Hungary's border patrol forces. Reports suggest no migrants have crossed in the areas where the scarecrows have been placed in the past month.
