737498_737498.article_context: Jeremy Ractliffe, former head of the Nelson Mandela Children's Fund, admitted to receiving three uncut diamonds from Naomi Campbell after a 1997 dinner attended by former Liberian president Charles Taylor. Ractliffe kept the stones to avoid legal and reputational issues and recently handed them over to South African authorities. The diamonds are linked to the war crimes trial of Taylor, who is accused of using illegal diamond sales to fuel Sierra Leone's civil war. Ractliffe expressed willingness to testify at the trial, while police investigate whether he possessed the diamonds illegally.

792462_792462.caption: Dominique StraussKahn is taken out of a police station in New York on May 15 2011
792462_792462.article_context: In his first major newspaper interview since his fall from grace, Dominique Strauss-Kahn discusses how a sexual assault accusation at the Sofitel hotel in New York in May 2011 ended his leadership at the IMF and his presidential ambitions in France. Strauss-Kahn suggests his downfall may have been orchestrated by political rivals, citing evidence of surveillance and alleging that French officials intervened in his legal troubles. Despite having the charges dropped after the accuser’s credibility was questioned, his reputation suffered irreparable damage. He also faces unrelated charges in France over attending sex parties. Strauss-Kahn maintains his innocence and expresses regret over not being able to help resolve the European debt crisis.

364658_364658.caption: President Obama pauses as he makes a statement to the press on April 2 in Chicago about the shooting at the Fort Hood military base in Texas
364658_364658.article_context: President Obama addressed the nation following a second mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas in five years, expressing condolences to affected families and emphasizing federal efforts to determine the cause of the tragedy and ensure the community's safety. He stated that his national security team was working closely with the Defense Department and FBI, and assured that the government was committed to supporting Fort Hood through both the investigation and its aftermath.

446938_446938.caption: Rob Ford attends a council meeting at city hall where councillor Pam MacConnell was knocked over
446938_446938.article_context: Toronto mayor Rob Ford admitted to smoking crack cocaine while intoxicated and acknowledged embarrassing himself and the city. Amid mounting scandals—including drug use, crude remarks, ties to a suspected drug dealer, and unruly behavior during council meetings—Ford was stripped of many mayoral powers by the city council but remains in office. Despite police investigations and calls for his resignation, Ford insists he is not an addict and continues to seek public support while facing significant backlash.

239910_239910.caption: President Obama announces new economic sanctions against the Russian economyat the White House on Tuesday
239910_239910.article_context: President Obama and the European Union announced new, broader sanctions against Russia targeting key sectors like energy, banking, and arms, in response to Russia's support for separatists in Ukraine and the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17. The measures aim to cripple Russia's economy and pressure President Putin to seek a diplomatic solution. These sanctions mark a significant escalation in tensions between Russia and the West, reminiscent of the Cold War era. Despite expectations that the penalties will increase Russia's economic isolation and hardship, analysts are uncertain whether they will immediately alter Putin's actions in Ukraine.

464081_464081.caption: Tony Abbott with his wife Margie and daughters Louise Frances and Bridgette celebrate his election victory in September 2013
464081_464081.article_context: Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott has pushed back against a UN Committee's recommendation to ban parents from smacking their children, arguing that such a ban could turn Australia into a 'nanny state.' Abbott, who admits to occasionally giving his own children gentle smacks, believes there is a place for mild physical discipline as long as it does not harm the child. The UN report also suggests that teachers and childcare workers report cases of smacking, but Abbott sees this as an example of excessive political correctness.

431555_431555.caption: Donald Trump addresses supporters celebrating his victory in the South Carolina Republican primary Saturday Feb 20
431555_431555.article_context: Marlene Ricketts, wife of billionaire J. Joe Ricketts, contributed $3 million to Our Principles PAC, a super PAC dedicated to opposing Republican presidential front-runner Donald Trump through negative ads and voter outreach. The PAC, led by Katie Packer, has spent over $3.5 million on anti-Trump efforts and plans to intensify its campaign in upcoming primary states, despite Trump's continued success. Ricketts has previously supported other Republican candidates, illustrating the party elite's resistance to Trump's candidacy.

169813_169813.caption: Jason Rezaian left hugs Bezos
169813_169813.article_context: At the opening ceremony of The Washington Post's new headquarters, reporter Jason Rezaian and Secretary of State John Kerry spoke about Rezaian's 18-month imprisonment in Iran and the challenging negotiations that led to his release. Both men emphasized the importance of bringing home Americans in trouble and highlighted the pivotal role played by U.S. officials and The Post in securing freedom for Rezaian and other detainees. Kerry also underscored the dangers faced by journalists globally and the critical importance of a free press, while expressing continued commitment to finding missing Americans such as Robert Levinson.

858380_858380.caption: Attorney Gloria Allred holds a vial of blood in Los Angeles representing the evidence police found in the OJ Simpson case
858380_858380.article_context: Celebrity lawyer Gloria Allred has taken on the representation of Yovanka Bryant, ex-girlfriend of the Miami face-eating attack suspect Rudy Eugene, continuing her pattern of involving herself in high-profile and sensational cases. Allred is renowned for representing clients in major media controversies, having previously played key roles in the OJ Simpson trial, lawsuits involving Dodi Fayed and Princess Diana, the Scott Peterson trial, paternity and harassment cases against celebrities like Eddie Murphy and David Boreanaz, and scandals involving figures such as Tiger Woods, Anthony Wiener, Herman Cain, and Jenna Talackova. Her presence often brings significant media attention and press conferences to her clients' cases.

373468_373468.caption: Actor Tom Selleck arrives Friday for funeral services being held for Nancy Reagan
373468_373468.article_context: Former First Lady Nancy Reagan was honored at a funeral held at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, attended by hundreds of friends, dignitaries, and family members. Speakers, including her son Ronald Prescott Reagan and former chief of staff James Baker, remembered her as a devoted wife to President Ronald Reagan and a strong, caring figure. The service brought together prominent figures from both political parties, including Michelle Obama, George W. Bush, Laura Bush, Rosalynn Carter, and Hillary Clinton. Nancy Reagan, who died at 94 of congestive heart failure, was laid to rest beside her husband, marking the event as a celebration of her life and enduring legacy.

397777_397777.caption: Nadezhda Tolokonnikova speaks to the media as she leaves the prison in Krasnoyarsk Russia Monday
397777_397777.article_context: Two members of the Russian punk band Pussy Riot, Nadezhda Tolokonnikova and Maria Alekhina, were released from prison after serving nearly two years for a protest performance at Moscow's main cathedral. Their early release, granted as part of an official amnesty, is widely viewed as an attempt by the Kremlin to address international criticism of Russia's human rights record ahead of the Sochi Winter Olympics. After their release, Tolokonnikova and Alekhina announced plans to collaborate on a human rights project.

636878_636878.caption: Barack Obama speaks to supporters in Cleveland during his last rally before the midterm elections
636878_636878.article_context: Barack Obama held his final campaign rally before the midterm elections in Cleveland, aiming to recapture the enthusiasm of 2008, but turnout was significantly lower, reflecting public disappointment and economic frustration. With Republicans favored to win control of the House and make major Senate and gubernatorial gains, the election is seen as a referendum on Obama’s presidency. Polls indicate widespread dissatisfaction, even among Democrats, with many open to a primary challenge against Obama in 2012. Republican leaders have vowed to reverse Obama’s policies if victorious, while Democratic hopes rely on young and early voters to mitigate expected losses.

64175_64175.caption: Democratic presidential candidate Bernie Sanders addresses a rally at the Santa Clara County Fairgrounds in San Jose Calif on May 18
64175_64175.article_context: Senator Bernie Sanders publicly endorsed Tim Canova, a former Capitol Hill staffer and his former adviser, in the Democratic primary against DNC Chairwoman Debbie Wasserman Schultz for her Florida congressional seat. Sanders stated that Canova's views align more closely with his own and said he would not re-appoint Wasserman Schultz as DNC chair if elected president. Canova, who models his campaign after Sanders with grassroots fundraising and union support, welcomed the endorsement, while Wasserman Schultz has maintained her position with strong fundraising and has avoided direct engagement with Canova.

413826_413826.caption: Donald Trump announces his presidential candidacy on June 16 2015 in New York City
413826_413826.article_context: Donald Trump announced his candidacy for the Republican presidential nomination, delivering a speech in which he made several inaccurate and misleading statements regarding the economy, jobs, unemployment rates, trade, national security, and health care. Fact-checks show that Trump exaggerated claims about negative economic growth, job availability, and unemployment rates, proposed tax measures on Ford that would violate trade agreements, and falsely stated that the Taliban prisoners swapped for Sgt. Bowe Bergdahl had returned to the battlefield. Additionally, Trump misrepresented health care premium increases by citing only extreme cases of proposed rate hikes while ignoring regulatory oversight and more moderate changes reported in most states.

507303_507303.caption: All Progressives Congress presidential candidate Muhammadu Buhari raises his hand during a campaign rally in the northeast city of Maiduguri earlier in February
507303_507303.article_context: Nigeria’s leading presidential challenger, Muhammadu Buhari, pledged to defeat Boko Haram insurgents by improving military equipment, training, and intelligence, criticizing President Goodluck Jonathan's government for prioritizing political goals over fighting terrorism. Buhari argued that the army lacked sufficient support and resources to rescue the Chibok schoolgirls and reclaim territories lost to militants, and questioned claims of progress against Boko Haram, noting that neighboring countries have had greater military success. He vowed that, if elected, Nigeria would regain stability and territorial integrity, while dismissing concerns about his health and calling for no further delays in the upcoming election.

167300_167300.caption: Leaders of the March on Washington including the Rev Martin Luther King Jr and John Lewis meet with President John F Kennedy
167300_167300.article_context: Civil rights leader and Congressman John Lewis publicly defended Edward Snowden, characterizing his actions as an example of civil disobedience akin to historical figures like Thoreau and Gandhi. In contrast to harsh criticism from government officials who labeled Snowden a traitor, Lewis argued that Snowden was justified in defying unjust laws, referencing the philosophy of non-violent protest. Lewis’s perspective stands out given his prominent background in the civil rights movement.

144226_144226.caption: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Terry McAuliffe campaigns at George Mason University in May
144226_144226.article_context: Virginia gubernatorial candidate Terry McAuliffe stated he was unaware of an SEC investigation into his former company, GreenTech Automotive, until contacted by the press. The investigation focuses on how GreenTech and a related firm, Gulf Coast Funds Management, solicited foreign investors through the EB-5 visa program. McAuliffe criticized Republican Senator Charles Grassley for releasing information about the inquiry for political reasons, although Grassley’s office cited national security and economic concerns about the program. Both GreenTech and Gulf Coast have confirmed receiving SEC subpoenas and pledged to cooperate with the investigation.

93787_93787.caption: Secretary of State John F Kerry addresses the meeting about the Paris Agreement on climate change in the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday
93787_93787.article_context: The Paris climate agreement is nearing formal activation, as 60 countries — almost reaching the required 55 percent of global emissions — have officially joined the pact. At a United Nations ceremony, key emitters like Mexico, Argentina, Ukraine, and the United Arab Emirates joined, and the European Union pledged rapid ratification, making entry into force likely this year. Once active, the agreement commits countries to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius. The speed of ratification surpasses expectations, driven by leadership from the United States and China. However, concerns persist over potential U.S. withdrawal under a possible Trump presidency, though such an exit would take four years. The rapid progress reflects unprecedented international consensus and momentum on climate action.

310658_310658.caption: Sarah Palin and her family were at a birthday party gone bad in Anchorage
310658_310658.article_context: USA TODAY revisited notable news stories from each state in 2014, highlighting major events that shaped the national conversation. Key stories included the wave of protests following the police-involved deaths of Michael Brown in Missouri and Eric Garner in New York, legal sales of recreational marijuana commencing in Colorado, Detroit exiting bankruptcy in Michigan, and Jeb Bush's announcement to explore a 2016 presidential run in Florida. Other significant events were the Arizona court ruling allowing 'dreamers' to obtain driver's licenses, Tesla's decision to build a large factory in Nevada, the tragic hot-car death and subsequent murder indictment in Georgia, the devastating Oso mudslide in Washington, and controversies like New Jersey's Bridgegate and Oklahoma's lethal injection protocols. National debates on issues such as police use of force, immigration, civil rights, and LGBT protections were also prominent, reflecting evolving public opinion and policy across America.

871602_871602.caption: Billy Ray Cyrus has been caught out on Twitter accidentally retweeting a picture of Jimmy Savile
871602_871602.article_context: Country singer Billy Ray Cyrus inadvertently retweeted a photo of notorious criminal Jimmy Savile after a follower falsely claimed the image was of his grandfather, who is supposedly a fan. This incident mirrors a similar earlier mistake by Donald Trump, highlighting a growing trend of tricking celebrities into sharing inappropriate images on social media. Both celebrities expressed regret over the incidents, prompting discussions about the risks of managing personal social media accounts.

980068_980068.caption: David Cameron at RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus last October at the beginning of the bombing campaign against Isis targets in Iraq
980068_980068.article_context: Senior Conservative MP Julian Lewis and former UK ambassador to Syria Peter Ford have warned against Prime Minister David Cameron's proposal to extend British airstrikes against ISIS from Iraq into Syria, calling it dangerous and pointless. They argue there are no credible ground forces in Syria to support such action and express concerns about potential escalation, including attacks on the Assad regime, which could lead to Islamist victories. The article highlights uncertainty over parliamentary support, risks for RAF pilots, and draws parallels to the destabilizing effect of previous interventions like Libya.

348026_348026.caption: Oscar Pistorius seen here at a February court appearance will stand trial in the shooting death of girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp
348026_348026.article_context: Oscar Pistorius, the double-amputee Olympian, was formally indicted in Pretoria, South Africa, on charges of murdering his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp, and illegally possessing ammunition. Prosecutors allege Pistorius shot Steenkamp intentionally and plan to present evidence suggesting an argument occurred before the shooting. Witnesses reportedly heard a woman scream before gunshots. Pistorius claims he mistook Steenkamp for an intruder. The trial, scheduled for March 3-20, will feature over 100 witnesses, and Pistorius faces a possible life sentence if convicted.

413038_413038.caption: Donald Trump addresses supporters during a campaign rally in Kissimmee Fla on Aug 11 2016
413038_413038.article_context: Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump attracted controversy by repeatedly claiming that President Obama founded the Islamic State (ISIS), and later suggested Hillary Clinton was a 'co-founder.' Despite these assertions being inaccurate, Trump defended his comments as sarcasm, criticizing media outlets for taking them literally. However, in interviews and rallies, he seemed to double down on his statements, leading to confusion and debate over his intent.

1252864_1252864.caption: Olympic and paralympic track star Oscar Pistorius in the dock during the trial for the murder of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp in March 2014
1252864_1252864.article_context: Oscar Pistorius, the Paralympian convicted of killing his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, was expected to be released from prison into house arrest after serving 10 months of a five-year sentence. However, South Africa's justice minister Michael Masutha halted the release at the last minute, citing a possible error in the parole board's application of the law regarding minimum time served for parole eligibility. This decision followed a petition from the Progressive Women’s Movement of South Africa, which has strong ties to the ANC’s Women’s League, and raised questions about political influence and the consistent interpretation of parole law. The move sparked debate over high-level interventions and the transparency of the justice process.

192366_192366.caption: Brazil s President Dilma Rousseff and former president Luiz Ignacio Lula da Silva attend a Workers Party s campaign rally in Sao Paulo in 2014
192366_192366.article_context: A major political crisis erupted in Brazil as President Dilma Rousseff appointed former president Lula da Silva as her chief of staff, widely perceived as a move to shield him from prosecution amid a sweeping corruption investigation known as Operation Car Wash. The decision provoked nationwide protests and legal battles, with a federal judge temporarily suspending Lula's appointment and another judge releasing wiretapped calls suggesting attempts to interfere in the probe. Both Rousseff and Lula are accused of trying to protect themselves and other political figures, while critics argue the investigation has become politically biased. The turmoil has intensified public outrage, divided legal opinion, and deepened Brazil’s political and economic instability.

389407_389407.caption: Vice President Biden delivers remarks on US policy in Iraq at the National Defense University April 9 2015 in Washington DC
389407_389407.article_context: Following Hillary Clinton's announcement that she is running for president in 2016, Vice President Joe Biden stated he still has time to decide whether he will enter the race. While Clinton commands significant attention and early support, a group of Biden supporters has launched a super PAC to encourage his candidacy, arguing that the nomination should not be a foregone conclusion. Biden remains noncommittal, citing ongoing responsibilities with President Obama and saying he will decide by summer. Both Biden and Clinton appeal to similar voter bases and represent continuity with Obama’s policies, but polling shows Clinton as the clear frontrunner. Biden’s ultimate decision may depend on Clinton’s fundraising and campaign momentum.

1222943_1222943.caption: Sarah Palin and John McCain on the campaign trail in the runup to the presidential election
1222943_1222943.article_context: Sarah Palin’s upcoming memoir, 'Going Rogue,' has generated significant hype ahead of its release, but early reports indicate it largely confirms known aspects of her political and personal life. The book details her troubled relationship with John McCain's campaign during the 2008 election, her dissatisfaction with how her daughter's pregnancy was handled publicly, and her negative experience in a televised interview with Katie Couric. Palin also discusses family matters, including her stance toward Levi Johnston, the father of her grandchild, expressing a desire to support him despite past conflicts. Meanwhile, Johnston has publicly criticized Palin, adding to the media attention surrounding the book and her nationwide promotional tour.

209480_209480.caption: Barack Obama takes the stage with Hillary Clinton at a June 2008 campaign event in Unity NH
209480_209480.article_context: President Obama formally endorsed Hillary Clinton for president, declaring her highly qualified and vowing to campaign for her. The endorsement followed Obama's meeting with Bernie Sanders, who indicated he will continue to push his policies at the Democratic convention despite Clinton securing enough delegates for the nomination. Senator Elizabeth Warren also endorsed Clinton, emphasizing the importance of defeating Republican nominee Donald Trump. While Sanders did not withdraw from the race, he affirmed his commitment to influencing the party platform and ultimately preventing Trump's victory in the general election.

154810_154810.caption: This image from video provided by the FBI shows James Whitey Bulger and his girlfriend Catherine Greig
154810_154810.article_context: Catherine Greig, longtime girlfriend of notorious Boston mob boss James 'Whitey' Bulger, was sentenced to an additional 21 months in prison for refusing to cooperate with a federal grand jury investigating Bulger’s years on the run. Greig, already serving an eight-year sentence for aiding Bulger as a fugitive, remained loyal and declined to testify about whether others helped Bulger evade law enforcement for 16 years. Her actions were criticized by the judge, prosecutors, and victims’ families, as her defiance delayed justice for Bulger's victims.

690500_690500.caption: Hamid Karzai spoke with John Kerry his principal interlocutor on the accord over the phone for the second time in as many days
690500_690500.article_context: As the US and Afghanistan near a security agreement that would keep some American troops in Afghanistan beyond 2014, the Obama administration is resisting Afghan calls for a formal apology for civilian casualties caused during the twelve-year war. While the administration may offer reassurances about commitment to Afghan security and acknowledge past mistakes, top officials insist that an apology is 'not on the table.' Discussions focus on the terms of continued US military presence, including permissions for US troops and addressing Afghan concerns, amid ongoing tensions and controversy over past incidents involving US forces.

672822_672822.caption: 3 October 2011 Lawyer Giulia Bongiorno embraces Raffaele Sollecito who also won his appeal against murder conviction
672822_672822.article_context: The murder of British student Meredith Kercher in Perugia, Italy in November 2007 led to a high-profile investigation and trial involving Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito, who were initially convicted of the crime. Rudy Guede was also arrested and sentenced for his role in the murder. Throughout a series of appeals and court hearings, Knox and Sollecito maintained their innocence, ultimately leading to their acquittal on 3 October 2011, while Guede's conviction remained. The case attracted significant international attention and sparked debates about the Italian legal system and media coverage.

616135_616135.caption: Pope Francis tells his weekly general audience in St Peter s Square This home of ours is being ruined
616135_616135.article_context: Pope Francis is set to release a landmark encyclical urging global action on climate change, emphasizing humanity's moral responsibility to protect the environment and move away from fossil fuels. The document, positioned as both a theological and practical guide, appeals for urgent action to prevent further damage to the planet, particularly for the poor. Its release, timed ahead of major international summits and Francis’s visit to the US, has drawn criticism from some conservative politicians but has been praised by progressives. The encyclical expands the Church's social teaching to include ecology, while also reaffirming traditional stances against abortion and contraception.

461346_461346.caption: Anders Behring Breivik appears in court in Oslo His sanity has become one of the key issues of the trial
461346_461346.article_context: During the trial of Anders Behring Breivik for the murder of 77 people in Norway, evidence was presented showing that social workers had considered removing him from his mother's care during his childhood due to behavioral issues. Two psychiatrists testified that Breivik suffered from paranoid schizophrenia when he committed the attacks, though this diagnosis was later disputed by another medical team. The court is focusing on whether Breivik was sane and can be held criminally responsible, with testimony drawing on his challenging upbringing, lack of remorse, and delusional beliefs about his own importance.

1523838_1523838.caption: Chancellor Merkel briefed Bundestag deputies on German foreign policy
1523838_1523838.article_context: At an EU summit in Latvia, European leaders met with six former Soviet states amid tensions over Russia’s recent actions in Ukraine. European Council President Donald Tusk accused Russia of using aggressive tactics against its neighbors, but stressed that the EU’s partnership was not aimed at isolating Russia. German Chancellor Angela Merkel clarified that the summit was not about EU expansion and rejected Russia’s return to the G7. The discussions were overshadowed by Russia’s involvement in the conflict in eastern Ukraine and pressure on its former allies. During the summit, the EU was expected to approve financial aid to Ukraine, while military drills involving US troops took place in Georgia and Ukraine, further highlighting the ongoing geopolitical divide.

70342_70342.caption: President Obama is greeted as he arrives for funeral services for Pinckney in Charleston REUTERSBrian Snyder
70342_70342.article_context: At the funeral for South Carolina State Sen. Clementa Pinckney, who was killed in the Charleston church shooting, President Obama delivered a moving eulogy and sang 'Amazing Grace.' He used the moment to reflect on the deeper meaning of grace, highlighting Pinckney's compassionate life and the importance of empathy and unity. Obama's public exploration of grace underscored themes of compassion, generosity, and healing, culminating in a call for grace to unite the nation during times of pain and difficulty.

464500_464500.caption: John Boehner the Republican speaker of the House of Representatives keeps an eye on President Barack Obama
464500_464500.article_context: This week, US lawmakers and the Obama administration have been negotiating over the looming 'fiscal cliff,' which refers to the expiration of Bush-era tax cuts and automatic government spending cuts. The debate centers on preventing potential economic fallout if no agreement is reached, affecting Americans’ paychecks and having broader global consequences. The article invites readers to participate in a live chat with finance experts to discuss unresolved issues and answer questions about the fiscal cliff and its impact.

333007_333007.caption: Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont speaks during a presidential campaign stop at the France A Cordova Recreation Sports Center on the Purdue campus in West Lafayette on April 27 2016
333007_333007.article_context: After a series of primary losses, Bernie Sanders announced he will continue his campaign for the Democratic presidential nomination, emphasizing the need for a 'political revolution.' Sanders admitted acknowledging a backup plan to influence the party platform at the upcoming Democratic National Convention, focusing on issues such as a $15 minimum wage, Medicare-for-all, and free public college. Despite trailing Hillary Clinton significantly in delegates, Sanders maintained his commitment to his agenda, appealing to supporters at Indiana college rallies and critiquing corporate practices that harm workers. Meanwhile, his campaign is restructuring and laying off staff as it shifts its focus toward shaping the convention.

672795_672795.caption: 2 November 2007 Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito outside the rented house where Meredith Kercher was found dead
672795_672795.article_context: In November 2007, Meredith Kercher was found murdered in Perugia, Italy, leading to the arrest and conviction of Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito. Rudy Guede was also convicted for the crime after being apprehended in Germany. Knox and Sollecito faced a highly publicized trial and were initially found guilty. However, after several years and multiple appeals, both were acquitted and released in October 2011, following widespread international attention and criticism of the investigation and judicial process.

750435_750435.caption: Indian Aam Aadmi party chief Arvind Kejriwal greets supporters during an election rally in Delhi
750435_750435.article_context: The anti-corruption Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), led by activist Arvind Kejriwal, achieved a landslide victory in Delhi’s state assembly elections, winning 67 out of 70 seats. This marks a significant setback for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which won only three seats, and further weakens the Congress party, which failed to win any seats. Kejriwal, campaigning on anti-establishment and pro-common man promises, is set to be sworn in as Delhi’s chief minister. Analysts say the results reflect a desire for change in Delhi politics and challenge the dominance of the BJP, indicating a shift in public sentiment towards alternative political leadership.

43327_43327.caption: Demonstrators march from the Immigration and Customs Enforcement headquarters to the White House while demanding that President Obama halt deportations The march took place Aug 28 in Washington DC
43327_43327.article_context: A recent Pew Research Center poll reveals that many Democratic-leaning Hispanics are dissatisfied with their party’s handling of immigration, with 52% saying Democrats aren’t doing a good job on the issue. This disappointment follows a steady decline in President Obama’s support among Hispanics since his 2012 re-election. Activists had hoped Obama would take decisive executive action on immigration before the midterm elections, but he delayed, further dampening enthusiasm. The White House still plans to act on immigration reform by the end of the year, which could help regain Latino support, but Democrats risk lower turnout from this key demographic if concerns aren’t addressed.

672836_672836.caption: 26 September 2008 Amanda Knox is escorted by penitentiary police officers to Perugia s court at the end of a hearing
672836_672836.article_context: In November 2007, British student Meredith Kercher was found murdered in Perugia, Italy. Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito were arrested and later convicted of the crime, while Rudy Guede was also implicated and sentenced to prison. Over a series of highly publicized trials and appeals, Knox and Sollecito maintained their innocence and faced significant international media attention. Ultimately, in October 2011, both Knox and Sollecito were acquitted and released after their murder convictions were overturned by an Italian appeals court, prompting emotional reactions from their families and supporters.

199504_199504.caption: US President Barack Obama delivers a live televised address to the nation on his plans for military action against the Islamic State
199504_199504.article_context: President Obama pledged to destroy the Islamic State with military action, but The Washington Post editorial argues this approach is insufficient. The article emphasizes that relying solely on airstrikes and training local forces will not end terrorism in Iraq and Syria, and warns that without U.S. support for building local institutions like governments and economies, terrorist groups will re-emerge. The editorial criticizes the proposed 'Yemen model' as ineffective in similar contexts and calls for a sustained commitment to nation-building, highlighting that America's involvement should go beyond merely targeting terrorists to fostering long-term stability.

112359_112359.caption: Bill Cosby departs the Montgomery County Courthouse in Norristown Pa May 24
112359_112359.article_context: A Pennsylvania judge has ordered Bill Cosby to stand trial on felony sexual assault charges stemming from allegations made by Andrea Constand, a former Temple University official who claims Cosby drugged and assaulted her in 2004. During a contentious hearing, Cosby's defense challenged inconsistencies in Constand’s statements but failed to convince the judge to dismiss the case. Prosecutors, relying on Constand’s interviews rather than her direct testimony, presented details of the alleged assault. Despite multiple accusers, this remains the only criminal case against Cosby, who has denied the charges. The trial date has not yet been set.

1519328_1519328.caption: Mr Trump addressed a rally at the same time as Mr Obama was speaking on TV
1519328_1519328.article_context: President Barack Obama publicly criticized the National Rifle Association (NRA) for misrepresenting his proposed gun control measures during a televised forum, while the NRA refused to participate, calling it a PR stunt. Obama clarified he aims to strengthen background checks, not confiscate firearms, and vowed not to support Democrats who oppose gun reforms. Meanwhile, Republican candidate Donald Trump pledged to eliminate gun-free zones in schools if elected. Earlier, Obama had announced executive actions to tighten background checks and improve mental healthcare related to gun ownership, facing strong opposition from Republican leaders.

380128_380128.caption: President Obama and Cuban President Raul Castro
380128_380128.article_context: At Nelson Mandela's memorial service in Johannesburg, President Obama briefly shook hands with Cuban President Raúl Castro, marking only the second handshake between U.S. and Cuban leaders in over 50 years. The gesture, though unplanned, drew international attention due to the longstanding lack of diplomatic relations between the two countries since Cuba's communist revolution. Both Obama and Castro delivered tributes to Mandela, emphasizing his legacy of unity and reconciliation. While recent small steps toward U.S.-Cuba rapprochement have raised hopes for improved relations, observers remain cautious about any major breakthrough.

92475_92475.caption: Carlos Hernandez his daughter Stephanie 9 and his wife Maria Gonzalez at their home in Waples Mobile Home Park in Fairfax County Va The family is facing eviction
92475_92475.article_context: Owners of Waples Mobile Home Park in Northern Virginia are seeking to evict about 15 immigrant residents who lack Social Security numbers and are in the country illegally, sparking a legal battle over fair housing rights. The park now requires Social Security numbers for identity verification, rejecting IRS-issued tax identification numbers commonly used by non-citizens, a shift that attorneys argue is discriminatory and violates state and federal laws. Many affected families, who have few affordable housing options and have invested significantly in their homes, are facing uncertainty and potential displacement, highlighting the precarious situation of low-income immigrant workers in the region.

667656_667656.caption: John Boehner speaks about the shooting in Arizona during a news conference in West Chester Ohio
667656_667656.article_context: Following the shooting of Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords and one of her staff, Speaker John Boehner has called for the FBI and Capitol Police to conduct a comprehensive review of security for members of Congress. The review aims to assess potential measures, such as increased security during high-risk events, but officials note that providing protection akin to that of the President for all 535 lawmakers would be impractical and costly. Despite a reported rise in threats amid heightened political tensions, many members remain committed to maintaining accessibility to the public and are reluctant to accept personal security details.

541610_541610.caption: Nick Clegg and Tim Farron on the campaign trail just days before the election
541610_541610.article_context: Tim Farron, the leading candidate in the Liberal Democrat leadership race, suggested that former leader Nick Clegg should take a prominent role in the party following the leadership transition, citing precedents of former leaders remaining influential after stepping down. Farron faced scrutiny over his stance on equal marriage, clarifying that he supports it despite previously abstaining from a vote due to proposed amendments for religious conscience protections. His rival, Norman Lamb, emphasized his consistent support for same-sex marriage, highlighting differences between them on this issue.

589623_589623.caption: Barack Obama and David Cameron bow their heads for a moment of silence at the Nato summit in Wales
589623_589623.article_context: The Obama administration is considering its failed attempt to rescue hostages in Syria as a possible legal precedent for future military action against Islamic State militants, arguing it has the right to act unilaterally when American citizens are at risk. While no military strikes have been announced, US and NATO officials are preparing political and legal justifications, including claims that the Assad regime lacks legitimacy and that the US does not need its permission for operations in Syria. These arguments are being weighed against international law and the question of whether congressional authorization is required, as discussions intensify over potential intervention in Syria.

532517_532517.caption: Silvio Berlusconi makes a speech in Rome on the day the Senate voted to expel him
532517_532517.article_context: Italy's Senate voted to expel former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi following his conviction for tax fraud, marking a major defeat in his long political career. The decision came after months of political turmoil and Berlusconi's last-minute pleas to delay the vote. Despite his absence from the vote and imminent legal challenges—including further trials for bribery and abuse of office—Berlusconi vowed to remain politically active and lead his party from outside Parliament. His ousting is expected to increase instability within the governing coalition and potentially disrupt legislative reforms.

222144_222144.caption: Oscar Pistorius is escorted by police officers as he leaves the high court in Pretoria South Africa earlier this year
222144_222144.article_context: Oscar Pistorius was found guilty of culpable homicide, not murder, in the shooting death of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, and was sentenced to five years in prison by Judge Thokozile Masipa. A separate three-year sentence for a firearm charge was suspended. The judge denied prosecutors' request to challenge the sentence, though they stated they plan to appeal. Pistorius could be eligible for house arrest after 10 months and is banned from Paralympic competitions during his sentence.

138177_138177.caption: Donald Trump second from left speaks as Marco Rubio left Ted Cruz and John Kasich listen
138177_138177.article_context: The Republican presidential candidates held a notably civil debate in Coral Gables, Florida, focusing on policy rather than personal attacks. Donald Trump and his remaining rivals—Marco Rubio, Ted Cruz, and John Kasich—discussed issues such as Social Security, foreign worker visa programs, trade deals, relations with Muslim countries, and veterans’ healthcare. The candidates highlighted substantive policy differences, particularly regarding Trump’s rhetoric and his stance on Social Security and trade. With crucial primaries approaching, especially in Florida and Ohio, the debate marked a shift away from insults as the race intensifies for the GOP nomination, while Trump maintains a substantial delegate lead and the Republican establishment remains divided over his candidacy.

504528_504528.caption: Oscar Pistorius in court in Pretoria South Africa
504528_504528.article_context: David Smith, the Guardian’s Africa correspondent, provided live updates via Twitter covering significant events as they unfolded in the region. His real-time reporting highlighted key developments and reactions, offering audiences immediate insights into the situation. The use of live tweets served to keep the public informed and engaged with the ongoing news in Africa.

831392_831392.caption: Amanda Knox speaks to the media outside her parents home in Seattle Washington
831392_831392.article_context: Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito were definitively acquitted of the murder of British student Meredith Kercher after Italy’s highest court annulled their convictions, ending an eight-year legal saga. Knox expressed joy and relief at the verdict, while the Kercher family described their shock and disappointment. The judges found insufficient evidence and stated Knox and Sollecito did not kill Kercher, leaving only Rudy Guede convicted of the crime. The decision ends international tension over possible US extradition of Knox, though she still faces a minor conviction for falsely accusing her former boss.

1683803_1683803.caption: Narendra Modi greeted Nawaz Sharif shortly after being sworn in as prime minister
1683803_1683803.article_context: After Nawaz Sharif's election win in 2013 and Narendra Modi's victory in India in 2014, both leaders initially showed interest in improving India-Pakistan relations, even holding landmark meetings. However, optimism quickly faded amid continued distrust, military confrontations in Kashmir, and unresolved issues like the Mumbai attacks and militant activities. Diplomatic efforts, including high-level talks, repeatedly stalled due to disagreements over topics such as Kashmir. Historical attempts at peace, including those by Sharif and Musharraf, also failed due to military interventions and political opposition. As tensions remain, neither side has made significant progress towards resolving longstanding conflicts.

157420_157420.caption: President Obama will deliver his 3rd State of the Union address tonight in Washington
157420_157420.article_context: President Obama is set to deliver his third State of the Union address, focusing on themes of fairness, equality in the tax code, and economic security for the middle class. The speech is expected to highlight sharp contrasts between his policies and those of Congressional Republicans, especially ahead of the presidential campaign. Analysts are watching to see whether Obama will present broad, visionary ideas for the country’s future or continue with targeted, practical proposals. The address will also be closely observed for partisan reactions, reflecting the current division and high levels of partisanship in Congress.

923662_923662.caption: Pope Francis visits an internally displaced people camp in Bangui Central African Republic
923662_923662.article_context: Pope Francis visited the Central African Republic, becoming the first pontiff in recent history to enter an active war zone. His visit to the capital, Bangui, was aimed at promoting peace and reconciliation in a country devastated by civil war between Christians and Muslims since 2013. Amid heavy security, Francis called for unity and urged people to reject fear and division. He addressed political leaders, visited a camp for displaced people, and planned to meet with Muslim community leaders in a troubled area of the city. The pope’s presence was met with hope that it could help mediate the conflict and inspire tolerance among all citizens.

452204_452204.caption: Jeremy Corbyn addresses over a thousand supporters at Middlesbrough town hall
452204_452204.article_context: Jeremy Corbyn, a frontrunner in the Labour leadership race, attracted over a thousand enthusiastic supporters to a rally in Middlesbrough, far outshining his rivals Andy Burnham and Yvette Cooper in terms of crowd size and excitement. Despite unfavorable weather conditions, people queued for hours to see him, expressing support for his anti-austerity stance and opposition to the welfare reform bill. The event featured passionate applause and chants, with Corbyn emphasizing unity within the party and distancing himself from the more right-wing leadership candidates. His popularity at the rally underscored the growing momentum behind his campaign.

1455947_1455947.caption: The journalists Edouard Elias Didier Francois Nicolas Henin and Pierre Torres were met by President Hollande and Foreign Minister Fabius
1455947_1455947.article_context: Four French journalists kidnapped in Syria by suspected Islamist rebels were released and have spoken about their ordeal, including being chained together and kept in dark basements for months. Didier Francois, Nicolas Henin, Edouard Elias, and Pierre Torres were found by Turkish soldiers near the Syrian border and reunited with their families in France. Their release comes after lengthy negotiations, though French officials deny paying ransom or providing weapons. The kidnapping is attributed to the jihadist group Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL). Their captivity highlights the serious dangers faced by journalists in Syria, one of the deadliest countries for media workers since the conflict began.

958951_958951.caption: Prime Minister David Cameron addresses Conservative Party supporters at Dean Clough Mills in Halifax kickstarting the general election year by promoting the Tories first campaign poster
958951_958951.article_context: The Conservative Party launched its first 2015 election campaign billboard, with David Cameron promoting a calm, centrist message reminiscent of Angela Merkel’s approach. The campaign aims to make the economy a priority issue for voters, capitalizing on the Conservatives’ reputation for economic management. However, challenges persist due to declining voter concern about the economy, rising anxieties over immigration, and overall low trust in major parties. The election landscape is increasingly fragmented, with the campaign’s success hinging on making economic stability salient to voters amid broader debates about unity and change.

581590_581590.caption: Mitt Romney at a campaign rally in Tampa
581590_581590.article_context: A Florida judge has ruled that the state's congressional districts were illegally drawn to benefit Republicans, violating the Fair Districts amendments that prohibit gerrymandering. The decision found that GOP political operatives secretly influenced the redistricting process in 2012, resulting in two unconstitutional districts and rendering the entire map invalid. The ruling isn't expected to affect this year's elections due to an anticipated appeal, but the state legislature is now required to redraw the districts, which could impact future political representation.

577441_577441.caption: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange at Ecuador s embassy in London where he has been for almost a year
577441_577441.article_context: The US government concluded its prosecution against Bradley Manning, the Army private accused of leaking hundreds of thousands of classified documents to WikiLeaks, in what is considered the most significant trial of a leaker in decades. The prosecution faced several setbacks, including missing key documents and lack of clear evidence linking Manning to a conspiratorial relationship with WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange or to knowingly aiding US enemies like al-Qaida. Manning has already pleaded guilty to lesser charges, but continues to contest the most serious accusation of 'aiding the enemy,' which carries a possible life sentence. The outcome of the trial has major implications for government whistleblowers and press freedom amid heightened scrutiny following other notable leaks such as those by Edward Snowden.

1639808_1639808.caption: Helmut Schmidt held a 1981 summit with GDR leader Erich Honecker in the East German town of Guestrow
1639808_1639808.article_context: Helmut Schmidt, former West German Chancellor from 1974 to 1982, has died at the age of 96. Schmidt is widely recognized for his role in founding the European Monetary System, which paved the way for the euro, and for steering Germany through periods of economic crisis and domestic terrorism, notably refusing to negotiate with the Red Army Faction. Known for his skilled diplomacy during the Cold War and strong pro-European stance, Schmidt helped consolidate Germany’s economic strength and foster closer Franco-German ties. Following his death, leaders across Europe praised his legacy and contributions to both Germany and the European Union.

423885_423885.caption: Hillary Clinton accompanied by her husband former president Bill Clinton speaks in Pittsburgh on July 30 2016
423885_423885.article_context: Hillary Clinton released a new TV ad highlighting Donald Trump's business record of outsourcing jobs overseas. The ad features Trump acknowledging on the David Letterman show that his clothing line was made in countries like Bangladesh and China. The ad criticizes Trump for outsourcing jobs to 12 countries, questioning his 'Make America Great Again' slogan. This comes as Clinton campaigns in swing states with a focus on job creation, including a visit to a tie manufacturer in Denver.

89065_89065.caption: Cuban President Raul Castro center with Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos left and FARC leader Timoleon Timochenko Jimenez in Havana last year Cuba is hosting the Colombian peace talks
89065_89065.article_context: The Colombian government and FARC rebels have reached a landmark agreement on a bilateral cease-fire and disarmament, marking a critical step toward ending fifty years of conflict. While not the final peace deal, this breakthrough effectively ends fighting between the two sides. President Juan Manuel Santos and FARC leader Timochenko are set to formalize the agreement in Havana, with global and regional leaders in attendance. The accord includes FARC fighters gathering in designated areas to hand over weapons to UN officials, rather than the Colombian military. Final peace terms must be approved by Colombian voters, with significant opposition from former President Álvaro Uribe. Parallel talks are ongoing with Colombia's second-largest rebel group, the ELN.

142279_142279.caption: President Obama addresses the nation from the Oval Office at the White House in Washington Sunday night Dec 6 2016
142279_142279.article_context: President Obama's Oval Office address focused on the existing strategy against ISIS and urged Americans to uphold the nation's core values in the face of terrorism. He warned against policies driven by bigotry or fear, emphasizing that such actions would undermine American ideals and further ISIS's narrative. The article highlights Obama's repeated attempts to push for a deeper understanding of real equality and liberty beyond simple concepts like tolerance and colorblindness, noting that he receives little credit for these efforts. Despite his calls for unity and thoughtful reflection, many critics fault him for not solving underlying issues of division and disparity in the country.

269158_269158.caption: Paralympian Oscar Pistorius arrives at the High Court in Pretoria on Sept 12
269158_269158.article_context: South African athlete Oscar Pistorius was found guilty of 'culpable homicide'—the equivalent of manslaughter—in the 2013 shooting death of his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp. Judge Thokozile Masipa ruled that Pistorius acted negligently but cleared him of murder charges, concluding prosecutors failed to prove intent. Pistorius was also convicted of one unrelated firearms offense and granted bail while awaiting sentencing. The verdict has sparked debate in South Africa, with some saying justice was not served and others calling for leniency.

58511_58511.caption: Bill Cosby arrives at court to face charges in connection with the alleged sexual assault of former Temple University employee Andrea Constand in 2004
58511_58511.article_context: Bill Cosby's 'Far From Finished' comedy tour has continued across the country despite widespread controversy and mounting public pressure stemming from more than two dozen women accusing him of sexual assault. While some venues have cancelled shows due to protests and financial concerns, others have proceeded under contractual obligation. Industry professionals express shock at Cosby's persistence, noting both the challenge for venues in canceling lucrative performances and the impact on public opinion. Cosby himself has avoided directly addressing the allegations on stage and has not been charged, but many believe this will be his final tour as his career faces irreversible decline.

1059240_1059240.caption: Nadiya Savchenko in court in Donetsk Russia
1059240_1059240.article_context: Ukrainian military pilot Nadiya Savchenko delivered her final statement in a Russian court by condemning the process as a farce and staging a defiant protest, including a hunger strike and singing the Ukrainian anthem. Savchenko faces a possible 23-year prison sentence, accused by Russian prosecutors of involvement in the deaths of two Russian journalists, charges she and her defense deny. Her detention and trial have sparked widespread international condemnation, with calls from leaders like US Secretary of State John Kerry for her release, but Russian authorities have so far resisted pressure. The verdict is expected on March 21, and Savchenko's case has become symbolic of broader political tensions between Russia and Ukraine.

630749_630749.caption: German chancellor Angela Merkel speaks at the end of the EU summit in Brussels She has repeatedly referred to Turkey s pivotal role in the refugee crisis
630749_630749.article_context: Angela Merkel has endorsed a multi-billion euro EU action plan to secure Turkey's cooperation in curbing the flow of refugees and migrants into Europe. At a summit, EU leaders backed a draft deal offering Ankara up to €3 billion in aid, visa-free travel for Turkish citizens, and renewed talks on Turkey's EU membership. Merkel emphasized the need for substantial financial support given the crisis's scale, while Turkey insisted it would only agree to the deal with concrete changes to EU visa policy. Merkel’s upcoming visit to Turkey underscores its strategic role in managing migration, but her outreach has drawn criticism due to President Erdoğan's growing authoritarianism and recent terror attacks in Turkey. The proposed cooperation has sparked debate over human rights issues and political ramifications both in Germany and the EU.

1138203_1138203.caption: Supporters Mitt Romney at a North Carolina rally Prochoice groups have said Romney is a threat to women s rights
1138203_1138203.article_context: Concerns over reproductive rights in the US have increased after Republican vice-presidential candidate Paul Ryan stated in a debate that a Romney administration would work to overturn Roe v. Wade, returning abortion decisions to individual states. Ryan also reaffirmed opposition to abortion except in cases of rape, incest, or danger to the mother's life, troubling pro-choice advocates who warn of serious threats to women's rights if Romney and Ryan are elected. The Romney campaign has sent mixed messages about their abortion stance, causing both criticism from reproductive rights groups and support from anti-abortion organizations. The debate also highlighted the significance of future Supreme Court appointments, which could shift the legal landscape on abortion for years to come.

1613053_1613053.caption: Oscar Pistorius was sick when images of Reeva Steenkamp s body were shown
1613053_1613053.article_context: The second week of Oscar Pistorius's trial for the alleged murder of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp has concluded, with the proceedings lasting longer than initially expected due to ongoing courtroom challenges and numerous witnesses still scheduled to testify. The trial, characterized by a contentious atmosphere between the defense and prosecution, is likely to be extended as key evidence and testimonies continue to unfold.

515437_515437.caption: Oscar Pistorius knew right from wrong during the night he shot dead girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp his trial was told
515437_515437.article_context: A psychiatric report revealed that Oscar Pistorius was not suffering from a mental illness when he shot and killed his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, meaning he can be held criminally responsible. Pistorius, who claims he believed Steenkamp was a burglar, is on trial for her murder in South Africa. The defence and prosecution both accepted the psychiatric findings and shifted focus to Pistorius's physical vulnerabilities. His defence argued that his disability limited his ability to respond to danger or break down the door, while expert testimony questioned whether neighbours could reliably identify screams coming from his house. The trial, followed worldwide, is nearing its conclusion, with both sides preparing final submissions before a judge delivers the verdict. Pistorius faces up to 25 years in prison if convicted.

120496_120496.caption: Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump answers a question during the debate with Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton
120496_120496.article_context: During the presidential debate, Donald Trump used a tactic similar to Russian President Vladimir Putin to deflect blame for the Democratic National Committee (DNC) hack, casting doubt on the ability to identify the true perpetrators and shifting focus to the leaked content itself. Both leaders questioned the evidence implicating Russia, suggesting alternative suspects and emphasizing the difficulty of tracing cyberattacks. Ultimately, they argued that public attention should center on the damaging revelations about the DNC, rather than on who carried out the hack.

80813_80813.caption: Donald Trump reacts as Sen Ted Cruz
80813_80813.article_context: While many Republican elites are alarmed by the rise of outsider candidates Donald Trump and Ted Cruz, a prominent group of supply-side conservatives are enthusiastic about their candidacies due to their pledges for large income and corporate tax cuts. Key figures like economist Arthur Laffer, along with the Committee to Unleash Prosperity, praise Trump and Cruz's tax proposals, despite concerns about their positions on immigration and trade. Critics argue this shows the supply-side faction prioritizes tax cuts for the wealthy over other conservative principles. Independent analyses warn the tax plans could significantly increase the national debt, but Laffer and allies argue the cuts would spur major economic growth, predictions that most mainstream economists reject.

121386_121386.caption: Donald Trump is set to endorse Mitt Romney for president Thursday afternoon
121386_121386.article_context: Donald Trump officially endorsed Mitt Romney in the 2012 presidential race, ending months of speculation about his own possible candidacy. The endorsement, announced at a Las Vegas press conference, is seen as benefiting Trump more than Romney, as it garners media attention for Trump himself. While Trump’s backing brings visibility, polls suggest it could alienate more voters than it attracts, making the endorsement somewhat of a sideshow for Romney’s campaign rather than a strategic advantage.

826320_826320.caption: Stephen Harper on the federal election campaign trail in Saskatoon Saskatchewan
826320_826320.article_context: Stephen Harper's tenure as Canadian Prime Minister has been marked by a series of controversies and allegations surrounding efforts to consolidate power, circumvent democratic norms, and suppress opposition. Election campaign tactics included illegal campaign spending, divisive wedge issues, voter suppression, and questionable voter identification laws, with the Conservative Party facing fines and officials being charged. Notable scandals included attempts to interfere with the democratic process through misleading robocalls, obstructing parliamentary investigations, and the Senate expenses cover-up involving Senator Mike Duffy. Harper's leadership style focused heavily on control of information and people, including restricting scientists and civil servants from speaking openly. He also maintained close ties with the oil industry, actively subverting climate science and weakening environmental regulations. Despite persistent accusations of undemocratic behavior and widespread unpopularity, Harper successfully secured three consecutive election victories and remained a formidable political force ahead of the 2015 election.

77095_77095.caption: Close to midnight Texas state Sen Wendy Davis
77095_77095.article_context: The Texas Senate passed a major bill imposing strict abortion restrictions, including a ban after 20 weeks and new requirements for clinics and doctors, amid intense protests and partisan debate. The legislation, expected to close most of the state’s abortion clinics, will soon be signed by Governor Rick Perry and could face legal challenges. While supporters claim the law protects women and unborn children, opponents warn it severely limits access to abortion and vow to continue fighting through courts and political activism.

756439_756439.caption: Martin Luther King seated third from left waits to speak at the Emanuel AME church in Charleston
756439_756439.article_context: The Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church, known as Mother Emanuel, is the oldest black congregation in the South and has played a significant role in African-American history, including slave revolts and the civil rights movement. On a Wednesday evening, Reverend Clementa Pinckney and eight church members were killed in a racially motivated mass shooting during a Bible study session, an act authorities are treating as a hate crime. The tragedy is deeply symbolic given the church's legacy of resilience against racism and violence, and it has prompted national reflection on issues of race and gun violence in America.

249418_249418.caption: Hillary Clinton takes the stage before giving an address on national security on June 2 2016 in San Diego
249418_249418.article_context: Hillary Clinton secured enough delegates to clinch the Democratic nomination for president, culminating a campaign marked by a prolonged competition with Bernie Sanders and increasing focus on opposing Donald Trump. Throughout her campaign, she addressed key controversies including her email server and Benghazi investigations, emphasized her policy approach as a pragmatic progressive, and criticized Trump's qualifications and foreign policy positions. Clinton also outlined plans for economic revitalization and renewable energy, and underscored the significance of strong families to America’s strength.

1499706_1499706.caption: Donald Trump seen at the Arizona rally leads in the Republican race
1499706_1499706.article_context: Protesters blocked a highway in Arizona as Donald Trump held a rally near Phoenix, causing significant traffic delays. Police arrested several protesters before the demonstration dispersed. The event is part of a series of increasingly tense Trump rallies marked by clashes between supporters and opponents, including a recent cancelled event in Chicago and altercations at rallies in Ohio and North Carolina. Trump criticized the demonstrators, attributing them to rival Hillary Clinton, and called for tougher enforcement. Additional protests took place in Tucson and outside Trump Tower in New York, reflecting growing unrest surrounding Trump's presidential campaign ahead of the Arizona primary.

83946_83946.caption: President Obama listens to remarks while hosting a community discussion on drug addiction in Charleston W Va on Oct 21
83946_83946.article_context: Critics have repeatedly accused President Obama of hating police officers, a perception that intensified after several high-profile incidents involving law enforcement and race, such as the arrest of Henry Louis Gates and the deaths of Michael Brown and Eric Garner. These accusations were fueled by statements Obama made advocating for police reform and criticism of specific incidents, as well as his engagement with Black Lives Matter. Despite these claims, fact-checkers found little evidence supporting the idea that Obama is hostile toward police; instead, the narrative reflects deeper political and racial tensions in the United States.

133077_133077.caption: Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton listens as former vice president Al Gore speaks during a rally
133077_133077.article_context: Hillary Clinton and former Vice President Al Gore appeared together at a rally in Miami to highlight the importance of combating climate change and to energize millennial voters ahead of the upcoming presidential election. Gore endorsed Clinton’s climate policies and warned against electing Republican nominee Donald Trump, who has called climate change a hoax. Gore and Clinton emphasized that every vote counts, referencing Gore’s loss in the 2000 election in Florida. The event aimed to draw attention to policy issues amid controversy surrounding Trump, as Clinton sought to appeal to young voters and reinforce the significance of voting to prevent a climate denier from winning the presidency.

363790_363790.caption: George Zimmerman arrives for the 16th day of his trial in Seminole circuit court July 1 in Sanford Fla
363790_363790.article_context: In George Zimmerman's murder trial for the fatal shooting of Trayvon Martin, police officers testified about Zimmerman's demeanor and his account of self-defense, with Zimmerman claiming Trayvon attacked him before being shot. Key evidence included Zimmerman’s videotaped statement and witness testimonies, some supporting Zimmerman and others depicting him as the aggressor. Racial profiling and motive were discussed, but investigators stated race did not seem to play a role. Experts were unable to confirm whose voice was heard calling for help on a 911 call. The jury heard conflicting accounts from various witnesses, including neighbors and friends, with both the state and defense presenting their version of events leading up to Trayvon’s death.

53826_53826.caption: DC Mayor Muriel E Bowser right speaks to DC Council member Yvette M Alexander outside a DC polling place June 14 Bowser supported Alexander in her race against Gray
53826_53826.article_context: After a contentious Democratic primary in Washington, D.C., party leaders and candidates gathered for a unity breakfast, promoting reconciliation despite lingering tensions. Mayor Muriel Bowser congratulated both victorious and defeated candidates, including Vincent C. Gray, who returned to public office by defeating incumbent Yvette M. Alexander for the Ward 7 council seat. Bowser’s allies suffered notable losses, including in Ward 8, but she affirmed her intention to seek reelection. The event marked public gestures of goodwill, yet underlying rivalries—especially between Bowser and Gray—remained evident. The primary also saw Robert White unseat longtime councilman Vincent B. Orange, signaling significant change within the city’s Democratic leadership.

251959_251959.caption: Bernie Sanders campaigns in Mount Vernon Iowa on Dec 13 2015
251959_251959.article_context: The article discusses several key political events, including Donald Trump's grievance towards PolitiFact for naming his false statements as 'Lie of the Year', and Republican candidates Ted Cruz and others (excluding Trump) pledging to support the First Amendment Defense Act, which is controversial due to concerns about discrimination against gay couples. Bernie Sanders criticized the Democratic National Committee for scheduling debates on low-viewership Saturdays, claiming it limits his exposure, while noting that the most recent debate achieved high ratings for a Saturday. Additionally, Chelsea Clinton announced her second pregnancy, and Chris Christie saw a rise in national polls but remained in fifth place.

79329_79329.caption: Donald Trump speaks at a campaign press conference moments after winning the republican presidential primary at Trump Tower in New York
79329_79329.article_context: Hillary Clinton won a decisive victory over Bernie Sanders in the New York Democratic primary, securing nearly 58% of the vote and gaining a substantial lead in delegates. This win strengthened her position as the frontrunner for the Democratic nomination, making it increasingly difficult for Sanders to catch up. Both candidates had heavily contested the state, which was seen as a crucial test, but Clinton’s strong performance—especially among registered Democrats and nonwhite voters—dampened Sanders’s momentum. Despite the loss, Sanders vowed to continue his campaign through the upcoming primaries. Clinton’s victory sparked renewed questions about party unity and her readiness for the general election against Republican rivals.

1546572_1546572.caption: Vladimir Putin as prime minister in 1999 the year after Mrs Litvinenko says he met her husband
1546572_1546572.article_context: At a UK public inquiry into Alexander Litvinenko’s death, his widow revealed he was paid £2,000 monthly as a consultant for a British intelligence agency, reportedly MI6, and also worked with Spanish security services on organised crime. Litvinenko, a former Russian spy, accused Vladimir Putin of links to organised crime, particularly during Putin’s tenure as deputy mayor of St Petersburg. After fleeing Russia and seeking asylum in Britain, Litvinenko received support from businessman Boris Berezovsky before working for MI6. He was fatally poisoned with radioactive polonium in London in 2006, and the inquiry suggests his murder was linked to exposing corruption in Putin’s government. Russian suspects named by UK police have denied involvement and remain in Russia.

1537321_1537321.caption: Mahmoud Abbas signed the ICC s founding treaty on Wednesday
1537321_1537321.article_context: Israel has suspended the transfer of $127 million in tax revenues to the Palestinian Authority after the Palestinians submitted documents to join the International Criminal Court (ICC), a move opposed by Israel and the US. The freeze is a response to Palestinian efforts to pursue legal action against Israel for alleged war crimes. Palestinian officials condemned the measure as collective punishment and a 'new war crime.' The ICC membership process follows the 2012 UN General Assembly vote granting Palestine non-member observer state status, making it eligible to join the ICC and seek prosecution of war crimes. Neither Israel nor the US is a member of the ICC.

1216707_1216707.caption: Alexis Tsipras and Vladimir Putin hold a press conference in the Kremlin on Wednesday
1216707_1216707.article_context: During a visit to Moscow, Greek Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras called on the EU to lift sanctions against Russia, warning that they could trigger a new cold war. Despite speculation, Tsipras did not seek financial aid from Russia, nor did President Putin offer any, and no major agreements were announced. Tsipras emphasized Greece's right to independent foreign policy and openly criticized Western measures against Russia’s actions in Ukraine, aligning himself closer to Moscow. However, Russia refused to make exceptions for Greece on its food import ban, which continues to impact the Greek economy. The meeting highlighted Greece’s skeptical stance on EU policy towards Russia but did not result in concrete shifts in economic or diplomatic relations.

958092_958092.caption: Amanda Knox arrives in Perugia s appeal court during the first session of her appeal against her murder conviction
958092_958092.article_context: Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito appeared in an Italian court for the opening of their appeal against convictions for the murder of British student Meredith Kercher. Knox, who looked anxious and thinner, faced Sollecito for the first time since their sentencing. Both hope to overturn their convictions by challenging forensic evidence and calling new witnesses, including Rudy Guede’s cellmate, to weaken the prosecution’s case. The prosecution also seeks to increase their sentences to life imprisonment. The session was brief and adjourned until December due to a lawyer’s absence.

271068_271068.caption: President Obama packing sandwiches at Martha s Table
271068_271068.article_context: President Obama visited Martha's Table food bank in Washington, D.C., where he volunteered to help package sandwiches alongside federal workers and schoolchildren. Despite initial difficulties with Ziploc bags and peanut butter, Obama participated in the community effort and joked about the experience, highlighting both the pressure of public attention and the teamwork involved in the event.

1109301_1109301.caption: Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak centre with Minister for Transport Hishamuddin Hussein left and civil aviaition director Azharuddin Abdul Rahman delivering a statement to the media this weekend
1109301_1109301.article_context: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 stopped communicating with ground control about 40 minutes into its journey, but this was not disclosed publicly for several hours, leading to criticism over Malaysia's handling of the crisis. Military radar showed the plane significantly veered off course and behaved erratically, but authorities were slow to share information. Investigators found that crucial communications systems were deliberately disabled, and satellite 'pings' indicated the aircraft continued flying for nearly seven hours after losing contact, possibly towards the southern Indian Ocean. The unclear communication, slow response, and contradictory information have fueled widespread speculation about the flight’s mysterious disappearance, eventually making the search for the plane extremely challenging.

141804_141804.caption: Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump speaking in Iowa on Saturday displayed unexpected staying power in 2015
141804_141804.article_context: In 2015, American politics saw several major shifts: Donald Trump defied conventional wisdom to emerge as the Republican presidential frontrunner by tapping into voter anger, while Hillary Clinton demonstrated strong resilience, surviving controversy and solidifying her lead among Democrats. The influence of super PACs proved overrated, as well-funded groups failed to rescue struggling candidates like Jeb Bush. The GOP establishment was weakened, losing control over both the presidential race and congressional leadership. Overall, the unexpected popularity of outsiders such as Trump, Bernie Sanders, and Ben Carson showed that voters were strongly demanding change from traditional politics.

293208_293208.caption: Nik Wallenda pedals a bicycle on a wire 12 stories above the street in Newark NJ on Oct 15 2008
293208_293208.article_context: Nik Wallenda, of the Flying Wallendas, performed a daring walk atop the newly launched Orlando Eye, the tallest observation wheel on the East Coast at 400 feet, to mark its grand opening. The Orlando Eye is part of the new $200 million I-Drive 360 entertainment complex in Orlando, featuring attractions like Madame Tussauds and SEA LIFE Orlando. The observation wheel opens to the public on May 4, offering panoramic views of Orlando and nearby landmarks, interactive tablets for information, and a 4-D cinema experience.

186027_186027.caption: Democratic presidential candidate and former secretary of state Hillary Rodham Clinton right and former president Bill Clinton arrive before the funeral
186027_186027.article_context: President Joe Biden chose Barack Obama to deliver the eulogy for his late son Beau Biden in 2015, emphasizing the deep personal bond between the two leaders that developed during their years in office together. The article highlights how Obama and Biden's partnership grew from a professional relationship into a close friendship, particularly as they faced major challenges like the economic crisis and personal family hardships. Despite differences in style and occasional tensions, their mutual trust and loyalty stood out, setting their relationship apart from other presidential and vice-presidential pairs. Obama’s heartfelt eulogy at Beau’s funeral symbolized not only public support but also the intertwining of the Obama and Biden families.

172610_172610.caption: They do nt care about the politics President Obama visits Orlando families
172610_172610.article_context: President Obama delivered a blunt, politically charged speech in Orlando following the mass shooting at Pulse nightclub, urging action on gun control. Departing from his usual uplifting rhetoric, Obama directly called on Congress, especially Republicans, to pass gun safety legislation, emphasizing the destructive power of assault weapons used in repeated mass killings. He also criticized Donald Trump's suggestions to increase firearm accessibility and impose a ban on Muslim immigrants, warning against divisive and xenophobic policies. Obama stressed that real change was needed to prevent future tragedies, expressing impatience with continued political gridlock.

225303_225303.caption: Arizona Sen John McCain speaks at a campaign rally in Henderson Nev late in the 2008 presidential campaign
225303_225303.article_context: Despite a declining percentage of Americans identifying as Christians, Republican presidential campaigns continue to focus heavily on appealing to conservative evangelicals, demonstrated by candidates speaking at major Christian events and universities. This is because evangelicals remain a politically active and influential voting bloc for the GOP, while the growing group of religiously unaffiliated Americans ('nones') tends to vote Democratic but has yet to match evangelicals' turnout levels.
