As nones grow younger and more numerous, both parties face challenges: Republicans must balance primary appeals to evangelicals with general election overtures to secular voters, and Democrats increasingly rely on less religious language and constituencies. Experts suggest that the influence of nones will continue to reshape American politics, moving the country toward greater secularism in the future.

133620_133620.caption: Mitt Romney at a campaign rally in Sanford Fla on Nov 5 2012
133620_133620.article_context: Mitt Romney, the 2012 Republican presidential nominee, spoke at Georgetown University, sharing his views on the 2016 presidential race. He predicted that Donald Trump would not become the Republican nominee, suggesting the eventual nominee would come from the mainstream conservative bracket. Romney criticized Trump’s rhetoric, expressed concerns about the GOP's image among minorities, and discussed his positions on policy issues such as poverty, immigration, Syria, and the Iran nuclear deal. While addressing repeated questions about his own potential candidacy, Romney firmly maintained he would not run in 2016, despite interest from his supporters.

699198_699198.caption: Nancy Pelosi meets with family members of Newtown victims as they visit Capitol Hill on Friday the sixmonth anniversary of the shooting
699198_699198.article_context: Smith & Wesson reported record gun sales of $588 million, a 43% increase over the previous year, amid a surge in demand following major incidents of gun violence in the US, such as the Sandy Hook school shooting and the Colorado cinema massacre. Background check requests and permit applications rose sharply after these events, as well as after President Obama's re-election due to concerns about tighter regulations. In response to the gun violence, some investors, including large pension funds and Cerberus Capital Management, divested from gun manufacturers linked to these tragedies. Smith & Wesson plans further financial measures, including a $100 million share buyback, as its stock price climbs.

343278_343278.caption: Jeb Bush participates in the CBS News Republican debate
343278_343278.article_context: Six Republican presidential candidates participated in a heated debate in South Carolina, hours after Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia's death. The candidates clashed over replacing Scalia, immigration, foreign policy, and economic issues, with Donald Trump and Jeb Bush engaging in several personal confrontations. Ted Cruz and Marco Rubio debated immigration and national security, while John Kasich and Ben Carson advocated unity and problem-solving over infighting. The debate highlighted divisions within the GOP field and the high stakes surrounding the 2016 election, particularly in light of the Supreme Court vacancy.

1090374_1090374.caption: Putin and Schroder hug at Schroder s 70th birthday party in St Petersburg a month after Russia passed a bill to annex Crimea
1090374_1090374.article_context: Matthias Warnig, a former East German Stasi agent, has become one of Vladimir Putin's closest and most influential associates in Russia, holding key positions in major Russian banks and energy companies, including Bank Rossiya, VTB Bank, Rosneft, Transneft, Rusal, and as managing director of Nord Stream AG. Warnig's relationship with Putin dates back to their time as secret service officers in the socialist states of East Germany and Russia. This longstanding personal and professional connection has given Warnig significant influence in Russian business and politics, symbolizing strong ties between Germany and Russia. However, the Ukraine crisis and Western sanctions have threatened these networks, further highlighting Warnig's pivotal role in navigating these geopolitical tensions.

720581_720581.caption: Foreign secretary William Hague makes a statement in the House of Commons on Britain s stockpile of nuclear warheads
720581_720581.article_context: UK Foreign Secretary William Hague announced a review of the country's nuclear weapons policy, revealing for the first time that Britain will not exceed 225 nuclear warheads and that only 160 are operationally available. The government signaled a move towards greater openness, aligning with similar US policy shifts, and is considering limiting the circumstances in which nuclear weapons might be used, excluding retaliation against biological, chemical, or conventional attacks, except potentially against Iran. This review comes as part of international efforts to promote transparency and global disarmament at a time when the US and France are also reducing their arsenals, and as the UK debates the future of the Trident nuclear system within broader defense discussions.

691326_691326.caption: US president Barack Obama alongside sign interpreter Thamsanqa Jantjie during the Nelson Mandela memorial service
691326_691326.article_context: The South African government has acknowledged that the sign language interpreter at Nelson Mandela's memorial service, Thamsanqa Jantjie, was unqualified and supplied by a company with a history of substandard service and fraud. Jantjie's performance, seen by millions and widely criticized by the global deaf community, was described as 'nonsense' and not in accordance with standard sign language practice. Jantjie claimed his actions were due to a schizophrenia episode during the event. While the government admitted errors in vetting, it stopped short of labeling Jantjie a fraud or ruling out working with him again, citing broader issues with the lack of a universal sign language standard in South Africa. An official investigation is ongoing, and the controversy has overshadowed Mandela's state memorial events.

1590448_1590448.caption: President Barack Obama emailed Mrs Clinton at her private address the White House has said
1590448_1590448.article_context: Hillary Clinton's use of a private email server during her tenure as Secretary of State became a major controversy in the lead-up to her 2016 presidential campaign. She relied exclusively on her personal server for both official and personal communications, raising concerns about transparency, security, and compliance with federal record-keeping laws. While Clinton argued her actions were for convenience and said she turned over all work-related emails, critics questioned the completeness and security of her disclosures, especially after some emails were later found to contain classified material. The FBI launched an investigation into her email practices, and Clinton's favorability in polls declined as the controversy became a prominent issue in the campaign.

120346_120346.caption: View Photo Gallery With the Republican presidential nomination apparently assured former Massachusetts governor Mitt Romney steps up criticism of President Obama
120346_120346.article_context: Mitt Romney's campaign issued a memo portraying President Obama's re-election effort as unfocused and reliant on personal attacks, likening it to a 'gyrating, intermittent lawn sprinkler.' Romney’s campaign manager argued that Obama avoids discussing key issues like unemployment, federal debt, and gas prices due to a weak record over the past three years. In response, an Obama spokesman accused Romney of dishonesty about his own and Obama's records, and criticized Romney's background as a corporate buyout specialist. The exchange signals a sharpening of attacks as both campaigns enter a new phase in the presidential race, highlighting economic issues and contrasting their visions for the country.

136723_136723.caption: Secretary of State John F Kerry travels from Jordan to Iraq on Wednesday for talks with its new leaders on their role in a new strategy against Islamic State
136723_136723.article_context: President Obama’s plan to escalate efforts against the Islamic State was widely welcomed by Iraqi leaders, who sought stronger US military intervention after the group seized significant territory. The new Iraqi government, supported by Obama and visited by Secretary of State John Kerry, called for a partnership with the US and international allies, with airstrikes potentially expanding to additional areas in Iraq and Syria. Key European countries like France and Britain offered support, while Russia and Syria criticized the plan and warned against unauthorized strikes. Iran questioned the US-led coalition’s inclusion of Sunni Arab states, and Israel affirmed its cooperation in the broader effort. The initiative also includes forming a new Iraqi national guard to rally moderate Sunni tribal forces against extremism.

114359_114359.caption: US President Barack Obama makes a statement on the situation in Iraq at Martha s Vineyard Massachusetts on August 11 2014
114359_114359.article_context: President Obama's approval ratings have remained consistently low, hovering in the low 40s throughout 2014, without significant change despite various political events. This stable but negative perception is hurting Democrats in the midterm elections, as Republicans use Obama's unpopularity to target Democratic candidates, especially in competitive Senate races. Historical trends indicate that support for Senate candidates closely follows public approval of the president, making Obama's stagnant ratings a significant liability for Democrats in key states.

57640_57640.caption: Former US secretary of state Madeleine Albright left introduces Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton during a campaign stop at Rundlett Middle School in Concord NH on Feb 6
57640_57640.article_context: A controversy erupted after feminist icons Gloria Steinem and Madeleine Albright criticized young women for not supporting Hillary Clinton in the 2016 Democratic primary, with Steinem suggesting young women back Bernie Sanders for social reasons and Albright stating 'there’s a special place in Hell' for women who don’t support other women. These comments sparked backlash for being dismissive of young women’s legitimate political views and highlighted divisions within the Democratic coalition, particularly along lines of race and age. The article argues that both Clinton and Sanders supporters have issues respecting differing perspectives among women voters, and emphasizes that political campaigns must earn votes by addressing voters’ actual concerns rather than assuming their support.

283156_283156.caption: Clinton listens as Bernie Sanders formally endorses her during a rally in Portsmouth NH on July 12 2016
283156_283156.article_context: A leaked email from Hillary Clinton's 2016 campaign chairman, released by WikiLeaks, revealed that prominent business leaders such as Tim Cook, Bill Gates, Melinda Gates, and Howard Schultz were considered as potential vice presidential candidates during the early stages of the selection process. The email showed a wide-ranging list of possible running mates, highlighting the campaign's interest in both political figures and high-profile executives.

1193187_1193187.caption: The former head of the Catholic church in Scotland Cardinal O Brien touches his cross Pope Francis accepted his resignation earlier this year because of sexual misconduct
1193187_1193187.article_context: The Scottish Catholic church issued a profound public apology to victims of child abuse, acknowledging decades of failures to investigate and punish abusers after an independent commission found widespread cover-ups and serious flaws in safeguarding procedures. Archbishop Philip Tartaglia pledged action following the commission's report, which emphasized the urgent need for reparations, greater support for victims, and external scrutiny of church policies. The inquiry, led by Andrew McLellan, highlighted an entrenched culture of secrecy and made eight key recommendations, including prioritizing support for victims, creating a counselling fund, and enforcing strict, consistent safeguarding standards across all dioceses. Survivors and the public were warned that the church’s future credibility depends on implementing these changes.

75789_75789.caption: Donald Trump debates Hillary Clinton in Las Vegas on Wednesday
75789_75789.article_context: The value of the Mexican peso has become a real-time indicator of the U.S. presidential race, fluctuating based on perceptions of Donald Trump's chances of winning. During debates and shifts in polls, the peso has weakened when Trump performed well and strengthened when Hillary Clinton was viewed as the victor. Trump's promises to renegotiate or discard NAFTA and enact protectionist policies have caused concern and volatility for both the Mexican and Canadian currencies, highlighting the economic impact of the U.S. election across North America. Experts emphasize that fears about Trump’s policies, along with other factors like oil prices and Mexico’s public finances, have driven this financial instability.

437013_437013.caption: Hillary Clinton officially launches her campaign for the Democratic presidential nomination during a speech on New York s Roosevelt Island June 13
437013_437013.article_context: On the one-year anniversary of Washington Post journalist Jason Rezaian's imprisonment in Iran on espionage charges, The Washington Post petitioned the United Nations to pressure Iran for his release, highlighting his harsh treatment in prison. Rezaian's case has drawn international attention, especially after his continued detention despite recent nuclear negotiations between Iran and world powers. In other news, U.S. home sales are surging to pre-crisis levels, Ferguson named a black interim police chief after major leadership changes prompted by Department of Justice findings, a poll shows Hillary Clinton trailing Republican candidates in key swing states, and the first trailer for the new James Bond film 'Spectre' was released.

166433_166433.caption: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan attends a ceremony marking the 101st anniversary of the Battle of Canakkale in Canakkale Turkey on Friday
166433_166433.article_context: Just days before the deadly Brussels bombings, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan warned European cities about the threat of terrorism, referencing a recent attack in Ankara carried out by Kurdish militants. Erdogan criticized Europe and the U.S. for their perceived tolerance of Kurdish groups, suggesting such attacks could occur anywhere in Europe. After the Brussels attacks, he reiterated the need for a unified stance against all types of terrorism, though analysts noted that the Brussels perpetrators were Islamist extremists unrelated to the groups responsible for recent violence in Turkey. The article highlights ongoing tensions over Western policies toward Kurdish factions and Turkey's struggle with frequent terrorist attacks.

378073_378073.caption: Bernie Sanders pledged to do everything possible to ensure Hillary Clinton wins the presidential race The former rivals appeared together at a unity rally in Portsmouth New Hampshire
378073_378073.article_context: Bernie Sanders formally endorsed Hillary Clinton for president, ending a contentious primary battle and pledging to help Clinton defeat Republican nominee Donald Trump. At a joint rally in New Hampshire, Sanders highlighted the significant progress made in shaping the Democratic Party platform to include key progressive policies while Clinton welcomed Sanders’ supporters and stressed unity. Although some Sanders supporters remain reluctant, Sanders vowed to continue promoting progressive causes and work to elect like-minded candidates nationwide. The endorsement signaled a major moment of party consolidation ahead of the Democratic National Convention.

976027_976027.caption: Demonstrators stage a protest outside the Quantico military base in Virginia where Bradley Manning is being held
976027_976027.article_context: Bradley Manning has been subjected to harsh pretrial confinement conditions since early March, including being forced to strip naked every night and parade in front of guards, following a sarcastic comment about self-harm. Despite a brig psychiatrist finding Manning at low risk for suicide, these measures were implemented without mental health justification and have continued indefinitely. Manning is held in near-solitary confinement, allowed only minimal personal items and limited exercise, prompting concerns and outside pressure over the punitive nature and lawfulness of his treatment.

369354_369354.caption: Hillary Clinton speaks during her Super Tuesday event at Stage One at Ice Palace Films Studios on March 1 2016 in Miami
369354_369354.article_context: Hillary Clinton won a decisive victory on Super Tuesday, capturing seven states including the key southern states of Texas, Virginia, Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, Arkansas, and Massachusetts, largely due to strong support from African-American voters. Bernie Sanders won in Oklahoma, Colorado, Minnesota, and Vermont. Clinton's string of victories significantly expanded her lead in delegates and put her on a clear path toward the Democratic nomination. Both Clinton and Sanders acknowledged each other's strengths, while Clinton increasingly turned her attention to potential Republican rival Donald Trump, criticizing his campaign rhetoric. Sanders vowed to continue his campaign, but the results made Clinton the firm front-runner in the Democratic race.

885830_885830.caption: Obama went out of his way Wednesday to praise Petraeus as head of the CIA and military commander in Iraq and Afghanistan
885830_885830.article_context: President Barack Obama dismissed Republican claims of a coverup surrounding the FBI's investigation into former CIA director David Petraeus, which uncovered his extramarital affair and led to his resignation after the 2012 election. Questions have arisen over why neither the White House nor Congress was informed earlier about the probe, with some Republicans suggesting the delay was politically motivated. The investigation began after harassing emails from Petraeus's mistress were reported, implicating other officials and raising concerns about possible security breaches. Obama stated there is no evidence national security was compromised and defended his administration's handling of the situation. The controversy also ties into Republican accusations of a White House coverup of the Benghazi attack, as Petraeus is set to testify to Congress and disputes continue over the administration's initial explanations of the incident.

1465531_1465531.caption: Mr Tsipras spent two hours with European Commission President JeanClaude Juncker on Thursday
1465531_1465531.article_context: Greece's negotiations with its international creditors have stalled, as IMF officials left Brussels citing significant unresolved differences, notably over pensions, taxes, and debt sustainability. Greece faces an urgent need to secure a cash-for-reforms deal to avoid defaulting on a €1.5bn repayment to the IMF by the end of June, when its bailout agreement also expires. While Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras has held high-level meetings with EU leaders and has intensified efforts to reach an agreement, little progress has been made. The creditors demand deeper economic reforms before releasing the final €7.2bn in bailout funds, and European leaders warned that time is running out for Greece to avoid default or a possible exit from the eurozone. Meanwhile, the Syriza government fulfilled a campaign promise by restoring the state broadcaster ERT.

701494_701494.caption: Washington Post correspondent Jason Rezaian right the IranianAmerican correspondent for the Washington Post released on Saturday
701494_701494.article_context: Iran emerged from years of international isolation after the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) confirmed Iran's compliance with a landmark nuclear deal, leading to the lifting of major economic sanctions. On the same day, Iran and the United States conducted a high-profile prisoner swap, which saw the release of Washington Post journalist Jason Rezaian and other Americans by Iran, in exchange for clemency and dropped charges for several Iranians held in the US. The sanction relief allows Iran to regain access to global banking, frozen assets, and trade, including purchasing new airliners. These developments mark a significant turning point in Iran's relations with the world and are seen as a triumph for diplomacy, with hopes for broader political and economic change within Iran.

655385_655385.caption: Edward Snowden in a still from a Wikileaks video speaks in Moscow last October after his leak of secret NSA files
655385_655385.article_context: Edward Snowden, a former NSA contractor, used simple and widely available web crawler software to automate the collection of around 1.7 million classified agency documents, evading detection due to outdated monitoring systems at his workplace. His unsophisticated technique raises questions about NSA's cybersecurity measures, especially since similar insider attacks had occurred before. Despite accusations of being a Russian spy, Snowden, now in Russia under asylum, denies the claims, while US officials urge him to return and face charges.

67046_67046.caption: Tom Brady leaving federal court in New York after contesting his four game suspension with the NFL on Aug 31 2015
67046_67046.article_context: During the Deflategate controversy, Tom Brady's legal team focused on challenging the scope of NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell's disciplinary powers under the collective bargaining agreement, rather than arguing for Brady’s innocence. The U.S. Court of Appeals upheld Brady’s four-game suspension, emphasizing that the legal fight should have centered on a lack of credible evidence showing any misconduct by Brady. Critics argue that Goodell abused his power and relied on questionable or manufactured evidence, while ignoring scientific explanations for the footballs’ deflation. The case highlights flaws in the NFL’s arbitration process and warns players that their individual rights can be sidelined by union strategies and vague league rules.

398232_398232.caption: President Obama makes a statement on the IRS controversy May 15 in the White House
398232_398232.article_context: President Obama has appointed Daniel Werfel, a respected White House budget official, as acting IRS commissioner following the resignation of two top IRS officials—including Joseph Grant—in response to revelations that the IRS targeted conservative groups for extra scrutiny. The scandal has prompted criminal and legislative investigations, and Obama has rejected calls for a special counsel, insisting current inquiries will uncover the facts and lead to necessary reforms. Werfel is expected to lead the agency's efforts to restore public trust during this turbulent period.

606648_606648.caption: Tony Abbott celebrates his election victory with his wife Margie and daughters Louise Frances and Bridgette
606648_606648.article_context: In the lead-up to the 2013 election, Tony Abbott and the Coalition campaigned on promises of no major cuts to health, education, or pensions, and a return to budget surplus without compromising spending. Upon winning, the Abbott government instead enacted significant budget cuts, introduced new taxes, and made policy changes not flagged before the election, leading to widespread criticism and allegations of broken promises. Abbott succeeded in repealing the carbon and mining taxes and stopping asylum seeker boats, yet struggled with Senate negotiations, internal inefficiency, and public relations. Although some foreign policy successes stabilized poll numbers, the government ended its first year unpopular, having eroded trust among voters and its core support base.

809508_809508.caption: Despite performance cancellations in Las Vegas and Worcester over sexual assault allegations Cosby gave two performances at Temple Buell Theatre in Denver on Saturday
809508_809508.article_context: Bill Cosby cancelled two stand-up comedy shows in Boston after Helen Gumpel, a former actress and model, publicly accused him of making sexual advances and lewd gestures on the set of The Cosby Show. Cosby now faces allegations of sexual assault from at least 15 women, though he denies the claims and has not been charged. The cancellations followed expected protests and heightened security, with most of Cosby's planned shows in Boston already called off, reflecting ongoing public controversy and pressure surrounding the accusations.

179027_179027.caption: Hillary Clinton gives an economic speech in Warren Mich on Thursday
179027_179027.article_context: Hillary Clinton publicly opposed President Obama's Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) trade deal in a speech aimed at appealing to progressive voters, especially Bernie Sanders supporters. While her stance received praise from influential progressive groups, such as Democracy for America, she faced further pressure to directly challenge Obama by demanding he halt efforts to pass the TPP before leaving office. This situation puts Clinton in a difficult position, having to choose between aligning with the progressive wing of her party and maintaining ties with Obama, who remains highly popular among Democrats. The ongoing debate underscores persistent skepticism about Clinton's trade positions and highlights divisions within the Democratic Party regarding the TPP.

87422_87422.caption: Donald Trump rallies with supporters Oct 25 at the Million Air Orlando airplane hangar in Sanford Fla
87422_87422.article_context: National polling results for the presidential race have shown widely varying outcomes due to differences in how pollsters interpret raw data, especially their assumptions about likely voters and how to weight responses. A New York Times experiment with identical Florida poll data resulted in divergent outcomes from different pollsters, illustrating this challenge. While averages help smooth out these discrepancies, the variation means that if the race tightens, uncertainty around poll accuracy could become significant. Ultimately, which polling method is most accurate will only be clear after Election Day, but strong partisan loyalty remains a key predictor of candidate support.

899633_899633.caption: Oscar Pistorius at the Pretoria High Court last week
899633_899633.article_context: South Africans were shocked when Judge Thokozile Masipa found Oscar Pistorius not guilty of premeditated murder in the shooting of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, convicting him instead of culpable homicide. The public reaction reflected deep frustrations with violence against women and perceived lack of accountability among the powerful. Many hoped the trial would set a precedent for justice and symbolize the fight against abuse, but Masipa's verdict, based on insufficient evidence for premeditated murder, left many feeling disappointed. The case highlighted widespread disillusionment with the justice system and broader societal issues of abuse, inequality, and perceived impunity for the privileged.

71300_71300.caption: Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally Aug 11 in Kissimmee Fla
71300_71300.article_context: Donald Trump's agriculture advisory committee includes several members who have previously supported comprehensive immigration reform, advocating legal status for undocumented workers crucial to U.S. agriculture—a stance at odds with Trump's calls for mass deportation. The committee comprises high-profile politicians, former executives, and industry leaders who argue that immigrant labor is essential for food production and consumer prices. Some have publicly opposed Trump's immigration policies, emphasizing the need for reforms to address labor shortages, while Trump's candidacy continues to emphasize strict deportation measures and anti-immigrant rhetoric.

174244_174244.caption: Poet Maya Angelou addresses the Million Man March on Capitol Hill DC Mayor Marion Barry is behind her
174244_174244.article_context: Ahead of the 20th anniversary rally of the Million Man March organized by the Nation of Islam in Washington, D.C., the U.S. Capitol Police circulated an internal newsletter warning officers of possible violence, citing concerns about the current racial climate and leader Louis Farrakhan's controversial rhetoric. The police chief quickly distanced the department from the newsletter, stating it did not reflect official views and was later rescinded. The union representing Capitol Police criticized the newsletter as inflammatory and called for accountability. Local mosques heightened security due to planned anti-Muslim protests coinciding with the rally, while organizers maintained the event would be peaceful, highlighting their history of nonviolent gatherings.

1596082_1596082.caption: Reeva Steenkamp s family look on as Oscar Pistorius arrives for the opening day of his murder trial
1596082_1596082.article_context: The trial of Oscar Pistorius, the South African athlete accused of murdering his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp in February 2013, began in Pretoria on March 3. Over the course of the first week, key moments and events were chronicled by reporters through tweets and video reports, as the high-profile case captured significant public attention.

344943_344943.caption: President Obama makes a statement on the death of American journalist James Foley on Martha s Vineyard in Massachusetts Aug 20 2014
344943_344943.article_context: President Obama condemned the Islamic State's beheading of American journalist James Foley, calling it an atrocity that shocked the world and vowing that justice would be served. He emphasized that ISIS does not represent any religion and urged Iraq to unify against extremism. The U.S. continued airstrikes against ISIS near the Mosul Dam and reviewed requests to bolster embassy security in Baghdad. U.S. intelligence confirmed the authenticity of the execution video, which also threatened another journalist, Steven Sotloff.

453554_453554.caption: Frances Abbott joins her father Tony Abbott on the campaign trail in 2013
453554_453554.article_context: Students and alumni of the Whitehouse Institute of Design expressed outrage after it was revealed that Prime Minister Tony Abbott’s daughter, Frances Abbott, received a previously undisclosed $60,000 scholarship, making her only the second recipient in the institute’s 25-year history. Many students claimed they were unaware such scholarships existed and questioned the fairness and transparency of the award, noting that they were told no scholarships were available for the bachelor’s program. The scholarship was reportedly recommended by the board chairman and awarded during her initial interview. The institute’s leadership has defended the process, arguing the scholarship was merit-based and did not require public disclosure, while the prime minister’s office stated the issue was the school’s responsibility.

526065_526065.caption: Pope Francis pictured in South Korea the day before his relatives fatal accident
526065_526065.article_context: Pope Francis was deeply affected by the deaths of three family members—his nephew's wife and two young children—in a car accident in Argentina, while his nephew remains in serious condition. The crash, which involved their car colliding with a grain truck, occurred shortly after the pope returned to Rome from South Korea and had reflected on his own mortality, suggesting he may have only 'two or three years' left. The Vatican released a statement asking for prayers, and Pope Francis also referenced the possibility of retiring from the papacy if he feels unable to continue his duties.

362998_362998.caption: Donald Trump speaks during a rally at the San Jose Convention Center in San Jose Calif on June 2 2016
362998_362998.article_context: Donald Trump strongly criticized Hillary Clinton following her speech calling him 'temperamentally unfit to lead.' Trump dismissed her address as 'pathetic,' accused her of criminal wrongdoing for using a private email server as Secretary of State, and argued she should be jailed. He attacked her alignment with Obama-era foreign policy decisions, suggested her participation in the presidential race was a disgrace, and expressed confidence in the FBI investigation of her actions. While Trump rejected Clinton's concerns about his suitability to handle the nation's nuclear arsenal, fact-checkers noted inconsistencies in his claims about opposing the Iraq War. The exchange highlighted escalating personal attacks and the centrality of Clinton's email controversy in the campaign.

142299_142299.caption: Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump speaks July 21 the final day of the Republican National Convention in Cleveland
142299_142299.article_context: The article focuses on Melanie Austin, a former railroad worker in Pennsylvania who, disillusioned with her town's decline and her own experiences of injustice, embraces the conspiracy-driven, anti-establishment rhetoric flourishing around the 2016 presidential election. Feeling empowered and validated by Donald Trump’s campaign, which she sees as championing her beliefs against political correctness and corruption, Melanie finds like-minded communities online that share her suspicions and anger toward prominent figures such as Barack and Michelle Obama and Hillary Clinton. Her fervent support for Trump, hospitalization following an online rant, and consumption of conspiracy theories illustrate how fringe beliefs moved into the mainstream for many Americans during this period, highlighting the polarization and distrust shaping the national political climate.

322793_322793.caption: President Obama speaks in the Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House on Oct 1 2015 about the shooting at the Umpqua Community College in Roseburg Ore
322793_322793.article_context: President Obama expressed frustration and sorrow over a mass shooting at Umpqua Community College in Oregon, calling the repeated cycle of gun violence in the U.S. 'routine' and urging the public to demand stronger gun laws. He criticized the effectiveness of thoughts and prayers alone, advocated for 'common sense' reforms like improved background checks and an assault weapons ban, and challenged gun rights groups, arguing that gun violence should be a politicized issue. Obama emphasized the need for federal and state action, reflecting on the frequent shootings during his presidency and urging voters to make gun control a priority.

398647_398647.caption: Gov Jerry Brown holds a chart showing the statewide average precipition by water year while declaring a drought state of emergency during a speech Jan 17 2014 in San Francisco
398647_398647.article_context: Governor Jerry Brown declared a statewide drought emergency in California, following record-low precipitation and severely diminished Sierra snowpack. The emergency allows the state to seek federal assistance, expedite water transfers, and suspend regulations to address water shortages. Brown urged Californians to voluntarily conserve water by 20%, warning of possible drinking water shortages and impacts on agriculture, which uses most of the state's water. The drought is hindering California farmers, prompting federal disaster relief eligibility and calls for new, sustainable water policies. Brown also ordered state agencies to reduce water use and increase firefighting resources in anticipation of a dry season and heightened wildfire risk.

374733_374733.caption: Randy Travis is in a Texas hospital where he s recovering from surgery following a stroke
374733_374733.article_context: David Traywick, the brother of country singer Randy Travis, was arrested in Union County, North Carolina, after authorities discovered a working methamphetamine lab in his home. Traywick, his wife Jessica, and two other women were charged with conspiracy to traffic meth and held on $500,000 bond each. This arrest follows a previous incident last year where Traywick was also accused of cooking meth. Meanwhile, Randy Travis remains hospitalized in Texas after recent surgery following a stroke.

91537_91537.caption: Beau Biden and President Obama after Vice President Biden is sworn in during the public ceremonial inauguration on the West Front of the US Capitol
91537_91537.article_context: Beau Biden, son of Vice President Joe Biden and former Delaware attorney general, died at age 46 after a battle with brain cancer. A rising political figure, Beau had served in the Delaware National Guard and was awarded the Bronze Star for his service in Iraq. He was viewed as a likely candidate for governor before his illness. His passing prompted statements of grief from the Biden family and President Obama. Beau is remembered for his dedication to public service and his family, leaving behind his wife, Hallie, and two children.

263213_263213.caption: Hillary Clinton gets a hug from her husband after winning her second Senate term as New York Democrats hold a rally on Nov 7 2006
263213_263213.article_context: The Democratic Party has undergone significant changes since Bill Clinton was nominated for president in 1996, shifting left on issues like trade, criminal justice, and social policy. Hillary Clinton's nomination in 2016 reflects both this evolution and her ability to adapt to a new political era, despite initial challenges from Bernie Sanders’ progressive campaign. The party's platform now emphasizes issues like climate change, LGBT rights, and income inequality, marking a stark contrast with its more centrist past. Hillary Clinton's policy positions also differ from her husband's, showcasing her independent political identity and alignment with contemporary Democratic values.

632009_632009.caption: Leon Panetta after arriving in Afghanistan
632009_632009.article_context: An Afghan interpreter working for foreign forces died from severe burns after crashing a stolen truck at a British airfield in Helmand province, Afghanistan, as US Defense Secretary Leon Panetta's plane was landing. The truck, carrying fuel, ignited during the crash and appeared to target a group of US Marines, although officials believe the incident was not directly linked to Panetta's arrival. A British soldier was also injured trying to prevent the theft. No one from Panetta's party was harmed.

1197473_1197473.caption: John Kerry speaks at Queen Alia airport in Jordan He announced that Israel and the Palestinians have agreed to return to peace talks
1197473_1197473.article_context: The US, led by Secretary of State John Kerry, has announced plans to host talks between Israeli and Palestinian negotiators next week in Washington, marking a significant step towards reviving the long-stalled Middle East peace process. After months of intensive diplomacy, both sides have agreed to a basis for direct negotiations, although the formalization of the process and its parameters remain undisclosed. Despite skepticism and political pressure within both camps, particularly over issues like the 1967 borders and the release of Palestinian prisoners, US intervention and recent EU guidelines targeting Israeli settlements have added urgency to the renewed talks, though major challenges and doubts persist.

47084_47084.caption: Former president Bill Clinton speaks in a show of support for California Democrats during during a Get Out The Vote rally in Oxnard on Oct 29
47084_47084.article_context: Following a significant defeat in the midterm elections, Democrats are confronting major questions about the party’s identity and strategy as they prepare for the 2016 presidential race. The results highlighted the limits of their campaign tactics and divisions within the party, particularly between centrist and populist factions. While demographic trends and the electoral map still favor Democrats, the party faces the challenge of formulating a clear, broad economic message and addressing doubts about its ability to govern. The potential candidacy of Hillary Clinton raises further discussions about leadership and the need for alternatives, as Democrats weigh how closely to associate with the Obama presidency amid widespread voter dissatisfaction. Republicans also recognize their own challenges going into 2016, cautioning against overconfidence from their midterm success.

535247_535247.caption: US president Ronald Reagan pictured at a rally in 1984 caused consternation with a joke about bombing Russia
535247_535247.article_context: President Reagan caused international controversy after joking, off-air but on a live microphone, that he had 'signed legislation to outlaw Russia forever' and 'we begin bombing in five minutes.' Although the remark was intended as humour and not broadcast live, it was recorded by technicians and circulated among the media, leading to criticism from political opponents and concern abroad, especially in the Soviet Union. The incident raised questions about the appropriateness of Reagan's jokes and the handling of off-the-record comments. The White House attempted to manage the fallout, noting prior media agreements about not publishing such remarks.

316012_316012.caption: Oscar Pistorius appears in court at a bail hearing Friday in Pretoria South Africa He has been charged with premeditated murder in the shooting death of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp
316012_316012.article_context: Oscar Pistorius, the South African Olympic and Paralympic athlete, was granted bail while awaiting trial for the shooting death of his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp. The magistrate ruled that Pistorius was not a flight risk or a danger to the community, setting bail at 1 million rand and imposing restrictions such as surrendering his passport and avoiding contact with prosecution witnesses. The case has been marked by controversy, including the removal of the lead police investigator after it was revealed he faced attempted murder charges and had mishandled key evidence. Pistorius claims he accidentally shot Steenkamp, mistaking her for an intruder, while prosecutors allege premeditated murder. The trial is set for June 4, and public opinion in South Africa is deeply divided over Pistorius' claims.

1449890_1449890.caption: Hugo Chavez and daughter Rosa Ines as he boards for Brasilia leading the polls for the 7 October election
1449890_1449890.article_context: Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez traveled to Brazil for his first official international visit since being diagnosed with cancer, marking a major step in his efforts to reassert his public presence ahead of October’s presidential election. The visit coincided with Venezuela’s admission to the Mercosur trading bloc, a process previously blocked by Paraguay until that country’s suspension. Chavez, emphasizing his recovery and readiness to run for a third term, has intensified campaign activities and maintains that Venezuela’s membership in Mercosur strengthens both the bloc and his country’s standing. His candidacy will be challenged by opposition leader Henrique Capriles in the upcoming election.

47643_47643.caption: Republican US presidential candidate Ted Cruz gestures over at rival candidate Donald Trump
47643_47643.article_context: President Obama is moving quickly for the United States to join the Paris climate agreement, working alongside China to urge rapid global adoption. If the agreement goes into force before Obama's term ends, the next president would face legal and bureaucratic hurdles to exit, having to wait until at least 2019 to begin formal withdrawal, which would then take another year. Leading Republican presidential contenders like Donald Trump and Ted Cruz have criticized the agreement and expressed skepticism about climate change, but an in-force Paris agreement would slow reversal of Obama's climate policies. While the agreement doesn't strictly bind future presidents to specific emissions reductions, it does require ongoing reporting and accountability, potentially increasing international political pressure if a future administration seeks to disregard its commitments.

78477_78477.caption: Clinton responds to criticism ahead of NY primary
78477_78477.article_context: A recent NBC-Wall Street Journal poll shows that Hillary Clinton is highly vulnerable in a general election, with a majority of voters viewing her negatively and questioning her trustworthiness. However, Republican frontrunners Donald Trump and Ted Cruz are even less popular with the broader electorate, making them poor challengers to Clinton. Both Trump and Cruz have historically low favorability ratings, particularly among key demographics such as women, millennials, and Hispanics. The article concludes that although Clinton is beatable, the current Republican candidates are unlikely to capitalize on her weaknesses, likely resulting in a Clinton victory and missed opportunity for the GOP.

281669_281669.caption: Sharapova takes silver in the 2012 Olympics losing to Serena Williams in the goldmedal match
281669_281669.article_context: Following Maria Sharapova's two-year doping ban, several major sponsors—Head and Evian—have reaffirmed their support for her, while Avon chose not to renew an expiring partnership, unrelated to the scandal. Head and its CEO criticized the decision to ban the substance meldonium, arguing it was added without sufficient scientific evidence. Some other sponsors, such as TAG Heuer and Porsche, had previously suspended their ties to Sharapova. Sharapova maintains her use of meldonium was for health reasons and will appeal the suspension to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, arguing the punishment is excessively harsh.

347525_347525.caption: President Obama and Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney greet each other before the start of the election season s final debate moderated by Bob Schieffer of CBS
347525_347525.article_context: President Obama and Mitt Romney participated in their final debate ahead of the 2012 presidential election, focusing primarily on foreign policy, especially the Middle East. Obama criticized Romney's inconsistencies and lack of foreign policy experience, citing his own record as commander in chief, while Romney accused Obama of weak international leadership and mishandling situations in the Middle East. Both candidates argued their economic policies were crucial to maintaining America's global strength, and clashed over issues such as military spending, handling of China, and domestic economic recovery. The debate, held in a more subdued atmosphere than previous encounters, marked their last opportunity to appeal to undecided voters before Election Day.

677421_677421.caption: Vladimir Putin and Dmitry Medvedev on their way to tell cabinet ministers that their New Year holidays had been scrapped
677421_677421.article_context: Russian President Vladimir Putin has canceled New Year holidays for government ministers due to the country's economic crisis, urging them to remain at work to address the situation. As Russia faces recession, with the rouble's value falling and currency reserves dropping below $400 billion, the government is taking measures to stabilize the economy, including raising interest rates and offering foreign currency loans to banks. Western sanctions and low oil prices have severely impacted Russia's financial stability.

179323_179323.caption: Ammon Bundy departs after addressing the media at the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge near Burns Ore
179323_179323.article_context: Militia groups in the United States have tended to proliferate during Democratic presidencies, with notable surges during the Clinton and Obama administrations. Data from the Southern Poverty Law Center shows that militia numbers peaked at 370 during Clinton's presidency, dropped to 35 in the Bush years, and rose again to 276 under Obama. The trend is attributed to group members' fears about increased gun control, government overreach, and conspiracy theories, concerns that intensify under Democratic leadership. These patterns highlight how political climate and party agendas influence the rise and fall of militias.

43530_43530.caption: Aaron Hernandez charged in Boston doublemurder
43530_43530.article_context: Former NFL star Aaron Hernandez has been indicted for the 2012 drive-by murders of Daniel Abreu and Safiro Furtado in Boston, following a revived investigation that began after Hernandez was charged in the 2013 killing of Odin Lloyd. Hernandez now faces multiple counts, including two for first-degree murder in the double homicide, which prosecutors say was a random encounter after leaving a nightclub. Evidence against Hernandez includes video footage and recovered physical evidence linking him to the crime. The revelation that Hernandez may have played an entire NFL season after the double homicide has intensified public scrutiny. He remains in jail awaiting trial for Lloyd’s murder, while new charges further complicate his legal situation and separate trials are expected.

326057_326057.caption: Hillary Rodham Clinton speaks during the Democratic presidential debate
326057_326057.article_context: During the first Democratic presidential debate in Las Vegas, several candidates made false or misleading claims. Hillary Clinton distorted her prior support for the Trans-Pacific Partnership, saying she 'hoped' it would be a gold standard, while she previously called it the gold standard. Bernie Sanders overstated the impact of his Social Security expansion plan and exaggerated rates of African-American youth unemployment, confusing underemployment with unemployment. Martin O’Malley falsely claimed 70% of Americans earn the same or less than 12 years ago, despite data showing wage increases. Lincoln Chafee overstated Rhode Island’s employment improvements during his tenure. Clinton’s statement about daily gun deaths included suicides, which make up most firearm fatalities. Sanders incorrectly asserted the U.S. leads in income and wealth inequality globally. Clinton’s use of a private email account as Secretary of State was technically allowed but did not comply fully with federal records policies. These errors and omissions highlight persistent misrepresentations in political debates.

1587062_1587062.caption: President Dilma Rousseff went on to the southern city of Curitiba after she recovered
1587062_1587062.article_context: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff reassured the public about her health after experiencing dizziness due to low blood pressure following a televised debate with her opponent, Aecio Neves, ahead of the tightly contested presidential run-off. During the debate, Rousseff and Neves exchanged accusations over nepotism and corruption, reflecting the increasingly bitter tone of the campaign. Rousseff's doctor attributed her episode to not having eaten enough and said no medical examination was needed.

369398_369398.caption: Donald Trump speaks to an audience at a rally at the David Lawrence Convention Center on April 13 2016 in Pittsburgh
369398_369398.article_context: Ahead of key primaries, both Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton are leading their respective party races, but a USA TODAY/Suffolk University poll reveals deep divisions among Republican and Democratic voters. Many Republicans are hesitant to support Trump if he becomes the nominee, and a significant portion of Bernie Sanders' supporters are unsure about backing Clinton. Allegations of a 'rigged' nomination process persist on both sides, especially among Sanders and Trump supporters. Poll results show Clinton with a shrinking lead over Sanders, while Trump maintains a strong edge over competitors Cruz and Kasich. In head-to-head matchups, Clinton and Sanders would both beat Trump, while Kasich is the only Republican shown to defeat Clinton. Party unity remains uncertain, with ongoing skepticism about the nomination process and possible long-lasting rifts heading into national conventions.

244483_244483.caption: Former Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky
244483_244483.article_context: Former U.S. senator George Mitchell, serving as Penn State’s athletics integrity monitor, has reported that the university is making significant progress on institutional reforms following the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse scandal. Mitchell’s first quarterly report highlights revised policies and extensive training for employees regarding child protection and mandated reporting, as well as greater transparency under the Clery Act. Football coach Bill O’Brien was praised for his leadership in opening athletic facilities to other teams and supporting changes. While noting that work remains, the report and NCAA President Mark Emmert commend the university’s efforts to reform its culture and compliance. Additional actions, such as implementing a new Code of Conduct, are slated for the coming months.

1271480_1271480.caption: Hillary Clinton speaks during a news conference at the US embassy in Islamabad after meeting Pakistan s leaders
1271480_1271480.article_context: Following the US raid that killed Osama bin Laden, US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton visited Pakistan to address the strained relationship between the two countries. Clinton urged Pakistan's leaders to take decisive steps against terrorism and highlighted the importance of Pakistan's cooperation for peace efforts in Afghanistan. The visit, which also included Admiral Mike Mullen, occurred amid heightened tensions and mutual suspicions, as well as ongoing militant violence in Pakistan. Clinton emphasized that US-Pakistan relations were at a turning point and that further progress depended on Pakistan's actions against militants.

248566_248566.caption: Actress Meryl Streep cheers on stage prior to speaking during the 2016 Democratic National Convention
248566_248566.article_context: At the Democratic National Convention in Philadelphia, Hillary Clinton was formally nominated as the first female major party presidential nominee in U.S. history. After a state-by-state roll call, Bernie Sanders moved to have Clinton nominated by acclamation, signaling unity within the party and drawing cheers from delegates. The roll call featured emotional moments, particularly from delegates who witnessed the advancement of women’s rights, and highlighted Sanders' significant impact on the party. While some Sanders supporters remained hesitant, most delegates came together in support of Clinton, reflecting a moment of historical significance and party solidarity.

306674_306674.caption: Ben Carson officially announces his candidacy for president on May 4 2015 in Detroit
306674_306674.article_context: When presidential candidates announced their campaigns for the 2016 election, Facebook saw spikes in conversations about each candidate, mainly concentrated in their home states or regions where they have strong connections. Notably, Hillary Clinton generated the most engagement in Illinois, Arkansas, Kentucky, West Virginia, and Washington, D.C., reflecting her broad national recognition. Facebook's analysis showed larger social media footprints for well-known candidates, such as Clinton, compared to lesser-known contenders. Experts note that while these initial bursts of online interest indicate where candidates have the most receptive audiences at the start, sustained engagement and focused outreach in key battleground states are more crucial for long-term campaign success.

1124191_1124191.caption: Barack Obama speaks in Tallinn Estonia on the eve of the Nato summit
1124191_1124191.article_context: At the upcoming NATO summit in Wales, the United States and Britain will discuss a range of military options to confront Islamic State (ISIS), including potential airstrikes in both Iraq and Syria, supplying more arms to local forces fighting ISIS, and exploring special forces rescue missions for hostages. The UK is cautious about direct intervention due to previous parliamentary opposition to actions in Syria, but officials note that the ISIS threat now targets British nationals and interests. Both countries are considering increased military assistance to Kurdish and Iraqi forces and possibly further training and support for vetted Syrian rebels. The broader strategy involves building a multinational coalition, applying diplomatic pressure on regional powers to cut financial support to ISIS, and reforming the Iraqi military for more effective ground operations.

114721_114721.caption: Police arrest activist DeRay Mckesson during a protest along a Baton Rouge highway that passes in front of the police department s headquarters there
114721_114721.article_context: Chad Copley, a white homeowner in Raleigh, North Carolina, called 911 to report a group of black men he described as 'hoodlums' outside his home early Sunday morning. After telling the dispatcher he was 'locked and loaded' and planning to confront the group, Copley fired a shot from inside his garage, fatally wounding 20-year-old Kouren-Rodney Bernard Thomas. Copley has been charged with first-degree murder and could face the death penalty. The incident has sparked local outrage and comes as Raleigh is still dealing with the aftermath of a previous fatal police shooting involving a black man. Copley’s lawyer has urged the public not to rush to judgment as the investigation is ongoing.

493334_493334.caption: Angelina Jolie Pitt addresses the Lords select committee
493334_493334.article_context: Angelina Jolie appeared before the House of Lords select committee on sexual violence in conflict, drawing significant attention due to her celebrity status. Joined by William Hague, their presence turned the committee meeting into a high-profile event, overshadowing its usual government proceedings. Despite the excitement, the discussion provided little new information about dealing with sexual violence in conflict, mainly reiterating that it remains a serious issue requiring more action. The appearance highlighted the committee’s consensus on the subject and also showcased how star power can influence parliamentary proceedings.

1187831_1187831.caption: David Cameron with Chloe Smith after her byelection victory at Norwich North yesterday
1187831_1187831.article_context: The Conservatives won the Norwich North by-election, taking the seat from Labour with a majority of over 7,000 votes and a significant swing in their favor. Chloe Smith, the Tory candidate, became Britain's youngest MP. David Cameron accused Gordon Brown and the Labour Party of running a misleading and divisive campaign focused on claims about Tory spending cuts. The election, held amid public anger over MPs’ expenses, was triggered by the resignation of Labour MP Ian Gibson. Labour cited local factors for their defeat, while the result was seen as validation of the Conservatives' approach and a sign that Labour’s attack strategy on spending cuts was ineffective.

51227_51227.caption: President Obama is greeted by Texas Gov Rick Perry as he arrives in Dallas on Wednesday to discuss the humanitarian situation at the southern border
51227_51227.article_context: President Obama defended his decision not to visit the Texas-Mexico border amid a surge of unaccompanied children crossing illegally, stating he was fully informed of the crisis and not interested in 'photo ops.' After meeting with Texas Governor Rick Perry, Obama urged Congress to approve $3.7 billion in emergency funding to address the situation. Perry requested increased border security measures and faster deportation processes, while Obama challenged Congress to prioritize problem-solving over politics. The president faced criticism from both parties for skipping a border visit during his Texas trip, but emphasized the need for legislative action rather than symbolic gestures.

159072_159072.caption: Clinton listens as Sanders speaks
159072_159072.article_context: A new Quinnipiac University poll shows Hillary Clinton leading Bernie Sanders nationally by just 2 points—the narrowest margin yet—marking a dramatic decline from her previous large leads. The poll suggests significant shifts in support and favorability for both candidates, but the article cautions that this result may be an outlier, as most other national polls still show Clinton with a stronger lead. The piece also notes that Sanders is perceived by voters as stronger against Republican opponents. Despite this tightening race, Clinton remains the Democratic front-runner and national polls are not always strongly predictive.

103942_103942.caption: President Obama speaks in Selma Our job s easier because somebody already got us over that bridge he said
103942_103942.article_context: President Obama delivered a speech at the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama, marking the 50th anniversary of 'Bloody Sunday' and honoring civil rights protestors who endured violence in the struggle for voting rights. He framed their courage as a deeply patriotic act and linked past battles for justice to ongoing movements for minorities, women, immigrants, and the LGBTQ community. Addressing current issues like voting rights restrictions and police violence, Obama urged continued reform and challenged lawmakers to restore the Voting Rights Act. Joined by former President George W. Bush and civil rights leaders, Obama emphasized that America's greatness lies in its ability to confront flaws and strive for a more just society.

911665_911665.caption: Former Thai prime minister Yingluck Shinawatra meets her supporters on 7 May in Bangkok after being forced to step down
911665_911665.article_context: Thailand's military, led by General Prayuth Chan-ocha, carried out a coup and detained former prime minister Yingluck Shinawatra along with nearly 200 politicians and activists, banning them from leaving the country. The coup follows months of political turmoil between pro- and anti-Thaksin factions, and the army claims it acted to restore order and stability. The junta has imposed significant media restrictions, faced widespread international condemnation, and warned of prolonged military rule, with analysts fearing a potential for lasting unrest or even civil war.

258302_258302.caption: Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump unveils his tax plan in New York Monday
258302_258302.article_context: Donald Trump has expanded his lead in the latest USA TODAY/Suffolk University Poll of Republican primary voters, with outsider candidates Ben Carson and Carly Fiorina also rising in support, reflecting voter dissatisfaction with traditional politicians. Jeb Bush and other established figures have lost ground, as nearly half of GOP voters now back candidates with no prior electoral experience. The poll, which shows Trump at 23% and Carson and Fiorina tied at 13%, highlights a shift toward unconventional contenders amid broader frustrations with the political establishment. Despite strong support among Republicans, Trump faces significant unfavorable ratings nationwide, and the field has narrowed to six main contenders.

1141465_1141465.caption: Allred comforts Chelan who claims Cosby gave her an antihistamine and lunged at her in his hotel room
1141465_1141465.article_context: Three women publicly accused Bill Cosby of sexual abuse during a press conference led by lawyer Gloria Allred, who urged Cosby to waive the statute of limitations to allow alleged victims to pursue legal action or to set up a $100 million compensation fund. These new allegations follow similar claims by more than two dozen women, including a recent lawsuit filed by Judy Huth, who alleged abuse in the 1970s when she was a teenager. The mounting accusations have severely damaged Cosby's reputation and career, resulting in cancelled performances and projects. Cosby's lawyer has denied the allegations and called them defamatory.

271515_271515.caption: Republican presidential candidate New Jersey Gov Chris Christie participates in the first primetime presidential debate
271515_271515.article_context: A new Suffolk University poll in Iowa shows Donald Trump still leads the Republican field after the first GOP debate, but his support has slipped, with many viewers now feeling less comfortable with him as a candidate. Jeb Bush’s standing has dropped significantly, while Marco Rubio made notable gains, rising to third place. Carly Fiorina impressed viewers in the afternoon debate and is now narrowly ahead of Bush. Nearly 20% of voters remain undecided, but Rubio, Carson, Fiorina, and Cruz received boosts from the debates. The poll indicates Trump performs better among those who did not watch the debate, and many Republican respondents expressed concerns over his comments about women. Overall, the debate reshaped candidate momentum in the key early caucus state.

153894_153894.caption: President Obama makes a statement regarding the budget fight in Congress and foreign policy challenges on Friday
153894_153894.article_context: On September 27, 2013, President Obama spoke about three major issues: his historic phone call with Iranian President Rouhani and ongoing diplomatic efforts to address Iran's nuclear program; the United Nations Security Council's impending vote to require Syria's Assad regime to eliminate its chemical weapons; and the looming threat of a U.S. government shutdown due to a standoff in Congress. Obama urged House Republicans to pass the budget and avoid a shutdown, criticized their efforts to tie the issue to repealing the Affordable Care Act, and warned of the serious economic risks posed by failing to raise the debt ceiling. He emphasized the need for responsible governance and bipartisan cooperation to protect the economy and serve the American people.

203821_203821.caption: Putin meets with Obama other leaders
203821_203821.article_context: During a D-Day commemoration in France, President Obama and Russian President Putin held a private discussion about the ongoing crisis in Ukraine, which U.S. officials called a positive and productive development. Putin also met briefly with Ukraine’s President-elect Petro Poroshenko, signaling a possible openness to dialogue and improved relations. Although no breakthroughs were achieved, both Obama and U.S. officials expressed increased optimism for diplomatic resolution, contingent on Russia recognizing Ukraine’s new government and ending support for separatists in eastern Ukraine. Western leaders warned Russia of further economic sanctions if it failed to de-escalate the crisis, while Putin indicated readiness to engage with Poroshenko’s administration.

64521_64521.caption: Gov Rick Snyder speaks during a news conference in Flint on Jan 11
64521_64521.article_context: The article compares the crises in Flint, Michigan and Chicago, Illinois, highlighting how both cities suffer from severe governmental failures and a lack of accountability. In Flint, newly released emails from Michigan Governor Rick Snyder reveal that political concerns and blame-shifting were prioritized over addressing citizens' complaints and public health warnings about the water crisis, resulting in widespread lead contamination. Similarly, in Chicago, Mayor Rahm Emanuel's administration attempted to obscure police misconduct, including fatal shootings and coerced confessions, by withholding evidence and resisting transparency. The piece argues that in both cities, officials have demonstrated a disregard for residents’ wellbeing, emphasizing the need for transparency and genuine public service in government.

133371_133371.caption: Hope Solo listens to attorney Todd Maybrown in Kirkland Municipal Court on Monday
133371_133371.article_context: Hope Solo, the U.S. women's soccer team goalkeeper, pleaded not guilty to domestic violence charges after allegedly striking her sister and teenage nephew at her home. She was released from jail on the condition that she avoids contact with the alleged victims and refrains from drinking alcohol, with a pretrial hearing scheduled for August 11. Solo's lawyer claims she was assaulted during the incident and asserts her innocence, expressing confidence that the full facts will come out in court.

963026_963026.caption: British prime minister David Cameron reacts during the funeral mass
963026_963026.article_context: World leaders, dignitaries, and thousands of mourners gathered at St Vitus Cathedral in Prague Castle for the state funeral of former Czech President Vaclav Havel. The ceremony featured tributes from notable international figures, including former US President Bill Clinton, French President Nicolas Sarkozy, and British Prime Minister David Cameron. The service included religious rites, performances, and a procession, with Havel's widow, Dagmar Havlova, and other close friends and family in attendance. The event saw widespread public participation, both inside and outside the cathedral, reflecting Havel's significant legacy in Czech and global history.

323705_323705.caption: Defendant Jodi Arias listens as prosecutor Juan Martinez makes his closing arguments during her trial at Maricopa County Superior Court in Phoenix on Thursday
323705_323705.article_context: As the high-profile murder trial of Jodi Arias neared its conclusion in Phoenix, her defense lawyer urged jurors to judge impartially, emphasizing doubts in the prosecution's theory of premeditation. Arias claims she killed her ex-boyfriend Travis Alexander in self-defense, while prosecutors argue it was a planned act fueled by jealousy and rage, showing evidence of stabbing, shooting, and blood at the scene. The case, a media sensation, centers on conflicting portrayals of their troubled relationship, with the jury considering charges ranging from first-degree murder, which could bring the death penalty, to manslaughter. Both sides presented closing arguments, with the prosecution portraying Arias as a manipulative liar and the defense questioning the logic of the state's case.

193870_193870.caption: President Obama at his victory party in Chicago JEWEL SAMADAFPGETTY IMAGES
193870_193870.article_context: The 2012 presidential election featured ten states with the closest margins between Barack Obama and Mitt Romney, with Florida being the narrowest at 0.6 percent. Obama won nine of these swing states, reinforcing their significance for future elections. In the aftermath, political leaders are signaling possible shifts, as House Speaker John Boehner indicated openness to new revenue sources in budget negotiations—a break from the GOP’s usual stance—while Democratic leaders asserted a mandate for their tax positions. Additionally, Democrats gained ground in some House races, and a few key contests—including Washington's gubernatorial race—remained too close to call. Overall, turnout was lower than in 2008, and the results prompted internal rethinking and jockeying for leadership positions within both parties.

216064_216064.caption: Specter reacts to Justice Sandra Day OConnor s retirement announcement on Capitol Hill on July 1 2005 Specter waged a very public battle with cancer
216064_216064.article_context: Arlen Specter, a longtime Pennsylvania senator known for his centrist views and bipartisan approach, died at age 82 from complications of non-Hodgkins lymphoma. Serving in the Senate for 30 years, Specter was notable for key votes on significant issues including the rejection of Robert Bork’s Supreme Court nomination, the support for economic stimulus and health care reforms under President Obama, and his role in high-profile judiciary hearings. He switched from the Republican to Democratic Party in 2009, influencing major legislation before losing a primary election. Specter’s legacy includes advocacy for medical research funding and efforts to maintain moderate, bipartisan politics amid growing partisanship in Congress.

661158_661158.caption: Red crosses over the faces of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
661158_661158.article_context: On July 10, 2012, activists from Reporters Without Borders staged a protest outside the Iran Air office on the Champs Elysees in Paris to denounce the imprisonment of journalists in Iran. The demonstration also commemorated the tenth anniversary of the death of Iranian photojournalist Zahra Kazemi in prison. Protesters used symbolic gestures such as fake injuries and chains to highlight the plight of imprisoned journalists under Iran’s regime, drawing attention to ongoing concerns about press freedom and human rights abuses.

313191_313191.caption: British Prime Minister Tony Blair addresses troops at Shaiba Logistics Base in Basra Iraq on Dec 22 2005
313191_313191.article_context: A long-awaited British inquiry led by John Chilcot concluded that the UK joined the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq based on flawed intelligence, inadequate planning, and without exhausting peaceful means or facing an imminent threat from Saddam Hussein. The report was highly critical of then-Prime Minister Tony Blair, but stopped short of declaring his decision illegal. Blair defended his actions but expressed deep regret and sorrow over the aftermath, including the sectarian violence and significant loss of life. The inquiry highlighted failures in both the military operation and post-war planning, leading to public protests and calls for accountability, with some families of fallen soldiers considering legal action.

1213126_1213126.caption: Journalist Rafael Marques de Morais sits in court in Luanda where he was given a sixmonth suspended sentence after being convicted of slander
1213126_1213126.article_context: Tiffany & Co., along with other notable figures and organizations, have signed an open letter urging Angola’s president to halt the prosecution of investigative journalist Rafael Marques de Morais, who exposed human rights abuses in the country’s diamond industry. Marques was given a six-month suspended sentence and ordered to withdraw his book, which accused army generals of complicity in torture and murder. Human rights groups and public figures criticize the trial as unfair, claiming it aims to silence Marques and prevent further investigations into corruption and abuse.

117480_117480.caption: Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump speaks about the results of Super Tuesday primary and caucus voting during a news conference in Palm Beach Fla on March 1 2016
117480_117480.article_context: More than 50 prominent Republican national security experts, including former officials from the Bush administration, have signed an open letter denouncing Donald Trump as unfit for the presidency. The letter criticizes Trump for his erratic foreign policy ideas, praise for Vladimir Putin, support for torture, and anti-Muslim rhetoric, describing him as 'fundamentally dishonest.' The signatories insist they will not support Trump, reflecting deep divisions in the Republican Party ahead of his likely nomination.

232070_232070.caption: Oscar Pistorius leaves the high court in Pretoria South Africa Wednesday
232070_232070.article_context: During cross-examination in Oscar Pistorius' murder trial, prosecutor Gerrie Nel accused the Olympic athlete of being self-centered in his relationship with Reeva Steenkamp and called his public courtroom apology to her family a calculated spectacle. Pistorius maintains he accidentally shot Steenkamp, believing her to be an intruder, while the prosecution argues he killed her intentionally after an argument. The trial presents two contrasting portrayals of Pistorius: one as a remorseful man making a tragic mistake, and the other as an egotist obsessed with firearms. The trial is being heard by Judge Thokozile Masipa, with Pistorius facing a possible sentence of 25 years to life if convicted.

310893_310893.caption: Jodi Arias looks at the family of Travis Alexander as the jury arrives on May 15 2013
310893_310893.article_context: Jurors are now deciding whether Jodi Arias should receive the death penalty or life in prison for the 2008 murder of her boyfriend, Travis Alexander, after both sides concluded their closing arguments in her sentencing retrial. Arias was previously convicted of first-degree murder, but her original jury could not agree on punishment, prompting this retrial. The process has been marked by defense claims of prosecutorial misconduct and arguments about Arias’ mental health and alleged abuse, while prosecutors contend she planned the killing. Arias testified in secret before withdrawing from further testimony, and if the current jury deadlocks, the death penalty will be removed from consideration, with a judge deciding her sentence.

433606_433606.caption: Former president George HW Bush is hospitalized with bronchitis in Houston
433606_433606.article_context: Former President George H.W. Bush has been hospitalized in Houston for a week due to bronchitis complications but is expected to be discharged soon. His condition remains stable, with doctors emphasizing that the situation was not life-threatening and treatment has been effective. Bush, who also has Parkinson's disease, received visits from family including his son, former President George W. Bush.

637321_637321.caption: President Barack Obama speaks in honor of Memorial Day at Arlington National Cemetery in Arlington Virginia
637321_637321.article_context: President Barack Obama, speaking at Memorial Day ceremonies at Arlington National Cemetery, urged Americans to honor the sacrifices of military personnel, emphasizing that service members are not always fully appreciated, especially as the US combat role in Iraq has ended and involvement in Afghanistan is winding down. Obama noted a disconnect due to the all-volunteer military and advanced technology limiting direct public engagement with war. He reminded the nation that, even as these conflicts conclude, America remains at war and must not forget its service members, referencing recent progress against terrorist threats but cautioning against complacency.

239735_239735.caption: Attorney General Loretta Lynch addresses a memorial honoring three Baton Rouge law enforcement officers killed in a July 17 shootout in Baton Rouge July 25
239735_239735.article_context: A memorial service in Baton Rouge honored three law enforcement officers—Matthew Gerald, Montrell Jackson, and Brad Garafola—who were killed in an ambush on July 17. The event, attended by Vice President Joe Biden, Attorney General Loretta Lynch, and Louisiana Governor John Bel Edwards, emphasized unity, peace, and gratitude for public service. The shootings followed heightened racial tensions after the death of Alton Sterling, which had sparked protests. Family members of the fallen officers spoke, with calls to reject hate and violence in favor of love and compassion.

365310_365310.caption: President Barack Obama hugs Vice President Joe Biden during funeral services for Biden s son Beau Biden June 6 2015 at St Anthony of Padua Church in Wilmington Del
365310_365310.article_context: Cpl. Eric Casebolt, the McKinney, Texas police officer criticized for his actions at a pool party, has resigned and will give more details through his attorney following public backlash and alleged death threats. Russian President Vladimir Putin is set to meet with Pope Francis amid calls for the pope to address Russia's role in Ukraine's conflict. A new survey shows that many NATO countries expect the U.S. to defend allies against Russia, with most respondents opposing military intervention by their own nations. New York City plans to propose that chain restaurants label high-sodium menu items with a warning symbol to help fight cardiovascular disease. Vice President Joe Biden made a brief return to work in Washington after the loss of his son Beau Biden to brain cancer.

721015_721015.caption: US President Barack Obama speaks on federal government shutdown at the Rose Garden of the White House in Washington DC on October 1 2013
