Kim Jong-un was shown overseeing the launch and declared the weapon boosted North Korea's strategic power. South Korea responded by reporting the North fired additional anti-ship cruise missiles and convened its National Security Council in an emergency session. Experts caution that North Korean claims require skepticism, though satellite evidence suggests ongoing submarine and missile development.

1466985_1466985.caption: Mikhail Khodorkovsky and Platon Lebedev were convicted together
1466985_1466985.article_context: A Moscow court upheld the fraud conviction of former oil tycoon Mikhail Khodorkovsky but reduced his 14-year sentence by one year. Khodorkovsky, the ex-owner of Yukos and once the richest man in Russia, was convicted of embezzling nearly $30 billion and money laundering, in a case widely criticized internationally as politically motivated for his opposition to Vladimir Putin. Khodorkovsky and his partner Platon Lebedev will remain in prison until at least 2016, despite claims by Khodorkovsky that the charges and trial were unjust and influenced from outside the court.

605952_605952.caption: I don t really like Westminster I spend as much time as possible away from there Labour MP Gloria De Piero
605952_605952.article_context: Reports emerged that The Sun newspaper would discontinue its controversial Page 3 feature, but unexpectedly published another topless photo, disappointing campaigners and politicians such as Gloria de Piero, Labour’s shadow women and equalities minister. The incident reignited debate about sexism in the media and the broader campaign against Page 3, reflecting long-standing frustrations with both the tabloid's practices and the challenges faced by women in politics. De Piero, noted for her accessible and relatable style, continues to champion women's voices and equal representation while navigating the complexities of media influence and public expectations.

224266_224266.caption: Missing baby Eliza Delacruz is seen in an undated photo provided by the Long Beach Police Department
224266_224266.article_context: A 3-week-old baby, Eliza Delacruz, was found dead in a dumpster in Imperial Beach after being abducted from a Long Beach residence where her parents and another adult were wounded in a shooting. Long Beach police are searching for a suspect, whose motive remains unknown but who is not believed to have acted randomly. Two of the shooting victims remain hospitalized in critical condition. Authorities are urging the public for information as they investigate the case.

1643363_1643363.caption: ThenSecretary of State Colin Powell was not immediately informed
1643363_1643363.article_context: A leaked White House memo reveals details from a secret Senate report on CIA interrogations, stating that the now-discontinued practices were brutal, ineffective, and caused significant harm. President Obama ended the program, which under President Bush saw suspected terrorists subjected to harsh methods at secret 'black sites.' The memo, sent accidentally to the media, acknowledges the interrogation program as a mistake and calls for the US to learn from it and never repeat such actions. The leak comes amid tension between the CIA and the Senate over the investigation, including a finding that CIA staff improperly searched Senate computers, prompting an apology from CIA Director John Brennan. Debate continues over the accuracy of the Senate report as some Republicans and the CIA dispute its conclusions.

1632604_1632604.caption: Norway s Progress Party led by Siv Jensen came third in Monday s vote the first general election since Breivik s attacks
1632604_1632604.article_context: Anders Behring Breivik, who murdered 77 people in the 2011 Norway attacks, has been allowed to study political science modules at the University of Oslo from his high security prison. While he cannot pursue a full degree or have direct contact with staff, the university emphasized fair treatment under Norwegian law. The decision has sparked debate about rehabilitation, justice, and moral values in Norway, especially since Breivik’s crimes targeted the Labour Party youth and he was formerly associated with the right-wing Progress Party, which has distanced itself from him.

214221_214221.caption: This undated photo is one of several pictures of deceased teen Trayvon Martin that defense attorneys are trying to introduce at the trial of murder suspect George Zimmerman
214221_214221.article_context: Judge Debra Nelson denied a request to delay George Zimmerman's June 10 trial for the second-degree murder of Trayvon Martin and ruled that evidence related to Trayvon's personal history, such as school records and cellphone data, would be excluded unless relevant issues arise during trial. The judge also denied prosecutors' attempt for a gag order and maintained jury anonymity. Most prosecution motions were granted, while some defense motions were denied or postponed. Nelson set further hearings to resolve media access to jurors, alleged evidence withholding, and expert testimony. Zimmerman was not present, but his legal team said they are prepared for trial, while Trayvon's family continued to challenge efforts to influence potential jurors. The case has attracted national attention over its implications for racial profiling and self-defense laws.

1549608_1549608.caption: Rotherham is trying to restore its reputation following the revelations in the Jay report
1549608_1549608.article_context: MPs have called for an urgent investigation into missing files related to the Rotherham child sex abuse scandal, amid concerns that important documents detailing institutional failures were stolen, possibly as part of a cover-up. The Home Affairs Select Committee highlighted repeated disappearances of key evidence, criticized local authorities and police for ignoring clear signs of abuse, and called for new laws to allow the removal of failing police commissioners. The report follows revelations that over 1,400 children were abused in Rotherham between 1997 and 2013, leading to high-profile resignations and further ongoing inquiries.

697934_697934.caption: Human rights activist Heba Morayef says despite Mubarak s removal protesters are still being tortured and imprisoned
697934_697934.article_context: In the months following Mubarak’s ouster in Egypt, the military has conducted numerous detentions and trials, setting a concerning precedent for justice and accountability during the transition. While some political reforms, such as allowing independent trade unions and new political parties, have been enacted, measures like the proposed ban on strikes and protests and limitations on freedom of expression undermine broader democratic progress. Widespread military trials for protesters—often conducted rapidly and without proper legal process—have resulted in thousands of prison sentences since Mubarak’s fall. Despite some prosecutions for recent abuses, long-standing impunity for security forces persists, and activists calling for greater accountability have received little public or media support. The climate of intimidation and ongoing detentions continues to threaten hopes for real change among Egypt’s youth and revolutionary activists.

545021_545021.caption: Some Syrian children have known nothing but war said UN special envoy Staffan de Mistura
545021_545021.article_context: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a major withdrawal of Russian troops from Syria, stating that their six-month intervention had accomplished its goals of stabilizing Bashar al-Assad’s regime and turning the tide against rebel and terrorist groups. The move coincides with the start of Syrian peace talks in Geneva, where Russia’s actions are expected to influence negotiations about Syria’s future, particularly Assad’s role in any political transition. Skepticism remains among Western diplomats over Russia’s intentions, as Moscow will maintain military bases in Syria and has previously been accused of targeting moderate opposition and causing civilian casualties. The announcement has intensified debates on Syria’s political future, with opposition groups hopeful for progress amid ongoing ceasefire and humanitarian efforts.

538328_538328.caption: A survivor of typhoon Haiyan holds a statue of the Virgin Mary he retrieved from his damaged house in Tanauan
538328_538328.article_context: Survivors of Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines, which killed over 3,600 and displaced nearly two million people, are struggling to recover as they shelter in makeshift evacuation centers with minimal resources. Many have lost homes, jobs, and loved ones, and now face an uncertain future while seeking aid, employment, and the means to rebuild their lives. The government has promised reconstruction plans and emergency employment schemes, but many survivors say they need jobs rather than handouts. Mental health support is being provided as the trauma and uncertainty weigh heavily on those affected by the disaster.

199996_199996.caption: Rashad Deihim 21 and Kailyn Bonia 20 were found guilty of assault to rape among other charges
199996_199996.article_context: In Massachusetts, two young adults, Kailyn Bonia and Rashad Deihim, were convicted of sexually assaulting, attempting to rape, and kidnapping a 16-year-old girl who was intoxicated and drug-impaired behind an elementary school in 2014. Cellphone videos of the assault were posted on Snapchat and witnessed by Sydnee Enos, who alerted authorities, leading to the rescue of the victim and arrests. Another teen, Timothy Cyckowski, who filmed and posted the videos online, pleaded guilty and was sentenced to juvenile detention and probation. The case highlighted issues surrounding social media evidence and the difficulty in prosecuting crimes when victims are manipulated by their assailants.

949038_949038.caption: Sonia and Rahul Gandhi s Congress party took just 44 seats in the 543member Indian parliament
949038_949038.article_context: India's Congress party, which suffered a historic defeat in the recent general election and lost power to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), has rejected the resignations of its leaders Sonia and Rahul Gandhi. The BJP, led by Narendra Modi, won a decisive majority, signaling a major shift in India's political landscape. The Congress defeat has been attributed to economic stagnation, rising prices, corruption scandals, and the inability of Rahul Gandhi to connect with voters compared to Modi's aspirational appeal. Despite calls for change, the party has decided to rally behind the Gandhi dynasty, although some analysts believe its influence will continue to wane in the face of modern political dynamics and changing voter attitudes.

55457_55457.caption: Law enforcement officials and relatives identified the gunman in Sunday s mass shooting at an Orlando gay nightclub as Omar Mateen a 29yearold from Fort Pierce Fla
55457_55457.article_context: The Orlando nightclub shooting, carried out by Omar Mateen, is being interpreted not only as the deadliest mass shooting in U.S. history but also within the context of the Islamic State's influence. While Mateen pledged allegiance to ISIS during the attack and the group claimed him as one of their 'soldiers,' officials have found no evidence of a direct operational link between him and the organization. Analysts highlight how ISIS blurs the line between directed and inspired attacks to amplify their perceived power, exploiting America’s mass shooting problem and fueling wider debates on terrorism, hate crimes, and gun control.

389078_389078.caption: FBI Director James Comey said 168 children were freed from child sex trafficking rings in a weeklong nationwide sweep
389078_389078.article_context: The FBI conducted a nationwide anti-trafficking operation, Operation Cross Country, rescuing 168 children from commercial sex trafficking and arresting 281 suspected pimps across 106 cities. The week-long campaign targeted locations such as truck stops, casinos, strip clubs, and websites advertising escort services. This effort involved multiple law enforcement agencies and is part of a broader initiative that has recovered about 3,400 children and secured over 1,450 convictions since its inception in 2003. The operation highlights the prevalence of child sex trafficking in the U.S. and the ongoing commitment of authorities to combat the exploitation and bring perpetrators to justice.

1202143_1202143.caption: Greek prime minister Lucas Papademos has pushed through an agreement on painful austerity measure
1202143_1202143.article_context: Facing imminent economic collapse, Greece's government agreed to harsh new austerity measures in exchange for critical rescue loans from European partners. Prime Minister Lucas Papademos secured reluctant support from coalition leaders after protracted negotiations, despite widespread opposition and concerns over severe cuts to wages, pensions, and public sector jobs. The measures, which include a significant reduction in the minimum wage and thousands of layoffs, are expected to provoke public anger and protests, while deep mistrust persists between Greek politicians and international lenders enforcing strict compliance with the deal.

885807_885807.caption: Amanda Knox in an interview with ABC s Good Morning America said she would never go willingly to face her fate in Italy
885807_885807.article_context: Amanda Knox has vowed to fight her reinstated conviction for the murder of Meredith Kercher after an Italian court sentenced her to 28 and a half years, alongside her former boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito, who received 25 years. Knox stated she would not return to Italy willingly and was emotionally distraught over the verdict, while Kercher’s family said they expect extradition if the conviction becomes final. Legal experts believe extradition is unlikely, and both Knox and Sollecito plan to appeal the ruling, with Italy’s highest court set to review the case next year. The Kercher family expressed ongoing pain and doubt about ever knowing the full truth of the events.

246405_246405.caption: Former Neptune Police Sergeant Philip Seidle is shown in State Superior Court in Freehold Thursday September 29 2016 He pled guilty to the aggravated manslaughter of his wife Tamara WilsonSeidle
246405_246405.article_context: Former Neptune police sergeant Philip Seidle was sentenced to 30 years in prison for shooting and killing his ex-wife, Tamara Wilson-Seidle, in front of their 7-year-old daughter in June 2015. The murder occurred shortly after the couple’s divorce and exposed a lengthy history of domestic violence within their family. Seidle pleaded guilty to aggravated manslaughter and child endangerment, with his actions described by prosecutors as 'pure, unadulterated evil.' The case also highlighted failures in responding to domestic violence incidents, as Wilson-Seidle did not pursue formal complaints against Seidle during their marriage, allowing him to retain access to firearms despite documented abuse. Seidle must serve at least 25.5 years before becoming eligible for parole.

1512836_1512836.caption: Dominic Isom wrapped Samantha Henderson s body in a plastic sheet and a duvet before putting it in a lake
1512836_1512836.article_context: Dominic Isom was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 17 years after being found guilty of murdering his fiancée, Samantha Henderson, in Dorset. Henderson's body was discovered wrapped and weighed down in a lake nine days after her disappearance, following a violent attack at their home. The trial revealed a troubled relationship between the couple and Isom’s attempts to mislead investigators. The case sparked discussions on domestic violence, with Henderson’s friends and family hoping her death will help raise awareness and prevent similar tragedies.

920490_920490.caption: Nisman died one month ago under mysterious circumstances after accusing Fernandez of attempting to cover up Iran s role in a 1994 terrorist attack
920490_920490.article_context: Thousands of Argentinians marched in silence through Buenos Aires and other cities to honor prosecutor Alberto Nisman, whose mysterious death has sparked national controversy. The march, led by Nisman’s family and colleagues, highlighted widespread public demands for answers and government accountability. Nisman died a month earlier after accusing President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner of attempting to cover up Iran’s alleged involvement in the 1994 AMIA Jewish center bombing. His death has intensified political tensions, with Fernández’s supporters claiming suicide and opponents alleging murder and government cover-up. The event underscored deep divisions in Argentina over the unresolved investigation and the handling of the AMIA case.

937882_937882.caption: The Hungarian president Pal Schmitt who has announced his resignation
937882_937882.article_context: Hungarian President Pal Schmitt announced his resignation following a plagiarism scandal in which his 1992 doctoral thesis was found to contain substantial copied material, leading to the revocation of his degree. Schmitt stated that the controversy was causing division in Hungary. Shortly after his announcement, the Fidesz party indicated that parliament would vote to accept his resignation and move quickly to select a new president.

342804_342804.caption: Max Levchin one of the founders of PayPal is speaking out against a new Indiana religious freedom law
342804_342804.article_context: Tech leaders including PayPal co-founder Max Levchin, Apple's Tim Cook, and Salesforce's Marc Benioff have publicly criticized Indiana's new Religious Freedom Restoration Act, which opponents argue could enable discrimination against gays and lesbians. Levchin urged Silicon Valley companies to reconsider business ties with Indiana, while Cook warned against similar bills in other states, such as Arkansas. The controversy has sparked a debate over the balance between religious freedoms and anti-discrimination protections, with business leaders asserting that such laws are harmful to both employees and overall business growth.

1171174_1171174.caption: 1990 Nelson Mandela gestures as he is accompanied by his wife Winnie moments after his release from Victor Verster prison after 27 years in Western Cape
1171174_1171174.article_context: This article traces the life of Nelson Mandela through a series of significant photographs, highlighting his journey from a young student and anti-apartheid activist, to his long imprisonment, and eventual rise as a global icon for peace and equality. Key events include Mandela’s legal activism, his leadership in the African National Congress, his trial and imprisonment for opposing apartheid, his release after 27 years, and his role in ending apartheid and becoming South Africa's first black president. The article also documents Mandela's later years as a celebrated statesman, his advocacy for poverty and HIV/AIDS awareness, until his death in 2013.

59921_59921.caption: A year after landmark Supreme Court case Obergefell says One person can change the world
59921_59921.article_context: Jim Obergefell, the named plaintiff in the landmark Supreme Court case Obergefell v. Hodges, reflected on the historic decision that legalized same-sex marriage across the United States and his role in it. Obergefell described his journey as an 'accidental activist,' motivated by the desire to marry his late husband John Arthur. He expressed both the emotional impact of the court's ruling and the surprising intensity of backlash against the LGBTQ community since the decision, especially targeting transgender individuals. Over the past year, Obergefell has become deeply involved in advocacy and education, speaking out for LGBTQ rights and working with various organizations, while also co-authoring a book about the case and continuing his activism.

1594544_1594544.caption: Mr Assad said his Turkish counterpart Recep Tayyip Erdogan had lost his nerve
1594544_1594544.article_context: Syrian President Bashar al-Assad stated that Russian air strikes in Syria, which began in late September, have significantly weakened the Islamic State (IS) and other militant groups, contrasting them with US-led strikes that he claims were less effective. Assad criticized Turkey for shooting down a Russian warplane, attributing it to Turkey's frustration with the changing dynamics caused by Russian involvement. While Russia claims its primary target is IS, the US maintains that many Russian strikes have targeted moderate opposition forces. US Secretary of State John Kerry expressed willingness to cooperate with Russia if their focus remains on IS, and NATO indicated increased readiness to combat the group.

90101_90101.caption: Clinton addressed supporters at the National Building Museum in Washington DC as her presidential bid drew to a close
90101_90101.article_context: As President Obama seeks congressional approval for military action against Syria following a chemical weapons attack, Hillary Clinton, a potential 2016 presidential candidate and former secretary of state, has publicly supported the president’s efforts. Clinton’s allies argue that her current position differs significantly from her 2002 Senate vote authorizing the Iraq invasion, which harmed her politically in 2008. While some caution that her stance on Syria could have implications if she runs for president, her supporters believe she faces less risk this time. Clinton’s level of public involvement in the Syria debate remains uncertain, but her alignment with Obama could affect public perception of her leadership should she launch another presidential campaign.

221853_221853.caption: Rezaian was among several Americans released by Iran under a prisoner swap agreement Video provided by Newsy
221853_221853.article_context: On the same day Iran’s compliance with a landmark nuclear deal was confirmed and international sanctions were lifted, Iran released five Americans, including Washington Post reporter Jason Rezaian, after nearly 18 months of detention. The release was part of a prisoner swap, with the U.S. agreeing to pardon or commute sentences for seven Iranians held on sanctions-related charges. The events underscored renewed diplomatic channels between the U.S. and Iran, following months of negotiation tied to the nuclear agreement. Iran also committed to continue cooperating in efforts to locate missing American Robert Levinson. The prisoner releases and the lifting of sanctions marked a significant breakthrough in U.S.-Iran relations.

279315_279315.caption: Egyptians opposed to President Mohamed Morsi set fire to the Muslim Brotherhood headquarters in Almoqatam district during clashes in Cairo on June 30 2013
279315_279315.article_context: Egypt’s interim President Adly Mansour reversed an expected appointment of pro-reform leader Mohamed ElBaradei as interim prime minister, amid opposition from the ultraconservative Salafi el-Nour party and ongoing political mediation. The decision comes during a deepening crisis following the military’s ouster of President Mohammed Morsi, with nationwide clashes resulting in at least 36 deaths and hundreds injured. Security was heightened in Cairo as Morsi’s supporters continued mass protests, and violence persisted in Alexandria and the Sinai Peninsula. Mansour, newly appointed by the military, has begun official meetings with top security officials to address the country’s ongoing turmoil.

241059_241059.caption: Katie Holland left is hugged by her mother Holly as they visit a makeshift memorial for bombing victims in Boston
241059_241059.article_context: Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the surviving Boston Marathon bombing suspect, is in serious condition but awake and communicating in writing with investigators at a Boston hospital. Authorities are investigating whether his neck wound was self-inflicted. No charges have been filed yet, and questions remain about possible additional attacks and the extent of the brothers’ radicalization, especially after Russian authorities had previously warned the FBI about Tamerlan Tsarnaev, the older brother who was killed by police. The family maintains their innocence, while scrutiny grows over the FBI’s previous handling of the case. Security remains heightened in Boston, but normalcy is gradually returning to the city, and community support for law enforcement is strong. Surveillance footage reportedly shows Dzhokhar involved in placing a bomb at the marathon, and debates continue over his legal rights during interrogation.

1575870_1575870.caption: Three Britons appeared in an Islamic State recruitment video in June
1575870_1575870.article_context: Following Islamic State's rapid territorial gains in Iraq and Syria, Western nations are increasingly intervening in the region through airstrikes, military advisors, and humanitarian aid, with the United States leading operations and allies including Britain, France, Germany, and Australia providing support. While the main goals are to save refugees, protect Kurdish areas, and support Iraq's government, there are growing concerns about 'mission creep,' the potential for shifting military objectives, civilian and military casualties, and the risk of terrorist 'blowback' in Western countries such as the UK, especially if Western involvement escalates.

307382_307382.caption: Esaw Garner wife of Eric Garner attends a news conference at the National Action Network headquarters in New York on Wednesday Dec 3
307382_307382.article_context: A New York City grand jury declined to indict police officer Daniel Pantaleo in the chokehold death of Eric Garner, a black man accused of selling untaxed cigarettes, sparking nationwide protests and outrage on social media. The incident, widely publicized through video footage showing Garner repeatedly saying 'I can't breathe,' was ruled a homicide by the medical examiner but resulted in no criminal charges against Pantaleo. In response to the grand jury's decision, the U.S. Justice Department announced a federal civil rights investigation. The case has intensified discussions about police conduct, racial justice, and the need for legal and policing reforms, echoing similar unrest following the recent non-indictment of Officer Darren Wilson in the shooting death of Michael Brown in Ferguson, Missouri.

696763_696763.caption: Labour s Douglas Alexander asked How would the government prevent Britishsupplied weapons falling into the wrong hands
696763_696763.article_context: The United States is supporting a British-led effort to persuade the European Union to amend its arms embargo on Syria in order to pressure President Bashar al-Assad into negotiating with the opposition. While some major EU countries back the idea, others remain opposed, and internal disagreements within the UK government complicate the plan. John Kerry pledged increased support for Syrian opposition forces if Assad refuses to negotiate, but concerns persist about weapons falling into extremist hands and the risks of escalating the conflict. The EU embargo is set to expire soon, raising the possibility of unilateral action. Humanitarian groups warn that supplying more arms could worsen the violence, which has already caused tens of thousands of deaths and millions of displaced people since the conflict began in 2011.

148447_148447.caption: Edna Valenzuela seen with her mother Nelly Jimenez Valenzuela was recently diagnosed with nonHodgkin lymphoma The 26yearold au pair from Colombia is being treated at the National Institutes of Health
148447_148447.article_context: Edna Valenzuela, a 26-year-old au pair from Colombia, is battling aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma while caring for a toddler in the United States and receiving free treatment at the National Institutes of Health. Her host family is fighting to extend her stay after AuPairCare, the agency that brought her to the U.S., refused to renew her visa, citing health policies. The family has launched a petition and sought support from Congress to prevent Valenzuela from having to return to Colombia, where she cannot access adequate cancer care. While AuPairCare agreed not to end her program immediately, they have not extended her visa, leaving her future in the U.S. uncertain.

1613863_1613863.caption: Rama Naga At JNU we fight for all people including the Dalits and Muslims
1613863_1613863.article_context: Five students from Delhi's Jawaharlal Nehru University, including Umar Khalid and Anirban Bhattacharya, faced sedition charges after organizing a protest, sparking national debate on nationalism and freedom of expression. Accused of being 'anti-national,' the students denied links to extremist groups and criticized the government's attempts to define and enforce narrow concepts of nationalism. Their case highlighted concerns about political intolerance and the suppression of dissent, with critics viewing the charges as a threat to democratic values and diversity in India.

1022919_1022919.caption: Admiral DK Joshi left briefs Indian politicians last year after an explosion on the INS Sindhurakshak submarine killed everyone on board
1022919_1022919.article_context: India's navy chief Admiral DK Joshi resigned after taking responsibility for a series of accidents, the latest involving smoke flooding a submarine during a training exercise off the Mumbai coast, with two officers still missing. The incident highlights concerns about the ageing fleet, insufficient crew training, and delays in procurement and modernization of submarines. Vice Admiral RK Dhowan will serve as acting navy chief, while investigations into the accident continue and criticism mounts over the leadership's handling of naval safety and modernization.

500396_500396.caption: Former NSW energy minister Chris Hartcher leaves after giving evidence on May 19
500396_500396.article_context: A series of prominent New South Wales Liberal Party politicians have resigned or withdrawn from their positions following investigations by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac). Key figures—including former state premier Barry O'Farrell, former assistant treasurer Arthur Sinodinos, and several other MPs—stepped down due to allegations involving illegal political donations and corrupt conduct. The scandal centered on prohibited campaign donations from property developers and improper financial dealings, leading to significant political fallout and a wave of resignations within the party.

476526_476526.caption: Egidio Coppola s villa in the outskirts of Naples was seized in 2012 by the Italian state following his arrest
476526_476526.article_context: The villa of jailed Camorra mafia boss Egidio Coppola near Naples, once a symbol of organized crime power, is being transformed into a museum dedicated to victims of the mafia. Scheduled to open with an art exhibit from the Uffizi Gallery, the project is seen as a sign of progress in the region's fight against the Camorra. Anti-mafia activists and local mayors express optimism about declining mafia influence, yet experts caution that ties to organized crime persist, notably among some political candidates and local businesses. New community initiatives, such as sustainable farming and symbolic products, aim to further break mafia control, but activists warn that true change requires a deeper shift in business practices and mentality.

1248261_1248261.caption: The Malaysian prime minister Najib Razak received a transfer of 681m into his personal bank account from the Saudi Royal family
1248261_1248261.article_context: Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak was cleared of corruption charges after the attorney general ruled that a $681 million transfer into his personal account was a gift from Saudi Arabia's royal family, with no criminal wrongdoing involved. Despite allegations that the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had recommended Najib be charged, a source close to the PM’s office stated it is constitutionally impossible to overturn the attorney general's decision, and Najib publicly welcomed the clearance. The scandal has damaged public trust and investor confidence but Najib remains strongly supported within his ruling party, and even key critics acknowledge he cannot be removed from office under current legal circumstances.

524130_524130.caption: Cambodia s opposition MP Mu Sochua speaks during a rally in Phnom Penh Cambodia
524130_524130.article_context: Ahead of Cambodia's national elections, opposition MP Mu Sochua has been campaigning for change despite an environment where critics are often persecuted. The Cambodia National Rescue Party (CNRP) was energized by the return of its leader, Sam Rainsy, although he was barred from running due to a decision by the National Election Commission, which the opposition alleges favors Prime Minister Hun Sen's ruling party. The CNRP accuses authorities of widespread voter suppression, with up to 1 million names allegedly deleted from the voter rolls, and fears vote rigging and violence loom over the election. Both the ruling party and opposition warn of potential unrest, and there are calls for the US to suspend aid if Hun Sen wins amid concerns about democracy and human rights.

1665308_1665308.caption: The drugs were seized in Belfast and Comber
1665308_1665308.article_context: Authorities in Northern Ireland have seized prescription drugs worth an estimated £75,000, including large quantities of oxycodone, during operations in south Belfast and Comber. A 31-year-old man from Belfast was arrested for suspected illegal importation from the Indian sub-continent. Health officials raised concerns about the growing misuse of oxycodone, known as 'hillbilly heroin', which is often abused as a heroin alternative due to difficulties in obtaining heroin. The drugs, classified as Class A in the UK, pose serious health risks when used without medical supervision. The seizure highlights ongoing efforts to combat illegal prescription drug activity and public health dangers linked to addiction.

543080_543080.caption: Colin Firth has been lined up to play a journalist following the murder of Meredith Kercher in a film planned by Michael Winterbottom
543080_543080.article_context: Director Michael Winterbottom is planning a fictional film inspired by the 2007 murder of British student Meredith Kercher in Italy, with Colin Firth considered for the role of a journalist covering the case. Winterbottom, known for his interest in journalistic stories, aims to explore the media's intense involvement rather than focus on the guilt or innocence of those convicted, Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito, who are appealing their sentences. As the real-life legal proceedings continue, including a separate slander case against Knox, Winterbottom conducts research in Perugia and surrounding areas, highlighting the ongoing fascination and controversy surrounding the case.

1152242_1152242.caption: British theatre producer David Cecil was arrested for staging a play about a gay man despite a temporary ban by Uganda s media authorities
1152242_1152242.article_context: A Ugandan court dismissed charges against British theatre producer David Cecil, who faced up to two years in jail for staging a play about homosexuality without government approval. The play, The River and the Mountain, sparked controversy in Uganda for its portrayal of homophobia as politically and religiously driven. The case was dropped after prosecutors failed to present evidence or schedule a trial, allowing Cecil to go free, although the case could be reopened. The incident highlights international concern over Uganda’s anti-homosexuality laws and government censorship.

963910_963910.caption: The militia group of the former Afghan prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar is said to have received money from Iran
963910_963910.article_context: Classified US military intelligence reports reveal that Iran is allegedly conducting a covert campaign to support Taliban insurgents, Afghan warlords allied with al-Qaida, and suicide bombers fighting against Western forces in Afghanistan. The reports, based on raw data from informants, detail instances of Iranian provision of arms, training, funding, and safe haven to militants, although it remains unclear if these actions are officially sanctioned by Tehran or orchestrated by hardline elements within the Iranian Revolutionary Guard. US embassy cables express high-level concern about Iran's growing political influence in Afghanistan, including alleged bribery and manipulation of opposition parties. Despite these suspicions, both the Afghan and US governments have agreed to publicly downplay evidence of Iranian involvement to avoid diplomatic friction, as Afghanistan seeks to balance its relations with Iran amid ongoing instability.

1216626_1216626.caption: The British army is sending 91 medics to Sierra Leone to help in the fight against Ebola by operating a treatment centre specifically for healthcare workers
1216626_1216626.article_context: The RAF concluded its largest airlift since the Berlin Airlift, withdrawing the last British combat troops from Camp Bastion in Afghanistan, marking the end of UK combat operations there. Defence Secretary Michael Fallon stated that British troops would not return to Afghanistan under any circumstances. Amid broader debates over military spending and priorities—including commitments to maintain defence spending at 2% of GDP until April 2016—the future of the British Army and its global posture is uncertain, prompting discussions about adapting defence policies to address new security threats beyond traditional military operations.

1027233_1027233.caption: Rick Perry accused Barack Obama of abandoning Israel in favour of the Arab street
1027233_1027233.article_context: The Palestinian bid for statehood at the United Nations intensified political tensions, becoming a focal point in the U.S. presidential race. Republican frontrunner Rick Perry accused President Obama of betraying Israel and supporting terrorists by treating Israeli and Palestinian grievances equally and advocating negotiations based on 1967 borders. While Obama pledged to veto the Palestinian request for UN recognition and criticized the move, Perry and other Republicans claimed his policies enabled the crisis and weakened Israel. Meanwhile, European leaders tried to persuade Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to reconsider the UN move and return to peace talks. The situation also heightened tensions on the ground, with hardline Israeli settlers staging protests and reports of increased violence ahead of the UN decision.

1583460_1583460.caption: Three London schoolgirls are believed to be among those who have travelled to Syria
1583460_1583460.article_context: Hundreds of UK nationals have traveled to fight for jihadist groups, mainly Islamic State, in Syria and Iraq, raising concerns about existing government anti-radicalisation schemes, which are seen as ineffective. Nazir Afzal, a former chief prosecutor, highlights that community-based initiatives led by Muslim women are proving more successful in countering radicalisation by supporting vulnerable youths, providing alternatives, and fostering resilience within families. These women-led groups operate with limited resources and often face community resistance, but their grassroots efforts are opening communication and preventing extremism more effectively than top-down government programs.

1480791_1480791.caption: Allan Smith had been suspended by Dorset Police since being charged in September
1480791_1480791.article_context: PC Allan Smith, a former Dorset police officer, was sentenced to nine months in prison for harassing a former partner with tens of thousands of threatening messages and calls, as well as disclosing police information and misusing the police computer for personal reasons. Smith was dismissed from the force for gross misconduct and has been given an indefinite restraining order against his victim. Dorset Police condemned his actions, emphasizing the importance of integrity within the police service.

1599144_1599144.caption: The news left Mr Goto s mother Junko Ishido distraught
1599144_1599144.article_context: Japan has strongly condemned the apparent beheading of journalist Kenji Goto by an Islamic State militant, with Prime Minister Shinzo Abe vowing not to give in to terrorism and pledging continued support to countries fighting IS. The killing, which follows the earlier execution of another Japanese hostage, Haruna Yukawa, was met with international outrage and statements of solidarity from the US, UK, France, and Australia. Goto had traveled to Syria in an effort to help secure Yukawa’s release. Negotiations involving Japan and Jordan for Goto and a captive Jordanian pilot broke down, with IS demanding a prisoner exchange and ransom. Japanese officials said they never made direct contact with IS, and the fate of the Jordanian pilot remains uncertain.

891066_891066.caption: The prosecutor of the international criminal court Luis MorenoOcampo has warned that Gaddafi may be guilty of crimes against humanity
891066_891066.article_context: President Barack Obama strongly condemned Muammar Gaddafi's violent crackdown against Libyan protesters, calling for Gaddafi to step down, as the International Criminal Court announced investigations into possible crimes against humanity by Gaddafi and his sons. The debate over imposing a no-fly zone over Libya led to disagreements between the US, UK, and other European allies, with Britain and France supporting the measure, while US Defense Secretary Robert Gates and Germany showed reluctance, emphasizing the need for UN approval. European leaders discussed coordination on humanitarian aid and considered military options, as internal divisions became apparent within the UK cabinet over how to respond to the crisis.

1530075_1530075.caption: Saera Wilson said her fiance Mathew James was shot in the shoulder chest and hip in the terror attack
1530075_1530075.article_context: During a terrorist attack on a beach in Sousse, Tunisia, at least 38 people were killed, with Islamic State extremists claiming responsibility. Among the victims was Mathew James, a Welsh tourist, who was shot three times while shielding his fiancée. Several other Welsh and British tourists were caught up in the chaos, with many evacuated back to the UK. The UK government responded urgently, and travel companies cancelled holidays and organized repatriation flights. The incident has sparked widespread fear, grief, and support efforts for those affected.

43283_43283.caption: Antigovernment protesters watch as an elderly man performs the traditional Baraa dance during a rally to demand the ouster of Yemen s President Ali Abdullah Saleh in Sanaa
43283_43283.article_context: Yemeni leader Ali Abdullah Saleh announced his intention to go into exile in Ethiopia after stepping down from power, though he aims to maintain influence through his allies in Yemen. His departure follows a year of unrest, starting with anti-government protests inspired by the Arab Spring. The political crisis saw resignations from his ruling party, deadly attacks on protesters, a temporary transfer of power after Saleh was wounded, and eventually his signing of an agreement to relinquish authority to Vice President Abed Rabbo Mansour Hadi, who was later sworn in as president, ending Saleh’s 33-year rule.

539305_539305.caption: New Zealand prime minister John Key claiming victory in 2011
539305_539305.article_context: Ahead of New Zealand's September election, the ruling National Party led by John Key has been thrown into turmoil following the release of investigative journalist Nicky Hager’s book, 'Dirty Politics.' The book, based on hacked emails and messages, alleges close ties between National Party officials and rightwing blogger Cameron Slater, exposing a campaign of smear tactics, leak-based attacks, and political manipulation. The scandal has dominated media, raised questions about Prime Minister Key's judgment and involvement, and prompted an official inquiry, although the National Party's poll support remains mostly intact. The controversy has upended the campaign narrative and could impact the election outcome, especially with more revelations promised by other political actors.

1240443_1240443.caption: Nestora Salgado La Comandata organizes locals to rise up against organized crime in Olinala in the state of Guerrero
1240443_1240443.article_context: Nestora Salgado, a former US immigrant and community leader from Guerrero, Mexico, led an armed uprising against drug cartels and corrupt officials in her hometown after years of escalating violence. Although her militia’s efforts briefly restored local security, she was later arrested and accused of kidnapping after detaining individuals linked to organized crime. Salgado spent 21 months in a high-security prison, enduring poor conditions before a hunger strike drew international attention to her case and secured her transfer to a medical facility. Her supporters argue she is being targeted for exposing state failures, while Salgado remains unrepentant, insisting her actions were necessary to defend her community.

1684843_1684843.caption: Labour leader Ed Miliband said he would not be lectured by Stefano Pessina
1684843_1684843.article_context: A public dispute erupted between Labour Party leader Ed Miliband and Stefano Pessina, the billionaire chief executive of Boots, after Pessina criticized Labour's proposed tax policies as harmful to business growth. Labour responded by highlighting Pessina’s status as a tax exile in Monaco and accused him of siding with the Conservative government and tax avoiders. The exchange has fueled a wider debate about the influence of business leaders in politics and whether their interventions affect voters’ decisions. Boots' parent company has since clarified that Pessina’s comments reflected his personal views, not the company's political stance.

246364_246364.caption: The June 3 1944 photo provided by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum shows Heinrich Himmler center as he reviews troops of the Galician SSVolunteer Infantry Division
246364_246364.article_context: Michael Karkoc, a 94-year-old resident of Minnesota, was identified by the Associated Press as a former commander of a Nazi SS-led unit accused of burning villages and massacring civilians during World War II. Karkoc reportedly lied about his military service to enter the United States in 1949, concealing his leadership roles in the SS-backed Ukrainian Self Defense Legion and the SS Galician Division—groups linked to war crimes and blacklisted by U.S. authorities at the time. Although there is no direct evidence of Karkoc personally committing atrocities, records and testimony indicate he led units that perpetrated mass killings. The discovery of his past has led German authorities to consider prosecution, as command responsibility can be grounds for war crimes charges. U.S. officials have previously deported individuals for similar deceptions on immigration forms, and Nazi hunters argue there is sufficient evidence for legal action against Karkoc.

940291_940291.caption: An emotional Jacky Greenwood is comforted by Jason Amos outside her 83yearold mother Irene Comstive s home in the suburb of Rosalie Brisbane
940291_940291.article_context: Residents and volunteers in Brisbane and nearby suburbs are undertaking extensive clean-up efforts following severe flooding. People are seen mopping homes, clearing debris, and removing mud from flood-damaged properties while emotional scenes unfold among those affected. As floodwaters recede, the community works together to restore homes, businesses, and streets, highlighting the widespread impact and resilience following the disaster.

913599_913599.caption: Macedonia s PM Nikola Gruevski said We are ready to discuss to open dialogue with them and to find some solution
913599_913599.article_context: Macedonian Prime Minister Nikola Gruevski expressed willingness to discuss changing his country's name in an effort to resolve a decades-long dispute with Greece over the use of 'Macedonia.' The disagreement, which began after Macedonia's independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, has led Greece to block Macedonia's accession to NATO and the EU and prompted the UN to use the provisional term 'Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.' Gruevski stated that any name-change agreement would be subject to a national referendum. Recent diplomatic gestures and optimism from officials on both sides suggest that conditions are improving for a possible resolution to the dispute.

170899_170899.caption: Demonstrators protest at the site where Michael Brown was killed on Canfield Drive in Ferguson
170899_170899.article_context: The Justice Department has ordered a third, independent autopsy in the investigation of Michael Brown’s death, following his fatal shooting by a police officer in Ferguson, Missouri. The announcement came amid escalating unrest, with violent clashes between protesters and police, gunfire, tear gas, and looting reported in Ferguson. Missouri’s governor declared a state of emergency and imposed a curfew in an effort to restore order. Michael Brown’s family and advocates, including Rev. Al Sharpton, called for a federal takeover of the case, criticizing local authorities’ handling of the investigation and the release of a video allegedly showing Brown committing a robbery. FBI agents are conducting interviews as part of an increasingly intensive federal civil rights probe running alongside the state investigation, while President Obama has been briefed on the situation.

589905_589905.caption: David Cameron has limited himself to calling for an immediate ceasefire while taking care to blame Hamas for sparking the crisis
589905_589905.article_context: British political leaders are divided over how to respond to Israel's military actions in Gaza, with Labour and Liberal Democrat leaders openly criticizing the disproportionate use of force and civilian casualties, while Conservative Prime Minister David Cameron and his ministers have avoided directly rebuking Israel, instead calling for a ceasefire and blaming Hamas for the crisis. Pressure is mounting within Cameron's own party from some senior figures to condemn Israel, but the memory of backlash against past criticism has made many Conservative MPs reluctant to speak out. Meanwhile, the US has strongly condemned an Israeli attack on a UN school, marking a rare moment of outspoken criticism from America.

77237_77237.caption: Aid packages for displaced Iraqi Christians fleeing violence await to be distributed inside St Joseph s church in Ainkawa a Christian suburb of the Iraqi city of Erbil
77237_77237.article_context: The debate over admitting Syrian refugees to the United States intensified following the Paris attacks, with some governors and GOP presidential candidates demanding exclusion of Muslim refugees, while President Obama condemned any religious test for entry. Despite Christians being a small minority among Syrian refugees resettled in the US, advocates argue that Christians and other minorities face unique persecution and should receive special consideration. The State Department is considering designating ISIS’s atrocities against Yazidis as genocide, prompting claims of bias from Christian advocates who believe Christians are also severely persecuted. The controversy highlights broader divisions in American attitudes towards religious minorities and the complex factors involved in refugee resettlement policy.

135657_135657.caption: David Davis the newly appointed secretary of state for exiting the European Union
135657_135657.article_context: Following Britain's vote to leave the European Union, Theresa May succeeded David Cameron as prime minister and made significant cabinet changes, including appointing David Davis as the secretary of state for exiting the EU. Davis, a longstanding Conservative Party member and Brexit supporter, will lead the newly formed Department for Exiting the EU and oversee negotiations for Britain's withdrawal. His appointment reflects May's commitment to carrying out Brexit and a desire to represent voices from diverse backgrounds. Davis, along with Boris Johnson as foreign minister and Liam Fox as international trade secretary, will play key roles in shaping the UK’s post-EU future, with Davis predicting a formal exit around December 2018.

1263346_1263346.caption: Asunta s adopted father Alfonso Basterra was also arrested
1263346_1263346.article_context: In September 2013, the adopted 12-year-old Chinese girl Asunta Fong Yang was found dead near Santiago de Compostela, Spain, triggering a high-profile investigation. Her adoptive parents, Rosario Porto and Alfonso Basterra, both once respected members of their community, became suspects after inconsistencies in their accounts and evidence emerged, including CCTV footage and toxicology reports showing Asunta had been repeatedly drugged over several months. Both parents were arrested and, despite a lack of direct physical evidence, were eventually convicted of murdering their daughter and sentenced to 18 years in prison. The case shocked Spain, led to scrutiny of adoption procedures and psychological screening, and raised enduring questions about motive, neglect, and the failures of social systems to recognize warning signs.

806879_806879.caption: Geoff Huegill and wife Sara Hills will appear in court
806879_806879.article_context: Olympic swimmer Geoff Huegill and his wife, Sara Hills, were allegedly found in possession of cocaine at Randwick racecourse in Sydney. NSW police apprehended the couple after being alerted by security and discovered a small quantity of suspected cocaine. Both are scheduled to appear in Waverley local court on 14 May.

416539_416539.caption: President Barack Obama announces a new set of tax reform rules Friday aimed at tracking down individuals who set up shell companies to avoid paying taxes in the United States
416539_416539.article_context: The anonymous source who leaked the Panama Papers—11.5 million documents exposing how wealthy individuals use offshore accounts to hide assets—has publicly defended their actions, calling for better protections for whistleblowers and stronger government responses to financial secrecy. Writing in Germany’s Süddeutsche Zeitung, the leaker criticized the U.S. and other countries for their insufficient legal reforms and transparency, as well as the poor treatment of whistleblowers like Edward Snowden. The source also highlighted flaws in corporate disclosure laws and lack of meaningful investigations or prosecutions following the leak. In response, the U.S. Treasury announced new rules requiring financial institutions to collect beneficiary information and proposed legislation for company ownership reporting, aiming to address the issues revealed by the Panama Papers.

1096756_1096756.caption: In a photograph from February 2002 Kurt Sonnenfeld is led in handcuffs to a court to face a firstdegree murder charge in the death of his wife Nancy
1096756_1096756.article_context: Argentina’s supreme court has ruled that American Kurt Sonnenfeld can be extradited to the US to face charges of murdering his wife, ending a years-long dispute between the US and Argentina that hinged on concerns about the death penalty. US authorities assured Argentina that Sonnenfeld would not face execution if convicted. Sonnenfeld fled to Argentina in 2003 after being charged in Denver, and has since claimed he was framed due to his possession of video footage related to the September 11 attacks. The date of his extradition is yet to be determined.

1548714_1548714.caption: Brockwell had absconded from a life sentence in the UK for a series of armed robberies
1548714_1548714.article_context: Derek Brockwell, a Scottish prisoner serving a seven-year sentence in Ireland for armed robbery, escaped custody after attacking two prison officers during a hospital visit in Dublin. Brockwell fled on a motorbike with an accomplice and authorities suspect he may be heading to Britain via Northern Ireland. Police across Ireland, Northern Ireland, and Britain are coordinating a search, and the public has been warned not to approach him. Ireland’s Justice Minister has requested a report on the escape and stressed the importance of recapturing Brockwell promptly.

964184_964184.caption: South Korean Kim Sungyoon right is reunited with her North Korean sister
964184_964184.article_context: Dozens of elderly North and South Koreans who were separated for decades by the Korean War took part in rare family reunions at North Korea’s Kumgang Mountain resort. These emotionally charged meetings, the first in over three years, came amid a period of reduced tensions between the two countries. The reunions, arranged after North Korea sought improved ties with the South, are tightly controlled and brief, with most participants unlikely to see each other again due to age and ongoing political divisions. The events highlight both the human impact of the continued separation on the Korean peninsula and the fragility of inter-Korean relations.

1595082_1595082.caption: Democrat Party leader Abhisit Vejjajiva has urged the National Reform Council to reject the constitution
1595082_1595082.article_context: Thailand's National Reform Council, appointed by the military government after last year's coup, voted to reject a new draft constitution intended to replace the one annulled by the coup. The draft was controversial for proposing a powerful National Strategic Reform and Reconciliation Committee, largely comprising military leaders, which would have been authorized to take control during crises, effectively allowing a legal coup. The constitution also weakened political parties, allowed a non-MP to become prime minister, and strengthened the appointed Senate's powers. Most politicians and parties opposed the draft, seeing it as a step back from democracy and an attempt to entrench military and elite control. Its rejection prolongs military rule and uncertainty, as a new version will be drafted and the military may remain in power until at least mid-2017.

664118_664118.caption: Guatemala s president Otto Perez Molina believes a new approach to Latin America s war on drugs is urgently needed
664118_664118.article_context: At the Summit of the Americas in Cartagena, Latin American leaders, including Guatemalan President Otto Pérez Molina, will openly acknowledge that the war on drugs has failed and call for alternative policies to prohibition. Leaders are urging a shift toward regulated drug policies, arguing that legalization under strict controls could be more effective than current approaches. The summit marks the first high-level discussion on the issue in decades and signals a growing regional consensus for reform. US President Barack Obama will attend, facing pressure as the US maintains its prohibitionist stance, though there are signs of openness to debate within his administration. The event is seen as a pivotal moment in rethinking global drug policy.

75325_75325.caption: FBI interviews Clinton in email probe
75325_75325.article_context: FBI agents interviewed Hillary Clinton for over three hours regarding her use of a private email account as secretary of state, signaling that the investigation is nearing its end. Clinton voluntarily participated and maintained she did not send or receive information marked classified. The investigation centers on whether her email practices mishandled classified material. Recent events, including a controversial meeting between Bill Clinton and Attorney General Loretta Lynch, have raised concerns about the probe's independence. Lynch later stated she would accept recommendations from career prosecutors and FBI agents in the case. Despite criticisms and an inspector general report highlighting failures in Clinton's email arrangements, formal charges remain unlikely unless evidence emerges that she intentionally mishandled classified information.

686981_686981.caption: Pakistan s president Asif Ali Zardari There are no shortterm answers and it is very difficult to make the American taxpayer understand
686981_686981.article_context: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari warned that the ongoing war in Afghanistan is destabilizing Pakistan and hindering its efforts to rebuild democratic institutions and economic stability after years of military rule. He criticized the slow pace of ending the Afghan conflict and pointed to misunderstandings among US politicians regarding the effects of American policies on Pakistan. Zardari highlighted the economic and human costs of the 'war on terror', stressed the urgent need for a diplomatic solution in Afghanistan, and urged for greater cooperation from the US, including sharing drone technology. He emphasized that peace efforts in Afghanistan must be Afghan-led, with Pakistan willing to contribute as long as its national interests are respected.

369442_369442.caption: Dallas Mayor Mike Rawlings holds the hand of a person paying her respects at the makeshift memorial of police cars
369442_369442.article_context: Following the fatal shooting of five police officers during a protest in Dallas, President Obama decided to cut short his Europe trip and return to Washington. He plans to visit Dallas to address the issues of racial tensions and policing highlighted by recent events, including the police killings of black men in Louisiana and Minnesota. Obama condemned the attack on law enforcement as senseless, called for national unity, and emphasized the need to address racial disparities and strengthen gun control measures. The White House expressed the challenge of balancing multiple priorities, as Obama prepared to shift his focus from diplomatic meetings in Europe to tackling domestic unrest and mourning with affected communities.

189838_189838.caption: Palestinian men who call themselves Mourabitoun shout slogans during a protest against their ban from the alAqsa mosque compound in Jerusalem s Old City
189838_189838.article_context: Israel has banned the Muslim civilian guard group, Mourabitoun, from the al-Aqsa mosque compound in Jerusalem, citing their role in provoking violent clashes with Israeli security forces and Jewish visitors. The decision comes ahead of the Jewish High Holy Days, when tensions typically rise due to increased religious activity at the site. While Israeli authorities claim the Mourabitoun incite trouble, Muslim leaders argue the group's actions are peaceful efforts to protect the sacred area. The move has sparked controversy and concern over keeping the peace at one of Jerusalem's most sensitive religious sites.

1500324_1500324.caption: Supporters of former Prime Minister Ali Benflis have been campaigning in the Sahara desert
1500324_1500324.article_context: Algerian President Abdelaziz Bouteflika, who has rarely appeared in public since suffering a stroke in 2013, is seeking a fourth term in upcoming elections amid controversy over his health and leadership. Despite protests, opposition boycotts, and withdrawal of several candidates who claim the election is predetermined, Bouteflika remains the favorite to win due to his established political influence and support for ending the 1990s civil war. Critics argue that state resources unfairly benefit Bouteflika and allege power is held by unaccountable networks, while supporters insist he is best suited to lead the country during regional uncertainty.

504738_504738.caption: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu right was forced to yield to the lastminute demands of Jewish Home chairman Naftali Bennett left in order to get the required majority of seats
504738_504738.article_context: Israeli prime minister Binyamin Netanyahu narrowly secured the formation of a rightwing coalition government just before the deadline, preventing his possible removal from office. The new coalition, made up of Likud, United Torah Judaism, Shas, Kulanu, and the Jewish Home parties, holds only a slim majority in the Knesset with 61 out of 120 seats. The government is dominated by hard-line and religious factions and faces criticism for its instability and potential conflict with allies such as the US. Key cabinet positions, including the justice ministry going to Jewish Home's Ayelet Shaked, were agreed upon after tense last-minute negotiations. However, the coalition's fragility and narrow majority have led to predictions that it will struggle to govern effectively and may not survive for long.

269947_269947.caption: Rev C T Vivian arrives for the events at the Edmund Pettus Bridge
269947_269947.article_context: President Obama, joined by his family and civil rights leaders including Rep. John Lewis, commemorated the 50th anniversary of the Bloody Sunday march in Selma, Alabama by walking across the Edmund Pettus Bridge and delivering a speech that honored the marchers’ role in advancing civil rights and the passage of the Voting Rights Act. Obama drew connections between Selma’s historic struggle for racial equality and ongoing issues in modern America, emphasizing continued progress and the need to protect voting rights amid recent setbacks. Thousands attended the event, and Obama signed legislation awarding the Congressional Gold Medal to participants in the original Selma demonstrations. The commemoration also highlighted lingering economic and racial challenges, while attendees and officials called for renewed efforts to strengthen civil rights protections.

772879_772879.caption: A barefoot Colton HarrisMoore is escorted by police to Nassau Bahamas yesterday
772879_772879.article_context: Colton Harris-Moore, known as the 'Barefoot Bandit,' was captured in the Bahamas after evading authorities for over two years across multiple U.S. states and Canada. Suspected of numerous burglaries and stealing planes and boats, Harris-Moore became a celebrated outlaw figure online, while victims from his hometown expressed relief at his arrest. Following a dramatic chase, he was apprehended by Bahamian police and now faces extradition and prosecution in several American states. His story, marked by his troubled background and daring escapades, is likely to inspire books and a movie.

1594652_1594652.caption: Ashley Young is currently injured after hurting his shoulder in a match against Tottenham in January
1594652_1594652.article_context: Manchester United footballer Ashley Young faces a possible driving ban after admitting to speeding at 71mph in a 50mph zone on the M6 toll in Warwickshire. Young, who already has nine points on his licence from previous offences, did not appear in court and will be sentenced later. His lawyer explained Young's absence due to football commitments and confirmed he can pay any financial penalties.

88720_88720.caption: Rep Paul Gosar to EPA chief You should be impeached
88720_88720.article_context: During a tense congressional hearing, Michigan Governor Rick Snyder and EPA Administrator Gina McCarthy faced sharp accusations over the handling of the Flint water crisis. Democrats blamed Snyder for appointing emergency managers who switched Flint’s water source and ignored warnings, while Republicans criticized the EPA’s slow response and alleged negligence. Both officials defended their actions, with Snyder acknowledging state failures and McCarthy insisting the EPA was misled by Michigan officials. The hearing highlighted deep partisan divides and left unresolved the question of who is ultimately responsible for the crisis.

1603081_1603081.caption: Amnesty says this photo was taken by an asylumseeker in the May incident on the boat carrying passengers to Australia prior to interception by Australian officials
1603081_1603081.article_context: Amnesty International has released a report alleging that Australian officials paid people smugglers to turn back asylum seekers' boats and threatened the migrants' safety during two incidents in May and July. The organization claims officials handed money to crews and forced passengers into unsafe vessels, some of which sank, and that asylum seekers were threatened with violence. The Australian government denies these accusations and defends its border protection policies, which include intercepting and returning migrant boats and detaining asylum seekers offshore. Amnesty is calling for a Royal Commission to investigate Operation Sovereign Borders, Australia's controversial military-led initiative to prevent asylum seekers from reaching its territory by sea.

1558567_1558567.caption: Papers say Mr Modi needs to do more to fully revive India s economy
1558567_1558567.article_context: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's first six months in office have been marked by key initiatives such as banking reforms, the Clean India campaign, and increased attention to foreign policy through visits to major countries. While economic indicators like inflation have improved and industrial output has risen, analysts highlight that significant challenges remain, including the need for bold economic reforms and job creation for millions of unemployed youth. Modi's preference for strong bilateral relationships over multilateral forums has been noted, but his policies towards neighboring China and Pakistan still face tests. Despite mixed results, Modi has successfully maintained the optimism of his supporters. Separately, an ATM machine was stolen in Delhi, raising concerns over security.

582927_582927.caption: There is scepticism in London that Putin s initiative is genuine rather than an effort to buy time and strengthen the Syrian army
582927_582927.article_context: Russian President Vladimir Putin has taken personal charge of efforts to implement a Syrian ceasefire, conducting intensive diplomatic outreach with regional leaders and ordering a reduction in Russian airstrikes. The ceasefire, brokered by Russia and the US, excludes groups like Islamic State and al-Nusra Front, and faces skepticism from Syrian opposition parties and Western governments regarding its credibility and Russia's motivations. While some armed factions have agreed to the truce, doubts remain over whether all opposition groups will comply. The UN successfully completed an air drop of aid to Deir ez-Zor, but humanitarian access remains limited due to ongoing government restrictions. Overall, there is cautious optimism but significant uncertainty about whether the ceasefire will lead to lasting peace in Syria.

1665495_1665495.caption: There are tensions between Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and army chief Raheel Sharif
1665495_1665495.article_context: Following the 2014 Peshawar school attack, Pakistan's army has gained increasing political influence by leading a major crackdown on militants under the National Action Plan. Military courts were established and tens of thousands of suspects detained, reducing militant violence and boosting the army's popularity. However, the crackdown has been selective, sparing groups targeting India and Afghanistan, while controversial figures remain untouched. Critics argue that civilian politicians have been sidelined from key decisions, and a cult of personality has grown around Army Chief General Raheel Sharif. The partnership between government and army is tense and driven by civilian fears of another coup, raising concerns about lasting change and the balance of power in Pakistan.

176048_176048.caption: Michelle Obama and Laura Bush share the stage to talk support for veterans
176048_176048.article_context: In the midst of a contentious 2016 election year, former First Lady Laura Bush notably appeared alongside current First Lady Michelle Obama at an event promoting support for military families, highlighting their ongoing bipartisan partnership and friendship. While the Bush family has remained publicly neutral and refrained from endorsing Donald Trump after Jeb Bush withdrew from the race, Laura Bush’s collaboration with Michelle Obama at several public events demonstrates a focus on unity and shared causes beyond party politics. Their visible camaraderie and advocacy work underscore a rare moment of bipartisanship during a divisive campaign season, implicitly contrasting their approach with the prevailing political discord.

471223_471223.caption: The US government argued that Manning aided alQaida when he released documents to WikiLeaks
471223_471223.article_context: Bradley Manning, the army private who admitted to leaking a vast amount of US state secrets to WikiLeaks, awaits a verdict from a military judge that could result in a life sentence without parole if found guilty of 'aiding the enemy.' The high-profile trial highlighted the government's efforts to set a precedent by arguing that Manning knowingly assisted al-Qaida, and has raised concerns over the future of investigative journalism and the treatment of whistleblowers. The trial concluded with sharply opposing characterizations of Manning, either as a traitor or as a well-intentioned whistleblower, and its outcome is expected to have significant implications for US policy on leaking classified information.

260232_260232.caption: Protesters jam the street near the convenience store where Alton Sterling was shot and killed in Baton Rouge La
260232_260232.article_context: The article highlights the grief and public responses of mothers whose children died in high-profile incidents involving law enforcement, including the cases of Alton Sterling, Walter Scott, Freddie Gray, Sandra Bland, Michael Brown, Eric Garner, Tamir Rice, and Trayvon Martin. These mothers have spoken out about their losses, the lack of justice or accountability, and the personal and national pain caused by these deaths. Many trials ended without indictments or convictions for the officers involved, intensifying the families’ calls for justice and sparking broader discussions about police violence and systemic racism in America.

653592_653592.caption: Liberian president Ellen Johnson Sirleaf announced that schools would reopen on 2 February
653592_653592.article_context: Liberia is nearing victory over Ebola, with infection rates dropping to just over four cases per day and plans to reopen schools next month. The US is preparing to withdraw half its troops as the situation improves, although medical authorities caution against complacency due to sporadic outbreaks. While Liberia has effectively contained the virus, neighboring Sierra Leone continues to face intense transmission, reporting far higher case numbers. International agencies stress that the fight is not over until all cases are eliminated across the region.

1108989_1108989.caption: A young boy leads fighters from alShabab which means the youth in Arabic on military exercise in Suqaholaha neighborhood in northern Mogadishu Somalia
1108989_1108989.article_context: Ugandan police suspect that the Somali militant group al-Shabab was responsible for the double bombing in Kampala, marking an escalation in the group’s activities beyond Somalia. Al-Shabab, originally a local armed wing of the now-defunct Union of Islamic Courts, has radicalized and expanded, pledging allegiance to al-Qaida and attracting foreign recruits. The attack is believed to be retaliation against Uganda for providing the bulk of African Union peacekeepers supporting Somalia’s government. Al-Shabab’s targeting of World Cup viewers reflects both their opposition to such events and their desire to strike soft targets, as well as the group’s increasingly extreme and international focus, despite internal divisions and growing opposition from moderate members.

777402_777402.caption: Markus R a former employee of the German intelligence agency BND waits ahead of his trial for espionage in a courtroom in Munich
777402_777402.article_context: A former employee of Germany's BND, identified as Markus R, admitted in court to passing over 300 classified documents to the CIA and three to the Russian consulate in Munich. He stated that lax security measures at the agency made him feel he was not at risk, and expressed regret for his actions, claiming he sought excitement rather than financial gain. Markus R reportedly received at least 95,000 euros for information on BND operations, personnel, and collaborations, using clandestine methods to deliver updates. His arrest strained relations between Germany and the US, amid broader concerns over American surveillance and espionage. Prosecutors charged him with treason, official secrets violations, and corruption; if convicted, he faces a potential life sentence.

893416_893416.caption: Iran s presidentelect Hassan Rouhani attends his first press conference after being elected in June
893416_893416.article_context: Iran’s president-elect Hassan Rouhani, two weeks after his election win, voiced progressive views on civil liberties, freedom of expression, and internet access, criticizing censorship and internet filtering as ineffective and politically motivated. He opposed the segregation of sexes, called for minimizing cultural and artistic censorship, and spoke against harsh enforcement of hijab and restrictions on women. Rouhani emphasized the need to respect citizens’ rights and supported more openness in media coverage, suggesting that the country's legitimacy depends on the people’s vote and free access to information. Since his victory, there has been a reported easing of internet restrictions, reflecting a shift toward moderation after Mahmoud Ahmadinejad’s presidency.

94385_94385.caption: Hong Young is accused of firing at several public places in Maryland including a building at the National Security Agency
94385_94385.article_context: Hong Young, a 35-year-old former prison guard, has been linked by authorities to at least eight shooting incidents across Maryland, including attacks on buildings at the NSA and the Intercounty Connector, as well as local restaurants. Young was apprehended last week, and police found a cache of legally-owned firearms and ammunition at his home. No serious injuries were reported in the shootings, and Young claimed to have acted under the influence of voices. Law enforcement is coordinating efforts across multiple jurisdictions to file additional charges.

849613_849613.caption: Tara Gilbert and her children Jodie and Kelsey who died in a fire at a Travellers site at Carrickmines near Dublin
849613_849613.article_context: A minute’s silence will be held at Ireland’s Euro 2016 qualifying match in Warsaw to honor the ten victims of a tragic fire at a Travellers site near Dublin. The disaster, the greatest loss of life ever suffered by the Irish Travelling community, claimed members of two families, including a six-month-old infant and a pregnant woman. In response, Prime Minister Enda Kenny ordered flags on official buildings to be flown at half-mast during the victims’ funerals, and communities across Ireland have opened books of condolence and held prayers for those affected.

515070_515070.caption: Lloyd Cele a pastor and graphic designer from Durban will find out tomorrow whether he has beaten fellow finalist Elvis Blue to this year s Idols title
515070_515070.article_context: South Africa's Idols TV show is set for a significant final between Lloyd Cele, a black pastor, and Elvis Blue, a white music teacher, sparking debate about race and voting patterns in post-apartheid South Africa. Despite black people representing the majority of the population, white viewers dominate the audience and voting due to socio-economic factors and access to pay-TV.
