The experience has tempered public expectations, and many believe outside help will still be needed for Croatia to fully benefit from EU membership.

1170845_1170845.caption: Former Blackwater security guard Evan Liberty After years of delays four former guards are facing trial in the killings of 14 Iraqi civilians
1170845_1170845.article_context: At the trial of four ex-Blackwater security guards accused of killing 14 Iraqi civilians in Baghdad in 2007, defense lawyers raised doubts about the reliability of prosecution witnesses, suggesting their testimonies may have been influenced by Iraqi investigators. The main witness, whose son was killed in the incident, denied that the Blackwater convoy was under attack, contradicting the defense’s self-defense argument. The case has attracted global attention due to the scale of the violence and is expected to feature many foreign witnesses. The defense argued there was evidence of incoming gunfire but prosecution witnesses and Iraqi officials rejected claims that the Blackwater guards were fired upon by Iraqi police.

933445_933445.caption: Shezanne Cassim and seven codefendants sentenced to jail after being convicted in connection to a satirical video
933445_933445.article_context: Shezanne Cassim, an American consultant living in the UAE, has been sentenced to one year in a maximum security prison after a satirical YouTube video he made was deemed a threat to national security under strict new UAE cybercrime laws. The video mocked wealthy Emirati youth imitating gangster behavior, but included a disclaimer of its fictional nature. Cassim had already spent nine months in custody awaiting trial, and his supporters argue the video was lighthearted and not intended to offend. Efforts are underway by family, lawyers, US politicians, and human rights campaigners to secure his release, but Cassim cannot appeal under UAE law.

1553856_1553856.caption: Mr Hammond also accused Russia over its air attacks in Syria
1553856_1553856.article_context: Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond stated that Britain needs a strong deal to remain in the EU, as Prime Minister David Cameron seeks reforms ahead of a possible referendum by 2017. Key areas of negotiation include limiting welfare access for EU migrants, with Hammond highlighting progress but noting unresolved details. Hammond also commented on Syria, accusing Russia of indiscriminate bombing and emphasizing Russia's pivotal role in ending the conflict. Discussions in Munich failed to produce a breakthrough, with both sides in Syria determined to continue fighting.

1228823_1228823.caption: Pilot Didier Esteyne celebrates after landing the EFan electrically powered plane following his successful crossing of The Channel from Lydd Airport in Kent
1228823_1228823.article_context: French pilot Hugues Duval completed what he claims is the first electric plane flight across the English Channel, flying from Calais to England and back in his single-seat Crici aircraft. However, Airbus contested his achievement, arguing that Duval launched from another aircraft and that it should not be recognized as an official record. Within hours, Airbus pilot Didier Esteyne successfully flew the battery-powered E-Fan from Kent, UK, to Calais, France, marking a significant milestone in electric aviation. Airbus hopes this accomplishment will advance the development of larger, low-emission electric planes. Both flights highlight progress toward clean and sustainable air travel.

1592948_1592948.caption: Ms Buckley s body was found in a barrel at this storage unit on High Craigton Farm
1592948_1592948.article_context: Alexander Pacteau admitted to murdering Irish student Karen Buckley after meeting her outside a Glasgow nightclub in April. He attacked her in his car, killed her by strangulation and repeated blows with a spanner, and later concealed her body in a barrel on a farm. After attempting to cover up his crime, Pacteau was arrested following a large police investigation and evidence linking him to the murder. The High Court heard emotional statements from Buckley’s family, who described Pacteau as 'evil' and called for a life sentence. The judge deferred sentencing, referring to the killing as a motiveless and brutal attack.

858466_858466.caption: Police officers control traffic near a derailed BNSF train burn just west of Casselton
858466_858466.article_context: A train carrying crude oil derailed and exploded near Casselton, North Dakota, prompting officials to evacuate most residents due to hazardous smoke concerns. The intense fire made it difficult for investigators to assess the damage until conditions improved. No injuries were reported, but health risks from air quality remain uncertain. Initial reports suggest another derailed train caused the oil cars to leave the tracks. The incident has raised questions about the safety of transporting oil by rail, especially as North Dakota’s oil shipments by train continue to rise. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation into the accident.

176454_176454.caption: Protesters hold hands and chant as they gather outside the DC police headquarters as part of a planned 28 Hours for Mike Brown protest
176454_176454.article_context: The Obama administration is set to announce new restrictions on racial profiling by federal law enforcement, expanding the definition to include religion and national origin, and banning the practice in national security cases for the first time. However, the policy will exclude significant areas of the Department of Homeland Security, allowing TSA agents and Customs and Border Protection officers to continue profiling at airports and borders. While Justice Department agencies such as the FBI, DEA, and ATF must comply with the new rules, DHS activities like border inspections remain exempt, sparking criticism from civil rights groups who have long called for broader protections. The changes come amid nationwide protests over racial profiling and police conduct.

997745_997745.caption: Hassan Munshi left and Talha Asmal both 17 who are believed to have travelled to Syria at Easter Asmal is thought to have become Britain s youngest suicide bomber
997745_997745.article_context: Talha Asmal, a 17-year-old from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, is believed to have become Britain’s youngest suicide bomber after reportedly detonating explosives for ISIS in Iraq. He had traveled to the region with his childhood friend Hassan Munshi, raising concerns for Munshi's safety. Asmal's death shocked his family and community, who condemned ISIS for exploiting his vulnerability and grooming him online. Community leaders and local officials expressed grief and called for stronger measures against youth radicalization, emphasizing the need for more government support for anti-radicalization programs in the UK.

1529845_1529845.caption: Jennifer Lauren leaves Ennis Courthouse in County Clare after being fined 2000 euros for air rages offences
1529845_1529845.article_context: Jenny Lauren, the niece of fashion designer Ralph Lauren, was fined 2,000 euros by an Irish court after pleading guilty to being drunk, breaching the peace, and behaving abusively toward airline staff during a Delta Air Lines flight from Barcelona to New York. Her disruptive behavior forced the flight to be diverted to Shannon Airport, affecting over 200 passengers and costing Delta $43,158. Lauren admitted to being intoxicated and threatening crew members, and expressed embarrassment over her actions.

1617762_1617762.caption: Mr Cameron said there were benefits of being around the table when the EU made key decisions
1617762_1617762.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron told Eurosceptics in Parliament that leaving the EU to follow the 'Norway model' would be problematic, as Norway contributes financially and accepts EU regulations but lacks influence in decision-making. While Cameron stated all options—including EU exit—remain open as he renegotiates Britain’s EU relationship, he cautioned against the Norway approach, urging factual clarity on alternatives. Iceland’s Prime Minister suggested a looser EU relationship benefited his country, but other officials noted trade-offs of being outside the EU. UKIP and Vote Leave campaigners disputed Cameron’s argument, insisting the UK could secure a better post-EU deal. The debate continues as Cameron discusses reforms with European leaders and the EU signals willingness to accommodate some UK concerns.

1491150_1491150.caption: Dzhokhar Tsarnaev could face the death penalty after his conviction in the Boston bombing case
1491150_1491150.article_context: During the sentencing phase of his trial, convicted Boston Marathon bomber Dzhokhar Tsarnaev showed rare emotion as several relatives, including an aunt who broke down in tears, urged the jury to spare his life. Tsarnaev, previously stoic, cried as his family members described his childhood and distance from them since moving to the US. The defense argued he was influenced by his older brother Tamerlan, the leader in the 2013 attack that killed three and injured hundreds. The jury is deliberating whether to impose the death penalty.

114647_114647.caption: Amal Clooney Egypt court s ruling sends dangerous message
114647_114647.article_context: An Egyptian court sentenced three Al Jazeera journalists—Mohamed Fahmy, Baher Mohamed, and Peter Greste—to three years in prison on charges of broadcasting without a license and spreading false news, despite a lack of evidence they manipulated footage. The ruling, which follows a retrial, has drawn international criticism as an attack on press freedom in Egypt, with rights groups and Al Jazeera condemning the verdict as politically motivated. The case highlights Egypt's wider crackdown on independent media since the 2013 ouster of President Morsi, and has become a focal point in debates over judicial fairness and freedom of expression in the country.

569239_569239.caption: Dr Craig Spencer who was diagnosed with Ebola at a New York hospital on Thursday
569239_569239.article_context: Dr. Craig Spencer, a physician who recently returned to New York from Guinea where he worked for Doctors Without Borders, has tested positive for Ebola. After developing symptoms, Spencer was hospitalized at Bellevue, a designated Ebola treatment center. Health officials quarantined his close contacts and are tracing his movements, which included trips on the subway and visits to public spaces before he showed symptoms. Authorities assured the public that Ebola is not airborne and emphasized that New York has significant preparedness measures in place. Efforts are focused on containment, monitoring, and reassuring citizens, with the CDC and local officials coordinating the response.

1225489_1225489.caption: Mara Carfagna the Italian former equalities minister said the ruling on gang rape sentencing sent the wrong message
1225489_1225489.article_context: The Italian supreme court has sparked outrage by ruling that individuals remanded for trial on gang rape charges do not have to be automatically kept in jail, allowing judges to consider alternative forms of custody. This decision, which overturned the jail sentence for two 19-year-old men convicted of gang raping a 16-year-old, has drawn strong criticism from politicians and women's rights advocates, who fear it could let rapists go free and undermine strict anti-rape legislation introduced in 2009. The ruling is seen as a setback for advocates of tougher laws on sexual assault, and has revived debate over previous controversial court decisions related to rape in Italy.

672872_672872.caption: Gui Minhai whose salacious and many suspect largely fabricated books irritated Communist party cadres in an undated picture
672872_672872.article_context: Gui Minhai, a Hong Kong-based publisher known for controversial books about China's political elite, vanished from his home in Thailand under suspicious circumstances. While three of his colleagues were abducted in China, Gui was suspected to have been kidnapped abroad, possibly linked to his publications that angered senior Chinese officials. Despite CCTV evidence and requests from the Swedish government, Thai authorities have shown little effort in investigating his disappearance. The case highlights an increasing trend of China pursuing dissidents overseas, particularly as Thailand's military government has strengthened ties with Beijing and deported numerous individuals wanted by China. Gui’s fate remains unknown amid concerns over clandestine operations and diminishing international protections for critics of the Chinese regime.

441608_441608.caption: Police search a Watertown Mass neighborhood for Boston Marathon bombing suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev
441608_441608.article_context: MIT police officer Sean Collier was shot and killed on the MIT campus after responding to a disturbance. Collier, 26, was found dead by Massachusetts General Hospital late Thursday night. He was recognized as a dedicated and well-liked officer, having previously worked in the Somerville Police Department before joining MIT in 2012. The incident has prompted an ongoing manhunt for the suspects, and tributes have poured in from colleagues and community members acknowledging Collier’s service and impact.

628998_628998.caption: Russian riot police detain an protester in Moscow as crowds opposed to Vladimir Putin take to the streets and postelection violence breaks out
628998_628998.article_context: Mass protests erupted in Moscow following a Russian parliamentary election widely criticized for vote fraud and irregularities, with international observers and foreign leaders voicing concerns about the legitimacy of the results. Riot police responded with force, detaining hundreds including opposition leaders and journalists. The ruling United Russia party, led by Vladimir Putin, suffered significant losses, reflecting growing public dissatisfaction with Putin’s expected return to the presidency. Despite reduced support and allegations of election manipulation, no major opposition figure is allowed to challenge Putin, and his victory in upcoming presidential elections is still anticipated.

1515496_1515496.caption: John Shattuck says democracy faces challenges and questions not asked since the fall of the Berlin Wall
1515496_1515496.article_context: Central European University, founded in Budapest with backing from George Soros after the fall of communism, was designed to foster democracy and open society in Eastern Europe. Today, the university faces new challenges as authoritarianism, nationalism, and illiberal democracy gain ground in the region, and liberal values come under pressure. Led by president John Shattuck, the university is responding by promoting academic inquiry, supporting marginalized groups, and exploring questions about democracy's future in the digital era and global economy. University leaders and students highlight rising xenophobia, economic insecurity, and the crisis of Western democratic models, emphasizing that democracy's resilience now depends on addressing these complex social and economic issues.

1070905_1070905.caption: Vladimir Putin with G8 leaders The Russian leader has agreed to let President Assad of Syria go on certain conditions
1070905_1070905.article_context: At the G8 summit, British officials revealed that Russian President Vladimir Putin is open to Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad's removal, but only if it avoids creating a destabilizing power vacuum. The summit resulted in agreement to push for a transitional government with executive powers in Syria and called for an investigation into chemical weapons use, but the final communique omitted any direct reference to Assad’s ouster due to Russian resistance. Western leaders, including UK Prime Minister David Cameron and French President François Hollande, reinforced that Assad has no place in Syria’s future, while Russia warned against arming rebels and insisted state institutions must be preserved during any transition. The possibility of Iran participating in future peace talks was also raised, pending further information on its new president’s stance.

760085_760085.caption: John Russell carried out the shootings at the Camp Liberty Combat Stress Centre near Baghdad in May 2009
760085_760085.article_context: US Army Sergeant John Russell has pleaded guilty to killing four fellow soldiers and a Navy officer at a Baghdad mental health clinic in 2009, one of the worst cases of soldier-on-soldier violence during the Iraq war. In exchange for his plea, Russell will avoid the death penalty and face a maximum sentence of life in prison. The shootings occurred while Russell was suffering from severe depression and post-traumatic stress disorder, as documented by military evaluations. His plea statement revealed he was in emotional turmoil and hoped to stop his pain. The case highlights ongoing concerns about mental health issues among military personnel in combat zones.

437053_437053.caption: Steve Harvey says he declined to join a lawsuit against NASCAR
437053_437053.article_context: Steve Harvey publicly distanced himself from a $500 million federal lawsuit filed by Terrance Cox and Diversity Motorsports Racing against NASCAR, which alleges discrimination against black-owned teams and drivers. Harvey clarified on his radio show that he has no issues with NASCAR and requested not to be involved in any litigation, emphasizing he has never pursued interests in motorsports. NASCAR denied the lawsuit’s claims, reaffirming their commitment to diversity through several initiatives, and stated they would defend against and counter the suit. Harvey explained his meeting with Cox focused on youth educational initiatives, not racing, and objected to any plans for boycotts against corporate sponsors.

1514200_1514200.caption: British bank NatWest s technology failures earlier this year should be seen as a warning writes Jason Liu
1514200_1514200.article_context: NatWest experienced a major IT failure in June, resulting in widespread disruption to customer accounts, unpaid bills, and damage to its reputation. The technical team struggled to identify and resolve the issue amid complex, interconnected systems, highlighting the challenges faced by large organizations as technology becomes more integral to customer service. The incident underscores the need for intelligent automation combined with human oversight to prevent and swiftly address errors, as reliance on digital platforms and consumer demands for real-time updates continue to grow.

835471_835471.caption: Jordan s monarch King Abdullah has twice questioned Syrian president Bashar alAssad s legitimacy as leader
835471_835471.article_context: A Syrian fighter pilot, Colonel Hassan Merhi al-Hamadi, defected from the Assad regime by flying his MiG jet to Jordan and requesting asylum, which was granted within hours. This is the first known instance of a Syrian air force pilot fleeing with a warplane during the 16-month uprising, marking a significant and rare defection from the regime’s senior ranks. Syria condemned the pilot as a traitor and demanded the return of the aircraft. The asylum move is expected to escalate tensions between Syria and Jordan, as Damascus has accused Jordan of supporting rebel groups. The defection is seen as a propaganda victory for the Syrian opposition, indicating cracks in the regime’s military loyalty.

1203566_1203566.caption: Before his death David Haines read a statement holding David Cameron directly responsible for his beheading
1203566_1203566.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron condemned the Islamic State after the militant group released a video showing the beheading of British aid worker David Haines, vowing to take all necessary measures to defeat ISIS and keep the UK safe. Cameron outlined a strategy including supporting the Iraqi government and Kurdish forces, working with the UN, backing US air strikes, providing humanitarian aid, and enhancing domestic counter-terrorism efforts, but did not yet commit to direct British military action. The murder of Haines, the third such killing by ISIS, prompted widespread condemnation from UK leaders, US President Barack Obama, and the Muslim community in Britain, who distanced themselves from ISIS and its ideology.

355903_355903.caption: Rep Mike Honda DCalif took an eightday trip to Turkey sponsored by a Gulenconnected group
355903_355903.article_context: A USA TODAY investigation found that organizations linked to the Turkish religious movement led by Fethullah Gülen secretly funded as many as 200 congressional trips to Turkey since 2008, potentially violating House rules and federal law. Many of these trips were approved by the House Ethics Committee based on falsified or incomplete disclosures, with some groups lacking proper nonprofit status or reporting inaccurate expenditures. The actual funding often came from Gülen-affiliated organizations in Turkey, and as much as $800,000 in travel costs were provided to lawmakers and staff. Despite the possibly improper sponsorship, the Ethics Committee found no evidence that members or staff knowingly broke the rules, but referred concerns about third-party deception to the Department of Justice. The revelations highlight the Gülen movement’s extensive influence in the U.S., its complicated network of organizations, and concerns over transparency and congressional ethics.

49998_49998.caption: Gloria Mendoza 24 says her autism was an issue during job interviews Mendoza has a college degree in computer science and music
49998_49998.article_context: The article highlights the significant barriers autistic adults face in finding and maintaining employment, noting that despite their skills and qualifications, high unemployment rates persist due to social and communication challenges in traditional hiring processes. It profiles individuals like Gloria Mendoza, who found success through specialized corporate programs, such as SAP's Autism at Work, which provide tailored support and technical training. Advocacy groups and some companies are developing initiatives to help autistic adults find jobs, but these efforts struggle to meet the scale of need as 50,000 autistic individuals enter adulthood in the U.S. each year. The article underscores the importance of employers making workplace accommodations and recognizing the unique talents autistic people can bring, framing inclusion as both a social need and a business imperative.

1207266_1207266.caption: 1985 Osama bin Laden in Afghanistan
1207266_1207266.article_context: The article traces significant moments in the life of Osama bin Laden, documenting his early years, involvement in Afghanistan during the Soviet war, rise as the leader of al-Qaida, and his role in major terrorist activities including the 1998 US embassy bombings and the 9/11 attacks. It also highlights his continued influence through videos and public appearances, ending with his death in 2011 when he was killed by American forces in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

370531_370531.caption: Ashley Elizabeth Zehnder 24 approached the assistant principal at Pasadena High claiming that students might have gotten access to a nude photo off of her old cell phone
370531_370531.article_context: Sandra Barnett, wife of former NFL player Buster Barnett, was kidnapped and killed by Buster's mistress, Lisa Brown, who then committed suicide after a police chase that ended in Alabama. Authorities revealed Brown had a criminal history, including a prior kidnapping incident in Texas. Both Barnett and Brown were longtime teachers in the Atlanta area.

1577475_1577475.caption: About 25 officers from Queensland Police and state emergency services looked for Ms Fraser
1577475_1577475.article_context: Shannon Leah Fraser, an Australian woman, was found alive after surviving 17 days lost in the bush in northern Queensland without food. Her disappearance sparked an extensive search operation, but she was ultimately discovered by a local farmer only 30 meters from where she first went missing. Fraser endured harsh conditions, surviving on creek water, small fish, and insects, and suffered from infected cuts and severe sunburn. Despite the ordeal, police do not suspect foul play in her disappearance.

145150_145150.caption: Former DC Council chairman Kwame R Brown after his June guilty plea
145150_145150.article_context: Former D.C. Council chairman Kwame R. Brown was sentenced to one day in federal custody, six months of home detention, and two years probation for bank fraud, after admitting to lying on loan applications. He also received a suspended 30-day jail sentence and additional probation for violating a city campaign finance law. Brown resigned from his position and apologized, acknowledging the impact of his actions on his family and public trust. His sentencing follows a broader investigation into public corruption among D.C. officials.

951978_951978.caption: Volunteers pack sandbags to proctect property near the Wimmera river in Horsham
951978_951978.article_context: Severe flooding has struck several towns in western Victoria, Australia, including Horsham and Beaufort, where flash floods have inundated streets, homes, and parks. Residents have been forced to navigate floodwaters, with some relying on sandbags to protect their properties while others witnessed roads being submerged and communities cut off. The images highlight both the challenges faced by locals and the community efforts in response to the widespread flooding.

971052_971052.caption: Chinchilla resident Jim Casey and his wife Lesley stand on their balcony
971052_971052.article_context: Severe flooding has affected multiple towns in Queensland, Australia, including Emerald, Bundaberg, Dalby, Chinchilla, and Watson. Residents have been evacuated, rescue operations are underway, and emergency supplies like food are being airlifted to isolated areas. Prime Minister Julia Gillard and Queensland Premier Anna Bligh have visited the affected regions to address the crisis, while authorities and Red Cross volunteers provide aid to those displaced by the floodwaters.

1629408_1629408.caption: Rodney McCune who works as an adviser to the executive minister Danny Kennedy thinks the result in South Belfast will be very tight
1629408_1629408.article_context: South Belfast is a highly contested seat in the general election, with incumbent SDLP leader Alasdair McDonnell facing strong challenges from Sinn Féin's Máirtín Ó Muilleor and candidates from both the DUP and Ulster Unionists, who failed to agree on a joint unionist candidate. Alliance Party's Paula Bradshaw and other parties are also fielding candidates, making this diverse constituency one of the most competitive in Northern Ireland. The campaign is marked by intense efforts from all sides, including heavy poster displays, and both nationalist and unionist camps expect a tight result with the outcome uncertain.

545134_545134.caption: John Prescottt says Labour only had 10m to spend on this year s election
545134_545134.article_context: John Prescott has warned that the Labour Party is £20 million in debt and close to bankruptcy, emphasizing the urgent need for smarter, more cost-effective campaigning to compete with the better-funded Conservatives. As a candidate for party treasurer, Prescott criticizes past financial mismanagement under Tony Blair and Gordon Brown, noting costly decisions and insufficient campaign resources. He argues that strengthening the treasurer's role is vital for financial accountability and campaign capacity, while outlining the challenge Labour faces from coalition government reforms and internal electoral rival Diane Holland. Prescott advocates for financial discipline to secure Labour’s future success.

1519533_1519533.caption: Ayatollah Khamenei may have a crucial role in what comes next for Iran but thoughts are already turning to his successor
1519533_1519533.article_context: Iran's recent parliamentary and Assembly of Experts elections resulted in a major upset, with pro-government and moderate forces sweeping all seats in Tehran and blocking key hardline candidates. Despite mass disqualifications of reformists and predictions of a hardliner victory, a late surge in online campaigning and tactical voting led to surprising wins for candidates supporting President Rouhani's moderate agenda. Although moderates gained ground, hardliners still retain influence over unelected bodies and critical institutions, meaning the political landscape remains complex. The results give Rouhani's government greater confidence to push reforms, but future developments will depend on the response of Supreme Leader Khamenei and how both camps leverage their positions.

87088_87088.caption: A Secret Service agent shouts a warning at spectators trying to take photos as Obama arrives at a university in Soweto South Africa
87088_87088.article_context: During a visit to Senegal, President Obama and his family toured the Door of No Return on Goree Island, a symbolic site tied to the transatlantic slave trade. Obama used the occasion to reinforce the importance of defending human rights and to promote stronger ties between the U.S. and emerging African democracies. The trip also included plans to visit South Africa and possibly Nelson Mandela, whose health was uncertain. Obama praised Mandela’s legacy and highlighted U.S. support for democratic values and judicial accountability in Africa, while acknowledging challenges such as LGBT rights, which remain contentious in countries like Senegal.

1103475_1103475.caption: People walk past homes severely damaged by cyclone Pam on Vanuatu s Tanna island
1103475_1103475.article_context: After Cyclone Pam devastated Vanuatu’s Tanna island, Prime Minister Joe Natuman urged citizens to rely on self-sufficiency and not depend solely on government aid, attributing current dependency to the legacy of French colonial rule. The cyclone left thousands homeless, destroyed crops, and damaged or destroyed most homes, while government response was sluggish due to damaged communications and reliance on international aid from Australia, New Zealand, and France. Aid delivery is prioritizing shelter and water, but concerns remain over imminent food shortages, limited medical resources, and inaccessible communities. Natuman acknowledged the disaster's severity and stressed the need for resilience as communities begin recovery.

1478275_1478275.caption: Mr Touil was detained on Tuesday night on a Tunisian arrest warrant
1478275_1478275.article_context: Italian police have arrested Moroccan national Abdelmajid Touil, who is suspected of involvement in the deadly March attack on Tunisia’s Bardo museum, which killed 22 people including foreign tourists. Touil had arrived in Italy illegally a month before the attack and was identified by authorities for allegedly supporting the gunmen responsible, though his exact role and location at the time remain unclear. The Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack, and Tunisian authorities have already arrested or killed other suspects linked to the incident.

1594669_1594669.caption: President Poroshenko has been given strong backing at the summit but Nato will only go so far
1594669_1594669.article_context: At the Nato summit in Wales, the alliance expressed strong support for Ukraine and condemned Russia's actions, including the annexation of Crimea, urging Moscow to withdraw its troops and pursue peace. Nato announced plans to strengthen cooperation with Ukraine but stopped short of offering direct military assistance. Fresh EU and US sanctions targeting Russia’s banking, energy, and defense sectors are set to be imposed. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Poroshenko and rebel leaders indicated a ceasefire could be agreed soon, pending talks in Minsk. The city of Mariupol is under threat from advancing pro-Russian rebels, and the overall situation in Eastern Ukraine remains volatile. Nato also discussed broader security challenges including the rise of Islamic State and continued violence in Afghanistan. The summit is considered highly significant, reflecting concerns among member states about Russian aggression and the need for the alliance to adapt to modern threats.

1655439_1655439.caption: Chinese papers say Mr Abe s economic policies have failed
1655439_1655439.article_context: Chinese media criticized Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's decision to call snap elections, labeling him a reckless political gambler amid concerns over Japan’s economic slowdown and nuclear energy debate. In contrast, outlets paid tribute to beloved Japanese actor Ken Takakura following his death, highlighting his cultural impact and role as a bridge between China and Japan. Reports also covered Hong Kong police clearing parts of a pro-democracy protest camp, with some criticism directed at the demonstrators. Separately, Chinese papers discussed the opening of the World Internet Conference, emphasizing China’s significant influence on global internet governance. Finally, media expressed alarm over the discovery of counterfeit elevators in several Chinese cities, raising safety concerns and calling for stricter government oversight.

1499085_1499085.caption: Darren Henry said Mr Baker was asleep when he was shot
1499085_1499085.article_context: A firearms officer has been arrested following the fatal shooting of Jermaine Baker, who was killed during an alleged attempt to free two convicts from a prison van in north London. The Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) has launched a homicide investigation and is appealing for witnesses, with further forensic examinations underway. Community tensions have risen, and many are demanding greater transparency and accountability from the police, referencing the previous case of Mark Duggan. The officer involved has been suspended pending the outcome of the inquiry, and authorities emphasize the need for a thorough and independent investigation into the circumstances of Baker's death.

1658693_1658693.caption: Jason Yendall Aaron Brannan and Jason Britton carried out the Argyll Arcade raid in daylight
1658693_1658693.article_context: Three men admitted to a £230,000 armed jewellery robbery at Glasgow’s Argyll Arcade in September 2014, stealing 21 high-value watches from Rox jewellers in a raid that terrified shoppers and staff. They were caught after two associates were seen wearing stolen watches. All five men also admitted to a £20,000 armed bank robbery in Edinburgh a week later. The stolen goods were not recovered, and all five, who have criminal histories, await sentencing next month.

392168_392168.caption: The body of Dmitriy Kanarikov 35 is removed from 425 W 59th Street on Dec 22 in New York City
392168_392168.article_context: In Manhattan, Dmitriy Kanarikov threw his 3-year-old son off the roof of a high-rise before jumping to his own death during his first unsupervised visit with the child after separating from his wife. The tragedy occurred when Kanarikov was supposed to return his son, who was in his mother's custody, to her at a police precinct. Police found both bodies on nearby rooftops, and authorities are investigating the case. The incident is the second fatal parent-child plunge in New York City this year.

586181_586181.caption: Mohammed Yusuf then leader of Boko Haram is arrested in 2009 A few hours later he was dead
586181_586181.article_context: The article traces the origins and rise of Boko Haram in Nigeria, highlighting how tightening police enforcement of helmet laws for motorcycle taxis in 2009 triggered violent clashes with the radical Islamist sect in Maiduguri, Borno State. Led by Mohammed Yusuf, Boko Haram evolved from a fringe religious movement with roots among disaffected youth and elites into a violent insurgency, culminating in a major uprising in 2009 and Yusuf’s controversial death in police custody. Under new leader Abubakar Shekau, Boko Haram launched devastating terror campaigns, including bombings, massacres, and mass abductions, destabilizing northern Nigeria and displacing millions. The Nigerian government struggled to respond effectively, with violence persisting into the 2010s despite military offensives and leadership changes. The article contextualizes Boko Haram’s appeal among marginalized populations and details the group’s expansion, recruitment tactics, and enduring threat.

669179_669179.caption: A firefighter carries the body of an infant who died in a landslide in the Morro de Borel area of Rio de Janeiro
669179_669179.article_context: Flash floods and landslides triggered by intense rainstorms killed at least 95 people in the hillside slums of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Rescue operations were underway as authorities warned residents to evacuate high-risk areas and stay indoors. The storms, described as the worst in Rio's history, submerged roads, stranded cars, and devastated poorer hillside communities. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and local officials emphasized the severity of the situation, while assuring that such disasters would not affect Rio's preparations for the 2016 Olympics.

147678_147678.caption: A boy looks inside the fallen statue of President Bashar alAssad s father Hafez alAssad in Raqqa province Syria
147678_147678.article_context: France, following Britain's lead, has threatened to supply weapons to Syrian rebel groups if the European Union does not lift its embargo on arms deliveries to Syria. French Foreign Minister Laurent Fabius argued that the current lack of balance—where Iran and Russia arm President Assad while rebels remain under-equipped—necessitates a change in EU policy. Both France and Britain are pressing for an early EU meeting to reconsider the embargo, although several northern European countries remain opposed, fearing escalation of the civil war. The issue comes amid a rising refugee crisis and ongoing calls from rebel leaders for advanced weaponry.

1490327_1490327.caption: Altaf Hussain retains a lot of support in Karachi
1490327_1490327.article_context: Altaf Hussain, exiled leader of Pakistan’s MQM party, was released on bail in London after being arrested on suspicion of money laundering. Hussain, who has lived in the UK since the early 1990s, was questioned by police and hospitalized for medical checks before his release. His arrest sparked major protests and celebrations among his supporters in Karachi. Hussain and his party are the subjects of multiple British investigations, including money laundering, tax issues, and alleged incitement of violence in Pakistan.

1536508_1536508.caption: The Typhoons have been deployed from RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus
1536508_1536508.article_context: After UK MPs voted to approve military air strikes against Islamic State (IS) in Syria, British Typhoon and Tornado jets launched their first missions from the RAF base in Cyprus. UK forces carried out air strikes on IS-controlled targets, including oil fields in eastern Syria, and conducted reconnaissance and intelligence-gathering flights. The US President Obama welcomed the UK's involvement and discussed further cooperation with Prime Minister David Cameron, who emphasized that these actions would contribute to achieving a political settlement in Syria. Meanwhile, Germany’s parliament also voted to provide military support to the US-led coalition against IS.

464982_464982.caption: Jiang Zemin s failure to attend a celebration marking the Communist party s 90th anniversary sparked speculation that he had died
464982_464982.article_context: Rumors of former Chinese president Jiang Zemin's death circulated widely online and in overseas media after his absence from a major political event, prompting an official denial from China’s state news agency, Xinhua. Despite this rare public rebuttal and attempts by Chinese authorities to censor related internet searches, speculation persisted due to the lack of public appearances and secrecy surrounding Jiang’s health. The situation highlights the challenges faced by the Chinese Communist Party in controlling information within a highly connected society.

927234_927234.caption: Ethiopian women wait to cast their vote Sunday May 23 2010 at a poling station in Nazret Ethiopia 100 km south of Addis Ababa Ethiopians began voting in national elections
927234_927234.article_context: Colin Poulton's research challenges the assumption that democratization in African countries leads to stronger pro-poor agricultural policies. Instead, many politicians secure votes by relying on ethnic allegiances and clientelist strategies, offering short-term handouts rather than long-term investments in agriculture. The study finds that governments are primarily motivated by threats to regime survival and economic dependence on agriculture, rather than the democratic process itself. Examples like Ethiopia and Rwanda show that significant rural investment is often driven by the need to prevent political instability. Poulton emphasizes the need for policy recommendations to be tailored to specific political contexts, highlighting that technical solutions alone are inadequate without accompanying political analysis and support. Civil society is identified as key to building awareness among rural voters and reducing ethnic divisions, but further research is needed on its effectiveness.

472543_472543.caption: The funeral of drowned threeyearold Alan Kurdi in Kobane Syria
472543_472543.article_context: The Guardian’s comment sections have seen massive growth and increasing polarization in recent years, particularly in response to major news stories like the refugee crisis, terrorism, and Russia’s bombing campaign in Syria. Moderators struggle to manage heated debates, personal attacks, and misinformation, especially on contentious issues where organized campaigns and paid trolls attempt to sway discussions. While some comment threads descend into vitriol and abuse, there are also positive communities built around shared interests. The rise in hostile and divisive comments has led some to question the value of online discussion, but Guardian staff believe moderation and reform can preserve its constructive potential.

684164_684164.caption: Israeli air strikes on Rafah in Gaza City
684164_684164.article_context: The article highlights the severe humanitarian impact of the Israeli military's actions in Gaza, including the destruction of critical infrastructure like the central electricity station, hospitals, clinics, and schools. It discusses the high number of displaced Palestinians, with over 200,000 now homeless due to ongoing violence and blockade. The piece references voices calling for peace and political solutions, such as Uri Avnery and Daniel Barenboim, and urges prioritizing humanitarian concerns and dialogue over military action. The author emphasizes that lasting peace and justice for children can only be achieved through negotiation and willingness to speak with all parties involved.

283715_283715.caption: Anthony Bosch center is escorted by Drug Enforcement Administration officials in Weston Fla
283715_283715.article_context: Tony Bosch, former director of the Biogenesis anti-aging clinic in Florida, was among 10 people charged with distributing illegal drugs, including performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs) and recreational drugs, to professional and high school athletes. Bosch has agreed to plead guilty to conspiracy to distribute testosterone and may cooperate with authorities for a reduced sentence. The investigation revealed Biogenesis supplied PEDs to both adult and minor athletes in South Florida and the Dominican Republic, recruiting youths as young as 12. Prominent baseball players, including Alex Rodriguez and Ryan Braun, were implicated and suspended by Major League Baseball after Bosch’s testimony and cooperation played a key role in the investigation.

311701_311701.caption: Madison Wahlgren 15 a sophomore at Marysville Pilchuck High School holds a candle as she stands outside following a memorial vigil at Grove Church in Marysville Wash
311701_311701.article_context: Jaylen Fryberg, a student at Marysville-Pilchuck High School in Washington, invited several friends to lunch via text message and then opened fire in the school cafeteria, killing two students and critically injuring three others before fatally shooting himself. The handgun used was legally registered to a family member, and authorities are still investigating how Fryberg obtained it. The motive remains unclear, with no evidence of physical confrontation before the shooting. Survivors, including Fryberg’s cousins, continue to recover in hospital as the community grapples with the tragedy.

1587732_1587732.caption: Vladimir Putin a sinister leader according to the Sunday Telegraph
1587732_1587732.article_context: The aftermath of Malaysia Airlines flight MH17’s crash continued to dominate headlines, with investigators facing severe obstruction from armed separatist rebels in eastern Ukraine. Many international and Ukrainian officials accused the separatists and possibly Russian regular troops of hindering access and tampering with the crash site, fueling suspicions over their involvement in downing the aircraft. Western nations, including the UK and Australia, pushed for a UN Security Council resolution demanding Russia ensure investigators’ access. Political commentary overwhelmingly blamed Russian President Vladimir Putin, with leaders like UK Prime Minister David Cameron calling the event an 'atrocity made in Moscow' and urging tougher measures on Russia. Meanwhile, British media also covered the domestic political fallout of Prime Minister Cameron’s cabinet reshuffle, noting public skepticism about its motives, and reported on a national increase in interest in cycling holidays.

365612_365612.caption: Hillary Clinton addresses the crowd as Bill Clinton and Chelsea Clinton stand behind her at a primary night event in Indianapolis on May 6 2008
365612_365612.article_context: As Hillary Clinton prepares to announce her second presidential campaign, former President Bill Clinton will initially take a behind-the-scenes advisory role rather than acting as her main campaigner. While Bill is considered a powerful asset due to his popularity and political skills, both he and Hillary believe she should establish her own connection with voters early on. Republicans are expected to focus on controversies from her tenure as Secretary of State. The Clintons aim to avoid missteps from Hillary's 2008 campaign, during which Bill’s prominent involvement sometimes proved controversial. Bill Clinton acknowledges his changing priorities as a grandfather and plans to support Hillary primarily through strategy rather than public appearances.

341448_341448.caption: Federal agents check Boston Marathon suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev for explosives as they treat him for wounds after his arrest in Watertown Mass
341448_341448.article_context: Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the surviving suspect of the Boston Marathon bombings, is awake and responding to investigators in writing while under heavy guard in a Boston hospital, recovering from injuries that may have been self-inflicted. Authorities are examining his and his deceased brother Tamerlan’s backgrounds, including previous FBI inquiries and Tamerlan’s trip to Russia, amid questions over possible missed signs of radicalization. While Tsarnaev faces interrogation, officials debate the use of Miranda rights, and federal defenders are being appointed. Surveillance evidences Dzhokhar’s involvement, but officials say no further immediate threats have been found. The Boston community is returning to normal following a week of lockdowns, with ongoing vigils for victims and expressions of gratitude toward law enforcement.

339040_339040.caption: St Louis County SWAT team prepare to search the attic of a house in Ferguson Mo
339040_339040.article_context: Ferguson, Missouri has faced escalating turmoil following the fatal shooting of Michael Brown, an unarmed black teenager, by a white police officer, culminating in widespread protests, resignations of top city officials, and the shooting of two police officers. A federal report highlighted systemic racial bias and a profit-driven court system in the city. In response, USA TODAY consulted various leaders and experts, who suggested solutions such as appointing diverse leadership, consolidating fragmented local governments, rebuilding community trust through engagement and reforms, disbanding the current police force, and fostering open dialogue between police and residents. All emphasized the need for significant structural change and community involvement to restore stability and trust.

150749_150749.caption: Cruz vows to carpet bomb Islamic State into oblivion
150749_150749.article_context: Senator Marco Rubio returned to Iowa for a campaign swing, where he and his supporters are engaged in intensifying battles with other Republican presidential contenders, including Ted Cruz, Chris Christie, and Jeb Bush. Rubio criticized Cruz and indirectly targeted him over national security and immigration policies, while super PACs from both sides released attack ads. Rubio is pursuing a campaign strategy of competing strongly in all early voting states, aiming to appeal to both conservative and moderate Republican voters. These escalating confrontations reflect Rubio’s efforts to maintain a competitive edge and unify the party as the GOP primary race heats up.

853864_853864.caption: Pakistani opposition politician Imran Khan speaks to his supporters during an antigovernment protest in front of the parliament building in Islamabad Pakistan
853864_853864.article_context: Hamid Mir, a prominent journalist for Pakistan's Geo TV, faces hostility from supporters of opposition leader Imran Khan, who accuses the channel of bias and blames it for alleged election rigging. Mir was critically injured in an April attack, which Geo controversially linked to the head of military intelligence, deepening tensions between the media, the government, and the military. The ensuing crisis has divided the media, weakened Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif’s position, and reportedly aided the military’s influence over civilian rule. Geo has suffered commercial setbacks due to government and military pressure, but Mir continues to speak out against army interference in politics despite personal risk.

897521_897521.caption: Earthquake survivor Anna Zizi takes a drink of water after being carried alive from the rubble one week after Haiti s devastating earthquake
897521_897521.article_context: Rescue teams in Port-au-Prince continued to pull survivors from the rubble a week after the devastating earthquake, defying expectations that few would remain alive. Several individuals, including a young boy and multiple adults, were found in good condition, with extraction efforts led by Haitian and international crews. Among those rescued was Natalie, a 26-year-old woman who survived seven days trapped in debris and was the 73rd live extraction reported. Another notable survivor was Ena Zizi, a 69-year-old woman rescued from a collapsed university building. These ongoing recoveries highlighted both the resilience of the Haitian people and the determination of rescue operations to find survivors.

246046_246046.caption: Donald Trump delivers remarks at a campaign rally in Fredericksburg Va on Aug 20 2016
246046_246046.article_context: Donald Trump has canceled at least three campaign events in Colorado, Nevada, and Oregon, though he is still set to attend fundraisers in Colorado and Nevada. His immigration speech in Denver was postponed, and rallies in Las Vegas and Portland were also canceled. The campaign attributed changes to his recent trip to Louisiana but did not provide detailed reasons for the cancellations. The decisions come as Trump trails Hillary Clinton in polling in key battleground states.

780310_780310.caption: Iran s new president Hassan Rouhani said in his first press conference that his government would be open to direct talks with the US should Washington show goodwill
780310_780310.article_context: More than 50 Iranian political prisoners have written an open letter to President Barack Obama, urging him to end crippling US sanctions and seize the opportunity for dialogue following the election of moderate president Hassan Rouhani. The prisoners criticized the devastating impact of sanctions on ordinary Iranians and called on Obama to pursue direct talks and mutual understanding, warning that ongoing pressure would fuel public distrust of the US. Both Rouhani and the US have recently indicated openness to improved relations, but the letter stresses that Rouhani's presidency may represent the last chance to resolve longstanding conflicts between the two countries.

84886_84886.caption: Ben Carson s alma mater Southwestern High School closed in 2012
84886_84886.article_context: Ben Carson, a Republican presidential candidate and renowned neurosurgeon, rose from deep poverty in Southwest Detroit, benefiting from government assistance programs and his mother's emphasis on self-reliance. Carson uses his life story to argue that anyone can succeed through hard work and faith, but critics point out his experience is exceptionally rare without government help, especially as Detroit’s social fabric and economy have deteriorated. While Carson advocates for reducing dependence on welfare and shrinking government intervention, anti-poverty experts contend that such aid is necessary for most in poverty. Carson’s personal journey is a major theme of his campaign, but it highlights ongoing tension between his individual success and the broader challenges facing communities like his childhood neighborhood.

864551_864551.caption: The canvass is timed to follow Tuesday s televised debate between Alex Salmond and Alistair Darling
864551_864551.article_context: Scotland's Radical Independence Campaign organized a mass canvass in low-voter-turnout urban areas to promote independence and emphasize the movement's separation from SNP leader Alex Salmond, following a televised debate between Salmond and Alistair Darling. The debate, watched by 1.7 million, was judged a win for Darling in post-debate polling, though support for independence remained close. The independence campaign is working to broaden its appeal beyond party politics, targeting disenfranchised communities, while SNP leaders acknowledge that linking the referendum too closely to Salmond could hinder support. With a tight margin between yes and no votes, pro-independence groups aim to mobilize non-voters and Labour supporters ahead of the September referendum.

1567033_1567033.caption: Cartoonist Will Kevans was in the Falklands as an 18yearold Welsh Guard
1567033_1567033.article_context: Welsh illustrator and Falklands War veteran Will Kevans has created a cartoon book titled 'My Life In Pieces,' drawing on his experiences serving with the Welsh Guards and interviews with fellow soldiers. The book uses dramatic images and text to depict the events of the Falklands War, offering a personal and artistic perspective on the conflict.

95556_95556.caption: Samuel plays with a ball found in the ruins while his father Phillip searches in what remained of their family home in Port Vila
95556_95556.article_context: Cyclone Pam, one of the most intense tropical cyclones ever recorded in the Pacific, devastated the island nation of Vanuatu with winds exceeding 150 miles per hour, causing widespread destruction and killing at least two people, though the death toll is expected to rise. The cyclone destroyed homes, blocked roads, and wiped out entire villages, especially on the islands of Efate and Tanna, including the capital city Port Vila. Vanuatu’s President has appealed for international aid as communication systems remain down and humanitarian needs for shelter, food, and medicine are urgent. Aid agencies are mobilizing emergency relief efforts. This disaster highlights Vanuatu’s vulnerability to natural catastrophes and underscores concerns related to climate change and rising sea levels affecting small island countries.

61417_61417.caption: Belongings described as being owned by Ryan Fogle are seen in this undated photo released by the press service of the Russian State Security Service
61417_61417.article_context: Ryan C. Fogle, a U.S. diplomat working in Moscow, was detained by Russian security services and ordered to leave the country after being accused of attempting to recruit a Russian intelligence officer as a U.S. agent. Russian authorities publicly identified Fogle as a CIA officer operating under diplomatic cover and released photos of alleged spy equipment and instructions. The incident has heightened tensions between the U.S. and Russia, complicating their recent efforts to cooperate on security matters, although officials have suggested the scandal may be short-lived and not seriously impact broader diplomatic talks.

638095_638095.caption: The Three Sisters rock formation in the Blue Mountains Australia near Leura where Gary Tweddle was staying when he went missing
638095_638095.article_context: Australian police searching for Gary Tweddle, a 23-year-old British man who went missing in the Blue Mountains six weeks ago, have discovered a body believed to be his during a rescue helicopter training flight. Tweddle disappeared after a work dinner, prompting extensive search efforts. Due to difficult terrain, authorities could not retrieve the body until the following morning for formal identification. Tweddle's family, who were involved in the search, have been notified, while official inquiries are being made to confirm the identity.

1277892_1277892.caption: This video image provided by KEYTTV shows a crowd confronting police at a disturbance on Saturday during a college party in southern California
1277892_1277892.article_context: A weekend college party known as Deltopia in Isla Vista, southern California, escalated into a violent street brawl, resulting in about 100 arrests and at least 44 hospitalizations. Police used teargas, pepper spray, and foam projectiles to disperse a crowd of approximately 15,000 after officers were assaulted with bottles, bricks, and other objects. The unrest required emergency backup from multiple agencies and left several officers injured, while much of the hospitalizations were related to excessive alcohol consumption. The situation was brought under control by Sunday morning, with authorities cleaning up the aftermath.

236772_236772.caption: Kentucky wide receiver Blake Bone dives for a touchdown against UT Martin
236772_236772.article_context: Top-ranked Florida State narrowly defeated Oklahoma State 37-31 in their season opener, despite expectations of a dominant performance. The Seminoles survived a strong challenge from an inexperienced Cowboys team, with a crucial defensive play by P.J. Williams late in the fourth quarter preventing an upset. Jameis Winston showed both brilliance and inconsistency, throwing for 370 yards but also two interceptions. Florida State struggled with its running game, raising concerns about their offensive effectiveness compared to last season. Oklahoma State's Tyreek Hill was a breakout performer, totaling 278 all-purpose yards. The Seminoles' victory keeps their College Football Playoff hopes intact.

78012_78012.caption: Donald Trump departs after a meeting with The Washington Post s editorial board in which he outlined an unabashedly noninterventionist approach to world affairs
78012_78012.article_context: AIPAC issued an unprecedented public apology after Donald Trump’s speech at its conference drew criticism for attacks on President Obama, which violated the organization’s nonpartisan standards. AIPAC President Lillian Pinkus expressed deep regret over the divisive rhetoric and the enthusiastic applause Trump received, stating respect for the office of the president and disappointment in the audience's reaction. While past speakers at AIPAC have criticized sitting presidents, Trump’s remarks and the crowd’s response led to unusually strong backlash from both AIPAC leadership and prominent voices in the Jewish community.

1657824_1657824.caption: US Ambassador Chris Stevens was killed in the attack
1657824_1657824.article_context: Ahmed Abu Khattala, the suspected ringleader of the 2012 Benghazi attack that killed US Ambassador Chris Stevens and three others, pleaded not guilty to 17 new charges, some carrying the death penalty, in a Washington court. Khattala, alleged by US authorities to be a senior leader of Ansar al-Sharia, was captured in a secret US raid in Libya and faces charges including murder, providing material support to terrorists, and attacking a federal facility. The Benghazi incident became a significant political controversy in the US, with debates over the administration's response and security measures.

234369_234369.caption: Donald Trump greets members of the National Diversity Coalition for Trump in New York City a day ahead of New York primary
234369_234369.article_context: In the lead-up to the crucial New York Democratic primary, polls show Hillary Clinton widening her lead over Bernie Sanders, with the latest NBC News/Wall Street Journal/Marist survey giving her a 17-point advantage. Clinton and Sanders engaged in a heated debate ahead of the vote, while Clinton’s campaign plans a statewide get-out-the-vote tour featuring Bill Clinton and key New York officials. On the Republican side, Donald Trump maintains a significant lead over his rivals, John Kasich and Ted Cruz. Polls indicate Clinton’s strength among older and suburban voters, with Sanders performing better among younger and first-time voters, and the allocation of delegates will depend on results across the state’s congressional districts.

1569016_1569016.caption: German Chancellor Angela Merkel has said she wants the UK to stay in the EU
1569016_1569016.article_context: At a Brussels summit, UK Prime Minister David Cameron officially presented his EU reform proposals, aiming for changes ahead of a promised in/out referendum by the end of 2017. Key demands include an opt-out from 'ever closer union,' protection for UK financial interests, curbs on EU migration through benefit cuts, and making the EU more competitive. While most EU leaders want Britain to stay, they strongly oppose Cameron’s push to restrict migration, arguing it violates core EU principles. Formal negotiations are set to begin, with the European Commission assessing if the proposals require treaty changes, but significant divisions remain.

294726_294726.caption: Police investigate an area in Brussels where terror suspect Mohamed Abrini was arrested April 8 2016
294726_294726.article_context: Mohamed Abrini confessed to Belgian authorities that he was the 'man in the hat' seen on surveillance footage before the Brussels Airport bombings in March, which killed 32 people. Abrini and three others were charged with terrorist murder and involvement in a terrorist group in connection with the airport and metro attacks. Abrini had already been wanted for his links to the 2015 Paris attacks. Among the other suspects, Osama Krayem is believed to be connected to the subway attack, and Bilal El Makhoukhi, who had previously been convicted for ties to Sharia4Belgium, was also charged.

46854_46854.caption: A sign above the Mayo Clinic in Minneapolis asks people to wear purple in memory of Prince
46854_46854.article_context: The deaths of Prince and David Bowie in 2016 marked the loss of two iconic artists who challenged traditional ideas of masculinity and gender identity. Both were known for their bold expressions of self through fashion, music, and their personas, inspiring greater acceptance of diversity in how men can present themselves and whom they can love. At a time of heated national debate over gender and LGBT rights, their legacies stand out as celebrations of individuality and as influential forces in breaking down societal norms around gender.

759652_759652.caption: Rahul Gandhi is seen as a likely Indian prime minister if his Congress party can win national elections due within months
759652_759652.article_context: Rahul Gandhi, a prominent figure in India's Congress party and member of its political dynasty, gave his first major interview, stating he is not motivated by power but by a desire to reduce people's suffering. As Congress faces tough elections and declining support amid economic issues and scandals, Gandhi emphasized his commitment to democratic empowerment and contrasted his views against those of BJP's Narendra Modi. He addressed his family's history of political tragedy, denied dynastic motivations, and called for greater inclusion and transparency in party politics, while defending Congress's stance against BJP and highlighting the need to empower youth and women.

359728_359728.caption: Vice President Biden and Beau Biden at the 2008 Democratic National Convention in Denver Beau Biden died May 30 2015
359728_359728.article_context: Vice President Joe Biden is considering entering the 2016 Democratic presidential race, but faces significant organizational and support hurdles due to Hillary Clinton's well-established campaign and Bernie Sanders' growing popularity. Biden is expected to make a decision by the end of the summer, but supporters worry that he may not have enough time to build a competitive campaign infrastructure in key early states. The recent death of Biden's son, Beau, has added a personal dimension to his deliberations, with friends and family emphasizing the emotional impact on the vice president. Despite Biden's strong personal popularity and long-standing relationships, especially in states like Iowa and South Carolina, he would start well behind Clinton in polls and face challenges related to fundraising and volunteer recruitment. Political observers note that a Biden candidacy could dramatically shift the dynamics of the race, but also caution that past campaign missteps and the timing of his entry could be significant obstacles.

1656551_1656551.caption: Museum President Philippe Blondin and Secretary General Norbert Cige unveil a plaque to the victims
1656551_1656551.article_context: The Jewish Museum of Belgium in Brussels is reopening four months after a terrorist attack left four people dead, including two museum staff and an Israeli couple. Security has been tightened, and a commemorative plaque honors the victims. The suspected attacker, Mehdi Nemmouche, was arrested and extradited to Belgium, with links to Islamist extremism and possible involvement in Syria. Despite heightened anxiety and ongoing investigations, the museum is determined to continue its educational mission and exhibitions, marking the reopening as a symbol of resilience and solidarity.

1073999_1073999.caption: Then opposition leader and Antananarivo Mayor Andry Rajoelina after proclaiming himself president in 2009
1073999_1073999.article_context: Nearly two years after Madagascar's 2009 coup, a breakthrough agreement was signed by most political parties on 17 September, potentially ending the country's prolonged crisis. The deal allows for the unconditional return of political exiles, including former president Marc Ravalomanana, though he faces arrest due to previous convictions. The agreement was brokered with support from the Southern African Development Community, but tensions remain as Ravalomanana and current leader Andry Rajoelina both intend to run in elections scheduled for next year. International sanctions are expected to be lifted if progress is sustained, aiming to alleviate Madagascar's deep economic hardships.

167899_167899.caption: People celebrate after winning the first prize of Spain s Christmas lottery named El Gordo
167899_167899.article_context: Journalists at China's Southern Weekly newspaper chose discreet protest over a planned mass strike, publishing subtle messages advocating for moderate media freedom and reform instead of directly opposing government censorship. The anti-censorship movement spread to other outlets like Beijing News, resulting in tense standoffs within newsrooms and ambiguous resignations. Public outrage was expressed via social media and street protests, challenging the Communist Party’s control over information and posing an early test for new leader Xi Jinping. Despite initial activism, most journalists refrained from striking, citing fears of job loss and retaliation, while observers noted an encouraging rise in ordinary citizens' support for free speech.

852067_852067.caption: President Barack Obama observes a moments silence alongside his wife Michelle
852067_852067.article_context: Following a mass shooting in Tucson, Arizona, that left six dead and 14 wounded—including Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords, who survived an assassination attempt—Americans nationwide joined in mourning and calls for reflection. The accused shooter, Jared Lee Loughner, appeared in court facing multiple charges, including murder and attempted murder. The event sparked discussions about the role of extreme political rhetoric and hate speech in enabling such violence. President Obama led a national moment of silence, while international and local leaders, including Nasa astronauts and Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, called for moderation and unity against extremism. Investigations continue into Loughner's motives and possible ties to far-right organizations. Giffords remains hospitalized in stable condition.

1606085_1606085.caption: Mr Tsipras and Mrs Merkel addressed questions before a second round of talks in the evening
1606085_1606085.article_context: Greek Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras and German Chancellor Angela Merkel met in Berlin, signaling a desire for improved relations amid tensions over Greece's bailout and economic crisis. Both leaders emphasized the need for cooperation and dialogue, but remained vague on concrete solutions to Greece's urgent financial problems. Merkel reiterated that Germany expects Greece to follow through on promised reforms before receiving further financial aid, while Tsipras stressed the social challenges and the need to break mutual stereotypes. The summit followed the EU's pledge of €2bn in aid to help the humanitarian crisis in Greece, but Merkel maintained that no new funds would be released absent specific reforms.

1177475_1177475.caption: A woman holds a child as refugees take shelter near the western Serbian village of Berkasovo close to the SerbiaCroatia border on Monday
1177475_1177475.article_context: Thousands of refugees stranded at the Serbia-Croatia border were finally allowed to cross into Croatia, easing dire conditions but increasing pressure on neighboring Slovenia, which has reached its intake limits. The situation reflects broader regional tensions and finger-pointing as Balkan countries struggle to manage the surge, following border closures by Hungary that redirected migrant flows. Meanwhile, Turkey, under pressure to curb refugee movement in exchange for EU funding, refused to act as the sole holding center for migrants, and aid agencies warned of severe humanitarian risks for vulnerable populations caught at closed borders.

640391_640391.caption: Beyonce and Jay Z leave the rally in New York where Trayvon Martin s mother Sabryna Fulton spoke
640391_640391.article_context: Following the acquittal of George Zimmerman in the shooting death of Trayvon Martin, large-scale rallies were held across more than 100 U.S. cities calling for justice and civil rights charges against Zimmerman. Trayvon Martin's mother, Sybrina Fulton, thanked supporters and promised to continue fighting against racial profiling. Calls also intensified to review and potentially change 'stand your ground' laws, with political figures like Senator John McCain joining the debate. President Barack Obama addressed the issue of racial discrimination publicly, drawing attention to the broader impact of the case on African American communities.

141303_141303.caption: Phoenix Mercury center Brittney Griner will miss the first seven games this season
141303_141303.article_context: WNBA star Brittney Griner, known for her resilience and authenticity, recently faced public scrutiny after a domestic dispute with her fiancée, fellow player Glory Johnson, led to mutual arrests and a suspension from the league. While Griner has overcome significant personal challenges and adversity throughout her life, her case has highlighted the often-overlooked issue of same-sex domestic violence and the complexities faced by victims in LGBTQ relationships. Despite setbacks, Griner is recognized as a supportive teammate and is expected to return to the court after her suspension, continuing her influential presence in women's basketball.

197901_197901.caption: President Obama s full remarks on the Keystone XL project
197901_197901.article_context: A new political partnership between billionaire environmentalist Tom Steyer and major public sector unions, endorsed by the AFL-CIO, has sparked strong opposition from leaders of eight building trade unions. The building trades are upset over Steyer’s stance against the Keystone XL Pipeline, which they supported for job creation. In protest, the unions have withdrawn support from the super PAC 'For Our Future,' accusing the AFL-CIO of prioritizing outside interests over blue-collar workers and allowing Steyer undue influence over the labor federation’s political agenda.

1646501_1646501.caption: Boy S was sentenced to life in prison at Manchester Crown Court
1646501_1646501.article_context: A 14-year-old boy in the UK, referred to as Boy S, became the youngest person convicted of a terrorism offence after attempting to incite a mass killing in Australia and engaging with global extremists online. Despite early warnings and intervention by anti-radicalisation programs, his violent behaviour escalated, leading to a life sentence with a minimum term of five years. The case has sparked debate about whether more could have been done to prevent his radicalisation, but the judge concluded that blame lay primarily with the extremists who exploited him. Authorities continue to consider ways to rehabilitate Boy S, who remains at risk of a prolonged prison term if he does not change.

1520989_1520989.caption: Moscowbacked security forces have been battling Islamist insurgents in Chechnya and other Russian republics of the Caucasus
1520989_1520989.article_context: Russia's Security Council has identified Islamic State (IS) as the greatest current threat to global peace, citing the group’s claim of establishing a province in Russia’s North Caucasus. Militants in multiple regions have pledged allegiance to IS, raising concerns that radicalization and the potential for terror attacks within Russia are increasing. Analysts note the significance of this shift among previously al-Qaeda-affiliated groups and warn that it may lead to further violence. The situation has prompted international discussions, including a call between Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Barack Obama addressing the IS threat. Local authorities, such as Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, downplay IS's claims but acknowledge the dangers, while the number of Russians attempting to join IS continues to grow.

238585_238585.caption: Serena Williams poses at the trophy presentation after winning her match against Garbine Muguruza to claim the 2015 Wimbledon women s singles title
238585_238585.article_context: Nationwide protests erupted following the fatal police shootings of two black men in Louisiana and Minnesota, resulting in clashes, arrests, and injuries to officers. Serena Williams and Andy Murray captured Wimbledon singles titles, with Williams equaling the Open Era Grand Slam record. Fox News chief Roger Ailes faced escalating sexual harassment allegations as over a dozen women came forward after Gretchen Carlson's lawsuit. In Spain, bullfighter Victor Barrio was fatally gored during a live broadcast, the first such death in over 30 years. Additionally, a single winning ticket for the $540 million Mega Millions jackpot was sold in Indiana, though the winner remains unknown.

291758_291758.caption: A man casts his ballot for the referendum on the peace agreement between the government and the FARC rebels in Cali Colombia
291758_291758.article_context: Colombians narrowly rejected a peace deal with the FARC guerrilla group in a national referendum, dividing the country over efforts to end its decades-long conflict. President Juan Manuel Santos vowed to continue pursuing peace despite the setback, maintaining the current ceasefire and planning to resume talks in Havana. Both the government and FARC leaders expressed commitment to finding an agreement, but uncertainty now looms over Colombia’s future path to peace. The failed deal, negotiated over four years, sought to end a 52-year war that has killed over 220,000 and displaced millions, but faced opposition due to perceived leniency toward rebels and insufficient reparations for victims.

1070019_1070019.caption: Kadiza Sultana Shamima Begum and Amira Abase going through security at Gatwick airport on their way to join Isis
1070019_1070019.article_context: In response to young British Muslims—including three London schoolgirls—leaving the UK to join Isis in Syria, activist Sara Khan and her organization Inspire have taken a prominent role in countering radicalisation, particularly among young women. Khan gained national attention through her widely circulated open letter rebutting Isis propaganda and has since worked with schools, community groups, and the government to teach educators and parents how to identify and resist radicalisation. While praised as an effective, authentic voice against extremism, Khan has also faced intense criticism from both Muslim communities and civil liberties groups for her support of the government’s Prevent anti-radicalisation strategy, which many see as heavy-handed and alienating to Muslims. As new government measures to combat both violent and non-violent extremism expand, Khan finds herself in a difficult position, viewed by some as too close to state policy while also believing that community-led efforts are essential to tackling extremism without eroding civil liberties.

1166923_1166923.caption: Litvinenko was poisoned with polonium210 a rare radioactive isotope made only at closed nuclear facilities controlled by Russia
1166923_1166923.article_context: Ahead of the inquiry report on Alexander Litvinenko's murder, British diplomats are advising Prime Minister David Cameron to exercise caution in responding to potential findings that implicate the Russian state, due to broader diplomatic interests such as cooperation over Syria. The inquiry, led by Sir Robert Owen, is expected to blame the former Russian agents Dmitry Kovtun and Andrei Lugovoi and may hold the Russian government responsible. Political pressure is mounting for targeted sanctions, similar to the US Magnitsky Act, but the Foreign Office prefers restraint to avoid escalating tensions with Moscow, especially since support for broader EU sanctions is waning and Russia’s cooperation remains crucial in international matters. The UK is expected to continue minimal cooperation with Russia's intelligence services and may seek extradition of the accused, though it is unlikely to succeed.

819195_819195.caption: A Cairo university student holds a flare during a protest against the acquittal of former president Hosni Mubarak over hundreds of deaths during the 2011 uprising
