461848_461848.caption: SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon campaigning at a shopping centre in Glasgow East I didn t think she would do so well said one panellist of the debate
461848_461848.article_context: In South Thanet, a focus group of voters reflected on the intense three-way competition between Ukip, Labour, and the Conservatives, with Labour's promise to scrap non-dom tax status energizing its core supporters and Ed Miliband's debate performance earning him renewed respect. However, personal attacks and negative campaigning were noted, and many still expected Ukip’s Nigel Farage to win the seat. In Glasgow East, undecided voters showed increasing support for the SNP, not for independence, but to give Scotland a stronger voice in Westminster. SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon was widely admired for her debate performance, while Labour's attempts to win back voters largely failed, except for concerns among some about splitting the vote and risking another Conservative government.

43218_43218.caption: Blue enjoys his reward for sniffing out explosives material on a moving target
43218_43218.article_context: The TSA is expanding its use of canine teams to screen passengers for explosives at airports, aiming to more than double the number of dogs and increase coverage to over 40 facilities by year’s end. These specially trained dogs detect bomb-making materials on moving people, helping both to identify potential threats and to clear low-risk travelers for expedited PreCheck screening. The canines, chosen for their friendly appearance, undergo rigorous training and are rewarded with toys for successful finds. This initiative enhances airport security by relying on the dogs’ advanced sense of smell, which can detect trace amounts of dangerous substances even in busy environments.

42972_42972.caption: A man is detained by police in front of Mama s Laundromat
42972_42972.article_context: Violence in Ward 7, one of Washington D.C.'s poorest and most violent areas, has sharply increased in 2016, with 21 homicides so far, nearly three times higher than the previous year and accounting for almost half the city’s total killings. Recent daylight shootings of Tayvon Devonte Cummings and Tracey Louise Cooper, believed linked to personal disputes, have underscored community anxiety and brought the issue into local political debates, with calls for urgent action and more police presence. Police Chief Cathy Lanier deployed extra officers and launched an early Summer Crime Initiative, though she cautioned that even increased law enforcement cannot always prevent determined acts of violence. Residents and business owners lament the ongoing trauma, while offering perspectives on the troubled but resilient neighborhood.

39699_39699.caption: ProEU protesters face riot police in front of the government headquarters in Kiev on December 9 2013
39699_39699.article_context: Paul Manafort, former Trump campaign chairman, resigned amid investigations into his extensive ties to pro-Russian political actors in Ukraine. Manafort began working with Ukrainian oligarchs and advised Viktor Yanukovych, a Putin ally, helping him win the presidency in 2010. His name appeared in secret ledgers as allegedly receiving millions in undisclosed payments from Yanukovych's party, though Manafort denies any wrongdoing. Additionally, Manafort's lobbying firm reportedly helped the pro-Russian Ukrainian government covertly influence U.S. media and funnel millions to prominent Washington lobbying firms, raising concerns about foreign interference and undisclosed payments.

55604_55604.caption: A member of the Iraqi forces rests on the front line near the village of Sin alDhuban south of Mosul
55604_55604.article_context: Iraqi and Kurdish forces, backed by U.S. air support, have launched a major offensive to retake Mosul from ISIS, encountering fierce resistance and extensive booby traps set by militants. Despite the obstacles—including suicide attacks, hidden explosives, and delayed advances due to coordination issues between Kurdish and Iraqi units—the coalition has made initial progress, capturing surrounding villages and advancing on key districts. The battle is expected to be prolonged and challenging, with ISIS employing defenses to slow the offensive. Both Iraqi and U.S. officials remain optimistic about eventual success.

43868_43868.caption: Donald Trump I understand the tax laws better than almost anyone
43868_43868.article_context: Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton both promised to address tax 'loopholes' in their presidential campaigns, but their approaches differ sharply. The recent disclosure of Trump’s use of a $916 million loss in 1995 to avoid paying income taxes highlighted these differences, as neither candidate’s plan would eliminate the provision that allowed such tax avoidance. Trump’s plan centers on cutting taxes for the wealthy, reducing corporate tax rates, and eliminating some loopholes like carried interest, while also adding new complexities and benefits for top earners. Clinton’s plan focuses on raising taxes on millionaires, closing loopholes that benefit the wealthy and corporations, and implementing policies like the Buffett Rule and higher estate taxes. Analyses show Trump’s plan would heavily benefit the richest Americans, whereas Clinton’s plan would have little effect on middle-income earners but substantially increase taxes for the top income bracket. Both candidates emphasize closing tax loopholes, responding to widespread voter concern about fairness in the tax system.

41816_41816.caption: Observers on a Japan Coast Guard Gulfstream aircraft discuss their mission brief before they begin searching for wreckage and debris
41816_41816.article_context: China is attempting to repair its relationship with Malaysia after intense criticism of Malaysia's handling of the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 caused a surge of Chinese nationalist anger and damaged diplomatic ties. Despite recent efforts by President Xi Jinping to strengthen ties through trade and diplomatic gestures, public outrage in China over the investigation strained relations, with protests and boycotts targeting Malaysia. The Chinese government initially encouraged strong reactions but later sought to soften its stance and shift blame toward Western media. Experts noted that significant diplomatic damage has been done, and restoring trust between the two countries may take years.

43455_43455.caption: A Bangladeshi border guard cries inside a prison van as he leaves a special court in Dhaka Bangladesh after a verdict in the 2009 mutiny
43455_43455.article_context: A Bangladesh court sentenced 152 people to death for their involvement in a 2009 mutiny by border guards, which resulted in the killing of dozens of military commanders. The mass trial included 846 defendants, with some receiving life sentences and others acquitted. The mutiny, driven by demands for equal pay and better conditions, caused deep tensions between the military and government. Human Rights Watch has criticized the credibility of the trial and called for a new one, citing inadequate legal representation and deaths of suspects in custody.

41944_41944.caption: After speaking in support of Ted Cruz Sarah Palin signed autographs and spoke to some of the 1000 Ted Cruz supporters during a rally for Cruz Friday July 27 2012 in The Woodlands Texas
41944_41944.article_context: Ted Cruz, a relatively unknown Texas Republican eighteen months ago, appears poised to win a runoff against Lt. Governor David Dewhurst, defying the state's GOP establishment and political expectations. Despite Dewhurst's strong fundraising, name recognition, and key endorsements, Cruz built support from national conservatives and the Tea Party, forcing a runoff and gaining momentum through strong fundraising and outside support. A Cruz victory would signal that GOP voters are willing to reject not only moderate or long-serving incumbents but also well-established conservative candidates deeply connected to the political establishment.

43281_43281.caption: People walk amid the rubble of destroyed buildings
43281_43281.article_context: Aleppo, Syria, suffered a new surge of deadly airstrikes and shelling, including attacks on a hospital and a mosque, resulting in more than 200 deaths within a week. The violence, carried out by both government and rebel forces, signals the collapse of a fragile cease-fire and has drawn international condemnation for the targeting of civilians and medical facilities. The UN, Doctors Without Borders, and rights organizations have denounced these violations of international law, warning that the situation in Aleppo is worsening amid concerns of an impending escalation.

448724_448724.caption: George Osborne All 26bn of business rates will be kept by councils instead of being sent up to Whitehall
448724_448724.article_context: Chancellor George Osborne announced major reforms to business rates, granting English councils the power to retain and control the full £26bn of business rate revenues, ending the uniform national rate. Councils will be able to cut rates to attract businesses, while only those with directly elected mayors can raise rates, using extra revenue for infrastructure projects. This move, described by Osborne as the largest transfer of power to local government in living memory, aims to incentivize enterprise and local growth but has sparked concerns about potential inequalities between councils and competitive tax cutting. Osborne also revealed the creation of a National Infrastructure Commission, chaired by Labour’s Lord Adonis.

47092_47092.caption: This image from a video released by the Israeli Defense Forces shows the downing of a drone that entered Israeli airspace in southern Israel Israeli jets scrambled to intercept a drone that crossed into Israeli airspace Saturday from the Mediterranean Sea bringing it down without incident in the south of the country a military spokeswoman said
47092_47092.article_context: At the 100-day mark of President Mohamed Morsi's term, Egyptians are openly evaluating his performance in a way unprecedented under previous authoritarian rule. While Morsi fulfilled only a handful of his 64 campaign promises, critics cite stalled services and unmet pledges, and only 42% of an online survey rated him favorably. Supporters, including the Muslim Brotherhood, argue Morsi made significant progress given Egypt's economic challenges and highlight shifts in foreign policy and political power away from the military. The broader significance lies in Egypt's emerging democracy, with robust public debate reflecting citizens' growing political empowerment after decades of repression.

46280_46280.caption: Rocky reefs in Kalbarri before left and after right a 2011 marine heatwave wiped out underwater forests of Australian kelps
46280_46280.article_context: A recent study revealed that an extreme marine heat wave in 2011 led to the widespread destruction of kelp forests in Australia's Great Southern Reef, similar to the well-known die-off of coral at the Great Barrier Reef. Ocean temperatures surged to record highs, causing a dramatic collapse of the kelp ecosystem, with some areas experiencing a complete loss of kelp. The study found that this event triggered a rapid and potentially irreversible shift in the ecosystem, allowing tropical species to take over. Researchers attribute the heat wave to climate change, warning that rising ocean temperatures are now devastative enough to threaten the adaptation and survival of sensitive marine habitats.

39906_39906.caption: The gorgeous colors of Yellowstone s Grand Prismatic hot spring are among the national park s myriad hydrothermal features created by the Yellowstone supervolcano A new University of Utah study reports discovery of a huge magma reservoir beneath Yellowstone s previously known magma chamber
39906_39906.article_context: Scientists from the University of Utah have published a study revealing a previously unknown, massive reservoir of hot rock beneath Yellowstone’s already-known magma chamber, providing the first comprehensive map of the volcano's underground 'plumbing.' This reservoir is much larger than the shallow magma chamber above and could fill the Grand Canyon, confirming Yellowstone remains a very active volcanic system. The discovery offers crucial insights into how giant caldera-forming eruptions may happen, although it does not fundamentally alter the current risk assessment, which estimates such catastrophic eruptions occur every several hundred thousand years. While there is no immediate indication of an impending eruption, the volcano’s unpredictable nature means ongoing scientific monitoring is essential.

39302_39302.caption: Police officers beat protesters as they try to disperse them outside the government headquarters
39302_39302.article_context: A Hong Kong court granted an injunction allowing authorities to potentially clear parts of a major protest site following violent clashes between police and pro-democracy demonstrators. The protests, demanding free elections in 2017 rather than Beijing-approved candidates, have lasted over two months despite crackdowns. Recent violence saw dozens injured and at least 40 arrests, revealing divisions among protest leaders. Some activists, including Joshua Wong, began a hunger strike to press for renewed government dialogue. Hong Kong’s chief executive warned of stricter enforcement going forward as international attention and diplomatic reactions continued.

452055_452055.caption: For the SNP s sums to add up the Bank of England will have to be relaxed about the abandonment of austerity
452055_452055.article_context: The SNP manifesto outlines ambitious policies, including higher minimum wage, increased NHS funding, and greater public spending, all without Labour's proposed spending cuts. The SNP aims to reduce the deficit by relying on strong economic growth rather than austerity measures. However, experts are skeptical that growth alone can close the deficit gap, and even optimistic revenue-raising measures, like a higher tax rate and Trident savings, are unlikely to make a significant impact. Ultimately, deficit reduction would be slower under SNP plans unless the economy performs exceptionally well.

471920_471920.caption: David Lammy would like to introduce a comprehensive programme of rent controls to protect tenants
471920_471920.article_context: David Lammy, former Labour minister known for his leadership during the 2011 London riots, has announced his candidacy for the Labour nomination for London mayor in 2016. The centerpiece of his campaign is tackling the city's housing crisis, with proposals including a programme of rent controls, a London landlords' register, and a new definition of 'affordable housing' linked to local earnings. Lammy will face strong competition from other senior Labour figures such as Tessa Jowell, Sadiq Khan, Margaret Hodge, and Diane Abbott. His announcement was accompanied by a detailed report outlining policy solutions to build the much-needed 63,000 homes annually in London.

56085_56085.caption: A proRussian supporter talks to Ukrainian policemen in Mariupol Ukraine Reports from Mariupol said that Interior Ministry troops had briefly regained control of the city administration building which had been occupied for weeks
56085_56085.article_context: Pro-Russian insurgents shot down a Ukrainian military helicopter near Slovyansk, eastern Ukraine, resulting in at least eight deaths and renewed fighting in the region. The Ukrainian government struggled to regain control over rebel-held cities and sent special police forces to Odessa after violent clashes and the release of detained militants. Ukrainian authorities also increased security nationwide and closed border crossings with Russian-annexed Crimea amid heightened tensions. Russia condemned Ukraine's military actions, while concerns about escalating violence and police loyalty persisted. The situation reflects deep instability as Ukraine faces difficulty asserting authority in its eastern regions.

45954_45954.caption: Mitt Romney seen here campaigning in Ohio in 2012 long ago ruled out a 2016 run but has been following the race closely and has ideas for the Republican Party to win back the White House
45954_45954.article_context: At a Georgetown University event, Mitt Romney, the 2012 Republican presidential nominee, discussed the 2016 election and criticized the current political climate, stating his belief that Donald Trump 'will not be the nominee' and predicting the Republican candidate would come from the mainstream conservative bracket instead. Romney expressed concerns over divisive rhetoric in the campaign and emphasized the need for Republicans to appeal to minority and working-class voters. He confirmed he would not run for president and shared his perspectives on domestic and foreign policy issues, including strong criticism of the Obama administration and the Iran nuclear deal.

42219_42219.caption: Ryan Anthony Salandy 22 of Germantown was charged with firstdegree murder in William McDaniel s death
42219_42219.article_context: Ryan Salandy, a 22-year-old known as the 'Christian Rapper,' stands accused of intentionally running over and killing William McDaniel following a dispute over a business transaction related to Christian rap music production. The incident took place in Clarksburg, Maryland, with Salandy later admitting to police he struck McDaniel on purpose. A judge has ordered Salandy to remain in jail without bond, citing the seriousness of the charges and public safety concerns. The case has deeply affected both families involved, with supporters of each present in court.

451334_451334.caption: Australia is banning the import and export of hunting trophies made from the body parts of lions
451334_451334.article_context: The Australian government has announced an immediate ban on the import and export of hunting trophies made from lion body parts, aiming to combat the cruel practice of 'canned hunting,' where captive-bred lions are killed by tourists. Environment minister Greg Hunt described canned hunting as inhumane and called for other countries to adopt similar measures to help protect declining lion populations. Conservation groups welcomed the move, noting that canned hunting contributes to the dwindling numbers of African lions, which have nearly halved in 25 years.

40174_40174.caption: Erika Civitarese a junior at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst rallies students at the campus Million Student March on Nov 12 2015
40174_40174.article_context: Thousands of students at over 100 college campuses participated in the Million Student March, demanding debt-free public college, the cancellation of all student debt, and a $15 minimum wage for campus workers. The movement was inspired in part by Senator Bernie Sanders’ calls for activism to address student debt and high tuition costs. Organizers sought to mobilize a broad coalition of students nationwide to highlight the growing burden of student loan debt and to press for significant reforms in higher education affordability.

41819_41819.caption: Administrative law judge Roy Pearson leaves court after the second day of his trial in Washington on June 13 2007 Jin and Soo Chung are being sued by Pearson for 54 million for what he calls misleading signage at their drycleaning business
41819_41819.article_context: Roy L. Pearson Jr., a former D.C. administrative judge who became nationally known for filing a $54 million lawsuit against a dry cleaner over a lost pair of pants, now faces possible disciplinary sanctions for his conduct during the case. A hearing committee found Pearson committed two ethics violations related to interfering with justice and making unsupported arguments, recommending he be put on probation from practicing law for two years. The final decision will be made by the D.C. Court of Appeals after further review.

41353_41353.caption: Fisherman unload their catch at the harbor in Tanmen Experts say that Chinese authorities consider fishing vessels tools to expand China s claims to disputed waters
41353_41353.article_context: China is increasingly deploying its vast fishing fleet, often backed by coast guard vessels and supported by government subsidies, to assert territorial claims in the disputed South China Sea. This strategy has intensified recent tensions with neighboring countries like Indonesia, Malaysia, and Vietnam, as Chinese fishing boats venture near their coasts, sometimes leading to confrontations and diplomatic incidents. Experts describe the approach as 'fish, protect, occupy and control,' with fishermen and organized maritime militia acting as the advance guard for China's broader ambitions of maritime dominance. This method not only furthers China’s economic and nationalistic interests but also raises ongoing risks of regional crises and international conflict.

454450_454450.caption: Labour lost their bid to delay the fuel duty increase until at least April by 48 votes
454450_454450.article_context: George Osborne avoided a Conservative backbench revolt by indicating the government might postpone a planned 3p fuel duty increase, following concerns over the cost of living. A Labour motion to delay the rise was defeated, but government ministers assured MPs that helping households remains a priority and a decision may come in the autumn statement. Key Conservative campaigners approved waiting for this announcement, while Labour argued for immediate action to aid struggling families amid rising fuel prices.

43906_43906.caption: Probe launched into DC baby s death and ambulance delay
43906_43906.article_context: After an infant in Southeast D.C. died while waiting for emergency medical help, city officials launched an investigation into the emergency response, as this incident highlighted the worsening shortage of available ambulances in Washington, D.C. Due to high call volumes and aging equipment, D.C. has increasingly relied on neighboring jurisdictions for ambulance support, but on the day of the incident, no help was available. The tragedy comes amid ongoing concerns and recent failures in the city's emergency response system, prompting pledges for more ambulances and improvements to address persistent delays and equipment shortages.

49877_49877.caption: The tent sheltering a family driven from their home by the battles
49877_49877.article_context: The Taliban has advanced to within four miles of Kunduz, a strategic northern Afghan city, marking their closest approach to a major urban center since being ousted in 2001. Over the weekend, they seized two key districts, trapping about 75 Afghan soldiers and policemen, and prompting Kabul to send reinforcements including special forces and U.S. advisers. The Taliban's offensive in Kunduz is part of a larger northern campaign supported by foreign fighters, aiming to establish a safe haven and destabilize the Afghan government. The escalation has led to a severe humanitarian crisis, with thousands of civilians displaced or caught in crossfire. Additionally, the Taliban staged a bold attack on the Afghan parliament, underscoring their capacity to strike national institutions even as they gain ground in provincial regions.

49607_49607.caption: A Pakistani supporter of cleric Tahirul Qadri uses a slingshot to lob a stone toward riot police during a protest in Islamabad
49607_49607.article_context: Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif is struggling to remain in power as mass protests in Islamabad led by opposition leaders Imran Khan and Tahirul Qadri grow increasingly violent, with demonstrators storming government buildings and clashing with police. Both leaders accuse Sharif of election fraud and poor economic management, demanding his resignation. The unrest has prompted fears of military intervention and political instability in Pakistan, a nuclear-armed country with a long history of coups. Despite mounting pressure, Sharif has refused to step down, and the military has issued statements supporting democracy while denying involvement in the crisis.

42416_42416.caption: Shin Donghyuk poses in Paris on May 2 2012 before a news conference to present the book Escape from Camp 14 by former Washington Post journalist Blaine Harden
42416_42416.article_context: Shin Dong-hyuk, a prominent North Korean prison camp survivor and human rights activist, has admitted that some details of his widely publicized story, including locations and timing of events, were inaccurate. Despite apologizing for these inconsistencies, Shin maintains that the abuses he described did occur and urges supporters to continue campaigning against North Korea’s human rights violations. His revised account comes as he faces pressure and scrutiny from fellow defectors and the North Korean regime, raising concerns among activists that this revelation could weaken international efforts to hold North Korea accountable for human rights abuses.

454162_454162.caption: Gordon Brown David Cameron and Nick Clegg will go headtohead in three live debates filmed in front of studio audiences
454162_454162.article_context: Gordon Brown, David Cameron, and Nick Clegg will participate in Britain's first-ever live televised prime ministerial debates during next year's general election campaign, following an agreement between the main parties and broadcasters. Three debates will air in prime time on ITV, Sky, and BBC, with each focusing on key topics such as the economy and public services. The format excludes smaller parties and Channel Four, drawing criticism from SNP and others. The debates provide Nick Clegg an opportunity to raise his profile, while Conservative supporters fear the move could aid Labour’s campaign. Separate regional debates will be held, and minor parties will be given subsequent opportunities to respond on BBC output.

39713_39713.caption: Displaced families from Ramadi wait in miles of traffic while fleeing an offensive by Islamic State militants in the Iraqi province of Anbar
39713_39713.article_context: Thousands of Iraqi families fled Ramadi as Islamic State forces advanced, overwhelming security services and causing chaos at checkpoints leading to Baghdad. Despite months of U.S.-led airstrikes, Ramadi is at risk of falling to the militants, threatening Iraq's stability and efforts to reclaim territory. The crisis has led to mass displacement, with reports of security forces retreating and strained relations between Sunni locals, the government, and Shiite militias. The Iraqi government is rushing reinforcements to the city, but humanitarian concerns and political tensions persist as local leaders and citizens criticize insufficient support.

49779_49779.caption: A man cuts the beard of another man who was evacuated by the SDF fighters from Manbij Men had been forced to refrain from cutting their beards for months
49779_49779.article_context: Turkey has launched a military offensive into northern Syria, escalating tensions between two major U.S.-backed groups: Syrian Kurdish forces and Arab/Turkmen rebels. Central to the conflict is the strategic town of Manbij, recently seized from ISIS by Kurdish fighters, whom Turkey wants out of the area to prevent further Kurdish expansion. Despite Kurdish claims of withdrawal, Turkey continued airstrikes against Kurdish positions and supported rebel advances, while clashes broke out between Turkish-backed rebels and Kurdish-aligned fighters near Jarabulus. This situation threatens to pit U.S.-supported groups against each other, complicating efforts to defeat ISIS and highlighting challenges in U.S. coalition strategy. Turkey’s main objectives are securing its border, blocking Kurdish territorial gains that could embolden Kurdish separatists within Turkey, and clearing ISIS and other groups from the region.

448167_448167.caption: Clearing up in the aftermath of superstorm Sandy
448167_448167.article_context: A draft report from US government scientists warns that global warming is already causing significant disruptions in America, such as increased floods, droughts, and damage to agriculture and infrastructure. The report attributes these changes primarily to human activities, especially the burning of fossil fuels. It stresses that severe weather events like superstorm Sandy will become more common, putting greater pressure on health, water, and transportation systems. The report argues that adaptation alone is insufficient, urging urgent international action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and highlighting that climate change is an immediate and ongoing issue.

40313_40313.caption: An undated image shows how the Soviets continued their effort to build their military forces within Cuba as negotiations between President John F Kennedy and Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev wore on This photo showed Soviet technicians assembling Ilyushin28 bombers that had been shipped in parts to Cuba
40313_40313.article_context: Recently released archival documents from the Cuban missile crisis underline the importance of understanding adversaries' true nuclear intentions, which holds lessons for today's Iran policy. The documents reveal that Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev did not support a nuclear first strike, contrary to U.S. assumptions at the time, leading both countries to dramatically expand their nuclear arsenals. This historical misunderstanding is compared to current uncertainties about Iran’s nuclear ambitions, with U.S. intelligence suggesting Iran wants nuclear capability but Iran’s leaders publicly denying intentions to build nuclear weapons. The article emphasizes the lessons of caution, verification, and the risk of escalation inherent in nuclear diplomacy.

43639_43639.caption: Norton says she ll cast a DC ballot for budget autonomy
43639_43639.article_context: Key Hill Democrats, including Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton and Rep. Jose Serrano, expressed support for a proposed budget autonomy referendum for the District of Columbia, which would give D.C. residents more direct control over their budget. Norton and Serrano both emphasized continued efforts in Congress for broader autonomy, maintaining a two-track strategy. Mayor Vincent C. Gray also confirmed he would vote in favor of the referendum, signaling broad local political support for the initiative.

49391_49391.caption: Residents gather outside the hideout of bin Laden Pakistani officials said the world must share the blame for failing to unearth bin Laden as a furor swelled over how the slain alQaeda leader had managed to live undisturbed near Islamabad
49391_49391.article_context: Army Gen. Raymond 'Tony' Thomas, head of U.S. Special Operations Command, publicly criticized the growing trend of current and former special operations personnel publishing books, starring in movies, and advising video games about their missions. He argued these actions violate operational security and damage the ethos of secrecy that is essential for such units. His remarks followed a major settlement with Navy SEAL Matt Bissonnette, who forfeited profits from his book on the Bin Laden raid after breaching nondisclosure agreements. Thomas emphasized that this issue affects all branches of special operations, warning that increased publicity undermines their effectiveness and calling for a return to greater discretion.

458275_458275.caption: A red deer stag between mature Scots pines in the Highlands The species faces a severe threat from two foreign pathogens
458275_458275.article_context: Scientists warn that the Scots pine, a symbolically and economically important British tree, is at high risk of being devastated by foreign pathogens already spreading in Europe. Following the ash dieback disease that threatens to wipe out most of Britain's ash trees, experts fear the Scots pine could be next, threatened by the pine wood nematode and the pitch canker fungus. Both pathogens are established in continental Europe and could soon reach the UK, with experts highlighting the rapid spread of tree diseases due to increased international plant trade and insufficient biosecurity measures. Researchers recommend stronger controls, such as plant passports and quarantines, to protect Britain's trees from further infections.

53814_53814.caption: A boy in the Malian town of Diabalay stands next to a French national flag hung on a goalpost meant to welcome French soldiers
53814_53814.article_context: French troops were welcomed as liberators in Diabaly, Mali, after driving out Islamist rebels who had seized the town. Residents expressed relief and gratitude for the intervention, citing the rebels' cruelty and the lack of civilian casualties from French airstrikes. Both Christian and Muslim locals felt safer after the militants' departure, though concerns remained about the rebels hiding nearby. While the initial reaction to French forces was positive, the article notes that prolonged foreign military presence could eventually change local attitudes.

49815_49815.caption: A Pakistani army ambulance arrives at Lady Reading Hospital in Peshawar after gunmen attacked the school
49815_49815.article_context: Taliban gunmen attacked an elite army-run school in Peshawar, Pakistan, killing at least 141 students and teachers in what was seen as retaliation for recent military offensives in North Waziristan. The massacre, targeting children in a military institution, provoked widespread outrage and unified condemnation across Pakistan's political and religious spectrum, as well as from international and even some Taliban figures. The Pakistani Taliban quickly claimed responsibility, stating the attack was a response to the army's actions. The tragedy intensified calls for decisive action against terrorism, highlighting persistent challenges in Pakistan’s approach to Islamist militancy.

51390_51390.caption: A Marine tells an Iraqi detained on suspicion of looting to be quiet and keep his head down About six looters were arrested after robbing a bank in Baghdad Local residents cheered Marines who captured the looters
51390_51390.article_context: A decade after the US invasion of Iraq, the country remains in a fragile state, balancing signs of progress with persistent chaos. While the Kurdish north and Shiite southern provinces experience economic and social growth, Sunni regions face disenfranchisement and ongoing protest against the central Shiite-led government. Sectarian and regional tensions, especially disputes between Baghdad and Kurdish authorities, fuel instability and periodic violence, including deadly bombings. Despite improved conditions in some areas, Iraq's political divisions and lack of US influence have left its future uncertain and vulnerable to renewed conflict.

42966_42966.caption: Mourners carry the body of Mehmet Agabey who was killed in an attempted coup during a memorial service at Kirazlitepe Omer Orhan Mosque in Istanbul
42966_42966.article_context: The Turkish government successfully suppressed an attempted military coup that sought to overthrow President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. In the aftermath, authorities detained thousands, including senior military officials and members of the judiciary suspected of involvement. The coup resulted in at least 265 deaths and significant violence in Istanbul and Ankara, with large crowds responding to Erdogan's call to support the government. Erdogan blamed U.S.-based cleric Fethullah Gulen for orchestrating the plot and demanded his extradition, while the U.S. supported a thorough investigation. The failed coup has raised concerns about further government crackdowns and the future stability of Turkey’s democracy and military standing.

49098_49098.caption: Harvard professor Henry Louis Gates Jr left Sgt James Crowley of the Cambridge Mass police department and Obama hoist their glasses during the beer summit in 2009 at the White House
49098_49098.article_context: As the first African American president, Barack Obama has faced the challenge of balancing the high expectations of black Americans with the broader responsibilities of leading a diverse nation. Throughout his presidency, Obama has grappled with issues of racial identity, criticism from both black and white constituencies, and racially charged controversies like the arrest of Harvard professor Henry Louis Gates Jr. While black voters remain steadfast in their support, polling shows a decline in white support and increasing racial polarization ahead of the 2012 election. Obama has sought to address the unique struggles of black communities while avoiding the appearance of favoritism, often working quietly behind the scenes with black leaders and business figures. Ultimately, Obama's presidency has symbolized significant progress for African Americans, yet questions persist about how much he can or should do specifically for black communities while serving as president for all Americans.

44437_44437.caption: Aiken prepares for an oncamera interview outside the facade of a general store at a regional fair He wo nt sing as he runs for Congress but he ll happily talk about immigration health care and veterans issues
44437_44437.article_context: Clay Aiken, former 'American Idol' runner-up, has shifted from his music career to running for Congress as a Democrat in North Carolina’s 2nd District—a predominantly Republican area. Despite his fame, Aiken faces skepticism about his political credibility and struggles with fundraising, as both Hollywood and local donors remain hesitant. While he leverages his celebrity for visibility, Aiken emphasizes his North Carolina roots and advocacy work, seeking to be seen as a serious candidate rather than a pop star. His campaign highlights his personal story and dedication to listening to constituents, but breaking out of his entertainer image remains a major challenge.

461297_461297.caption: David Cameron has warned he will not rein in current austerity measures even if the UK economy does not start to recover soon
461297_461297.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron has asserted that he will not weaken austerity measures, even if the UK's economy continues to struggle, dismissing public and political pressure revealed in a poll showing 59% of voters supported slowing spending cuts. Cameron argued that changing course would risk Britain's financial stability and higher interest rates. He emphasized his commitment to maintaining austerity, stating he would rather serve one term as prime minister doing 'the right thing' than compromise for electoral gain.

42862_42862.caption: An investigator points to El Centro College while working the scene of a shooting in downtown Dallas Friday July 8 2016 Snipers opened fire on police officers in the heart of Dallas during protests over two recent fatal police shootings of black men
42862_42862.article_context: El Centro College in Dallas went into lockdown after a peaceful protest against police shootings turned deadly, with a sniper targeting police officers outside the campus. The attack resulted in the deaths of at least five officers and injuries to seven others. The suspect, who expressed anger over recent police shootings, was killed by police using a bomb robot after a prolonged standoff. No students or staff from the college were injured, but the campus remained closed as authorities investigated, and damage to several buildings was assessed. Counseling services were being provided remotely to those affected.

42344_42344.caption: Relatives of missing passengers block a car carrying South Korean Prime Minister Jung Hongwon during a protest in Jindo to demand a meeting with President Park Geunhye
42344_42344.article_context: Yoo Byung-un, the elusive billionaire linked to the sinking of a South Korean ferry that killed hundreds, was found dead in an orchard, ending the country's largest manhunt. Yoo, who led a church considered a cult and had a history of fraud, became the focus of investigations after the disaster. Authorities sought him for embezzlement and other charges related to the company behind the ferry, though his direct connection was disputed. His mysterious death raised further questions, while his followers remained fiercely loyal amid allegations and controversy.

42568_42568.caption: Washington PostABC News poll Dec 1721 2014 among 1011 adults conducted on conventional and cellular phones
42568_42568.article_context: A new Washington Post-ABC News poll shows strong and growing American support for reestablishing diplomatic ties with Cuba and ending the longstanding trade and travel bans. Sixty-four percent of Americans support diplomatic relations, while 68 percent favor ending the trade embargo and 74 percent back lifting travel restrictions, with increased support across party lines since 2009. Although most Republicans still split on diplomatic relations and GOP leaders in Congress are moving to block President Obama’s recent policy changes, majorities among Democrats, independents, and Hispanics support normalization. A separate poll of Cuban Americans found views more divided, with younger and U.S.-born Cuban Americans generally more supportive of Obama’s policy shift.

460175_460175.caption: Floating PennywortWhy One of the most invasive water plants in Britain Established in 1990 it will completely congest a river or canal changing the water course and affecting many other plants and animals After being removed it will regrow vigorously from even the smallest section of remaining stem Early warning is the best way to try to manage itMore information bitlyobserverpennywortReport to nonnativespeciesorgrecordingWhen to spot it All year
460175_460175.article_context: Several non-native species, such as the American signal crayfish, grey squirrel, muntjac deer, ring-necked parakeet, red-eared terrapin, harlequin ladybird, horse-chestnut leaf-miner, rhododendron, floating pennywort, and Himalayan balsam, have become established in Britain over recent decades. These species pose various threats to local ecosystems, outcompeting native wildlife, damaging trees and habitats, and altering environments. Conservationists and government agencies are monitoring their impacts and encouraging the public to report sightings to help manage and control their spread.

41614_41614.caption: After Ruwaished drivers face empty sometimes narrow roads to Baghdad or Mosul that are prowled by brigands and punctuated by rolling roadblocks operated by Islamic State militants
41614_41614.article_context: Truckers hauling goods from Jordan into Islamic State-controlled areas of Iraq face extreme danger and hardship, navigating lawless roads, frequent roadblocks, and threats from militants and militias. Despite the perilous conditions—marked by the risk of violence, bombings, and extortion—the route remains a vital lifeline supplying food, medicine, and other essentials to besieged Iraqi cities. The number of trucks crossing has sharply decreased since Islamic State’s rise, but many drivers are still drawn by the lucrative pay, often traveling in convoys and paying hefty 'taxes' to pass through militant checkpoints. The treacherous journey highlights the ongoing crisis in Iraq and the resilience of those sustaining its civilian population under siege.

460223_460223.caption: A chemical plant in Hefei China Some developing countries will present commitments that are partly conditional ie depending on financial support said Fabius
460223_460223.article_context: Ahead of the crucial UN climate conference in Paris this December, French foreign minister Laurent Fabius has warned that developed countries must uphold their financial commitments to poorer nations or risk jeopardizing global climate negotiations. The G7 will discuss climate finance, as poor countries expect at least $100bn per year from rich nations—promised at Copenhagen in 2009—to help them cut emissions and adapt to climate change. So far, only about half of this target has been met, with disagreements on what constitutes 'climate finance.' Fabius insists that concrete deals on both emission limits and financial support must be secured before the Paris talks, emphasizing that trust and solidarity between rich and poor nations are essential for a successful global climate agreement.

42691_42691.caption: Sanders knocks Clinton ahead of more primaries
42691_42691.article_context: A new Bloomberg poll shows Bernie Sanders with a narrow national lead over Hillary Clinton in the Democratic primary race, with Sanders at 49% and Clinton at 48%. This close contest contrasts with earlier polls that gave Clinton a substantial lead. The poll reveals that Sanders' strength comes from Democratic voters’ concerns about economic issues, where he is seen as stronger than Clinton, while Clinton leads on foreign policy. However, foreign policy is less of a priority for Democratic voters compared to the economy. Controversies surrounding Clinton, such as her ties to Wall Street and changes in stance on trade deals, also concern voters, while Sanders’ lack of foreign policy experience is his main weakness. Despite Sanders’ polling boost, Clinton retains a significant advantage in pledged delegates, making it hard for Sanders to overtake her in the overall race.

50429_50429.caption: Gov Charlie Crist right and President Obama hug in 2009 The embrace helped to derail Crist s career in the Republican party
50429_50429.article_context: Former Florida Governor Charlie Crist’s embrace of President Barack Obama in 2009 became a defining moment in his political career, sparking backlash among conservatives and undermining his Senate campaign as a Republican. After losing support within his party, Crist switched to run as an independent, eventually aligning with Democrats and running for office under their banner. The event is widely regarded as one of the most significant and controversial gestures in recent American politics, symbolizing Crist’s shift across the political spectrum.

43184_43184.caption: A Syrian civil defense member and a volunteer carry a little girl rescued from under the rubble of destroyed buildings after a reported airstrike
43184_43184.article_context: The Syrian government has blocked United Nations aid convoys from entering besieged areas of Aleppo despite a cease-fire brokered by the United States and Russia, raising concerns about the effectiveness of the truce and humanitarian access. Although fighting has decreased and a demilitarized corridor was agreed on, security and mistrust between government forces and rebel groups have stalled the distribution of vital supplies. The impasse has led UN officials to criticize both the Syrian government's restrictive permit process and the lack of trust between both sides, while possible tensions between Washington and Moscow threaten broader cooperation under the cease-fire agreement.

41786_41786.caption: Gay rights advocate Vin Testa waves a rainbow flag in front of the Supreme Court on June 26 2013
41786_41786.article_context: Federal employees played a crucial but understated role in the progress of marriage equality, with early legal challenges to the Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA) initiated by figures such as Nancy Gill, a postal worker. Gill’s lawsuit was among the first major challenges to DOMA’s Section 3, paving the way for federal recognition of same-sex marriages. The Supreme Court’s recent decision to uphold lower court rulings effectively allows same-sex marriages in most states, building on last year's landmark Windsor decision, which was itself influenced by Gill’s case. The collective efforts of these individuals have been key drivers behind the rapid advancement of gay marriage rights in the United States.

448526_448526.caption: Pipe dreams the 500km pipeline that transports oil from Lago Agrio to the port of Esmeraldas on the Pacific Coast The oil discovery destroyed the area
448526_448526.article_context: Yasuni National Park in Ecuador is considered one of the most biodiverse places on the planet, home to vast numbers of unique insects, plants, birds, and mammals, as well as isolated indigenous tribes. In 2007, the discovery of nearly a billion barrels of oil beneath Yasuni sparked debate between exploiting the oil for financial gain or preserving the untouched rainforest. Led by former oil minister-turned-ecologist Alberto Acosta, Ecuador proposed leaving the oil untouched in exchange for international compensation to protect the park and invest in renewable energy. This Yasuni initiative, backed by donors and administered by a UN trust, aims to conserve the park and prevent the environmental devastation seen in other oil-rich regions. While there is widespread support for conservation, the threat of oil exploitation and its destructive consequences remains a pressing concern for Yasuni’s future.

50797_50797.caption: Ukraine calls for peacekeepers as its soldiers withdraw
50797_50797.article_context: Hopes for a cease-fire in Ukraine have faded as fighting intensified across the eastern region, particularly following the Ukrainian military’s defeat and chaotic withdrawal from Debaltseve, a key railway hub now controlled by pro-Russian rebels. The government reported significant casualties and missing soldiers, while President Poroshenko requested U.N. peacekeepers, signaling waning faith in Ukraine's ability to defend itself alone. Russia opposes the peacekeeping plan, and both sides continue to use heavy weaponry, violating last week’s Minsk peace agreement. Internal dissent is growing within Ukraine’s government and military, while European leaders insist on upholding the cease-fire despite ongoing violence.

41765_41765.caption: Brian Williams loses his Nightly home
41765_41765.article_context: NBC News announced that suspended anchor Brian Williams will return to the network, but not as anchor of 'NBC Nightly News.' Williams will instead take on a role covering breaking news at MSNBC and serve as a substitute for major NBC broadcasts. His suspension followed revelations of numerous exaggerated reports, damaging his credibility. Lester Holt, who filled in during Williams’s absence, will become the permanent 'Nightly News' anchor, marking a historic appointment as the first African American solo anchor of a network newscast. NBC management expressed support for second chances, while Williams apologized publicly and pledged to regain trust in his new role.

52701_52701.caption: Destyni Tyree is a 16yearold who has lived at the homeless shelter with her mother and younger sister since February She is excited about the new teen lounge area planned for the homeless shelter as there are few places for her and other girls to hang out she says
52701_52701.article_context: The Homeless Children’s Playtime Project, a nonprofit, is leading an initiative to create a dedicated teen center at D.C. General, Washington D.C.’s largest homeless shelter. The renovated space will give teens and tweens a safe area to use computers, do homework, and socialize, addressing their need for independence and privacy. The project, funded in part by a $30,000 grant from Lowe’s and supported by volunteers and city officials, aims to improve living conditions for homeless youth and is set to open in October. This effort follows the group’s successful campaign for a playground at the shelter and reflects increased attention to the needs of homeless children in the city.

453923_453923.caption: Chemical dispersant spreads after being released into the Gulf of Mexico this month
453923_453923.article_context: Scientists and officials have expressed grave concerns over BP's use of an untested toxic dispersant, Corexit 9500, to mitigate the Gulf of Mexico oil spill following the Deepwater Horizon rig explosion. Despite warnings about potential environmental and health risks, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency approved the chemical for deep-sea application, heightening controversy over its impact on marine life. President Obama strongly criticized oil executives and regulators for ongoing blame-shifting and called for accountability. Efforts to contain the leak have failed so far, with BP planning additional stop-gap measures in the coming days. Experts warn that the long-term effects of the dispersants are unknown and that they may harm a wide range of marine species, while substantial oil slicks threaten Louisiana’s delicate coastal wetlands.

457771_457771.caption: A pond in Khomnal village at Mangalwheda in Solapur Maharashtra has become completely dry It serves primarily as recharge for ground water sources in the village and usually has water around the year
457771_457771.article_context: A Greenpeace-commissioned report reveals that existing coal power plants use enough water to supply 1 billion people, a figure that could nearly double if all planned plants are built, with almost half of these new plants located in areas already suffering high water stress. The study found that a significant number of current and planned coal plants are in regions where water use is unsustainable, particularly in China, India, and Turkey. Greenpeace calls for a halt to coal expansion in these water-stressed 'red list' regions, the phase-out of existing plants, especially older ones, and the transition to renewable energy to save both water resources and reduce climate impacts.

55051_55051.caption: An Afghan policeman checks the scene next to the damaged entrance of a restaurant that was attacked in Kabul The target of the attack was La Taverna du Liban a Lebanese restaurant in the heart of Kabul s most exclusive and heavily guarded residential district
55051_55051.article_context: A Taliban attack on the popular Kabul restaurant La Taverna du Liban resulted in the deaths of at least 21 people, including the beloved proprietor Kamel Hamade, shattering the sense of security once felt by the international and Afghan community who frequented the establishment. The restaurant, known as a sanctuary amid Kabul's instability, had become a symbol of civility and comfort for many. This violent incident marked a profound loss for the city's social scene and highlighted the growing danger and uncertainty faced by residents and foreigners in Afghanistan.

468726_468726.caption: Vince Cable will unveil plans to shine a harsh light into the murky world of corporate behaviour
468726_468726.article_context: Business Secretary Vince Cable is set to deliver a forceful critique of capitalism, highlighting issues such as corporate short-termism and unchecked market behavior. At the Liberal Democrat conference, he will announce a major consultation aimed at reforming takeovers and executive pay, with the goal of increasing shareholder influence and improving corporate transparency. Cable's remarks, which liken current practices to destroying competition for profit, have drawn criticism from business leaders but are defended as necessary for proper market regulation. The initiative comes as the government also warns banks against excessive bonuses, threatening higher taxes if they persist.

41940_41940.caption: The body of a victim killed during Wednesday s clashes is carried from a mosque in Cairo
41940_41940.article_context: The Obama administration plans to significantly curb nonessential military aid to Egypt, including halting the delivery of Apache helicopters, following the military's ousting of President Mohamed Morsi three months ago. Essential aid for counterterrorism, border security, and support for maintaining Egypt’s peace with Israel will continue. The decision reflects U.S. frustration with Egypt’s slow progress toward new elections and ongoing political violence. The move aims to pressure Egypt's military government while maintaining some strategic ties, amid longstanding U.S. aid linked to the country’s peace agreement with Israel.

451062_451062.caption: Boats tackle the blaze on the Deepwater Horizon oil rig in the Gulf of Mexico which exploded on 21 April
451062_451062.article_context: Over 90 oil workers were evacuated from Statoil’s Gullfaks platform in the North Sea due to a dangerous build-up of pressure in an offshore well, raising fears of a possible explosion and environmental disaster. Statoil responded by pumping cement to control the situation, while halting about 70,000 barrels of daily oil production. This incident is the third well control issue on Gullfaks within six months, prompting daily consultations between Statoil and Norway’s petroleum safety regulators. Environmental groups and industry critics have raised concerns about regulatory shortcomings and the ongoing risks of offshore oil extraction, especially in light of recent accidents.

41743_41743.caption: A trail of roses line the road in St Louis where Michael Brown was killed
41743_41743.article_context: Hillary Clinton addressed the shooting death of Michael Brown in Ferguson, expressing grief for Brown's family and the local community, and urging Americans to rebuild trust and confront ongoing racial inequities in the justice system. She praised President Obama for sending Attorney General Eric Holder to Ferguson and called for peace, justice, and reconciliation in the aftermath of the incident. Clinton linked the urgency of these issues to the enduring mission set forth by Martin Luther King Jr.

467782_467782.caption: Peter Robinson left and Martin McGuinness Robinson said The PSNI must not be the subject of republican bullyboy tactics
467782_467782.article_context: The ongoing police questioning of Sinn Féin president Gerry Adams over the 1972 murder of Jean McConville has sparked political tensions in Northern Ireland. First minister Peter Robinson accused Sinn Féin of attempting to blackmail and intimidate the police, while Sinn Féin hinted they might reconsider their support for policing if Adams is charged. Adams remains in custody, with detectives facing a deadline to charge or release him. The incident has deepened divisions between the Democratic Unionist Party and Sinn Féin, and McConville's daughter has vowed to pursue a civil case against Adams regardless of the police outcome.

45341_45341.caption: Faheema Titi s hands are covered with the blood of her brother Mahmoud Titi after embracing him during his funeral at the AlFawwar Palestinian refugee camp near the West Bank town of Hebron Israeli troops shot Mahmoud Titi on Tuesday after he and others hurled rocks and firebombs at them the military said The death was the latest in a new uptick in violence in the area where protests in support of prisoners held in Israeli jails have led to clashes between the Palestinian protesters and Israeli forces
45341_45341.article_context: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has finalized a coalition agreement with Yair Lapid’s centrist Yesh Atid party and Naftali Bennett’s right-wing Jewish Home party, allowing the formation of a new government ahead of President Obama’s upcoming visit. The coalition excludes the ultra-Orthodox parties that have traditionally held significant influence, potentially reducing funding for religious institutions and ending military service exemptions for ultra-Orthodox men. Key cabinet positions will go to Lapid (finance minister) and Bennett (economy and trade minister), while Netanyahu retains control over the defense and foreign ministries. The coalition’s composition sends mixed signals about future peace negotiations with the Palestinians, as Yesh Atid supports talks while Jewish Home backs settlement expansion. The government, holding 68 out of 120 seats, is considered fragile and vulnerable to collapse if key partners withdraw.

43486_43486.caption: Supporters of Macri celebrate his win in downtown Buenos Aires
43486_43486.article_context: Mauricio Macri was elected president of Argentina, defeating ruling party candidate Daniel Scioli with 51.4% of the vote, marking the end of 12 years of leftist rule under the Kirchners. Macri, the mayor of Buenos Aires and a businessman, rose to prominence by tapping into widespread frustration over government corruption, economic stagnation, and rising inflation. His victory signals a shift away from Argentina's protectionist policies and combative nationalism, with promises to reform the economy, attract foreign investment, and improve relations with the United States. The election reflects a broader change in Latin American politics, as centrist and conservative voices gain ground.

50592_50592.caption: On June 24 2013 the Pakistan Association of Tour Operators hold a demonstration to condemn the killing of foreign tourists by Islamic militants Their country s already embattled tourism industry is struggling to deal with cancellations after a vicious attack on a group of climbers
50592_50592.article_context: A planned family trip to Pakistan's Fairy Meadow was canceled after a deadly terrorist attack by the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) at a hotel near Nanga Parbat, which killed 10 people, mostly foreign tourists. This incident is part of a recent wave of Taliban violence in Pakistan, including attacks on a women's university and a mosque, leading to numerous civilian deaths and highlighting the dangers faced by both locals and visitors. While the Pakistani government has sought political dialogue with the TTP, ongoing U.S. drone strikes and Taliban retaliation have complicated peace efforts. The persistent violence has left innocent civilians and tourism at risk, undermining hopes for stability in the region.

455303_455303.caption: Gordon Brown and Ed Balls wanted strict conditions to be met before Britain joined the euro
455303_455303.article_context: After World War II, European integration was led by France and Germany, with Britain initially staying on the sidelines before applying for membership in the 1960s. The UK's entry into the European Economic Community was delayed by a French veto but finally happened in 1973. The 1975 referendum confirmed public support for staying in, but debates over Europe continued to divide both major parties. Margaret Thatcher initially supported the EEC but later became a leading Eurosceptic, influencing the Conservative Party’s growing opposition to further political and economic union. These divisions persisted under John Major, whose leadership was plagued by internal Tory disputes. Under Labour, Tony Blair and Gordon Brown were pro-European but split on joining the euro. Rising Euroscepticism, particularly within the Conservative party and fueled by the emergence of UKIP, led David Cameron to promise a renegotiation of EU membership terms and an in/out referendum, setting the stage for a major decision on Britain’s future in the EU.

52992_52992.caption: Russians look skyward as the vapor trail of the falling meteorite passes over Chelyabinsk before crashlanding
52992_52992.article_context: On the same day that a large asteroid safely passed by Earth as expected, an undetected meteor exploded over Chelyabinsk, Russia, injuring around 1,200 people and damaging thousands of buildings. The meteor, the largest to impact Earth since 1908, created a powerful shockwave and highlighted the limitations of current asteroid detection systems, as it was too small and approached from a sun-blinded direction. The event has renewed calls for greater investment in planetary defense and highlighted the unpredictable threat posed by space objects, coinciding with ongoing international discussions about improving asteroid tracking and response capabilities.

466782_466782.caption: David Cameron wielded the UK veto at the EU summit
466782_466782.article_context: UK Prime Minister David Cameron used his veto to block an EU treaty aimed at addressing the eurozone crisis, a move that pleased Conservative Eurosceptics and the City of London but left Britain diplomatically isolated within Europe. While Cameron argued he was protecting the UK's financial sector from tighter EU regulation, the decision risks reducing Britain's influence in the EU and straining the coalition government with the Liberal Democrats. The veto could have significant economic and diplomatic repercussions if the eurozone crisis escalates, and has sparked debate over Britain's future relationship with Europe.

41311_41311.caption: Kim Davis gives water to her husband Mark in October at Sentara Hospice House in Virginia Beach Mark who had an aggressive form of prostate cancer died a few days later
41311_41311.article_context: The article highlights growing concerns in the U.S. medical system about the overuse of aggressive, often futile, treatments for chronically ill and elderly patients at the end of life, often resulting in unnecessary suffering and high costs. Dr. Paul Marik and other ICU staff criticize the practice of prolonging death rather than improving patient comfort, pointing to financial incentives and reluctance among families and doctors to face mortality. The story underscores the importance of advance care planning and hospice care, illustrated by a patient's transition from distressing interventions in the ICU to a more peaceful end-of-life experience in hospice after her family's difficult decision. The piece calls for greater awareness and action to ensure patients' preferences are respected and unnecessary interventions are avoided.

41512_41512.caption: Some residents of the proGaddafi town of Tawurgha were executed and others were exiled from their homes which were then damaged as a way to send a message
41512_41512.article_context: Libya is currently divided between two rival governments, each claiming legitimacy and supported by different power bases, with Prime Minister Abdullah al-Thinni in the east and Prime Minister Khalifa al-Ghwell in the capital, Tripoli. The country is mired in civil war, economic collapse, and increasing lawlessness, with Islamist groups like the Islamic State growing bolder. The United Nations is attempting to broker a unity government to resolve the crisis, but deep divisions, powerful militias, and competing factions over control of resources—especially oil—pose significant obstacles. If no agreement is reached soon, Libya risks losing international recognition entirely, further destabilizing the nation and potentially inviting renewed foreign involvement.

40792_40792.caption: Tim Wirth s 1993 testimony on whackamole antiterrorism policy
40792_40792.article_context: President Obama invoked the 'Whac-a-Mole' metaphor to describe the challenges of fighting terrorism in the Middle East, highlighting the need to develop local security forces rather than continuously chasing emerging threats. The article reviews the history of this metaphor in U.S. military and political discourse, illustrating how officials have repeatedly likened the fight against terrorism and insurgency to a futile game in which eliminated threats quickly reappear elsewhere. Past leaders and analysts have called for more adaptive and coordinated strategies, underscoring the long-standing concern that a purely reactive approach leads to ongoing instability and risks. The piece also briefly notes the origin of the Whac-a-Mole game and its inventor's later mishap.

46685_46685.caption: Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton waves to supporters in Columbia after winning the South Carolina primary
46685_46685.article_context: Hillary Clinton won a decisive victory in the South Carolina Democratic primary, bolstered by overwhelming support from black voters. This victory reestablished her as the front-runner in the Democratic race, especially after earlier, closer contests with Bernie Sanders. Clinton’s strong performance raised doubts about Sanders's ability to compete in Southern states and increased her lead in delegates. Both candidates immediately shifted focus to the upcoming Super Tuesday primaries, where Clinton is favored in several key states.

55104_55104.caption: Layla Khamas 24 left and Zaineb Khamas 12 chat after breakfast at their home in the Sadr City area of Baghdad The sisters live with their mother Halima Daham 44 and their four other siblings their father died in March
55104_55104.article_context: Ten years after the U.S. invasion of Iraq, many commonly held beliefs about the war and its aftermath have proven inaccurate. The 2007 U.S. troop surge helped reduce violence but failed to achieve political compromise among Iraq’s main groups, leaving ongoing sectarian tensions. Despite lower levels of violence than during the civil war years, Iraq remains unstable and dangerous for its citizens. Although Iraq has formal democratic institutions, Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki has centralized power and marginalized Sunni opponents, evoking comparisons to Saddam Hussein’s rule. Iran exerts significant influence over Iraq, particularly in supporting Maliki’s government and regional policies, but Iraqi leaders act on their own interests as well. Finally, while most U.S. troops have withdrawn, a substantial American presence remains through military personnel, diplomats, and security contractors.

41032_41032.caption: Hundreds of advocates for marijuana legalization rally and smoke pot outside the White House Only two people were given citations
41032_41032.article_context: Over 100 marijuana legalization advocates protested outside the White House, smoking marijuana and displaying a giant joint-shaped balloon to draw attention to federal cannabis laws. The event, organized by Adam Eidinger, aimed to urge President Obama to remove marijuana from the Schedule 1 list of controlled substances. While the activists avoided arrest by staying on District-owned property where pot possession is legal, two people received minor citations for public consumption. The protest highlighted ongoing tension between local and federal marijuana policies.

39817_39817.caption: Nancy Waters performs a wedding ceremony for Lori Hazelton and Stephanie Ward the first samesex couple to receive a marriage license in Muskegon Mich
39817_39817.article_context: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton advised county officials with religious objections that they may refuse to issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples, following the Supreme Court's nationwide legalization of same-sex marriage. Paxton described the court's ruling as 'lawless' and asserted that officials’ First Amendment religious rights remain intact. His position was immediately challenged by gay rights advocates, who argued that the guidance undermines the law and could result in discrimination. Paxton acknowledged that officials who refuse service could face legal action, and offered support from lawyers for those defending their religious beliefs.

56139_56139.caption: Two boys look at the site of a car bomb attack in Baghdad s Hurriya neighborhood
56139_56139.article_context: A wave of deadly car bombings in Baghdad, claimed by the al-Qaeda-affiliated group ISIS, has killed dozens and highlighted Iraq’s escalating security crisis, nearly two years after U.S. troops withdrew. The attacks, which are part of a broader surge in violence that has claimed over 5,300 Iraqi lives this year, signal a major resurgence of ISIS, now operating across both Iraq and Syria. The group's campaign of bombings, assassinations, and large-scale prison breaks has undermined recent security gains, fueled sectarian tensions, and exposed deep political divisions between Iraq's Shiite-led government and the Sunni minority. As Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki prepares to seek more U.S. military support, the violence has also heightened fears of renewed civil conflict ahead of national elections.

46932_46932.caption: Teacher Meghan Neary gives a highfive to John Montano 8 left at the school While teachers celebrated students testscore gains others felt uncertain about the tests educational value
46932_46932.article_context: Carlin Springs Elementary, a predominantly poor and Hispanic school in Arlington, Virginia, saw significant improvements in third-grade standardized test scores after teachers implemented six weeks of intensive test preparation, progress tracking, and after-school tutoring. While these efforts led to double-digit gains in passing rates for math, reading, history, and science, educators expressed mixed feelings about the value of 'teaching to the test,' questioning whether it truly reflected students' knowledge. The story highlights ongoing debates over the role of standardized testing in education, the effectiveness of test prep strategies, and concerns that heavy focus on test results may overlook deeper learning, especially for schools serving immigrant and non-native English-speaking students.

44414_44414.caption: Donald Trump holds an event at the Eisenhower Hotel and Conference Center Oct 22 2016 in Gettysburg Pa
44414_44414.article_context: Donald Trump and his supporters have amplified unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud in the lead-up to the election, circulating misleading videos and encouraging groups like Oathkeepers and 'Vote Protectors' to monitor polling places for supposed fraud. Many of these claims are based on glitches or technology imperfections, not evidence of rigged voting, as shown in the misattributed viral video and minor software issues in Texas. These efforts, which have included Republican-led voter-watch initiatives, risk intimidating voters and undermining public confidence in the electoral process, serving as a means for Trump to cast doubt on the election results and justify potential defeat.

475837_475837.caption: East Glasgow Proindependence and prounion campaigners are pictured outside a polling station
475837_475837.article_context: On referendum day in Scotland, voters across the country went to polling stations to decide on the future of Scottish independence. Key political leaders, including Ed Miliband, Gordon Brown, Alistair Darling, Nicola Sturgeon, and Alex Salmond, were seen campaigning and casting their votes. Both pro-independence and pro-union campaigners were active outside polling stations in cities and remote communities, reflecting high engagement and spirited debate over the historic decision.

450253_450253.caption: Polls show that Nick Clegg s mouldbreaking performance in the first of the televised leaders debates has dramatically boosted his party s support
450253_450253.article_context: Nick Clegg's strong performance in the first televised leaders' debate dramatically boosted support for the Liberal Democrats, disrupting the general election race. Polls showed the Lib Dems surging ahead of Labour and close to the Conservatives, leading both major parties to target Clegg’s policies for scrutiny. Labour and the Conservatives debated which party suffered more from the debate, while Conservative aides reconsidered strategy to counter Clegg’s outsider appeal. With the Lib Dems drawing voters from both rivals, all parties acknowledged that the election had become highly unpredictable. Both Labour and the Conservatives signaled increased focus on policy and strategy, with the Tories unveiling new proposals to regain support. The election landscape was fundamentally altered as the Lib Dems emerged as a serious contender.

48375_48375.caption: This interlocking is seen on Metro s Silver Line It s similar to the interlocking in downtown DC where a nonpassenger train derailed Thursday morning
48375_48375.article_context: A Washington Metro train derailed near downtown D.C. between the Federal Triangle and Smithsonian stations, likely due to an issue at an interlocking where trains switch tracks. Three cars from the six-car train went off the tracks, leading to a major service disruption affecting several lines and key transfer stations. Metro officials are still investigating the exact cause, which could involve infrastructure, rail car, or human error. The derailment forced the use of shuttle buses for commuters and created crowded conditions, with potential disruptions expected during the evening rush hour as crews work to re-rail the train and restore normal service.

40455_40455.caption: A man in Liberia reads a newspaper whose frontpage headline Sept 17 was about the US deployment
40455_40455.article_context: In response to the ongoing and deadly Ebola outbreak in West Africa, President Obama announced that the U.S. military would lead efforts to combat the virus through Operation United Assistance. Up to 4,000 service members are being deployed to provide medical, logistical, and security support, including building a hospital for infected healthcare workers and constructing 17 treatment units across Liberia. While local residents expressed mixed feelings about the military presence, U.S. officials emphasized collaboration with Liberian authorities. Troops have been specially trained for the mission, treating Ebola as a new and invisible threat.

47745_47745.caption: Deanna Durbin the internationally famous child star from Hollywood s Golden Age who brought her pure soprano voice and natural girlnextdoor looks to nearly 30 movies died in April in Paris She was 91 READ Deanna Durbin dies at 91 star power made her among biggest box office draws in old Hollywood
47745_47745.article_context: Following the death of Sen. Frank Lautenberg, New Jersey Governor Chris Christie faces a crucial decision regarding the appointment of a replacement and the timing of a special election for the Senate seat. Christie could appoint a Republican ally, but might consider a bipartisan gesture by selecting a Democrat, such as frontrunner Newark Mayor Cory Booker, though this risks angering the GOP. The timing of the special election is uncertain due to complicated state laws, but holding it in November 2013 alongside other state elections is possible. Whoever wins the seat must run again in 2014, making the political landscape in New Jersey unexpectedly dynamic.

457785_457785.caption: A King Cobra About 5 million people are bitten by snakes every year of whom 100000 die
457785_457785.article_context: Doctors Without Borders has warned that the world will run out of the life-saving snakebite anti-venom Fav-Afrique by June, due to Sanofi Pasteur ending its production last year. This shortage could endanger tens of thousands of lives, mostly in developing countries, as no effective alternative is expected for at least two years. Sanofi Pasteur cited market competition from cheaper, less effective products as the reason for discontinuing Fav-Afrique and had offered to transfer production technology. The charity called for urgent international action, especially from the World Health Organization, to address the impending crisis and ensure access to effective snakebite treatment.

43367_43367.caption: Despite the onset of a snow storm thousands participate in the 43rd annual March for Life commemorating Roe v Wade
43367_43367.article_context: Despite a historic blizzard shutting down much of Washington, D.C., thousands of abortion opponents gathered for the annual March for Life, highlighting their commitment to the cause. While the crowd was smaller than usual due to weather conditions, organizers and participants expressed optimism about the current state of the anti-abortion movement, especially following the release of controversial videos about Planned Parenthood. The event saw participation from both Catholic and evangelical groups and featured speeches from political figures such as Republican candidate Carly Fiorina. Many attendees felt that American culture is slowly shifting in favor of their views, and the harsh weather underscored the dedication of those present.
