460096_460096.caption: A device for measuring air quality is located in Oxford Street on July 9 2014 in London England Researchers from King s College London have found that concentrations of nitrogen dioxide in Oxford Street are the worst on earth
460096_460096.article_context: Boris Johnson, the mayor of London, has acknowledged scientific evidence showing that Oxford Street has some of the highest nitrogen dioxide pollution levels in the world, reversing his earlier public denial. This admission followed pressure from MPs and researchers at King’s College London, whose findings have spotlighted severe diesel-related air quality issues. In response, Johnson and Transport for London have proposed an ultra-low-emission zone for central London starting in 2020 to tackle air pollution, though critics note that EU limits should be met by 2015. Johnson stressed that King’s College research funding is not at risk and maintains that some data has been misrepresented.

461342_461342.caption: Rescuers take people to safety in WaltononThames Surrey
461342_461342.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron has called for an end to cabinet infighting and criticism of the Environment Agency as the UK faces severe flooding, particularly along the Thames Valley, with thousands of homes at risk. The disputes involved Communities Secretary Eric Pickles, who initially blamed the Environment Agency and criticized previous flood policies, and Environment Secretary Owen Paterson. Pickles later reversed his stance, calling for government unity. Cameron emphasized prioritizing effective flood response over political blame, expressing support for the Environment Agency and urging ministers to focus on helping affected communities. Meanwhile, experts warn of further heavy rain, high winds, and ongoing disruption, as the country grapples with unprecedented weather and widespread evacuations.

39646_39646.caption: Taya Kyle widow of Chris Kyle sits in the gallery before the start of the Eddie Ray Routh capital murder trial in Texas
39646_39646.article_context: Chris Kyle, renowned Navy SEAL and subject of the film 'American Sniper,' was fatally shot along with his friend Chad Littlefield at Rough Creek Lodge, Texas, by Marine veteran Eddie Ray Routh. The meeting had been arranged at the request of Routh's mother, hoping Kyle could help her troubled son, who suffered from severe mental health issues. Routh shot both men at the shooting range using Kyle's own firearms, then fled the scene in Kyle's truck, leading police on a high-speed chase before being apprehended. At his murder trial, Routh’s defense argued insanity due to his psychiatric conditions, while the killings shocked the veteran community and drew national attention.

470055_470055.caption: Two Fathers 4 Justice campaigners protest on the roof of the deputy Labour leader Harriet Harman
470055_470055.article_context: Two Fathers 4 Justice campaigners dressed as superheroes climbed onto the roof of Labour deputy leader Harriet Harman's London home to protest fathers' rights. They easily accessed the property and unfurled a banner calling for equal rights for fathers, while police responded to the incident. The protest marks a renewed wave of public stunts by the group, which campaigns for better access to children for separated fathers.

41923_41923.caption: Obama Wonderful day for Americans freed from North Korea
41923_41923.article_context: After spending two years imprisoned in North Korea, American Kenneth Bae was released alongside fellow American Matthew Todd Miller and returned to his family in Washington state. Bae expressed gratitude to his supporters and U.S. officials, and celebrated his freedom with pizza and Starbucks. His imprisonment was reportedly linked to his Christian faith and resulted in serious health issues. The release was secured following a visit by U.S. intelligence director James Clapper, who delivered a letter from President Obama. Bae’s family is now focusing on recovery and has requested privacy, while the case has drawn attention to ongoing human rights concerns in North Korea.

465111_465111.caption: Anna Maxwell Martin plays Heather Brooke in the BBC s new film about the investigative journalist
465111_465111.article_context: Journalist Heather Brooke, known for her five-year campaign to expose MPs' expenses, is the subject of a new film dramatizing her efforts. The film, titled 'On Expenses,' features actress Anna Maxwell Martin portraying Brooke and highlights the challenges of bringing real-life events to the screen. Brooke recounts her surreal experience consulting on the film’s production, including set visits and the costume designer’s attention to her personal style. The film will air on BBC4.

46056_46056.caption: Global Refugee Trends 2013 June 2014
46056_46056.article_context: A UN refugee agency report revealed that, in 2013, the number of refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced people worldwide surpassed 50 million for the first time since World War II, largely due to ongoing conflicts in Syria, South Sudan, and the Central African Republic. The Syrian crisis alone has created millions of refugees and internally displaced people. The report also highlights that half of the displaced are children, and there was a significant increase of 6 million displaced people from the previous year. UN officials emphasize the urgent need for political solutions to prevent further mass displacement.

44220_44220.caption: Edwin Cooley left talks to Labor Secretary Thomas Perez far right about an apprenticeship program on May 13 in East Providence RI
44220_44220.article_context: Labor Secretary Thomas Perez and Housing Secretary Julián Castro, both considered potential vice presidential picks for Hillary Clinton, have recently announced significant policy changes boosting their profiles among progressive and Latino communities. Perez unveiled new rules expanding overtime pay eligibility for millions of workers, while Castro is working on reforms to federal programs for selling distressed mortgages, though facing criticism from some liberal groups for the pace of changes. As the formal vetting process for Clinton’s running mate approaches, both officials’ moves are seen as enhancing their progressive credentials and professional qualifications, amid calls for increased Latino representation in national politics.

47562_47562.caption: Antigovernment protesters take cover while under fire from police snipers during clashes with riot police in central Kiev Although the fighting Thursday morning fell short of developing into a fullscale battle the Health Ministry confirmed five deaths in clashes near government offices
47562_47562.article_context: Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych went missing as protesters took control of his presidential residence and central Kiev, following months of escalating anti-government demonstrations. Police withdrew from downtown Kiev, and opposition figures claimed authority over the city. Parliament voted to dismiss Yanukovych, appointed Oleksandr Turchynov as interim speaker, and approved steps for swift presidential and parliamentary elections. Former Prime Minister Yulia Tymoshenko was ordered released from prison, and key officials, including the interior minister, were sacked. The upheaval marked a significant shift in power after violent clashes that resulted in dozens of deaths, prompting international concern and intervention from leaders in the U.S., Russia, and the EU. The situation remained volatile as protesters demanded Yanukovych’s immediate resignation and legal accountability.

40923_40923.caption: Fairfax County police said unidentified vandals spray painted one of their marked cruisers sometime overnight Saturday
40923_40923.article_context: A police cruiser in Fairfax County was discovered with unauthorized graffiti-style paint, including smiley faces and colorful stripes, making it nearly unrecognizable. The incident occurred overnight, and local police are seeking information from the public to identify whoever is responsible.

451304_451304.caption: Wolverines need deep snow to den and were largely wiped out of the Rocky Mountains in the 1930s due to unregulated trapping and poisoning
451304_451304.article_context: Federal wildlife officials have decided to withdraw proposed protections for the wolverine, reversing earlier plans to safeguard the climate-sensitive species. The US Fish and Wildlife Service cited uncertainties about the localized effects of climate change on wolverine habitat, despite consensus that global warming reduces the deep snow these animals need for denning. This decision contradicts recommendations from agency scientists and follows opposition from several western state wildlife agencies. Wildlife advocates intend to challenge the move in court. The reversal reflects broader difficulties in using climate models to make long-term species protection decisions and could impact future policies for other climate-affected species.

47435_47435.caption: Tea Party supporter William Temple holds up a tea pot as he shouts against President Barack Obama s 2010 healthcare overhaul outside the Supreme Court in Washington June 28 2012 REUTERSJason Reed
47435_47435.article_context: The Supreme Court upheld President Obama's healthcare law, marking a significant political victory for his administration and validating his signature legislative achievement. This decision strengthens Obama's campaign narrative of achieving major reforms and allows him to shift from defending the law to promoting its benefits. While public opinion is unlikely to change, the ruling energizes Democratic supporters and reframes the upcoming presidential election as a decisive referendum on healthcare. Republicans, meanwhile, use the outcome to rally their base, emphasizing the need to elect Mitt Romney to overturn the law, but the day is broadly seen as a win for Obama and the Democrats.

46526_46526.caption: Basic popularity ratings present a challenge to the Republican frontrunner as his campain attempts to focus on possible general election fight
46526_46526.article_context: A new Washington Post-ABC News poll shows Mitt Romney at a record high in unfavorable ratings, with half of Americans viewing him negatively—a significant obstacle as he prepares for a potential campaign against President Obama. While 53% of Americans have a favorable view of Obama, only 34% say the same about Romney. Romney also struggles among independents, with more seeing him unfavorably compared to Obama. Despite these image problems, recent polls suggest Romney and Obama are competitive in head-to-head matchups, indicating that factors beyond basic popularity influence voter decisions.

40681_40681.caption: Firefighters climb the building seized by the separatists after an explosion in Luhansk
40681_40681.article_context: U.S. officials reported that Russia has redeployed additional troops, including special forces, to its border with Ukraine and is supplying arms to pro-Russian separatists, while Russia denies any military buildup. Ukraine’s president, Petro Poroshenko, announced a week-long unilateral cease-fire, offering amnesty and safe passage to separatists who surrender, as part of a broader peace plan. Despite these efforts, separatist rebels have rejected the cease-fire proposal, and fighting continues in eastern Ukraine. Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury imposed new sanctions on separatist leaders, and Ukraine aims to seal its border to prevent further support for the rebels.

449694_449694.caption: Grey cranes flock over the Agamon HaHula Lake at the Hula valley in northern Israel Local farmers feed the birds with corn to prevent them from destroying their crops
449694_449694.article_context: This news article showcases a series of global wildlife and nature events, highlighting endangered species and environmental challenges. Endangered animals like the Moroccan magot monkey, Bornean orangutan, and Saharan cheetah face threats from habitat loss, poaching, and droughts, while illegal ivory trade endangers Southeast Asian elephants. Photographs also capture unique animal behaviors, such as foxes nesting in trees and brown hares in decline due to agricultural changes. Signs of spring, conservation efforts, and environmental issues like lake pollution in Nicaragua underscore ongoing efforts and concerns for wildlife and natural habitats across the world.

43609_43609.caption: In this photo released by Mexico s Attorney General Office
43609_43609.article_context: Mexican and U.S. authorities coordinated a nine-day operation culminating in the arrest of Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, the world's most wanted drug lord and leader of the Sinaloa cartel, in Mazatlan, Mexico. The successful capture resulted from a combination of U.S.-provided wiretap intelligence, surveillance, and key arrests of cartel associates, which allowed law enforcement to track Guzmán’s movements and dismantle his network of safe houses. Guzmán was apprehended without resistance and subsequently taken to a maximum-security prison, marking a significant victory for both Mexican and U.S. officials in the fight against organized crime.

466150_466150.caption: Nigel Farage said the Times s story on his expenses was politically motivated
466150_466150.article_context: Ukip has publicly challenged The Times over an article alleging that Nigel Farage misused EU parliamentary allowances, claiming the report was politically motivated and influenced by journalists with Conservative links and privileged backgrounds. In retaliation, Ukip published a list of Times journalists with supposed establishment ties. The dispute revolves around claims that Farage claimed significantly more for office costs than expenses actually incurred, though accounts of those costs vary. The Times and its journalists responded by dismissing Ukip's criticisms and questioning the accuracy of Ukip's claims.

52742_52742.caption: Women sit at the One Level Up restaurant on the rooftop of the Zafer Tower overlooking Gaza City The popular night spot was shelled during the past summer s war but the owner repaired the damage soon after
52742_52742.article_context: Despite Gaza's ongoing devastation from conflict, unemployment, and blockades, a small Palestinian middle class persists, enjoying limited luxuries such as fine dining, private beach resorts, spin classes, and luxury cars. New businesses, gyms, and restaurants are opening, catering to those who can afford brief escapes from daily hardships. However, most Gazans still endure extreme poverty and rely on aid, highlighting the stark contrasts in the territory amid slow reconstruction and economic collapse.

42258_42258.caption: Technicians work on an engine on one of two Japanese Government P3 aircraft after their arrival at a base in Bullsbrook Australia The sighting of a wooden pallet and other debris raised hopes of a breakthrough in the international search for the missing plane
42258_42258.article_context: The search for missing Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 intensified as planes and ships from several countries spotted floating objects in a new search area of the Indian Ocean. However, it remains unconfirmed if the debris is related to the aircraft, which vanished on March 8 with 239 people aboard. The search operation, recently moved northeast following new data analysis indicating the plane flew faster and farther than previously thought, is racing against time to find the black box before its signal stops. Meanwhile, families of the mostly Chinese passengers continue to demand answers from Malaysian authorities, while unfavorable weather is expected but search efforts persist.

42407_42407.caption: Ukrainian servicemen ride atop an armored personnel carrier as they patrol an area near Donetsk
42407_42407.article_context: A convoy of Russian aid trucks departed for eastern Ukraine, sparking concerns among Ukrainian and Western officials that the delivery could be a cover for boosting pro-Russian rebels in the conflict zone. While Russia and Ukraine tentatively agreed to hand over the aid for International Red Cross distribution at a Ukrainian-controlled border post, doubts remained about the logistics, intentions behind the convoy, and whether Russian vehicles would be permitted entry. Ukrainian authorities stated any unapproved border crossings would be treated as aggression and called for strict inspection and delivery according to their rules. Western leaders echoed concerns, insisting aid should be coordinated with Ukraine to avoid military use disguised as humanitarian relief.

40253_40253.caption: Commuters from Annandale Va forced to take VRE because the Metro line they usually use to commute was shut down try to navigate an unfamiliar ticketing system
40253_40253.article_context: Following a track fire near McPherson Square that led to a 24-hour shutdown of the subway system, Metro officials announced monthly inspections of power cables and electrical equipment beginning April 1. Emergency inspections uncovered 27 immediate fire hazards and hundreds of additional problems despite previous assurances that such issues had been resolved. The leadership expressed frustration over repeated failures to fix longstanding defects and lack of accountability. Metro General Manager Paul J. Wiedefeld pledged transparency and a broader, more comprehensive inspection regime moving forward.

40875_40875.caption: Hiroshi Shimizu senior vice president of global quality assurance at Takata Corp speaks during a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing in Washington DC on Dec 3 2014 Takata Corp snubbed the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
40875_40875.article_context: Millions of vehicles have been recalled due to defective Takata air bags that can explode and cause serious injury or death. While automakers are executing these recalls, the debate over financial responsibility continues, with Takata insisting automakers should pay since they installed the air bags. Automakers, meanwhile, are focusing on customer safety and repairs but may seek to recover costs from Takata. The uncertainty over liability, contract details, and possible legal disputes is ongoing, especially as the U.S. government pushes for a nationwide recall. The shortage of replacement air bags and concerns about both Takata’s survival and automakers’ reputations further complicate the issue.

47446_47446.caption: It s been a rough year for media experts said Willie Robertson Duck Dynasty star But I have a theory about how they missed the Trump train They do nt hang out with the regular folks like us
47446_47446.article_context: Senator Ted Cruz took a significant political risk by refusing to endorse Donald Trump during a highly visible speech at the Republican National Convention. Cruz's calculated move was based on the expectation that Trump would lose the general election and that the Republican Party would later regret supporting Trump's candidacy. Cruz hopes to position himself as the principled figure within the party, contrasting with other Republicans who backed Trump. However, his decision was met with widespread criticism from GOP members, and his political future hinges on the outcome and interpretation of the November election.

42824_42824.caption: GW student Cam Tucker is silhouetted behind a rainbow flag in front of the Supreme Court on March 27 2013 in Washington DC
42824_42824.article_context: Gay-rights activists are intensifying efforts as Illinois, New Mexico, and Hawaii each consider legalizing same-sex marriage by the end of the year. In Illinois, legislators are working to secure enough votes for a marriage equality bill. The New Mexico Supreme Court is hearing arguments that could determine the legality of same-sex marriage statewide, while Hawaii’s legislature is meeting in a special session to vote on a similar bill. These developments are part of a broader movement following several major legal and political victories for same-sex marriage across the country in 2012 and 2013, indicating mounting momentum for marriage equality in the United States.

449085_449085.caption: David Cameron is planning to announce that the Tory manifesto for the next election will include a pledge to repatriate powers to Britain
449085_449085.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron faces intense political pressure within the Conservative Party over Britain’s relationship with the EU, as Eurosceptic MPs push for radical reforms while pro-European figures prepare to defend full membership. The government is expected to reject the most extreme proposals from the Fresh Start group, including giving the UK a veto over EU financial regulations and ending the working-time directive, but may support less drastic measures to repatriate powers. Cameron plans a major speech announcing a referendum on revised membership terms after the next election. Meanwhile, senior political figures such as Kenneth Clarke and Lord Mandelson are launching campaigns to counter rising Euroscepticism, and Labour leader Ed Miliband has warned Cameron's actions could inadvertently lead Britain toward leaving the EU.

39948_39948.caption: Autopsy reveals St Louis teen was shot in back
39948_39948.article_context: Mansur Ball-Bey, an 18-year-old African American, was fatally shot in the back by St. Louis police during a chase, according to a preliminary autopsy. Police claim Ball-Bey pointed a gun at officers, while his family’s attorney asserts he was unarmed and not involved in the property search that led to the incident. The shooting sparked protests in St. Louis, echoing previous fatal police encounters in the area, and has prompted an ongoing police investigation amid heightened community tensions.

43406_43406.caption: Members of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters and their supporters attend a rally outside the Capitol in Washington on April 14 The demonstrators protested a plan by the Central States Pension Fund to reduce payments to retirees
43406_43406.article_context: The Central States Pension Fund, one of the nation's largest multi-employer pension plans, may soon implement significant benefit cuts for more than 250,000 retired and active truckers and their families due to financial distress. These potential reductions, allowed under a 2014 law, aim to prevent the fund's insolvency by 2025 but could reduce pension payments by an average of 23%. Retirees are protesting the changes, warning it could set a precedent for other struggling pension plans. While some lawmakers advocate for government assistance instead of cuts, the Treasury Department is expected to make a decision soon, which could impact pensioners as early as July 1.

45059_45059.caption: Army Command Sgt Maj Bennie Adkins is shown here in 1966 the year in which led soldiers through a multiday battle
45059_45059.article_context: Nearly five decades after their heroic actions during the Vietnam War, two U.S. soldiers, retired Command Sgt. Maj. Bennie G. Adkins and Specialist Donald P. Sloat, were awarded the Medal of Honor in a White House ceremony. Adkins was recognized for leading his Special Forces unit through an intense week-long battle, repeatedly risking his life to rescue wounded comrades and evade enemy forces. Sloat was honored posthumously for sacrificing himself by shielding a grenade to save his fellow soldiers. The awards required special congressional approval due to the long delay in recognition.

462860_462860.caption: The protection given to the eastern lowland gorillas in conflictravaged Democratic Republic of Congo has been recognised with an award to John Kahekwa Munihuzi
462860_462860.article_context: Ekwoge Enang Abwe and John Kahekwa Munihuzi were awarded the Whitley Fund for Nature prize for their innovative conservation work with gorillas and other wildlife in Cameroon’s Ebo forest and the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Kahuzi Biega National Park, respectively. Abwe succeeded in reducing wildlife hunting by motivating pride among local communities, promoting education, and fostering sustainable livelihoods, while Munihuzi’s 'Pole Pole' foundation involved former poachers in conservation activities, resulting in a partial recovery of the gorilla population despite conflict and poverty. Their locally driven approaches highlight the importance of community involvement in conservation and are celebrated by the Whitley Fund, which has supported over 160 leaders worldwide.

52230_52230.caption: Ukrainian Security Service releases video claiming Moscow s interest in rebelsecured MH17 black boxes
52230_52230.article_context: The Ukrainian Security Service released recordings allegedly capturing pro-Russian rebels in eastern Ukraine discussing efforts to keep the Malaysia Airlines MH17 crash evidence, including the black boxes, away from independent investigators at Moscow’s request. The authenticity of the recordings and those involved has not been independently verified. The OSCE monitors faced restricted access to the crash site by the rebels, though greater access was reportedly granted later. Ukrainian officials accused the rebels of tampering with evidence, while rebel leaders claimed they would hand over the black boxes to the International Civil Aviation Organization and denied hindering investigators. Previous recordings released by Ukraine purportedly show rebel involvement in the attack and possession of weapons capable of downing the plane.

461259_461259.caption: Hugh FearnleyWhittingstall gave away imperfect parsnips outside a Morrisons branch to highlight the problem of cosmetic standards
461259_461259.article_context: Chef Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall criticized Morrisons for its inadequate efforts to sell misshapen vegetables, calling their trial with wonky courgettes 'pathetic.' Morrisons responded by promising to sell a wider range of imperfect produce at reduced prices. Fearnley-Whittingstall also condemned supermarkets’ reliance on anaerobic digestion to handle food waste, arguing that surplus food should be fed to people rather than used for energy. He highlighted the broader issue of food overproduction and called on both government and consumers to take greater responsibility for reducing waste, including a better understanding of 'use-by' dates.

50731_50731.caption: Egypt s Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Badi speaks to the media outside a polling station in Beni Suef on December 15 2011 during the second round of parliamentary voting
50731_50731.article_context: Egypt's first post-revolution parliamentary elections have positioned the Muslim Brotherhood’s Freedom and Justice Party as the dominant political force, potentially claiming over 40 percent of seats. This sets up a likely power struggle between the Brotherhood, seeking real legislative authority and influence over the new constitution, and the ruling military council, which aims to retain behind-the-scenes control. As Egypt transitions to democracy, the Brotherhood is pushing for greater parliamentary power, reevaluation of U.S. military aid, and a review of the peace treaty with Israel, while U.S. policy shifts to engage with the group. Analysts predict an eventual clash as the Brotherhood moves to challenge the generals’ authority and solidify civilian rule.

42680_42680.caption: Republican Bob Turner won a New York seat that Democrats expected to hold
42680_42680.article_context: Republican businessman Bob Turner won a special election for New York’s 9th congressional district, a seat previously held by Democrat Anthony Weiner. Turner’s upset victory in a traditionally Democratic area was seen as a repudiation of President Obama’s policies, particularly regarding the economy and Israel. The district, which faces possible elimination due to upcoming redistricting, has shown eroding Democratic support in recent years. Turner’s win, along with a Republican hold in Nevada’s 2nd district, boosted GOP optimism ahead of 2012 and raised concerns for Democrats, who fielded a weak candidate and struggled with internal divisions.

43251_43251.caption: A handout image released by the South Korean Coast Guard taken from cellphone video footage by a Coast Guard officer on April 16 shows Lee Joonseok right the captain of the Sewol fleeing from the sinking ferry near Jindo island South Korea
43251_43251.article_context: Yoo Byung-un, the mysterious and controversial billionaire who was linked to the South Korean ferry disaster that killed hundreds, was found dead in an orchard after being the target of the country's largest manhunt. Yoo was known for his ties to the Evangelical Baptist Church, considered by some to be a cult, and had a previous history of fraud and bankruptcy. Authorities had sought him for charges related to financial wrongdoing that allegedly contributed to the ferry's sinking, although his exact involvement was debated. The strange circumstances of his death and the loyalty of his followers continue to raise questions and suspicions.

458794_458794.caption: Farmers in Zhejiang province in Eastern China make as much noise as possible to scare wild boars away from their crops
458794_458794.article_context: Farmers in eastern China are using noisy tactics such as vuvuzelas, gongs, and firecrackers to protect their crops from a rapidly increasing wild boar population, which has grown fivefold in Zhejiang province over the past decade. The surge is attributed to fewer villagers living in rural areas and stricter gun controls implemented for the Shanghai Expo. With hunting restricted, boars have moved closer to farmland and suburbs, causing major crop damage and threatening yields. Other regions like Jiangxi have responded by issuing hunting licenses, but Zhejiang faces greater challenges due to its proximity to Shanghai and ongoing security measures.

42251_42251.caption: According to Slate s Joshua Keating when Slovakia declared itself a sovereign state after the Nazi invasion of Czechoslovakia on March 15 1939 CarpathoUkraine found itself in an awkward position So the region declared itself independent on March 15 1939 with a president a prime minister and a flag which later became the Ukrainian flag as we know it In the photo are peasants from Ruthenia in CarpathoUkraine
42251_42251.article_context: Crimea voted overwhelmingly in favor of breaking away from Ukraine and joining Russia, with over 96% supporting annexation amid a heavy Russian military presence. Western governments, including the US, condemned the referendum as illegitimate and threatened sanctions, citing Russian occupation and limited campaigning for alternatives. The vote intensified tensions, prompting unrest and pro-Russian rallies in other Ukrainian cities, and marked a significant escalation in conflict between Russia and the West since the Cold War. Many Crimean Tatars and ethnic Ukrainians boycotted the vote, while celebrations erupted in Crimea. The outcome deepened the crisis that followed the ousting of Ukraine’s pro-Russian president and Russia’s subsequent intervention in the region.

42288_42288.caption: An antique car drives past a billboard with the phrase Long live a free Cuba
42288_42288.article_context: Former Cuban president Fidel Castro sharply criticized President Obama’s recent historic visit to Cuba, rejecting Obama’s message of reconciliation and calls to move beyond past hostilities. In a scathing article published in the Communist Party newspaper Granma, Castro dismissed Obama’s appeals for friendship and openness, citing decades of U.S. embargoes and interventions. Castro insisted that Cuba would not trade its achievements or sovereignty for gifts from the U.S., and urged Obama to better understand Cuban history before offering advice. His comments contrasted with the positive atmosphere during Obama’s visit, which included meetings with current President Raúl Castro and a public address promoting renewed U.S.-Cuba relations.

41945_41945.caption: Julie Harris a star of film and stage who had won an unprecedented five Tony Awards for best actress died Aug 24 at her home in West Chatham Mass READ Actress Julie Harris dies at 87
41945_41945.article_context: Following the death of Sen. Frank Lautenberg, New Jersey Governor Chris Christie faces a critical decision regarding the appointment of a temporary replacement and the scheduling of a special election for the Senate seat. Christie, a Republican, could choose to appoint a member of his own party or demonstrate bipartisanship by selecting a Democrat, with Newark Mayor Cory Booker seen as a leading Democratic contender. Complicating matters, New Jersey's ambiguous election laws leave the timing of the special election uncertain, with the next possible dates being in November 2013 or potentially later. The outcome will not only affect the political dynamics of the Senate race but also have significant implications for Christie's own political future.

453892_453892.caption: The Fukushima nuclear reactor Following the disaster many countries are questioning the future of nuclear energy
453892_453892.article_context: In the wake of Japan's Fukushima nuclear disaster, UK Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg suggested Britain may reconsider its commitment to nuclear power, citing increased uncertainties and potential costs that could require public subsidies—which the coalition government opposes. The issue is causing tensions within the coalition, as Conservatives see nuclear as crucial for energy and carbon reduction, while Liberal Democrats remain skeptical of subsidizing the industry. The government awaits a safety review of British reactors, while nuclear policy has become a contentious issue ahead of future elections. Similar anti-nuclear sentiment has surged in Germany, where public protests and political shifts are pressuring the government to reconsider its nuclear plans.

50220_50220.caption: Afghan supporters run to get a good spot near the stage after they entered a field April 2 2014 to see Afghan presidential candidate Abudullah Abdullah speak at an election rally on the outskirts of Kabul
50220_50220.article_context: Afghan voters turned out in unexpectedly high numbers to elect a new president despite Taliban threats and sporadic violence, marking the country's third presidential election since 2001 and its first democratic transfer of power. The election day was largely peaceful, with only minor attacks reported and no large-scale disruptions as feared. Some polling stations ran out of ballots due to high turnout, but violence and security concerns prevented nearly 1,000 polling sites from opening. Preliminary estimates suggest around 7 million people voted, and if no candidate secures more than 50% of the vote, a runoff will be held. The election is seen as a critical step in Afghanistan's transition after years of war and as U.S. forces withdraw from the country.

448778_448778.caption: Police at the post office where Craig HodsonWalker was shot dead Three detectives face disciplinary action over the failure to arrest Anselm Ribera who was convicted of the murder
448778_448778.article_context: Three West Mercia police detectives face disciplinary action after the Independent Police Complaints Commission found serious failings in their handling of armed robbery investigations linked to Anselm Ribera. Despite DNA evidence tying Ribera to several robberies, he was not apprehended for months and subsequently murdered Craig Hodson-Walker during a raid. The IPCC attributed the mistakes to both individual and organisational shortcomings and recommended improvements in supervision and intelligence management. Ribera and his accomplices received prison sentences of at least 34 years for murder.

472063_472063.caption: You have to present people with solutions not problems members of the Core Cities lobby group who are campaigning for more power to be devolved to the UK s biggest cities outside London
472063_472063.article_context: The leaders of the UK's 11 largest cities outside London, forming the Core Cities group, are campaigning for greater devolution and autonomy from central government. They are preparing to launch a Charter for Local Freedom, seeking commitments from Labour and Conservative parties to include devolution in their election manifestos. Inspired by successful devolution deals like Manchester's, the group argues that more local control over budgets and powers is essential for economic growth and efficiency. Despite challenges and resistance from national politicians and varying views within local government, there is growing support for transferring more authority over taxation and public services to city regions, with ongoing debates about balancing autonomy with fiscal redistribution.

46301_46301.caption: ProRussian supporters are seen as they take over an administration building in Mariupol Ukraine
46301_46301.article_context: Pro-Russian insurgents shot down a Ukrainian military helicopter near Slovyansk as fighting intensified in eastern Ukraine, resulting in at least eight deaths and dozens wounded. The Ukrainian government struggled to regain control over key cities and dispatched special police units to Odessa after deadly clashes between pro-Russian and pro-Ukrainian groups. The military faced significant challenges due to inadequate resources and the use of civilians as shields by militants. Amid escalating tensions, Ukraine closed border crossings with Crimea, increased security ahead of national holidays, and replaced local police leadership in Odessa following failures to control the violence. Russia condemned Ukraine's actions, further heightening the crisis.

45026_45026.caption: A Syrian family fleeing violence sits inside a car at the LebaneseSyrian border at Masnaa Lebanon
45026_45026.article_context: Amid ongoing violence and hardship in Syria, civilians are using dark humor, such as satirical letters to Santa Claus, to cope with daily suffering under both government and rebel forces. In Aleppo, a city devastated by a five-month stalemate, residents face severe shortages of food, medicine, and fuel as the humanitarian crisis deepens. The rebels' failure to secure and govern Aleppo has intensified public frustration and undermined their support, while continued fighting and abuses by both sides leave hope for a peaceful resolution increasingly remote.

40257_40257.caption: Texas Ranger Michael Adcock holds a 308 caliber rifle with the lettering American Sniper etched on the side as he answers questions from defense attorney R Shay Isham
40257_40257.article_context: Former Navy SEAL Chris Kyle, famed as the 'American Sniper,' and his friend Chad Littlefield were shot and killed at the Rough Creek Lodge rifle range in Texas by Eddie Ray Routh, a Marine Corps veteran struggling with mental health issues. Kyle had met with Routh at the request of Routh's mother, hoping to help him, but became uneasy during their encounter, texting Littlefield about Routh's unstable behavior. Both victims were killed with Kyle's own guns and did not fire back. After the shootings, Routh fled in Kyle's truck, was later captured following a high-speed police chase, and subsequently admitted to the killings, claiming he acted because 'they wouldn’t talk to me.' At Routh's trial, his defense argued insanity due to his history of mental illness.

50641_50641.caption: The body of a Ukrainian policeman is covered on the ground outside police headquarters after Ukrainian forces attempted to drive out proRussian militants in Mariupol
50641_50641.article_context: Pro-Russian insurgents shot down a Ukrainian military helicopter near Slovyansk as intense fighting erupted between rebel and Ukrainian forces, resulting in at least eight deaths and dozens wounded. The clashes occurred as the Ukrainian government sought to regain control of Odessa and responded to escalating unrest by deploying special police units and closing checkpoints between Ukraine and Crimea. The violence highlighted weaknesses in Ukraine's military and police, prompting dismissals and reorganizations of local police leadership. Tensions between Russia and Ukraine continued to rise, with Russia condemning the Ukrainian government's actions and neighboring Moldova increasing border security. The crisis intensified following deadly confrontations in Odessa, signaling a deepening and more widespread conflict.

41697_41697.caption: A young migrant girl is helped ashore as she arrives with others aboard a dinghy after crossing from Turkey to Lesbos
41697_41697.article_context: The United States has announced an additional $419 million in humanitarian aid to support Syrian refugees and the nations hosting them, bringing its total contributions since 2011 to $4.5 billion—making it the largest donor. This funding aims to provide medical care, food, water, and shelter, and will be channeled primarily through UN agencies. Alongside this, President Obama has ordered preparations to admit at least 10,000 Syrian refugees in the next year, amidst calls to increase that number further. The U.S. administration faces criticism for not accepting more Syrian refugees, even as they stress that ultimately, resolving the crisis will require ending the Assad regime and defeating ISIS.

52009_52009.caption: Why Mali has become a target for terrorism
52009_52009.article_context: Gunmen affiliated with an al-Qaeda group attacked the Radisson Blu Hotel in Bamako, Mali, killing at least 20 people and taking hostages during a seven-hour siege. Security forces eventually freed the remaining hostages and killed or captured the attackers. The assault, claimed by the al-Mourabitoun group, highlighted Mali's continued vulnerability to Islamist militants despite years of multinational military efforts. Victims included local Malians and foreign nationals, with at least one American and several Chinese citizens among the dead. The incident underscored the persistent threat extremist groups pose in the region and the ongoing challenges for security and stability in Mali.

43178_43178.caption: What we know about the Washington state mall shooting
43178_43178.article_context: A manhunt is underway in Washington state after a gunman killed four women and one man during a shooting at the Cascade Mall in Burlington. The shooter entered Macy’s with a rifle and opened fire, then escaped on foot, prompting police searches with helicopters and K-9 units. Authorities have not identified the suspect or established a motive, and the FBI is assisting the investigation, though there is currently no evidence of terrorism. The mall remains closed, and local officials have expressed shock and grief over the tragedy.

463402_463402.caption: Ed Miliband at a Labour rally in Leeds on 23 April
463402_463402.article_context: A new opinion poll shows Labour leader Ed Miliband has overtaken Prime Minister David Cameron in public trust on managing the NHS, as Labour’s lead on the issue has more than doubled since February. Labour’s campaign focus on the NHS is resonating with undecided voters, while the Conservative strategy to limit debate on health after pledging £8bn extra NHS funding has not gained traction. The poll highlights health as the key election battleground, with a significant portion of voters still undecided and increasing pressure on the Conservatives to address NHS policy more directly.

446421_446421.caption: A controlled burn of oil from the Deepwater Horizon well in the Gulf of Mexico The report cites the Gulf of Mexico oil spill as an extreme example of the potential impact of inadequate environmental controls
446421_446421.article_context: A United Nations report warns that financial risks from biodiversity and ecosystem loss have dramatically increased and now pose a greater concern to businesses than international terrorism. The report highlights that environmental degradation—from overfishing to pollution—could result in severe business impacts ranging from $10 billion to $50 billion. Financial institutions are beginning to factor in these risks, prompted by high-profile cases like BP’s share crash after the Gulf oil spill. The UN study found that the world's largest corporations were responsible for $2.15 trillion in environmental costs in 2008. Despite rising awareness, most companies still fail to assess nature’s value in their financial performance, and major global institutions, including the World Bank, are calling for the integration of ecological costs into business and policy decisions.

460928_460928.caption: Michael Fabricant s tweet about Yasmin AlibhaiBrown
460928_460928.article_context: Conservative MP Michael Fabricant faced widespread criticism after tweeting that he might punch journalist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown in the throat following her TV clash with commentator Rod Liddle. His comments sparked backlash from political figures and the public, prompting demands for a full apology. Although Fabricant issued multiple apologies on Twitter, Alibhai-Brown dismissed them as inadequate. The incident reignited debates on misogyny and violence in politics, and further scrutiny of Fabricant’s controversial social media conduct.

42529_42529.caption: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi left a transgender rights activist and Anjali Gopalan center executive director of the Indian Naz Foundation Trust participate in a news conference in New Delhi after India s top court ruled that consensual samesex acts are illegal The twojudge Supreme Court bench reversed a landmark 2009 verdict by the Delhi High Court that said consensual sex between adults of the same sex was not a criminal offense
42529_42529.article_context: India’s Supreme Court ruled that gay sex is a criminal offense, overturning a 2009 lower-court decision that had decriminalized consensual same-sex relations. The court upheld a British colonial-era law, stating that any changes should be made by Parliament. This decision drew criticism and shock from LGBT activists and supporters, who expressed concern about increased stigma, harassment, and threats to their safety and rights. The ruling highlights resistance to gay rights in India, in contrast to progress made in other regions, and its impact is expected to be felt in various aspects of life for the country’s LGBT community.

46558_46558.caption: A government worker walks to his office along Capitol Plaza The Senate on Friday passed a shortterm spending bill 54 to 44 after voting to restore funding for President Obama s healthcare law
46558_46558.article_context: Washington is facing another crisis as Democrats and Republicans are not engaging in meaningful negotiations to prevent a government shutdown, with partisan divisions deepening since previous fiscal standoffs. House Republicans are demanding a delay to the Affordable Care Act in exchange for keeping the government funded, an ultimatum Democrats consider political extortion and refuse to entertain. Both parties have retreated further from compromise, while past negotiators have become less involved and the parties remain focused on irreconcilable differences. The current impasse highlights the breakdown in bipartisan cooperation and the increased risk of economic damage if no resolution is found.

451922_451922.caption: Two groups that are usually combative in their stance over climate change got together for a dinner party in Bath UK
451922_451922.article_context: Twelve prominent climate scientists and sceptics gathered for a private dinner hosted by Nicholas Lewis in Bath to discuss ways to ease tensions in the climate change debate. Despite differing views on the rate and impacts of global warming, both sides agreed that current online polarisation and name-calling hinder rational scientific discussion. The participants found their disagreements were relatively minor, and all acknowledged the reality of global warming and the need for action. The dinner helped build bridges and foster understanding, with plans proposed for more collaborative events, such as joint conferences, to encourage wider participation and scrutiny of various perspectives within climate science.

462511_462511.caption: The new Alps waterprocessing system at Fukushima Daiichi has raised hopes that it may be possible to decontaminate the radioactive water at the site
462511_462511.article_context: Akira Ono, the manager of the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant, acknowledged continuing challenges in managing radioactive water nearly four years after the 2011 disaster. The plant has amassed over 500,000 tonnes of contaminated water, making containment efforts critical. Tokyo Electric Power (Tepco) is relying on new water treatment technologies and the construction of a large underground frozen barrier to address leaks, though experts doubt their effectiveness. Recently, workers successfully removed spent fuel from reactor No 4, reducing one major risk, but the most dangerous task—removing melted fuel from reactors 1, 2, and 3—remains. Full decommissioning is expected to take at least 40 years and cost around 10 trillion yen.

39761_39761.caption: Afghan policemen investigate at the scene of a suicide attack in Helmand province on Thursday A suicide car bomber attacked a NATO armored vehicle in the southern city of Lashkar Gah killing at least four civilians and wounding 31 others
39761_39761.article_context: A suicide bomber targeted a NATO-led convoy in Afghanistan’s Helmand province, killing three Afghan civilians and injuring over 30 others, including a female coalition official. The attack occurred outside the governor’s compound in Lashkar Gah and was claimed by the Taliban. This incident is part of a recent surge in militant attacks, despite their public willingness to discuss peace with the United States.

449006_449006.caption: In this 11 March 2013 file photo a protest sign stands in a field near Bradshaw Nebraska where the Keystone XL pipeline is proposed to run
449006_449006.article_context: The Keystone XL pipeline project advanced after a US State Department report raised no major objections, prompting supporters to urge swift approval and opponents to continue legal challenges, protests, and civil disobedience planning. The pipeline would transport oil from Canada to Texas, but faces opposition from environmentalists, landowners, and some Nebraska residents who worry about ecological risks, particularly to the Sandhills region and the Ogallala Aquifer. Activists are mobilizing for action if President Obama approves the pipeline, while upcoming political campaigns and lawsuits aim to keep the issue at the forefront ahead of the November elections.

46124_46124.caption: Astronaut Scott Kelly reflects after 11 months in space
46124_46124.article_context: NASA astronaut Scott Kelly is concluding his record-setting 342-day mission on the International Space Station, marking the longest continuous stay by an American on the ISS. The mission focused on studying the effects of extended spaceflight, with scientists comparing Kelly’s health to that of his identical twin, Mark, who remained on Earth, in hopes of gaining insights relevant for future deep-space missions. Kelly also became a prominent social media figure and contributed to experiments supporting long-duration astronaut life, such as growing plants in space. He will return to Earth alongside Russian cosmonaut Mikhail Korniyenko, with their findings expected to inform future human space exploration.

44142_44142.caption: Police guard the front door of Excel Industries in Hesston Kan where a gunman finished a rampage that killed three people and injured 14
44142_44142.article_context: In Hesston, Kansas, Cedric Larry Ford, a troubled employee with an extensive criminal record, carried out a mass shooting at the Excel Industries factory, killing three people and injuring 14 others before being fatally shot by police. The attack began after Ford was served with a restraining order, which authorities believe may have triggered the rampage. The shooting deviated from patterns seen in other recent tragedies, as Ford was African American, had a significant criminal background, and used both a pistol and an assault-style rifle that he obtained illegally through an acquaintance, Sarah T. Hopkins, who was later charged. Hesston’s police chief Doug Schroeder responded quickly and confronted Ford without waiting for backup. The incident left the small, blue-collar community shocked and grieving, amid an ongoing national debate about mass shootings.

43413_43413.caption: If the Supreme Court does not stay a lower court ruling samesex marriages will begin next week in Virginia
43413_43413.article_context: Defenders of Virginia's same-sex marriage ban have asked the Supreme Court to halt a lower court ruling that would allow gay marriages to begin in the state next week. The request, filed by Alliance Defending Freedom, comes after a federal appeals court declared the ban unconstitutional. Virginia's Attorney General agrees that the ban should be overturned but also supports delaying marriages until the Supreme Court decides whether to take up the case. Similar stays have been granted in other states following lower court decisions on same-sex marriage, and the Supreme Court may soon decide whether to review these cases and resolve the issue nationally.

48869_48869.caption: Donald Trump is reaching out to people who believe awful things and might take a pop at Hillary Clinton Va Del Mark Levine
48869_48869.article_context: Virginia Democratic delegate Mark Levine sparked controversy by stating on Fox News that Donald Trump is 'appealing to people who are mentally deficient,' arguing that Trump's rhetoric could incite violence. The Republican Party of Virginia quickly condemned Levine's remark, likening it to Hillary Clinton's earlier 'basket of deplorables' comment. Levine clarified that he did not label all Trump supporters this way, but said Trump's comments might influence dangerous individuals.

53762_53762.caption: People affected by the quake sit under a makeshift sunroof near the rubble of their destroyed homes in Awaran
53762_53762.article_context: Rescue and relief efforts in southwestern Pakistan following a devastating 7.7-magnitude earthquake have been hindered by attacks on security officials and aid workers, particularly in the insurgency-hit Baluchistan province. The quake resulted in over 355 deaths and more than 600 injuries, with thousands of homes destroyed and many areas still inaccessible. Insurgent groups targeted army helicopters and relief teams, raising concerns about the safety of ongoing operations, though Pakistani authorities have vowed to continue assistance. Calls have been made for greater international support, with organizations like the UN and WHO already beginning to provide aid despite volatile conditions.

450337_450337.caption: The proposals suggest setting up dummy businesses to buy antiwind billboards and creating a counterintelligence branch to track the wind energy industry
450337_450337.article_context: A coalition of ultra-conservative groups, many funded by the Koch brothers, has intensified efforts to undermine public support for wind energy and President Obama's renewable energy policies. These organizations, including Americans for Prosperity and the American Legislative Exchange Council, are coordinating campaigns to overturn state laws promoting wind power, launching national PR initiatives, and organizing strategy meetings among local anti-wind activists. Newly revealed documents show plans for widespread subversion tactics and the establishment of a network dedicated to opposing wind farms. The coordinated opposition is seen as part of a broader political strategy leading up to the elections, aiming to frame clean energy as ineffective and reliant on government support.

447783_447783.caption: John Swinney announced overall health spending would rise to 13bn in his budget for Scotland
447783_447783.article_context: Scotland’s finance secretary, John Swinney, announced a budget that increased NHS funding by £500 million, raising health spending to £13 billion, while imposing significant cuts to local councils, arts, environment, justice, and rail services. Swinney introduced a new 3% tax surcharge on second homes and raised business rates for large firms, aiming to boost public finances ahead of the upcoming Scottish elections. The budget froze council and income taxes for another year, despite having new powers to adjust income tax rates. Critics argued the council cuts would lead to major job losses and diminished local services, while Swinney defended his decision to prioritize health funding amid ongoing fiscal challenges.

49303_49303.caption: Watch Marco Rubio deny he s running for his Senate seat again and again
49303_49303.article_context: Senator Marco Rubio has decided to run for reelection in Florida, reversing his earlier stance of not seeking another Senate term. Recent polling shows Rubio leading his potential Democratic opponents, Patrick Murphy and Alan Grayson, though Florida voters remain divided in their opinions of him. While Rubio benefits from strong support among Republican leaders and voters, along with significant fundraising ability, he faces significant challenges—including unimpressive approval ratings, baggage from his failed presidential run, and the possibility of being impacted by Donald Trump’s presence on the ballot. Overall, the Florida Senate race is expected to be closely contested regardless of Rubio's decision to run.

41491_41491.caption: Petraeus speaks at the Association of the United States Army s annual meeting before he became top commander in Afghanistan He replaced Gen Stanley McChrystal who stepped down after remarks published in Rolling Stone magazine
41491_41491.article_context: Former CIA director David Petraeus has agreed to testify before Congress about the September 11 attack on the U.S. mission and CIA base in Benghazi, Libya, despite his recent resignation over an extramarital affair with Paula Broadwell. Petraeus's testimony, expected to take place in closed-door sessions, is highly anticipated by lawmakers seeking clarity on the events leading up to the attack, which killed four Americans, including Ambassador J. Christopher Stevens. Petraeus has denied passing classified information to Broadwell, and the FBI is investigating whether she had unauthorized documents. Congress had indicated it might subpoena Petraeus if he did not appear voluntarily, and his insight is considered crucial for understanding what happened in Benghazi.

458256_458256.caption: The city named Paso de Los Toros sits just north of the Rio Negro in central Uruguay Flowing from east to west the Rio Negro s course takes it through oxbow curves on either side of the city surrounding Paso de Los Toros on three sides Normally the river s banks are smooth and welldefined The torrential rains that struck South America in late November 2009 however pushed the Rio Negro well above its banks and broadened the channels of the smaller water bodies flowing into the river
458256_458256.article_context: In December 2009, several significant natural events and phenomena were observed worldwide: Tens of thousands were evacuated in the Philippines as Mayon Volcano threatened to erupt, with visible lava flows and heightened seismic activity. The eastern United States experienced a record-breaking Nor’easter snowstorm, coating the Mid-Atlantic states with historic snowfall. Agricultural fires were widespread across western Africa, affecting air quality. Severe flooding occurred in Uruguay due to torrential rains, while major snowstorms also covered Texas and the Canadian Arctic. Other notable earth observations included cloud formations over the South Pacific and Kerguelen Islands, sand dunes in the Sahara’s Tenéré Desert, active mining in Western Australia, and landscape features of Malta, Indochina, Fiji, and Hawaii, including historic Pearl Harbor. These satellite and astronaut photographs captured both dramatic weather events and distinctive geological and human-made features across the globe.

42060_42060.caption: Migrant children play in the Jungle a migrant encampment in Calais France that is largely occupied by those hoping to illegally cross the English Channel and enter Britain by way of the Port of Dover in England
42060_42060.article_context: A UNICEF report highlights that unaccompanied child refugees in northern France, particularly in the Calais area, are facing severe exploitation and abuse as the European Union struggles to manage the ongoing refugee crisis. With an estimated 500 children living in unofficial camps, many endure months of dangerous conditions, fall prey to smugglers, and experience sexual exploitation. Efforts to relocate vulnerable children to safer countries, such as Britain, have been slow and fraught with bureaucratic delays, while overall E.U. commitments to resettle migrants have fallen short, leaving many children at risk.

43234_43234.caption: Carper said he and Bowser discussed issues of fairness during their Tuesday meeting
43234_43234.article_context: Washington, D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser met with key federal lawmakers, including House Speaker John Boehner, to discuss issues affecting the District. Bowser noted that Boehner is focused on national priorities and unlikely to intervene in the D.C. marijuana legalization initiative currently under congressional review. Their meeting centered more on Boehner’s ongoing support for the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship Program, a federally funded school voucher initiative that remains a point of contention between Republicans and Democrats. Bowser also met with senators overseeing D.C. affairs, emphasizing concerns over federal budget impacts on the District. Overall, Bowser aimed to establish relationships to better represent D.C.'s interests in Congress.

48322_48322.caption: Police in Diyarbakir Turkey use tear gas and water cannon to disperse people marching to protest the double suicide bombing in Ankara
48322_48322.article_context: Two bomb blasts hit a peace rally in Ankara, Turkey, killing at least 97 people and injuring 246, marking the deadliest terror attack in Turkish history. The attack targeted a gathering of pro-peace activists, including Kurds, amid escalating violence between Turkish forces and Kurdish separatists. While there was no immediate claim of responsibility, officials suspect suicide bombers linked to ISIS, and the attack has heightened concerns over Turkey's internal security and regional instability. The bombings occurred as the Kurdish militant group PKK announced a temporary cease-fire before upcoming general elections, further complicating Turkey's political climate.

467412_467412.caption: Proindependence supporters have donated more than 150000 to a series of crowdfunded initiatives and websites
467412_467412.article_context: Scotland's independence movement has increasingly turned to crowdfunding as a major source of fundraising, collecting over £150,000 for projects such as films, websites, street stalls, and supporting pro-independence bloggers. This grassroots approach offers benefits like consciousness-raising and collective engagement. Despite some successful campaigns, including Wings over Scotland exceeding its targets and raising money to fund opinion polls and wages, other efforts like Newsnet Scotland and Bella Caledonia fell short of their goals. Crowdfunding is viewed as a way to keep the movement community-led and transparent, an issue especially pertinent amid controversy over the official campaign Yes Scotland’s lack of donor disclosure. Overall, crowdfunding is helping independence activists bypass reliance on wealthy donors and fund tangible campaigning efforts.

475869_475869.caption: Bridge of Allan Stirling Campaigners outside the Allan Centre polling station
475869_475869.article_context: On the day of the Scottish independence referendum, voters across Scotland headed to polling stations from major cities like Glasgow and Edinburgh to remote Highland communities, with both pro-independence and pro-union campaigners making their presence felt. Prominent political figures such as Ed Miliband, Gordon Brown, Nicola Sturgeon, Alex Salmond, and Alistair Darling participated in the process, either campaigning or casting their votes. The atmosphere was marked by visible campaigning, local traditions, and a diverse turnout, reflecting the significance of the historic vote.

40124_40124.caption: Sen Durbin President Obama committed to bipartisanship
40124_40124.article_context: Senator Dick Durbin addressed questions about President Obama's ability to work with Congress, asserting that Obama remains committed to bipartisanship. Durbin also discussed his own political prospects during the interview, emphasizing efforts for cooperation in Washington ahead of the upcoming presidential election.

41511_41511.caption: Palestinian women wearing traditional Keffiyeh head scarves gather stones to throw at an Israeli guard tower in the West Bank city of Bethlehem
41511_41511.article_context: Jerusalem is experiencing heightened tension and fear among both Jewish and Muslim residents following the abductions and killings of three Israeli and one Palestinian teenager. Parents are keeping their children indoors, and neighborhood watch groups have formed amid concerns of further revenge attacks. At the same time, Israel faces frequent rocket fire from Gaza, primarily launched by Hamas, prompting Israeli airstrikes and the deployment of additional troops in the south. Six Israeli Jews were arrested in connection with the Palestinian youth's murder, with several confessing to the crime. Political divisions have emerged in Israel regarding how to respond to Hamas, while Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned the murder and promised justice for the Palestinian victim.

44051_44051.caption: Police officers erect a screen around a vegetable stall near the scene of the shooting rampage
44051_44051.article_context: An 18-year-old with dual German and Iranian citizenship carried out a shooting rampage in a busy Munich shopping area, killing nine people and wounding 21 before committing suicide. The attack, considered an act of 'suspected terrorism,' led to a city-wide lockdown and large-scale police operation. Authorities have not determined a clear motive, but are investigating possible ties to anti-immigrant sentiment or Islamist extremism. This shooting marks the third major violent incident in Europe within eight days, following attacks in Nice and Würzburg. Unlike previous attacks, no direct links to Islamic State were found in the case of the Munich gunman.

41530_41530.caption: Waysons Bingo on Thursday November 08 2012 in Lothian Md Bingo halls in Anne Arundel County have seen a drop in revenue with the opening of Maryland Live last June
41530_41530.article_context: Maryland's commercial bingo halls are suffering significant declines due to the expansion of casino gambling, losing customers and revenue to newer, larger venues like Maryland Live and upcoming casinos in Baltimore and National Harbor. Once thriving social and gambling hubs, bingo halls such as Wayson’s have seen attendance drop sharply, their core older demographic dwindling without incoming younger players. The recent approval of expanded gambling, including additional casinos and table games, is expected to further threaten the survival of local bingo operations.

50868_50868.caption: A view of the many lanes of traffic through Tysons with both highoccupancy toll lanes and the regular lanes of the Capital Beltway Virginia is warming to a plan for express lanes on Interstate 66 but the evidence so far that HOT lanes are good for traffic management is problematic
50868_50868.article_context: Virginia transportation officials are considering replacing I-66's HOV lanes with tolled express lanes, aiming to better manage traffic and fund infrastructure improvements, possibly through public-private partnerships. While the existing Beltway HOT lanes are showing improved revenue and usage, early financial returns were below expectations, raising questions about negotiations with private partners. Officials cite anecdotal evidence of reduced congestion and greater travel reliability, though comprehensive data is lacking. The move also seeks to encourage carpooling and bus use, but most current express lane users still opt to pay tolls. Decision-makers caution that assumptions should be questioned as discussions about the project continue.

43777_43777.caption: In 2014 Youlen recorded 77 arrests and ticket citations and handed out 162 parking violations according to his statistics He responded to 221 calls for service Here he s writing a ticket for driving on a suspended license
43777_43777.article_context: Virginia has seen a significant rise in private police officers, known as Special Conservators of the Peace (SCOPs), who are authorized to carry guns, make arrests, and operate in neighborhoods and businesses. While demand for private policing grows as public resources decline, concerns have emerged regarding the limited training and oversight for these officers—just 40 hours until new legislation increased it to 130 hours, still much lower than municipal police standards. Notable incidents, including arrests and abuses involving SCOPs, have drawn scrutiny. The Virginia legislature has passed a bill to increase SCOP training and regulation, with further restrictions on their use of police titles and equipment expected. The trend reflects a nationwide increase in private security, which outnumbers public police, but the rapid expansion has raised questions about accountability and public trust.

43075_43075.caption: Watch Texas police officer pull gun on teens at pool party
43075_43075.article_context: A police incident in McKinney, Texas, where a white officer was filmed aggressively handling a black teenage girl at a pool party, went viral and sparked national debate about police conduct, racial dynamics, and the impact of video recordings in law enforcement. Despite being filmed by several bystanders, the officer used excessive force, leading to his placement on administrative leave. The event highlighted how video footage can both reveal and shape public perceptions of policing, raise questions about officer training and awareness of being recorded, and renew calls for body cameras and better community relations. Experts note that while video transparency offers accountability, it captures only certain moments and does not always reflect the full, complex context of police interactions.

44438_44438.caption: The report Evans filed with Myrtle Beach police via the Smoking Gun
44438_44438.article_context: After two decades of mystery, the identity of 'Grateful Doe', a young man killed in a 1995 car accident in Virginia, was finally revealed as Jason Callahan, thanks to efforts by amateur detectives on Facebook and Reddit. Internet users circulated his photos online, which ultimately reached Callahan's mother, prompting her to file a missing person's report 20 years after he vanished. DNA tests confirmed his identity, bringing closure to a cold case and highlighting the growing impact of social media in solving missing persons cases.

52295_52295.caption: A Free Syrian Army fighter throws a hand grenade inside a Syrian army base during heavy fighting in the Arabeen neighborhood of Damascus
52295_52295.article_context: Syria’s Druze minority, historically neutral in the conflict, is increasingly joining the opposition against President Bashar al-Assad, according to activists and rebel commanders. Recent months have seen anti-government protests and armed rebel activity in the Druze heartland of Sweida province, culminating in significant battles and casualties. While government forces have maintained support from many minority groups, growing insecurity, lack of basic services, and fears of sectarian violence are driving some Druze to rebel. The opposition has formed Druze-dominated units, reflecting shifting loyalties within the community and rising pressure on the Assad regime.

51051_51051.caption: In March 2003 President George W Bush announced a war against Iraq saying its goal was to disarm Iraq of weapons of mass destruction and remove Saddam Hussein from power US forces launched airstrikes on Baghdad then began a ground invasion of the city that quickly lead to the collapse of Hussein s rule The United States formally pulled out of Iraq in late 2011
51051_51051.article_context: The U.S. is preparing to strike Syrian government targets in response to alleged chemical attacks on civilians, a move that experts warn could pull America deeper into Syria's civil war. Historical examples of limited U.S. military interventions, such as strikes in Afghanistan, Sudan, and Iraq, have yielded little strategic success and produced unintended consequences. Some legislators demand congressional approval for any action, stressing the risks of escalation and lack of clear objectives. Analysts caution that punitive strikes without a political strategy could worsen the conflict or strengthen the Assad regime, highlighting concerns over the unpredictable nature and potential fallout of such military operations.

47321_47321.caption: Marines and sailors participating in the Marine Raider Memorial March will carry a plate like this in their rucksack next month
47321_47321.article_context: In March of last year, a UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter crashed off the Florida coast, killing seven elite Marine Raiders and four Louisiana National Guardsmen during a training exercise. To honor their memory, members of Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) will embark on the Marine Raider Memorial March, a grueling 770-mile trek from Navarre Beach near the crash site to Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. The march will raise funds for the Brothers in Arms Foundation and commemorate the fallen by carrying personalized plates and a symbolic paddle decorated with their dog tags. The event highlights the enduring brotherhood among special operations forces and their commitment to honoring those lost in service.

42485_42485.caption: Supporters grasp President Obama s hand as he works the rope line during a campaign stop at the Kissimmee Civic Center in Kissimmee Fla
42485_42485.article_context: The 2012 presidential election, in which President Obama won a second term, revealed several key political shifts. First, the election was not solely an economic referendum, with voters also valuing personal connection and empathy. Second, Republicans faced significant challenges with Hispanic voters, whose growing influence could alter future electoral maps if not addressed. Third, Virginia and North Carolina solidified their status as swing states, expanding the Democratic advantage. Fourth, the youth vote proved consistently influential for Democrats, suggesting a lasting trend. Finally, Democrats appear to have a higher potential electoral vote ceiling than Republicans, raising strategic concerns for future GOP presidential campaigns.

42520_42520.caption: Migrants cross cornfields from Serbia to Croatia on Sept 18 just as thousands did before them in the previous week
42520_42520.article_context: Thousands of child refugees from war-torn countries like Syria and Iraq, including families such as Noor's, are enduring perilous journeys across Europe in search of safety. Many children experience intense trauma from dangerous sea crossings, separation from family, and harsh conditions. Experts warn of serious psychological impacts, but stress that restoring stability, family unity, and access to school can help most children recover. As Europe struggles to address the refugee crisis, a significant number of children are arriving unaccompanied, raising concerns about their vulnerability to abuse and exploitation.

444941_444941.caption: A seagull at Marazion near Penzance Cornwall Like many parts of the UK Cornwall is enjoying milder weather after one of the harshest winters on record Normally due to the effects of the gulf stream winters in Cornwall are among the warmest in the country but this winter the gulf stream was diverted leading to Arctic weather conditions
444941_444941.article_context: A series of environmental and wildlife events were reported globally, including unusually harsh winter weather in Cornwall due to a diverted gulf stream, delayed snowfall amidst severe drought in Beijing, and heightened risks of flooding in Sri Lanka from atypical monsoon patterns. Notable animal stories feature mass seagull migrations to Thailand, habitat loss for red pandas in China, and Asian elephants in Sri Lanka straying into human areas. Conservation efforts and discoveries are highlighted, such as the finding of new frog species in Madagascar and the rescue of abused lions in South Africa. Other stories include wildlife photography competition winners and animal trafficking cases in Thailand.

53828_53828.caption: The USS Oklahoma was sunk by several bombs and torpedoes during the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor A total of 429 crew members died when the ship capsized
53828_53828.article_context: The remains of Navy chaplain Lt. j.g. Aloysius H. Schmitt, a Catholic priest who heroically helped sailors escape from the battleship USS Oklahoma during the Pearl Harbor attack in 1941, have been identified almost 75 years after his death. Father Schmitt sacrificed his life by allowing others to escape before him and was posthumously awarded the Navy and Marine Corps Medal for heroism. His remains were identified using DNA analysis as part of a broader project to identify unknown Pearl Harbor victims. Schmitt will be buried at Loras College in Iowa, where a chapel was built in his honor.

48752_48752.caption: Members of the Nahal Oz kibbutz in Israel gather with their children at the first outdoor group dinner since the start of the current escalation between Israel and Hamas Many of the members who brought their children to the dinner did not stay the night at their home in the kibbutz but chose to return to their temporary shelters farther away from the Gaza Strip
48752_48752.article_context: Residents of Israeli kibbutzim near the Gaza border, such as Nahal Oz and Kfar Aza, are cautiously returning home following a cease-fire between Israel and Palestinian militants. While the cease-fire has brought temporary calm and allowed some families to visit, most residents remain wary due to past experiences of renewed violence and ongoing security concerns. The communities were largely evacuated during the recent conflict, which left homes damaged and some residents traumatized. Many are unsure whether it is safe to return permanently, expressing doubts about lasting peace and noting the persistent risks of living so close to Gaza.

43989_43989.caption: A protester writes on the road in Turkish as he and others gather during a commemoration of the Saturday s bomb blast
43989_43989.article_context: Two bomb blasts at a peace rally in Ankara, Turkey, killed 97 people and injured 246 others, marking the deadliest terror attack in the nation's history. The rally was organized by Turkish trade unions and included Kurdish and leftist activists calling for an end to escalating violence between Turkish security forces and Kurdish militants. Turkish authorities suspect Islamic State (ISIS) involvement, but no group has claimed responsibility. The attack heightened concerns about Turkey's stability amid regional conflicts and domestic polarization, especially ahead of the upcoming November elections.
