Following the bombings, the militant Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) announced a temporary cease-fire. International leaders, including President Obama, condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Turkey.

41080_41080.caption: Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov wins landslide electoral victory celebrates in a suit of armor
41080_41080.article_context: Ramzan Kadyrov, the controversial leader of Chechnya and close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin, celebrated his landslide reelection—reportedly winning about 98 percent of the vote—by attending a public ceremony in a full suit of medieval armor. Kadyrov is widely accused by rights groups of ruling Chechnya through repression and violence, and his loyalty to Putin has been compared to that of a feudal vassal. His latest public display reinforces his reputation for eccentric and flamboyant behavior, as well as his authoritarian style of governance.

454665_454665.caption: Ukip leader Nigel Farage The party has been chasing the Christian vote since the coalition s passage of samesex marriage legislation
454665_454665.article_context: Ukip has released a mini-manifesto targeting Christian voters, promising to protect those who oppose gay marriage on religious grounds. While the party says it will not seek to overturn existing same-sex marriage legislation, it proposes legal safeguards for people expressing religious conscience at work, such as bakers refusing to make cakes for gay weddings or counsellors serving only heterosexual couples. Ukip leader Nigel Farage emphasized the party’s commitment to Britain’s Judaeo-Christian heritage and traditional family values, including increasing the marriage tax allowance for families with a stay-at-home parent.

448312_448312.caption: An antifracking protest outside parliament on Monday The Tories were forced into a Uturn on fasttrack fracking
448312_448312.article_context: The UK government reversed its plan to fast-track fracking after accepting Labour proposals for stricter environmental regulations, amid strong public opposition and the threat of defeat in Parliament. The new rules will ban fracking in national parks and water collection areas, slowing down exploration. While a moratorium on shale gas was rejected, numerous Labour-backed changes to improve safety and oversight were adopted. The move represents a significant policy U-turn, though critics argue the measures are insufficient, and debate over fracking’s future continues as the proposal moves to the House of Lords.

450444_450444.caption: Angela Eagle with Jeremy Corbyn who is rapidly running out of colleagues with whom he sees eye to eye
450444_450444.article_context: Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn faced significant internal party turmoil and public criticism following a series of missteps, including appointing Ken Livingstone to co-chair Labour’s defence review, which angered several colleagues. Corbyn appeared visibly worn and isolated during a challenging Prime Minister’s Questions session, struggling with party disputes and poor communication. Meanwhile, Prime Minister David Cameron capitalized on Labour’s disarray, further highlighting Corbyn’s difficulties as dissent continued to grow within the Labour ranks.

455401_455401.caption: Leanne Wood leader of Plaid Cymru says Scotland gives us in Wales opportunities to point to demonstrable examples of an alternative to neoliberalism
455401_455401.article_context: Plaid Cymru leader Leanne Wood argued that voting for Scottish independence is not a lack of solidarity with England and Wales, but could instead inspire positive change throughout the UK. She urged Scots not to trust Westminster promises of more powers in the event of a 'no' vote, asserting that only independence guarantees greater autonomy. Wood emphasized that Scottish independence could set an example of social justice, contrasting with current UK government policies, and encourage Wales to reconsider its constitutional future. She also called for Wales to move toward self-government, suggesting that a new Welsh constitution should be created by its citizens.

39578_39578.caption: Former Florida Governor Jeb Bush said this week that people should accept court rulings that legalize samesex marriage and show respect for gays in committed relationships while reiterating his longheld belief that marriage is a sacrament
39578_39578.article_context: Jeb Bush, a likely 2016 Republican presidential candidate, has called for acceptance of court rulings legalizing same-sex marriage and urged respect for gay couples, despite personally holding that marriage is a sacrament. This marks a notable shift in tone from previous Republican stances, which were more strongly opposed to same-sex marriage. Bush’s comments highlight divisions within the GOP, where some view the issue as less central while others remain staunchly opposed. As public opinion increasingly favors same-sex marriage and most Democrats support it, Bush’s approach signals a potential new direction for Republicans as they navigate changing societal attitudes.

40754_40754.caption: London Mayor and Conservative Party parliamentary candidate for Uxbridge and Ruislip South Boris Johnson center shakes hands with counting staff as he arrives at the counting center in London
40754_40754.article_context: As Britain's general election campaign intensified, immigrants faced increased scrutiny and scapegoating from politicians, with immigration becoming one of the top campaign issues. A crowdfunded 'I am an immigrant' poster campaign was launched to highlight the positive contributions of immigrants and counter negative rhetoric. Major parties, including the Conservatives and Labour, discussed plans to reduce immigration and control borders, while UKIP's anti-immigration stance pushed the topic further into the spotlight. Despite being blamed for various societal issues, immigrants remain a significant and influential voting bloc, with advocates urging politicians to recognize their value to British society.

469984_469984.caption: David Miliband is to step down as an MP with immediate effect to take up a New York based charity job
469984_469984.article_context: David Miliband has announced his resignation from British politics to become chief executive of the International Rescue Committee charity in New York. His departure will trigger a byelection in South Shields, where he has served as MP since 2001. Miliband, a former foreign secretary and previous contender for Labour leadership, made the decision to end ongoing speculation about his political future and relationship with his brother Ed, the current Labour leader. Prominent Labour figures paid tribute to Miliband’s significant contributions but indicated he could return to politics in the future.

473787_473787.caption: Poster boy Labour s official campaign advert depicts David Cameron as Gene Hunt
473787_473787.article_context: The Labour party is unveiling its first official political poster created by a member of the public, depicting Conservative leader David Cameron as Gene Hunt from the TV series 'Ashes to Ashes,' with the slogan warning against a return to 1980s policies. The poster, chosen from around 1,000 entries in an online competition, reflects Labour's increasing reliance on internet engagement and grassroots creativity due to limited financial resources compared to the Conservatives. Labour hopes the poster will appeal to young voters by highlighting issues like youth unemployment in the 1980s. Meanwhile, the Conservatives are launching their own nationwide advertising campaign targeting Labour and Prime Minister Gordon Brown, bolstered by significant funding. Both parties are adapting digital strategies and recognizing the potential impact of humor and user-generated content in political advertising.

41702_41702.caption: The 639foot freighter New Carissa sits beached while slowly leaking oil into the waters around Oregon s Coos Bay The freighter which ran aground in a storm Feb 4 1999 leaked 70000 gallons of its fuel oil into the ocean The owners of the freighter later sued the Coast Guard for 96 million saying navigational charts omitted warnings about unsafe conditions in the waters where the ship went aground and broke apart A Coast Guard report in October 1999 faulted the ship s operators saying the captain dropped anchor and did not let out enough chain
41702_41702.article_context: Two BP well site leaders, Robert Kaluza and Donald Vidrine, are facing felony manslaughter charges for their roles in the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil rig disaster, which killed 11 crew members and led to the largest oil spill in U.S. history. Their attorneys argue they are being scapegoated for a catastrophe caused by multiple failures across several companies involved. BP has admitted simple negligence and agreed to pay $4.5 billion in fines as part of a criminal plea deal, but the company continues to face a massive civil case and potential further penalties. No onshore BP officials or contractors have been charged. The disaster investigations have found widespread management failures and regulatory oversight issues as key factors contributing to the blowout.

443679_443679.caption: Safari guide Thomas Nkwazi captures the moment when a female leopard grabs a male lechwe around the neck in Okavango Delta Botswana the lechwe incredibly managed to shake free and escape
443679_443679.article_context: This week saw several significant environmental and wildlife events worldwide. Scientists revealed Arabian Sea humpback whales are the most genetically unique and isolated population globally. Southern California experienced record-breaking rainfall, offering drought relief, while China's Poyang Lake dried up, exposing impacts of drought and dam activity. Conservation efforts continue, including the world's largest rat eradication project on South Georgia to protect seabirds. COP 20 UN climate talks opened in Lima, Peru. California banned prize hunting of non-game animals, and Hong Kong activists protested the ivory trade, highlighting concerns over poaching and illegal wildlife trafficking.

49470_49470.caption: Kids analyze the candidates on the eve of the caucuses
49470_49470.article_context: A small focus group of children aged six to eight were shown debate clips of leading presidential candidates and asked for their honest reactions. Their responses, sometimes mirroring adult opinions and sometimes revealing childlike perspectives, highlighted the simplicity and authenticity of children's views on politics. Experts noted similarities between the way some adults and children respond to political discourse, particularly in their willingness to trust candidates without critical thinking. The article suggests that both children and adults can be influenced by personality and entertainment value, as exemplified by the strong reactions to Donald Trump.

40996_40996.caption: Breanne Brodak left and Cortney Tucker kiss after getting married in Pontiac Mich Michigan was one of 14 states enforcing a ban on samesex marriage ahead of Friday s Supreme Court ruling
40996_40996.article_context: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton issued a statement advising county clerks and other officials that they may refuse to issue same-sex marriage licenses on religious grounds, following the Supreme Court's recent decision legalizing same-sex marriage nationwide. Paxton called the ruling a 'lawless decision' and argued that religious liberties are still protected. His guidance has drawn strong criticism from gay rights advocates, who argue that public officials have a duty to serve all couples equally. Paxton acknowledged potential legal risks for officials who refuse to issue licenses and suggested they delegate the task, while also offering legal support for those who object on religious grounds.

44982_44982.caption: Kerry urges Afghan leaders to break presidency dispute
44982_44982.article_context: U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry visited Kabul to urge Afghanistan's presidential candidates, Ashraf Ghani and Abdullah Abdullah, to cooperate with the ongoing audit of disputed election results and to respect the outcome. Kerry's involvement aims to expedite the election review and support a peaceful transfer of power, crucial for the planned withdrawal of U.S. combat forces. Both candidates claim victory amid allegations of widespread fraud, and the election process has been delayed by disputes and public feuding. Kerry previously brokered a deal for an audit and a power-sharing arrangement, but disagreements persist over its implementation, raising concerns about Afghanistan's political stability and future international aid.

48960_48960.caption: Republicans who do nt want to vote for Donald Trump could crowdfund alternatives
48960_48960.article_context: As Donald Trump moves closer to securing the Republican presidential nomination, anti-Trump Republicans are exploring ways to support an alternative candidate, including through crowdfunding platforms like Crowdpac. Crowdpac allows donors to pledge support to any potential conservative candidate—such as Condoleezza Rice, Paul Ryan, Mitt Romney, or Ben Sasse—with donations only charged if the candidate officially enters the race. This system offers both financial backing and anonymity for donors, aiming to encourage prominent Republicans to consider an independent run in the general election. The effort reflects dissatisfaction among GOP voters and activists with Trump’s candidacy and hopes to galvanize enough support and funds to attract a credible third-party conservative alternative.

41439_41439.caption: Wellwishers filled the building to capacity Family friends Howard officials and Mayor Vincent C Gray
41439_41439.article_context: Howard University is preparing for the arrival of students amid renewed concerns about campus safety following two serious crimes: the fatal shooting of a student during a robbery and the reported rape of a campus visitor, both in July. These incidents have intensified scrutiny of campus security, especially as the school also faces financial challenges and staff layoffs. In response, Howard officials have increased security measures, such as more police patrols, 24-hour guards at dorms, and expanded shuttle services. While crime statistics show a decline in robberies over recent years, the university still has a higher rate of street robberies compared to other D.C. schools. Despite the concerns, some students and visitors express confidence in improved safety, and officials are considering long-term strategies to revitalize the surrounding neighborhood.

460350_460350.caption: A shale gas drilling platform in Fort Worth Texas the industry has avoided heavy regulation in the US
460350_460350.article_context: Cuadrilla Resources has announced the discovery of a vast shale gas field under Lancashire and plans to use controversial fracking methods to extract it, sparking concerns about minimal government oversight. Letters between the company, government agencies, and engineers reveal a lack of specific regulations, minimal site inspections, absence of environmental impact studies, and confusion over agency responsibilities. Environmentalists and experts warn that without strong regulation, Britain could face risks similar to those experienced in the US, including water contamination and public health hazards. While some authorities downplay the need for stricter regulation, critics argue that self-monitoring by companies is insufficient to safeguard the environment and public safety.

39375_39375.caption: Rosario Reyes right and Ivania Castillo on a hunger strike in Washington s Lafayette Square opposite the White House They want President Obama to protect certain illegal immigrants against deportation
39375_39375.article_context: A group of undocumented immigrant mothers, known as 'Dreamer Moms,' staged a 10-day hunger strike near the White House, urging President Obama to grant them temporary legal status through executive action. Led by Rosario Reyes, who hoped to benefit from a potential policy change due to her U.S.-citizen child and a son with deferred deportation status, the protest came after Congress failed to pass comprehensive immigration reform. The fast drew attention to the struggles of families divided by immigration laws and increased pressure on Obama to take administrative action that could protect up to 5 million undocumented parents of legal children. The strike ended due to hunger and cold weather, but the activists believed their efforts succeeded in raising national awareness as rumors circulated about imminent presidential action.

447179_447179.caption: Alexander coauthored the paper which says Labour should admit it was not tough enough on the banks
447179_447179.article_context: A pamphlet co-authored by senior Labour figures argues that voter distrust of Labour’s handling of taxpayers’ money poses an existential threat to the party. The report warns that denying public concern over economic competence, as some members do, ignores clear evidence and jeopardizes Labour's chances of election victory. It criticizes Labour’s 2015 campaign for its unclear messaging and leadership, urges the party to appeal to self-employed and older voters, and stresses the need to respect English identity to counter threats from rival parties. The authors advocate balancing pride in past Labour achievements with admissions of past governance failures, particularly regarding banks, welfare, and immigration reform.

469873_469873.caption: Supporters of Andrew Mitchell say the letter is evidence of police heavyhandedness before the Plebgate confrontation
469873_469873.article_context: A previously unreleased letter revealed that Andrew Mitchell, a cabinet minister, was repeatedly denied entry by armed police while cycling into Downing Street more than a year before the 2012 'Plebgate' incident, prompting a formal complaint from No 10 to the Metropolitan Police. Supporters argue this shows a pattern of police obstruction against ministers, suggesting the later Plebgate confrontation was not an isolated case. The letter raises questions about the police's conduct and the investigation into Plebgate, as well as the Met's policy of restricting entry, which has been cited as legal justification. The ongoing dispute has fueled calls for an end to the related libel case and further scrutiny of police actions.

454599_454599.caption: BP s share prices rose almost 5 but fell back after report was published
454599_454599.article_context: A major US federal report on the Deepwater Horizon oil spill found BP primarily responsible for the disaster due to a series of cost-cutting and risk-increasing decisions, but also cited significant failures by its contractors, Halliburton and Transocean. The investigation identified a faulty cement barrier, installed by Halliburton, as a central cause, and highlighted BP's lapses in safety oversight and failure to respond to warning signs. The report cited violations of multiple federal regulations across all companies involved and stated that stronger regulations might have lessened the chances of such a catastrophe. While legal responsibility and financial liabilities remain under dispute, BP acknowledged its role and called for other parties to do the same. The spill killed 11 people and released nearly 5 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico in 2010.

451741_451741.caption: Pope Francis talks to Ana Laura Perez Jaimes right a victim of forced labour who addressed the conference on Modern Slavery and Climate Change at the Vatican
451741_451741.article_context: Pope Francis expressed optimism that a key international agreement on climate change could be achieved in Paris and emphasized the United Nations' central role in combating global warming and related human trafficking issues. His comments came during a Vatican-hosted meeting of global mayors focused on the link between environmental challenges, migration, and modern slavery. Harrowing testimonies from survivors of trafficking highlighted the humanitarian crisis. The Pope reiterated the message of his recent encyclical, calling for action on climate change, phasing out fossil fuels, and addressing social inequalities, and stressed the crucial role of local leaders in driving effective reforms.

464955_464955.caption: Nigel Farage said he would work with whichever group is designated as the official no campaign
464955_464955.article_context: Nigel Farage, leader of Ukip, has launched a UK-wide tour advocating for Britain to leave the EU, but stressed he is not seeking to head the official 'no' campaign in the forthcoming referendum. Farage emphasized Ukip's capacity for grassroots mobilization while expressing willingness to collaborate with whichever group is chosen as the official campaign, amid competition between Conservative-backed and Ukip-affiliated factions. The controversy over Ukip’s role persists within the party and among Eurosceptics, with Farage asserting that immigration and migration within Europe will be central issues in the debate.

450141_450141.caption: Alex Salmond says the three party leaders vow was cooked up in desperation from the last days of the campaign
450141_450141.article_context: Alex Salmond, Scotland’s outgoing first minister, accused UK party leaders of misleading voters into rejecting Scottish independence by reneging on their promise of greater devolution following the referendum, where 55% voted against independence. Tensions arose between Prime Minister David Cameron and Labour leader Ed Miliband over reforms linking Scottish powers with the voting rights of Scottish MPs in Westminster. Amid accusations that the devolution pledge was being delayed or diluted, pro-independence parties saw a surge in membership and called for renewed efforts ahead of the next general election. UK party leaders and officials insist the timetable for increased Scottish powers will be honoured, despite disputes and growing public skepticism.

42077_42077.caption: General Powell said at a meeting of the Long Island Association that he would be voting for Hillary Clinton a spokeswoman confirmed Oct 25 Powell added in an interview that he picked Clinton because I think she s qualified and the other gentleman is not qualified
42077_42077.article_context: A new Washington Post-ABC News poll shows that Bernie Sanders supporters are quickly rallying behind Hillary Clinton, with only 8 percent now willing to support Donald Trump—down from 20 percent last month. This swift shift is helping Clinton expand her lead over Trump to double digits. Compared to similar situations in past elections, Clinton is consolidating Democratic support much faster than Barack Obama did in 2008. The poll suggests that Trump's hopes of winning over Sanders voters are unfounded, as most Sanders supporters are strongly opposed to the Republican Party.

459767_459767.caption: EPA says the proposed cut is part of a larger Republican project to roll back years of environmental and safety protection
459767_459767.article_context: Republicans in Congress have proposed a 17% budget cut to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and challenged its authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions, arguing these measures are necessary to curb 'job-killing' regulations. EPA chief Lisa Jackson defended the agency, warning the moves are part of a broader Republican effort to weaken environmental protections such as the Clean Air Act. The hearing highlighted deep divisions on climate change, with Republicans questioning the science and legality of EPA actions, while Democrats and former officials insisted the agency has a legal responsibility to address climate risks. The proposed cuts also target funding for high-speed rail, energy efficiency, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Agency.

47538_47538.caption: A helicopter purportedly carrying Trump arrives in Mexico City
47538_47538.article_context: Donald Trump met with Mexican President Enrique Peña Nieto in Mexico City, where both leaders struck a surprisingly cordial tone and avoided direct confrontation, particularly about Trump's long-promised border wall. However, hours later in Phoenix, Trump returned to his hardline immigration rhetoric, vowing to deport those in the United States illegally and promising zero tolerance for criminal offenders. The apparent contrast between Trump’s moderated posture in Mexico and aggressive stance in the U.S. raised questions about his true intentions on immigration policy. Disagreements about the border wall persisted, with Peña Nieto publicly insisting Mexico will not pay for it, despite Trump's campaign promises. The events highlighted shifting campaign strategies as Trump attempted to appeal to more moderate voters amid declining poll numbers.

442951_442951.caption: Megadairy factory farms are too high risk and not a sound longterm option
442951_442951.article_context: Britain’s dairy industry is facing a serious crisis, with thousands of farms shutting down due to economic pressures and an unsustainable business environment. The number of dairy farms has plummeted from around 30,000 to just 11,000 in the last decade, and many remaining farmers are leaving the sector. While large-scale, US-style ‘mega-dairies’ are promoted as a solution, they pose significant financial and animal welfare risks and may not provide the promised economic benefits. Entrepreneur Deborah Meaden warns against abandoning traditional, small-scale dairy farming in favor of risky, intensive models, and calls for support of sustainable practices to preserve the UK’s rural landscape and farming heritage.

464042_464042.caption: Eustice says farmers would continue to receive subsidies from an independent UK
464042_464042.article_context: At the National Farmers’ Union conference, farming minister George Eustice argued that leaving the European Union would provide the UK with an £18 billion annual ‘Brexit dividend,’ enabling increased national spending on farming and environmental measures. Eustice assured farmers that industry subsidies would be maintained post-Brexit, and emphasized that the UK could create more effective agricultural policies outside the EU. Meanwhile, environment secretary Liz Truss urged caution, highlighting risks to food exports and farm income if access to the single market were lost. The event underscored the split within the UK government over the Brexit issue, particularly concerning the future of British agriculture.

39151_39151.caption: A North Korean defector prepares to release balloons bearing leaflets condemning North Korean leader Kim Jong Il and his son Kim Jong Un during an antiNorth Korea demonstration at the Imjingak Pavilion near the border village of Panmunjom in South Korea on Dec 21 2011
39151_39151.article_context: North Korea has sharply reduced the number of defectors leaving the country this year, following a major crackdown on border crossings under new leader Kim Jong Eun. The government has increased security along the Chinese border, dispatching extra soldiers and threatening severe punishments for both defectors and their families. These measures have resulted in a 42 percent drop in North Koreans arriving in South Korea compared to last year, reversing a long-running trend of growing defections. Aid groups report higher bribe demands and new penalties for using Chinese cellphones, making escape more difficult and dangerous, and causing defectors in South Korea to hesitate before helping family members attempt to flee.

42008_42008.caption: ProRussian activists hold red flags with the communist hammer and sickle and the soviet USSR initials during a rally at the regional administration building in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kharkiv
42008_42008.article_context: Violence escalated in eastern Ukraine as Ukrainian authorities launched a major 'anti-terrorist operation' against pro-Russian separatists occupying government buildings in the Donetsk region, resulting in a deadly gun battle and multiple casualties. The conflict prompted international concern, with the United States warning of tougher sanctions on Russia if aggression continued, and Russia condemning Ukraine's actions while threatening serious consequences. Despite offers of amnesty, separatists have refused to vacate occupied buildings, expanding control across several towns amid reports of police defections and the presence of tens of thousands of Russian troops at the border. The UN Security Council convened but failed to reach a resolution, as Western nations accused Russia of orchestrating the unrest and manipulating media coverage.

52110_52110.caption: George Mason University students Kristyn Moskey and Alex Grazian record water data in Gunston Cove as part of the PEREC project to monitor and minimize the impact of wastewater on the cove the Potomac River and the Chesapeake Bay
52110_52110.article_context: George Mason University’s Potomac Environmental Research and Education Center (PEREC), in partnership with the Noman M. Coleman, Jr. Pollution Control Plant, has significantly reduced pollution entering the Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay by monitoring and improving wastewater treatment since the 1980s. Their collaborative efforts have resulted in notable ecological improvements and recognition from environmental agencies. The program also includes environmental education initiatives for local students, fostering awareness and interest in science careers. Plans are underway to build a new $23 million research and education center at Belmont Bay, which will further expand laboratory facilities and public outreach.

44820_44820.caption: A police officer collects evidence at the site of the explosion near the shrine
44820_44820.article_context: Thai authorities have ruled out international terrorism as the cause of the deadly pipe bomb attack at Bangkok's Erawan Shrine, which killed 20 people and injured more than 120, many of whom were tourists. Investigators believe the attack was planned months in advance by a network of at least 10 people, with no group yet claiming responsibility. The motive appears aimed at damaging Thailand's economy and tourism industry, but officials have not determined whether Muslim separatists or domestic political activists were involved. Police are seeking international assistance to identify a key suspect seen leaving a backpack at the blast site, and have issued a sketch and a substantial reward for information leading to an arrest.

50928_50928.caption: A man crosses the street in Tunis as Tunisians protest the Belaid s killing In a recent television interview Belaid accused the Islamist Ennahda party of giving a green light to political assassinations
50928_50928.article_context: Chokri Belaid, a prominent Tunisian opposition leader and critic of the Islamist-led government, was assassinated outside his home, highlighting deepening political tensions in post-Arab Spring Tunisia. The killing triggered protests and clashes between Belaid’s supporters and police, with opposition members blaming extremist Islamist groups and the governing Ennahda party. In response, Prime Minister Hamadi Jebali announced plans to dissolve the government and form a technocratic cabinet to address the crisis. Belaid’s death, the first political assassination since Tunisia’s 2011 revolution, underscores the growing struggle between Islamist factions and secular opponents, and raises concerns about increasing political violence and instability across North Africa.

44360_44360.caption: Ballot boxes are opened at Prime Minister David Cameron s constituency election count in Witney England
44360_44360.article_context: As Britain’s general election campaign draws to a close, immigrants complain of being unfairly blamed for social problems by politicians and the media, who have made immigration a central issue alongside the economy and health care. In response, the Movement Against Xenophobia launched a nationwide 'I am an immigrant' poster campaign to highlight positive immigrant contributions. Politicians from major parties, including Conservative leader David Cameron and Labour’s Ed Miliband, promise stricter immigration controls, while the anti-immigration UK Independence Party has influenced public debate with inflammatory statements. Despite political scapegoating, immigrants remain a significant voting bloc, leading observers to caution parties against alienating minorities as demographic shifts continue.

42888_42888.caption: Christy Romero special inspector general with the Troubled Asset Relief Program
42888_42888.article_context: The Office of the Special Inspector General for the Troubled Asset Relief Program (SIGTARP) has successfully prosecuted over 100 senior bank executives since 2008 for misusing government bailout funds during the financial crisis, resulting in significant prison sentences and billions in restitution. While most convictions have targeted community bankers rather than major Wall Street figures, SIGTARP’s robust criminal authority and cooperation with other agencies have set a precedent for accountability. Lawmakers are praising SIGTARP’s effectiveness and encouraging other financial regulators to pursue more criminal referrals, highlighting an ongoing debate about the best ways to address banking misconduct.

45049_45049.caption: A construction worker swings a sledgehammer while cutting reinforcement bars to repair an apartment complex destroyed by a car bomb in a Shiite neighborhood of Abbas Town in Karachi The sectarian attack killed at least 45 people and wounded more than 135 in March Sectarian killings are just one of the variety of categories of crime the residents of Karachi face
45049_45049.article_context: Karachi, Pakistan's largest city, is facing a surge in violence and insecurity as the Pakistani Taliban strengthens its presence. A sharp increase in terrorist attacks, targeted killings of police officers, and sectarian violence have left residents fearful and local authorities overwhelmed. The Taliban and other militant groups are taking control of neighborhoods, forcing residents to contribute to their cause. The rising threat has led to increased sales of armored vehicles and personal security measures among civilians. Despite government efforts to negotiate and launch security operations, many believe the city is teetering on the brink of lawlessness, with ordinary crime also thriving under the climate of fear.

44617_44617.caption: President Obama makes a campaign stop at Elm Street Middle School in Nashua NH
44617_44617.article_context: In the final days of the 2012 presidential campaign, President Obama embarked on a frantic 48-hour tour of key swing states as his campaign sought to shore up support amidst tightening national polls. David Plouffe, Obama's top strategist, remained focused on battleground state data, dismissing concerns about national momentum favoring rival Mitt Romney and rejecting unfavorable poll results as unreliable. The campaign emphasized its ground game and turnout efforts, particularly among traditionally less reliable Democratic voters such as Latinos, African Americans, and the young. Despite signs of fatigue, both Obama and his team projected confidence, while supporters expressed anxiety over the race’s closeness. Ultimately, the Obama campaign’s strategy centered on maintaining discipline, boosting enthusiasm, and controlling the narrative as Election Day approached.

46255_46255.caption: House GOP praises vote to defund Obamacare
46255_46255.article_context: The House of Representatives, led by Republicans, passed a spending bill that includes provisions to defund President Obama's Affordable Care Act, setting up a major political standoff with Senate Democrats and the White House. The vote increases the risk of a government shutdown if no compromise is reached before the funding deadline on September 30. President Obama responded strongly, accusing Republicans of prioritizing political games over the nation's wellbeing. As the bill moves to the Senate, GOP leaders like Ted Cruz and Mike Lee promise further efforts to block Obamacare, intensifying tensions and uncertainty over federal funding and the debt ceiling.

55950_55950.caption: Mourners attend a funeral in Istanbul for Gulsen Bahadur 29 who was killed in the attacks at the airport
55950_55950.article_context: A suicide attack by three suspected Islamic State militants at Istanbul's international airport killed at least 44 people and wounded over 200, deepening fears and worsening an already dire tourism slump in Turkey. The wave of terrorism, including attacks attributed to Kurdish and Islamic State groups, has caused tourism—a major part of Turkey's economy—to plummet to its lowest levels in 17 years, leaving hotels and shops in historic areas like the Grand Bazaar and Sultanahmet nearly empty. Economic analysts predict further negative impacts, including slowed growth and persistent inflation. There is some potential optimism as relations improve with Russia, which may lead to a return of Russian tourists, but overall, the sector faces unprecedented challenges.

475906_475906.caption: Edinburgh The leader of the Better Together campaign Alistair Darling with his wife Maggie and no campaigners outside the polling station at the Church Hill Theatre
475906_475906.article_context: Voters across Scotland turned out to polling stations as campaigning for and against independence continued on referendum day. Key political figures from the Labour and Conservative parties, as well as leaders of both the Yes and No campaigns, were seen supporting their causes, engaging with local communities, and casting their ballots. The atmosphere was marked by public displays of support and activism, highlighting a significant moment as Scottish citizens participated in deciding the country's future.

40563_40563.caption: Michael Ugbo 5 holds the hand of a St George fireman as residents are evacuated from floodwaters in Baton Rouge
40563_40563.article_context: A historic flood in southern Louisiana forced twenty-two school districts to close, affecting tens of thousands of students and delaying the start of the school year. While most districts plan to reopen within two weeks, school leaders say their biggest challenge is a shortage of teachers and staff, many of whom have been displaced from their homes. Districts are considering combining schools and creating new bus routes to accommodate students, many of whom are already disadvantaged. Damage to facilities is extensive, with some schools unfit for use and many employees and students having lost everything. Authorities hope to restore stability and continuity for students, while providing support for their mental health amid ongoing recovery efforts.

461338_461338.caption: School children are ferried by boat after the Thames burst its banks in Old Windsor
461338_461338.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron has urged his cabinet to end internal disputes and focus on the government's response to severe flooding in the Thames Valley, as thousands of homes face evacuation amid record rainfall and rising river levels. Cabinet ministers clashed publicly over the handling of the crisis and the role of the Environment Agency, leading Cameron to emphasize the need for unity and immediate action. Emergency services and the army have been deployed, with further bad weather expected, while officials warn that recovery efforts may take months. Calls to assign blame were dismissed, with Cameron and the Environment Agency stressing that now is the time for practical support, not criticism.

53802_53802.caption: An officer with Afghan National Police inspects vehicles entering Jalalabad City near the Behsud Bridge
53802_53802.article_context: In Afghanistan’s Nangahar province, the rise of the Islamic State (ISIS) has brought unprecedented brutality, prompting many locals to view the Taliban as a lesser evil. The ISIS fighters, mostly defectors from the Afghan and Pakistani Taliban, seized control of villages, executed civilians and imposed harsh social decrees, particularly targeting women and girls. This has sparked mass displacement, with tens of thousands fleeing their homes. The group’s extremist ideology, enforcement of Wahhabism, and violent tactics have shattered previous US-backed social gains and intensified regional instability. While ISIS's presence is expanding across Afghanistan, interviews indicate that most Afghans do not support their ideology. The chaos caused by ISIS has led some villagers to look back on Taliban rule as preferable, highlighting the deepening humanitarian crisis and complex power struggles in the region.

50850_50850.caption: Edie Windsor left an activist for samesex marriage and Julie Milligan
50850_50850.article_context: President Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama hosted a State Dinner on February 11, 2014, at the White House in honor of French President Francois Hollande. The guest list included prominent political figures such as Vice President Joe Biden, Secretary of State John Kerry, and members of Congress, as well as French government officials and celebrities like JJ Abrams, Mary J. Blige, Stephen Colbert, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, and Elon Musk. The event was a demonstration of diplomatic relations and cultural exchange between the United States and France, showcasing the importance of State Dinners in strengthening international partnerships.

43616_43616.caption: In this photo released by China s Xinhua News Agency Chinese President Xi Jinping right greets North Korean Vice Marshal Choe Ryong Hae in Beijing Friday May 24 2013
43616_43616.article_context: North Korea has signaled a possible willingness to rejoin international negotiations on ending its nuclear weapons program, following months of tensions and provocations. A high-level envoy delivered a letter from leader Kim Jong Un to Chinese President Xi Jinping, indicating a desire to reengage with China and other parties. President Xi urged North Korea to resume dialogue aimed at denuclearization and regional stability. While North Korea expressed openness to negotiations, skepticism remains due to its past tactics of escalating tensions to secure concessions, and doubts persist regarding the effectiveness of future talks.

454314_454314.caption: Vince Cable said companies should have no wriggle room to abandon assurances
454314_454314.article_context: Business Secretary Vince Cable announced that foreign companies taking over British firms could face multimillion-pound fines if they break promises to protect jobs and investment. This follows concerns raised by Pfizer's attempted takeover of AstraZeneca and Kraft's earlier broken pledge after acquiring Cadbury. The government is considering tightening laws and potentially broadening the public interest test to give ministers more power to block hostile takeovers in vital sectors, though this proposal has not yet gained full support. Cable emphasized the importance of inward investment but stressed that stricter measures are necessary to protect national interests and ensure companies are held to their commitments. He also defended the government's handling of the Royal Mail sale and criticized proposed Tory changes to strike ballot laws as unnecessary.

467010_467010.caption: David Cameron is facing questions on emergency brake critics say won t make any impact on immigration
467010_467010.article_context: Downing Street faces criticism from both pro- and anti-EU sides over the proposed 'emergency brake' on migrant benefits, with many arguing it will have little impact on reducing migration to the UK. David Cameron’s team admits key details of how the mechanism would work are still unresolved, while prominent figures such as Labour’s Alan Johnson and Conservative MP David Davis dismiss the measure as ineffective, arguing that migrants are attracted by higher wages rather than benefits. As Cameron seeks support for his EU reform proposals ahead of meetings with European leaders, some positive signals have emerged from figures like François Hollande and Justine Greening, though divisions remain within the leave campaign.

53290_53290.caption: A Free Syrian Army fighter fires his weapon in Aleppo s Saif alDawla district
53290_53290.article_context: The Syrian government has intensified its use of crude 'barrel bombs' in aerial attacks on Aleppo and nearby towns, leading to hundreds of civilian deaths, including many children. These improvised explosive devices, dropped by helicopters, have caused widespread destruction and terror, prompting international condemnation from the US and UK. The escalation comes ahead of planned peace talks in Geneva, with activists and rebel fighters accusing the regime of increasing violence to gain leverage. Clashes between government forces and rebels have also erupted in sectarian hotspots, highlighting the deepening divisions in Syria's ongoing civil war.

47138_47138.caption: Daughter of undocumented parents I do nt feel brave every day
47138_47138.article_context: At the Democratic National Convention, 11-year-old Karla Ortiz, daughter of undocumented immigrants, delivered a moving speech about her daily fear of her parents being deported, highlighting the anxieties felt by millions of American children in similar situations. Her story exemplified the power of personal storytelling in political advocacy, framing immigration not just as a policy issue but as a human one. The article contextualizes Karla’s speech within broader debates over U.S. immigration policy, contrasting the approaches of Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton, and explores how emotional narratives like hers can mobilize support, stir empathy, or provoke opposition across partisan lines.

45010_45010.caption: Republican presidential nominee Mitt Romney and his wife Ann talk to supporters at an airport rally in Newington NH Romney began an eightstate tour in New Hampshire on Saturday in a final bid to woo undecided voters in swing states
45010_45010.article_context: The upcoming vice presidential debate between Joe Biden and Paul Ryan is seen as unusually important following Mitt Romney’s strong performance in the first presidential debate. Biden aims to halt Romney's momentum and defend the Obama record, while Ryan seeks to build on recent Republican gains and solidify his reputation as a key party leader. Polls show a tightening race, especially in battleground states, making this debate a potentially pivotal moment in the campaign. Both candidates are experienced and have much at stake, with their performances likely to influence public opinion ahead of the next presidential debate.

444578_444578.caption: David Cameron and Nick Clegg At 520000 split between Tories and Lib Dems it was the largest donation in the last three months
444578_444578.article_context: After public debate, the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats decided to donate a £520,000 bequest from Joan Edwards to the Treasury, following clarification that her will intended the money for the government rather than political parties. The funds will provide a financial boost during ongoing austerity measures.

446106_446106.caption: John Sawers the UK ambassador to the UN who has been appointed head of MI6
446106_446106.article_context: British foreign secretary David Miliband downplayed concerns after personal family photos of Sir John Sawers, the incoming head of MI6, were found on Facebook and published by the Mail on Sunday. The images, uploaded without privacy settings by Sawers’s wife, showed details of their private life and family, leading to claims they could have security implications. Miliband dismissed calls for a review of Sawers’s appointment, defending his suitability for the role and criticizing the media for sensationalizing the story. While some politicians called for an inquiry, others made light of the issue, doubting its real significance to national security.

45925_45925.caption: Rebecka Ortiz puts away their groceries as Sariah grabs some juice drinks that her mother had just put away Rebecka read that the average monthly SNAP benefit lasts a family 17 days and she knows from personal experience the anxiety headaches that come at the end of every month when their SNAP money runs out their bank account is empty and she is left to ply Woonsocket s emergency food pantries
45925_45925.article_context: In Woonsocket, Rhode Island, the local economy experiences a dramatic surge each month when nearly $2 million in SNAP (food stamp) benefits are distributed to one-third of the town's population. Stores prepare for a rush of customers on the first of the month, stocking up and hiring extra staff to accommodate the influx. For many residents, such as the Ortiz family, SNAP funds provide a crucial lifeline, though the benefits often run out after a couple of weeks, forcing them to rely on food pantries and endure cycles of scarcity. The monthly SNAP distribution has become so central that it shapes business operations, grocery shopping habits, and daily life in the town, highlighting ongoing economic challenges and the deep reliance on government assistance.

41392_41392.caption: People look at a missile embedded in the street after shelling in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk
41392_41392.article_context: As heavy fighting intensifies in eastern Ukraine between pro-Russian rebels and government forces, leaders from Ukraine, Russia, Germany, and France met in Minsk for high-stakes peace talks aimed at brokering a cease-fire. The discussions focused on implementing a previous, failed truce, pulling back heavy weaponry, and negotiating autonomy for rebel-held regions—while Ukraine demanded Russia halt military support to the rebels. The conflict has worsened Ukraine's economy, raised tensions between Russia and the West, and prompted debates about arming Ukraine, with U.S. officials warning Russia of escalating consequences if hostilities continue.

459156_459156.caption: Dominic Raab People who are coasting it should be easier to let them go
459156_459156.article_context: Dominic Raab and other Conservative MPs from the Free Enterprise Group are calling for radical reforms to Britain's economic and workplace policies, arguing that the country suffers from a weak work ethic and excessive worker protections. Their forthcoming book, Britannia Unchained, controversially criticizes Britain as a nation of 'idlers' and urges less regulation and lower wages as part of a move towards more aggressive neoliberal policies. These views reflect a broader movement on the Tory right that believes current austerity measures are insufficient, advocating deeper spending cuts and deregulation. Despite gaining influence, these MPs face resistance from the coalition government and uncertain public support, with the possibility of such reforms only likely if the Conservatives secure a clear future majority.

444008_444008.caption: 1943 Winston Churchill and President Franklin D Roosevelt arrive at the White House
444008_444008.article_context: The article presents a chronological photo timeline highlighting the longstanding relationship between British prime ministers and US presidents from World War II to the present. Key moments are depicted from Churchill and Roosevelt during WWII, through various leaders such as Thatcher and Reagan, Blair and Clinton, up to recent meetings between Obama and Cameron. The series illustrates the continuity and importance of the transatlantic alliance over several decades.

43956_43956.caption: Inmates carry boxes of produce to those in need after tending to a garden at the Eastern Correctional Institution in Westover Md
43956_43956.article_context: Prison officials across the United States, including those at Maryland’s largest penitentiary, have embraced inmate gardening programs as tools for rehabilitation and transformation. Inmates, some convicted of serious crimes, work together to cultivate large gardens, producing fresh vegetables for themselves and donating food to local communities in need, promoting both restorative justice and healthier diets. These programs have shown promising results in reducing recidivism rates, with less than 10 percent of participants returning to prison compared to the national average of over 60 percent. Prisoners report finding purpose and hope through gardening, while correctional staff and nonprofit organizations support the expansion of these programs nationwide.

44918_44918.caption: President Obama right holds an immigration reform roundtable with business owners and entrepreneurs in the Roosevelt Room of the White House in Washington
44918_44918.article_context: President Obama's approval rating has significantly increased over the past year, rising from a majority disapproving at the start of the year to a majority approving according to recent Gallup polls. This improvement has been driven largely by more favorable views among independents, as well as increases among Hispanics, young people, and women, while groups such as college graduates, older individuals, church-goers, and black Americans have shown little change. The shift in Obama's popularity could have a positive impact on the Democratic Party during an election cycle featuring generally unpopular major-party nominees.

41660_41660.caption: A detained protester cries in front of a burning barricade during a protest against the president in Bujumbura
41660_41660.article_context: Burundi is facing a deepening political crisis following President Pierre Nkurunziza's decision to seek a third term, which many see as a violation of the peace accord that ended the country's civil war. This move has sparked daily protests, violent clashes, and at least nine deaths, while over 40,000 people have fled the country fearing further unrest. The constitutional court's endorsement of Nkurunziza's decision intensified the situation, raising concerns of a return to widespread violence and threatening regional stability, especially as neighboring countries face similar issues regarding presidential term limits.

53610_53610.caption: Sunni men play dominoes at a small coffee shop in the Adhamiyah neighborhood of Baghdad The men all taxi drivers say they recently began to refuse to take fares into predominantly Shiite areas due to fears of sectarian violence
53610_53610.article_context: Sectarian killings have resurfaced in Baghdad amid the ongoing conflict with ISIS, raising fears of a return to the violence that ravaged the city during Iraq’s 2005-07 civil war. Sunnis in Baghdad are growing increasingly anxious as Shiite-dominated security forces and militias, mobilized in response to the ISIS threat, have been implicated in abductions and killings reminiscent of earlier sectarian cleansing. While Shiite communities largely view these militias as defenders against ISIS, Sunnis feel vulnerable and marginalized, lacking both protection and recourse to authorities they mistrust. The renewed violence highlights enduring sectarian tensions and a lack of reconciliation since the U.S. troop withdrawal, with many fearing a relapse into widespread bloodshed.

53960_53960.caption: An Iraqi prisoner of war comforts his 4yearold son at a regrouping center for POWs captured by the Army s 101st Airborne Division near Najaf Iraq Nearly 4500 Americans were killed in the eightyear war and by some estimates more than 100000 Iraqis died
53960_53960.article_context: A decade after the U.S. invasion, Iraq remains deeply divided, balancing between pockets of progress and ongoing chaos. While the northern Kurdish region and southern Shiite provinces have experienced economic growth and security, predominantly Sunni areas are mired in disenfranchisement, protests, and renewed insurgent threats. Tensions between the central government under Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki, Sunni communities, and the autonomous Kurds, particularly over political representation and control of oil-rich regions, risk returning the country to sectarian violence. Despite some success stories, such as development in Najaf, Iraq is still grappling with unresolved ethnic and sectarian divisions, fragile governance, and the legacy of war.

42353_42353.caption: Cattle bask in the sun at Cappadona Beefmasters in Linn Tex Ranch owner Fred Cappadona says more illegal immigrants are beginning to trespass on his property and he welcomes the Texas National Guard to the area
42353_42353.article_context: President Obama’s decision to delay promised changes to immigration policy until after the November elections sparked intense backlash from undocumented immigrants and advocacy groups, who accused him of putting political concerns ahead of Latino families’ needs. Activists and community leaders expressed deep disappointment, highlighting a longstanding pattern of unfulfilled promises to address immigration reform. While some Democratic lawmakers saw the move as a pragmatic step to protect Senate control, Latino leaders warned it could erode trust and voter support, especially among communities directly affected by deportation and family separation. The decision reignited debates over Obama’s commitment to meaningful action on immigration, leaving uncertain whether Latino voters will mobilize for Democrats in upcoming elections.

49177_49177.caption: A Syrian girl carries her brother in the Al Zaatri refugee camp in the Jordanian city of Mafraq Jordan s public embrace of refugees and defectors is potentially risky for a nation that is a relative oasis of stability in a volatile region
49177_49177.article_context: Syrian refugee camps in Jordan, particularly Zaatari, are experiencing a rise in outside men—especially from Gulf countries—seeking to marry Syrian women, often widows and underage girls. Driven by poverty and desperation, families sometimes accept dowries, though many face pressure and exploitation, with marriages frequently brokered through matchmakers and websites. Relief officials warn of non-consensual unions, child brides, and risks of abandonment or forced prostitution. The practice has sparked concern and resistance among refugees, with some forming groups to confront would-be suitors, while aid organizations and the UN are attempting to curb the trend.

55617_55617.caption: McCain warns of growing Islamic State presence in Afghanistan
55617_55617.article_context: Senator John McCain warned in Kabul that the Obama administration’s plan for a calendar-based withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan would be a serious mistake, potentially emboldening the Taliban and risking the country’s security gains. McCain argued that ongoing Taliban attacks and the emergence of ISIS show the need for a conditions-based approach, recommending that the U.S. maintain 5,000-6,000 troops after 2016 instead of sharply reducing numbers as planned. His remarks followed a deadly Taliban attack on Afghan police near Kabul and highlighted political instability in the Afghan government, including the parliament's rejection of a key defense nominee.

42162_42162.caption: A Ukrainian serviceman from the Azov Battalion trains volunteers in the southeastern Ukrainian city of Mariupol
42162_42162.article_context: Fighting erupted near Donetsk airport, threatening the eight-day cease-fire in eastern Ukraine. Ukrainian Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of aiming to destroy Ukraine and argued that only NATO membership could protect the country from Russian aggression. Despite ongoing violations of the cease-fire and continued harsh rhetoric, government forces still hold the airport while the city remains under separatist control. Meanwhile, a second Russian convoy delivered humanitarian aid to the region, crossing the border into Luhansk without major incident.

43608_43608.caption: Busboy Juan Romero right aids Sen Robert F Kennedy shown lying on the kitchen floor of the Ambassador Hotel moments after being fatally shot by assassin Sirhan Sirhan
43608_43608.article_context: A photograph of Boston Marathon runner Bill Iffrig, knocked down by the blast during the 2013 bombing, has become an iconic image widely circulated in media. Iffrig, a 78-year-old grandfather, was instantly recognized as the 'Fallen Runner,' joining the ranks of individuals who have come to symbolize tragic moments in history through powerful photographs. The article reflects on how poignant single images—like those from Kent State, Oklahoma City, and other crises—capture the humanity and personal impact of such events, helping society process and remember them. It ultimately notes that while tragedy is distilled into images, what endures is resilience, as represented by Iffrig getting up to finish his race.

42097_42097.caption: The Federal Election Commission meets on April 25 and hears Craig Engle lower right discuss a point about contributions from same sex married couples and single or joint checking accounts
42097_42097.article_context: President Obama's early promises to reform campaign finance and reduce special interest influence have largely faded since his reelection, disappointing advocates of stricter regulations. Key reform efforts have stalled, including failing to fill vacant roles at the Federal Election Commission and not pursuing actions to overturn Citizens United. Obama’s decision to convert his campaign organization into a political advocacy group accepting unlimited donations has drawn criticism from reformers and former allies. Despite initial steps to increase transparency and restrict lobbying, the administration has not prioritized campaign finance reform amid political polarization and lack of public demand, leaving the current system largely unchanged.

50937_50937.caption: Sen Ted Cruz speaks with his wife Heidi by his side during a primary night campaign event in Indianapolis Cruz ended his presidential campaign eliminating the biggest impediment to Donald Trump s march to the Republican nomination
50937_50937.article_context: As Ted Cruz and John Kasich’s alliance to block Donald Trump’s nomination crumbles, Cruz announces Carly Fiorina, from California, as his vice-presidential pick. This strategic move aims to attract California delegates and hinder Trump’s momentum ahead of the state’s primary, leveraging Fiorina’s local ties, appeal to female and moderate Republican voters, and her positive favorability among party members. Cruz’s announcement is seen as a last-ditch effort to stop Trump from clinching the required delegate majority before the convention.

460089_460089.caption: Stephanie Pomfrett on Corbyn s performance I m hoping that Corbyn can continue to grow in confidence
460089_460089.article_context: Jeremy Corbyn's first Prime Minister's Questions (PMQs) as Labour leader was marked by a notable change in style, with Corbyn adopting a calm and thoughtful approach and crowdsourcing questions from the public instead of traditional political sparring. Many commentators found his performance moderate and refreshing, emphasizing substance over theatrics. While some saw his lack of polish and follow-up as weaknesses, others praised the new tone and his focus on issues like mental health and housing. David Cameron responded with familiar rhetoric and at times appeared defensive. Overall, Corbyn's debut was seen as a low-key but positive shift from the usual adversarial PMQs, with public engagement and empathy taking center stage.

52450_52450.caption: Iraqis chant antiAmerican slogans as the charred mutilated bodies of private US military contractors hang from a bridge over the Euphrates River in Fallujah west of Baghdad The killings were a catalyst for a US siege of the city
52450_52450.article_context: A decade after the U.S. invasion, Iraq remains deeply divided with pockets of progress and ongoing chaos. The Kurdish region in the north and Shiite provinces in the south are experiencing economic growth and relative stability, while Sunni areas face disenfranchisement, protests, and increasing violence. Political tensions between Baghdad and the Kurds over disputed territories and oil independence have heightened the risk of ethnic conflict. Sectarian divisions, government crackdowns on Sunni politicians, and lingering insurgent activity continue to undermine security and democratic development. Despite moments of optimism in some regions, much of Iraq is still beset by instability and uncertainty about its future.

42558_42558.caption: A protester addresses a rally to draw attention to the plight of the abducted Nigerian schoolgirls at the Unity Fountain in Abuja Nigeria More than 270 schoolgirls were seized on April 14 by Islamist extremist group Boko Haram
42558_42558.article_context: Nigeria’s chief of defense staff claimed the military knows the location of 276 abducted schoolgirls taken by Boko Haram but is hesitant to attempt a rescue, fearing harm to the girls. The statement has sparked confusion and debate, especially given previous conflicting reports and failed mediation efforts, while some government supporters urge patience and negotiation over armed intervention. Opposition figures and activists remain skeptical about official transparency and the government’s actual strategy, as Boko Haram’s demands reportedly shift from prisoner swaps to the release of detained family members.

43749_43749.caption: This house in Fort Worth was Alexis s last known address Police said he had been staying in hotels after arriving in the Washington area
43749_43749.article_context: A Pentagon review into the September 16 Navy Yard mass shooting revealed serious failures in the Defense Department's security clearance procedures and workforce monitoring. Investigators found officials repeatedly missed opportunities to intervene with gunman Aaron Alexis, whose troubling behavior went unchecked, allowing him to retain clearance and access to military facilities. As a result, the Pentagon will reduce security clearances by at least 10 percent and overhaul its personnel screening process, including implementing continuous monitoring systems. The reviews highlighted widespread inadequacies in background checks and called for systemic reforms, though no Pentagon officials have been disciplined. The shooting, which killed 12 people, has spurred renewed calls for reform and accountability.

40876_40876.caption: An antiMorsi protester shout slogans during a protest in Tahrir Square in Cairo
40876_40876.article_context: Egypt's military ousted President Mohamed Morsi, the country's first democratically-elected leader, and installed Adly Mansour as interim president. Authorities immediately ordered the arrests of senior Muslim Brotherhood figures, including the group's 'supreme guide' Mohammed Badie and his deputy Khairat al-Shater, placing Morsi and others under house arrest. The Muslim Brotherhood called for peaceful demonstrations in response, but fears of further violence remain. The crackdown highlights the military's unwillingness to reconcile with the Brotherhood and raises international concerns, particularly for the United States, about the future of democracy and stability in Egypt.

40139_40139.caption: Rounded up residents wait to be transported to a police station as part of an operation in President Rodrigo Duterte s War on Drugs in Manila Duterte raised his bloody anticrime war rhetoric to a new level Friday saying he would be happy to slaughter 3 million addicts
40139_40139.article_context: Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte has created diplomatic uncertainty for the U.S. by issuing controversial statements and threats to reduce or cancel military cooperation with America, including joint exercises. His unpredictable remarks and anti-American rhetoric reflect a shift in Philippine foreign policy towards improving ties with China and Russia, partly motivated by domestic popularity and his upcoming visit to China. Despite objections from the U.S., EU, and UN over his violent anti-drug campaign, Duterte retains strong support at home, strengthening his political position and complicating Washington’s response. Analysts suggest Duterte’s actions are strategic, aiming to balance relations with both the U.S. and China as he asserts Philippine sovereignty.

455686_455686.caption: Avoiding flying is not an option says Dominic Lowe the boss of Green Black s chocolates
455686_455686.article_context: Dominic Lowe, head of Green & Black's, argued in British Airways' magazine that reducing air travel is not a viable solution to climate change due to the importance of in-person meetings, suggesting instead small environmental actions like changing lightbulbs and driving fuel-efficient cars. Meanwhile, BA chief Willie Walsh claimed that adding a third runway at Heathrow would cut carbon emissions by reducing aircraft wait times, though his reasoning is open to challenge.

458594_458594.caption: The sun sets on the US Capitol Tomorrow 10000 young climate change protesters arrive
458594_458594.article_context: Over 10,000 young climate activists are convening in Washington DC for Power Shift, the largest youth climate event in US history, aiming to pressure political leaders to pass ambitious climate and energy policies. The gathering features notable speakers, extensive workshops, and widespread media attention, and marks the first major climate lobbying effort of President Obama's term. Participants will meet with hundreds of lawmakers to advocate for climate action, with international solidarity events echoing their call, reflecting the critical influence of US policy decisions ahead of global climate negotiations.

44019_44019.caption: Before Va vote frantic governor campaign
44019_44019.article_context: Latino voters in Northern Virginia turned out to support Democrat Terry McAuliffe in the governor's race, motivated in part by Republican Ken Cuccinelli’s controversial remarks perceived as anti-immigrant, and his opposition to healthcare reform. Many voters felt Cuccinelli’s comments showed disrespect toward immigrants, while issues like immigration reform and support for Obamacare led them to favor McAuliffe. The election also featured Latino candidate Richard Cabellos running for the Virginia House of Delegates, inspiring minority voters who seek greater representation in local politics. Not all Latino voters opposed Cuccinelli; some supported his pro-business and anti-Obamacare stance, citing personal experiences and concern about government overreach.

462797_462797.caption: Sea ice concentration data for 11 September 2015 the fourth lowest extent on record The yellow line shows the historical ice edge for the same day
462797_462797.article_context: Arctic sea ice reached its fourth lowest level on record this year, with coverage shrinking to 4.41 million square kilometers, according to US scientists. The decline, observed by the National Snow and Ice Data Centre, is seen as a clear sign of climate change, reflecting ongoing long-term trends driven by warmer weather and ocean temperatures. Experts highlight the need to monitor not only ice extent but also thickness, as the latter supports the stability of the ice cap. The news comes amid predictions of record global temperatures in 2015 and 2016 and controversially recent approvals for Arctic oil drilling, prompting calls from environmental groups for urgent action to protect the region.

54979_54979.caption: Fighters from the Islamic Front an umbrella organization of Islamist rebel groups drive past buildings damaged in clashes between Syrian government and opposition forces in Aleppo
54979_54979.article_context: The United States has begun accelerating its covert efforts to deliver arms and support to vetted moderate Syrian rebel groups along the Turkey-Syria border, aiming to counter advances by both President Assad's government and Islamist extremists such as the Islamic State. However, the aid may have come too late, as moderate rebels are suffering defeats, heavy losses in Aleppo, desertions, and infighting, while Islamic State and government forces consolidate their control over key territories. The fragmentation among rebel groups and the shift of fighters to extremist factions further undermine the opposition's strength and prospects, raising doubts about whether the new support can reverse their declining fortunes.

49282_49282.caption: President Obama carries a wreath with New York Police Officer Stephanie Moses left New York firefighter Joseph Lapointe and Port Authority Police Officer John Adorno during a wreathlaying ceremony at Ground Zero Obama also visited a New York Fire Department firehouse and met with families of victims of the Sept 11 terrorist attack
49282_49282.article_context: U.S. Army Gen. Raymond 'Tony' Thomas, head of Special Operations Command, criticized current and former elite military personnel for writing books, making movies, and advising video games about their missions, arguing that such publicity violates operational security and tradition. His comments follow high-profile cases like Navy SEAL Matt Bissonnette, who forfeited $6.6 million in profits for publishing a book without Pentagon clearance. Thomas emphasized the negative impact of these disclosures across all special operations units, not just SEALs, and called for a return to greater secrecy, echoing similar warnings from his predecessor.

475834_475834.caption: Edinburgh A commuter reading a free newspaper on the way to work reminding her to Vote
475834_475834.article_context: On a significant polling day in Scotland, voters of all ages turned out across cities and rural areas to cast their ballots, amid a vibrant atmosphere of both pro-independence and pro-union campaigning. Key political figures including Ed Miliband, Gordon Brown, Alex Salmond, and Nicola Sturgeon were seen engaging with supporters and voting, while campaigners gathered outside polling stations across the country. The event was marked by diverse expressions of political sentiment, highlighting Scotland's heightened political engagement.

41535_41535.caption: Why UK s nuclear deal with China got the green light
41535_41535.article_context: The British government has approved the controversial Hinkley Point C nuclear power station, a $24 billion project financed by China and run by France’s EDF, after a two-month review prompted by security concerns. While moving forward with the plant, the UK imposed new laws to allow greater government oversight of future foreign investments in critical infrastructure. The decision, welcomed by both EDF and China General Nuclear, comes amid criticism over the project's cost and the security risks posed by Chinese involvement in the energy sector. Environmental groups denounced the project, favoring investment in renewable energy alternatives.

454134_454134.caption: Mark Serwotka After the expenses scandal the public are still very sceptical about the financial affairs of politicians
454134_454134.article_context: Unions are pressing for clarity on whether MPs will have to increase their pension contributions in line with wider public sector reforms, after it was revealed that Commons Leader Sir George Young is privately negotiating MPs’ pension arrangements. While pay responsibility for MPs has been shifted to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (Ipsa), the move to transfer pension oversight is being delayed amid ongoing discussions. This has sparked concerns about transparency and fairness, given that MPs currently benefit from a more generous pension scheme than other public workers. The delay is reportedly linked to doubts over Ipsa's capability to manage the scheme, as well as unease about MPs potentially exempting themselves from pension cuts affecting others.

39836_39836.caption: A poodle confiscated in an animal cruelty case in Parker County Tex waits for his dinner in 2014
39836_39836.article_context: Hillsborough County, Florida, has passed a law creating a publicly searchable registry for convicted animal abusers, similar to sex offender registries, in an effort to prevent repeat offenses and protect both animals and people. Retailers and shelters must check the registry before allowing pet adoptions or sales. While other places, including some counties in New York, Cook County, Illinois, and Tennessee, have adopted or considered similar measures, the registries face criticism for being local rather than nationwide, potentially overbroad, and relying on offenders' compliance. Supporters argue the registries help safeguard communities and animals, while opponents—including some animal welfare advocates—question their effectiveness and warn about possible unintended consequences.

39431_39431.caption: Authors say they re feeling the squeeze as Amazon hashes it out with Hachette REUTERSDado Ruvic
39431_39431.article_context: Amid an ongoing contract dispute between Amazon and Hachette Book Group that has delayed many book shipments, Amazon proposed offering Hachette authors its share of e-book revenues if Hachette also gave up its share during the dispute. Authors Guild president Roxana Robinson rejected the offer, criticizing it as an attempt to pressure the publisher into unfavorable terms and arguing it does not resolve broader issues in the publishing ecosystem. Robinson emphasized the need for a healthy, fair market and cautioned against short-term solutions, highlighting concerns over Amazon's market dominance and calling for systemic change rather than temporary deals.

447473_447473.caption: Ballot papers are counted in Glasgow The suspicious ballot was counted but police are investigating possible fraud
447473_447473.article_context: Police in Scotland are investigating a reported case of electoral fraud after a person allegedly voted using someone else's identity at a Glasgow East polling station. The ballot in question was handed over to police for evidence but still counted in the official tally. The incident occurred during the general election in which the SNP's Natalie McGarry won the seat from Labour's Margaret Curran.

42057_42057.caption: A 2000 BMW 740iL similar to the one stolen from the Hooters in Fairfax City by a couple headed to a wedding It was found Tuesday and returned to its owner five weeks later
42057_42057.article_context: A BMW reported stolen from outside a Hooters restaurant was found undamaged and unlocked in a nearby shopping center parking lot by Fairfax County police. The car still contained all reported items, including an engagement ring and laptop. Authorities decided not to pursue a stolen auto investigation due to lack of evidence that the car was permanently taken, and no charges are expected. The owner retrieved his car and possessions, and police advised increased caution in the future.

40479_40479.caption: Police stand near the truck that slammed into revelers late Thursday in Nice France
40479_40479.article_context: On Bastille Day in Nice, France, a truck drove into a crowd celebrating the national holiday, killing at least 84 people and injuring dozens more in what authorities called a terrorist attack. The driver, identified as a 31-year-old French-Tunisian man, also fired into the crowd before being shot dead by police. The attack, which also claimed the lives of two Americans and more than ten children, occurred after a fireworks celebration along the city's popular Promenade des Anglais. In response, France declared three days of national mourning and extended its state of emergency. President François Hollande condemned the attack as terrorism and vowed to intensify France’s military operations against ISIS in Syria and Iraq.
