The groups argue that such measures, alongside a proposed £1.5bn retrofit scheme for public buildings and firm commitments to zero-carbon standards in new homes, are vital for stimulating economic growth, improving energy efficiency, and tackling fuel poverty. While the government is prioritizing deregulation to boost construction, industry leaders emphasize that targeted regulation can benefit both businesses and the wider community. Notably, the Builders Merchants' Federation opposes the move, highlighting ongoing divisions within the sector.

40717_40717.caption: During an exercise roleplaying attackers lie prone after the trainees take control of the situation
40717_40717.article_context: In response to the deadly 2012 Benghazi attacks on U.S. diplomatic posts in Libya, the State Department has implemented more intensive combat-style training for its Diplomatic Security Service (DS) agents. At a mock consulate built for realistic war games in Virginia, agents now undergo a rigorous 10-week high-threat course, doubling previous training duration and culminating in simulations of terrorist assaults. These measures address past security failures and aim to better prepare agents for dangerous postings worldwide, as diplomatic missions increasingly face risks without military support. The training also emphasizes both defensive tactics and diplomatic soft skills, with ongoing initiatives to improve the capability of host-nation security forces.

39798_39798.caption: Muhiydin Moye DBaha of the Black Lives Matter movement speaks to the news media following a North Charleston City Council meeting in North Charleston
39798_39798.article_context: Michael Slager, a white South Carolina police officer, was charged with murder after a video surfaced showing him shooting Walter Scott, an unarmed black man, in the back as Scott ran away during a traffic stop. Despite initial reports that the case could carry the death penalty, the prosecutor stated that the statutory requirements for a death sentence are not met, and Slager will likely face 30 years to life in prison if convicted. The case is expected to take time to proceed through the legal system, with a grand jury review still pending. The incident has prompted discussions about police accountability, as officers are rarely prosecuted for shootings, and the North Charleston Police Department has vowed to equip officers with body cameras in response.

447525_447525.caption: Silver Fox an antifracking protestor outside county hall in Preston as Lancashire county council met to decide whether to approve Cuadrilla s plans for two of the biggest test sites for shale gas extraction at Little Plumpton and Roseacre Wood
447525_447525.article_context: Lancashire county council has postponed planning decisions on two major fracking proposals from Cuadrilla for eight weeks to allow for public consultation on revised plans, after initial recommendations to reject the projects over noise and heavy truck traffic concerns. The deferral has heightened uncertainty and frustration among local residents and councillors, while Cuadrilla insists its new mitigation measures will address safety and noise issues. Fracking remains divisive in Lancashire and across the UK, with government support for shale gas extraction clashing with environmental and health concerns from campaigners, and other regions like Scotland and Wales considering bans or devolved licensing powers.

50983_50983.caption: AntiTrump demonstrators dressed as a wall stand in Public Square
50983_50983.article_context: At the Republican National Convention, House Speaker Paul Ryan and Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell publicly backed Donald Trump as the GOP presidential nominee, despite previous tensions and disagreements. Their support was driven primarily by a desire to maintain Republican control of Congress and defeat Hillary Clinton, rather than full alignment with Trump's platform. Both leaders emphasized their own legislative priorities and signaled willingness to distance themselves from Trump if his candidacy jeopardizes their congressional majorities. The relationship between Trump and the party establishment remains uneasy and pragmatic, focused on party unity leading up to the election.

444890_444890.caption: Gordon Brown at the Progress meeting in London The former prime minister has tried to allay Labour supporters fears over Scottish independence
444890_444890.article_context: Gordon Brown has urged the UK Parliament to allocate time for debating increased devolution for Scotland as the independence referendum nears, aiming to reassure pro-Union voters of Labour’s commitment to more powers for Holyrood. Amid a surge in support for independence, Brown emphasized that promised further devolution would be upheld, distinguishing these pledges from unfulfilled promises in previous referendums. Labour leader Ed Miliband also pledged significant party campaigning in Scotland, and Brown warned that an independent Scotland using the pound would face economic disadvantages.

47012_47012.caption: Workers make final preparations on the inaugural platform at the Capitol
47012_47012.article_context: Republican strategists and lawmakers, including pollster Frank Luntz, are returning to private dinners to discuss strategy in the wake of President Obama's second inauguration. After an initial high-profile dinner in 2009 where GOP leaders devised a plan for unified opposition to Obama, Republicans are now reassessing their approach following electoral setbacks. While some see past strategies as successful in helping their party win House majorities, others express skepticism about prospects for compromise with Democrats and suggest the next phase of conservative action will take place at the state level. Internal divisions persist over whether to focus on confrontation or problem-solving, but the gatherings continue to serve as forums for shaping the party’s future direction.

43750_43750.caption: Demonstrators confront police near Camden Yards during a protest against the death of Freddie Gray after he was injured while in police custody
43750_43750.article_context: Baltimore officials acknowledged police mishandling during the arrest of Freddie Gray, who suffered a fatal spinal injury in custody, including not securing him in a seat belt and denying his requests for medical help. Gray's death has sparked widespread protests and calls for justice, prompting officials like Governor Larry Hogan and Mayor Stephanie Rawlings-Blake to urge calm. Authorities are investigating the incident, and advocacy groups are demanding broader state action on police reform. The case has intensified the national conversation on police conduct and accountability.

51029_51029.caption: A Muslim woman waits for her children in front of a public school in Vilvoorde Muslim communities in Belgium say they feel under siege Their children are taunted at school and antiMuslim graffiti has been scrawled near mosques
51029_51029.article_context: Following the Paris attacks, Belgian Muslims are experiencing heightened suspicion, alienation, and harassment, particularly in towns like Vilvoorde, known for high numbers of young people leaving to join jihad in Syria. Authorities are conducting anti-terror raids and considering tough new security measures targeting Muslim communities, including the potential stripping of citizenship for those fighting abroad. The Muslim community, already feeling marginalized, faces increased hostility and fears collective punishment, while experts and community leaders warn that these policies could deepen divisions and worsen radicalization. The situation reflects a broader struggle across Europe between countering extremist threats and addressing the integration and alienation of Muslim populations.

40755_40755.caption: An East German border policeman hands a flower back to West Berlin citizens sitting on the Berlin Wall near the Brandenburg Gate on Nov 10 1989
40755_40755.article_context: Russian lawmakers, led by State Duma Speaker Sergey Naryshkin, are considering a proposal to officially condemn the 1989 reunification of Germany, labeling it as an 'annexation' of East Germany by West Germany. This move is seen as a reaction to Western criticism of Russia's actions in Crimea, with proponents drawing controversial parallels between the two historic events. The proposal, put forward by Communist Party lawmaker Nikolay Ivanov, argues that German reunification lacked a democratic referendum, unlike Russia's disputed annexation of Crimea. The initiative has drawn criticism and ridicule, including from former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, who called it 'nonsense,' and highlights ongoing tensions between Russia and Germany over issues of territorial integrity and international relations.

44266_44266.caption: US President Barack Obama pauses while speaking during an event in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House campus August 3 2012 in Washington DC Obama spoke to urge Congress to pass tax cuts for the American middle class
44266_44266.article_context: President Obama faces significant historical challenges in seeking re-election, as the U.S. unemployment rate has remained above 8 percent for 42 consecutive months. With economic projections showing it is unlikely to fall below that benchmark before the election, Obama must make a compelling case to voters that his policies prevented an even worse downturn and that his opponent, Mitt Romney, is not a preferable alternative. Unlike Ronald Reagan, who benefited from a clear economic recovery before his re-election, Obama lacks a steady decline in unemployment to bolster his campaign, making his path to a second term unprecedented and demanding a persuasive two-pronged argument.

46183_46183.caption: Candidates speak after Super Saturday contests
46183_46183.article_context: The Associated Press quickly called the Louisiana Republican primary for Donald Trump when early, absentee votes showed him with a large lead. However, as more election day votes were counted, Ted Cruz significantly narrowed the gap, suggesting a shift in voter sentiment. This highlighted a notable difference between early and election day voting patterns, possibly influenced by recent events like debates or effective get-out-the-vote efforts by Cruz. The evolving results raised questions about whether the race was called too soon and underscored the impact of campaign organization on primary outcomes.

456349_456349.caption: The Goldsmith leaflet delivered to British Indian Londoners shown to the Guardian
456349_456349.article_context: Zac Goldsmith, the Conservative candidate for London mayor, has been accused of targeting minority ethnic communities with divisive campaign materials, warning Indian and Tamil voters that Labour rival Sadiq Khan would support a wealth tax threatening family heirlooms. The leaflets claimed Khan's party would endanger their economic security and criticized his absence from Indian Prime Minister Modi's UK visit. These tactics drew criticism from recipients and community leaders, who labelled them patronising and divisive, while some observers condemned Goldsmith's approach as misinformed and harmful to community relations.

442197_442197.caption: Daedalus a mythical Greek architect and sculptor was imprisoned by King Minos of Crete He made wings out of wax and feathers so he and his son Icarus could escape to Sicily However Icarus wings melted when he flew too close to the sun and he fell into the sea and drowned
442197_442197.article_context: The article draws parallels between historical figures' ambitions, such as Cecil Rhodes' imperialist expansion and the myth of Icarus, to humanity's current struggle with climate change and technological advancement. It highlights the IPCC’s urgent climate warnings, the contradiction of glamorous but resource-intensive innovations like flying cars and space tourism, and the need for practical solutions such as renewable energy adoption and improved urban infrastructure. The piece critiques inadequate policies, such as the EU’s emission reduction targets, arguing they fall short of what is necessary. Ultimately, it calls for wiser choices to avoid ecological self-destruction, suggesting that if humanity fails, life will move on regardless.

45138_45138.caption: Monica Wehby greeted supporters at campaign headquarters in Oregon City after winning the Oregon Republican Primary race for Senate on May 20
45138_45138.article_context: A political group funded by conservative billionaire Charles Koch has entered the Oregon Senate race to support Republican candidate Monica Wehby, whose campaign has been struggling. The group is expected to provide financial and organizational backing in hopes of increasing Wehby's chances against the Democratic incumbent. This move highlights the national interest and outside influence in the closely watched Senate contest.

50238_50238.caption: Elizabeth Warren s remarks on wage growth after Reagan
50238_50238.article_context: Hillary Clinton is unlikely to choose Elizabeth Warren as her vice presidential nominee despite Warren’s popularity among progressives. While Warren could help unite the Democratic Party after a divisive primary, she has not endorsed Clinton and has often criticized her, particularly on issues related to Wall Street and economic reform. Additionally, there is a lack of personal rapport between the two. Clinton is expected to pick Warren only if party divisions drastically worsen and she needs Warren to mend fences with the liberal base, but current polling suggests most Democrats would support Clinton regardless.

448961_448961.caption: Sir Richard Dannatt questioned worth of Trident
448961_448961.article_context: General Sir Richard Dannatt revealed he was invited by Conservative leader David Cameron to advise on defence due to the Tory team's lack of expertise. Dannatt accepted the role to ensure the armed forces, especially in Afghanistan, were properly supported. He also questioned the value and cost of renewing the Trident nuclear deterrent, despite its official backing by the party. Dannatt’s appointment to the House of Lords and potential ministerial role sparked internal Tory disagreements, as some senior party members were not consulted and expressed concern. Cameron confirmed Dannatt’s new advisory position in his conference speech, emphasizing his military service, amid ongoing debate about Dannatt’s future roles and political involvement.

41051_41051.caption: Bonnie Liebold a 29year member of Schaefer s former church Zion United Methodist Church of Iona as well as the former youth choir director is one of the people who complained
41051_41051.article_context: Frank Schaefer, a United Methodist pastor in Pennsylvania, became an advocate for gay rights after officiating the wedding of his gay son, Tim, in 2007, violating church doctrine. His actions led to a church trial and his defrocking in 2013, sparking national debate and increasing divisions within the denomination over LGBTQ inclusion. Schaefer’s personal journey, shaped by the coming out of three of his four children, transformed him from a private supporter to a public activist for gay equality, making him a prominent figure in the movement. The controversy has reignited broader discussions about the future of the Methodist Church, which is deeply split over LGBTQ issues, while Schaefer continues to speak nationally, embracing his role as a mediator and advocate.

44147_44147.caption: Lynch is sworn in for her hearing at the Senate Judiciary Committee
44147_44147.article_context: Loretta Lynch was confirmed by the Senate as U.S. attorney general after a lengthy five-month delay, making her the first African American woman to hold the position. The confirmation vote was 56 to 43, with ten Republicans joining Democrats in support. Her nomination was stalled by partisan disagreements, particularly over immigration policy and unrelated legislation on sex trafficking. Lynch replaces Eric Holder and is expected to be sworn in as the nation’s 83rd attorney general, with President Obama stating she will bring valuable experience and leadership to the Justice Department.

42197_42197.caption: King Salman attends the funeral of the late Saudi king Abdullah who was his halfbrother in Riyadh
42197_42197.article_context: Since becoming king in January, 79-year-old Salman has dramatically shifted Saudi Arabia’s foreign policy, launching a military campaign against Shiite rebels in Yemen and increasing support for anti-government forces in Syria to counter Iran’s influence. King Salman has also restructured the royal succession, promoting a younger generation, including his son Mohammed bin Salman, to powerful leadership roles. While adopting a more assertive regional stance and projecting strength at home, Salman has maintained Saudi Arabia’s critical security ties with the United States amid concerns over Washington’s warming relations with Iran and threats from jihadist groups like the Islamic State.

39767_39767.caption: Iran s case against Washington Post reporter Jason Rezaian seen in this Nov 6 2013 photo has been assigned to a branch of the Revolutionary Court run by a conservative judge known for harsh sentences
39767_39767.article_context: Iranian hardliner Hamid Rasaei has publicly accused imprisoned Washington Post reporter Jason Rezaian and his wife, Yeganeh Salehi, of espionage, alleging they infiltrated sensitive areas of the president’s office under the guise of journalism. Rezaian has been held in Tehran’s Evin Prison since July 2014, with authorities yet to provide formal charges, drawing criticism from his family, The Post’s editors, and the U.S. State Department, who call the allegations baseless and demand his release. The case, overseen by a conservative Revolutionary Court, highlights tensions between Iran’s hard-liners and centrist officials, and has sparked international concern and campaigns for Rezaian’s freedom.

456611_456611.caption: Sandbags outside a shop in Hebden Bridge after a month s worth of rain falling in under an hour
456611_456611.article_context: Repeated and severe flooding has affected numerous communities across the UK, including Croston in Lancashire, due to record rainfall and inadequate flood defences. Flood protection schemes for multiple towns were approved in 2010 but have since been delayed or abandoned following substantial government spending cuts to flood defences after the election. This has left hundreds of projects unfunded, increasing the vulnerability of thousands of homes and businesses as climate change raises flood risks. Calls for urgent investment have intensified, with experts and local officials warning that failure to act will lead to greater economic and personal losses in the face of worsening weather extremes.

449414_449414.caption: London mayor Boris Johnson has published a draft air quality strategy
449414_449414.article_context: The European Commission has rejected the UK government's request for more time to meet legal limits on PM10 air pollution in London, potentially subjecting the UK to legal action and multi-million pound fines. The commission determined that London's air quality plans did not meet minimum EU requirements for a deadline extension, intensifying pressure on Mayor Boris Johnson, whose own air quality strategy delays key measures aimed at reducing pollution. London remains the only UK area in breach of the 2005 European directive on particulate matter, which is linked to thousands of premature deaths annually. While the UK government expressed disappointment and plans to submit further proposals, the commission insists on urgent compliance, prompting calls for more radical action to avoid penalties and improve public health.

444761_444761.caption: William Hague said a second Commons vote would only be possible if there was a dramatic change in circumstances
444761_444761.article_context: US Secretary of State John Kerry and UK Foreign Secretary William Hague are set to discuss delaying potential military action against Syria until after UN weapons inspectors report on the alleged chemical attack and the matter is revisited at the UN Security Council. France and other European countries also insist on waiting for the inspectors' findings before supporting any intervention. Parliamentary and public opposition in the UK remains strong, with Labour leader Ed Miliband maintaining resistance to strikes and former officials urging reconsideration if circumstances change. Kerry is working to build international consensus as the US Senate prepares to vote on President Obama's proposed military plan.

43124_43124.caption: Nathan Brown 26 leads protesters in chants against the Confederate flag
43124_43124.article_context: At the first court appearance of Dylann Roof, who was charged with murdering nine people at the historic Emanuel AME Church in Charleston, relatives of the victims addressed Roof directly, choosing to express forgiveness and pray for his soul despite their grief. The bond hearing was held via video, with no bond granted for the murder charges but $1 million set for a related firearm charge. The case is being investigated as a hate crime and potentially as an act of domestic terrorism, with prosecutors yet to decide on seeking the death penalty. The event sparked nationwide discussions about forgiveness, racial violence, and justice.

464357_464357.caption: The 1010 campaign to cut carbon emissions by 10 by the end of 2010 launched yesterday
464357_464357.article_context: The 10:10 campaign, aimed at reducing carbon emissions by 10% in 2010, has received broad support from UK political parties, including pledges from Conservative and Liberal Democrat leaders and endorsement from the Green party. Energy Secretary Ed Miliband committed to personal and departmental cuts, while political leaders highlighted the importance of voluntary action. Public support is strong, with a Guardian poll showing most Britons favor individual steps to reduce emissions. The initiative coincides with international climate negotiations and is seen as a signal to encourage global action at the upcoming Copenhagen summit.

52911_52911.caption: State Dept Israel was consulted on FAA travel ban
52911_52911.article_context: The FAA imposed a 24-hour ban on U.S. airlines flying to or from Tel Aviv after a rocket landed near Ben Gurion International Airport, prompting Delta, US Airways, and United Airlines to suspend flights due to security concerns. Several international carriers, including Air France and Lufthansa, also canceled Tel Aviv routes. Israel's transportation minister asserted the airport's safety despite the measures. The incident follows heightened global anxiety after the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 over Ukraine, though the rockets from Gaza differ from the missile used in that attack. The U.S. State Department advised citizens to delay non-essential travel to Israel amid ongoing conflict with Hamas.

466731_466731.caption: Demonstrators against education cuts in 2010 In a letter to Guardian six unions and a group of Labour MPs have voiced support for students planning to protest on 9 November 2011
466731_466731.article_context: Several major unions and Labour MPs have publicly supported upcoming student demonstrations in London on November 9 against government education cuts and reforms proposed in the higher education white paper. In a joint letter, union leaders and politicians emphasized that education should remain a public service without a profit motive and called for it to be funded through taxation of the wealthy. The unions and MPs are joining forces with students to oppose cuts, with a large public sector strike also being planned. Student leaders accuse the government of undermining education, scrapping support for disadvantaged students, and pushing through harmful reforms, predicting significant turnout at the protests.

463267_463267.caption: Peter Robinson applauds Arlene Foster s election as DUP leader in December 2015 On Monday she also replaced him as first minister
463267_463267.article_context: Arlene Foster has been appointed as Northern Ireland’s new first minister, becoming the first woman to hold the position and succeeding Peter Robinson after his retirement. Her confirmation marks a smooth transition in Northern Ireland's power-sharing government, with Foster, leader of the DUP, assuming office alongside Sinn Féin deputy first minister Martin McGuinness. The appointment has been widely recognized as historic and symbolic for women in politics. Foster called for greater consensus and cooperation in government, while politicians acknowledged the challenges ahead in maintaining peace and unity in the region. Her decision not to attend Dublin's Easter Rising centenary celebrations drew criticism from some republicans.

43458_43458.caption: A girl and a woman look out from their home next to a crime scene where a woman was shot dead after an unidentified gunman opened fire inside a house in Ciudad Juarez Mexico According to local media unknown gunmen killed three other women over a period of four hours in different parts of the city
43458_43458.article_context: As President Felipe Calderon's term ends, Mexico's six-year war against drug cartels has resulted in at least 60,000 deaths, widespread violence, and no significant reduction in drug flows to the United States. While the government succeeded in targeting top cartel leaders, cartel violence soared and overall crime rates increased, leading to public ambivalence and the electoral defeat of Calderon's party. Incoming president Enrique Peña Nieto has pledged to continue anti-drug efforts with a focus on reducing homicide rates rather than targeting cartel leadership. Calderon's military-led approach was criticized for escalating violence and failing to bring lasting improvements to Mexico’s justice system.

44356_44356.caption: Brooke gestures to Republican presidential hopeful Rep John B Anderson
44356_44356.article_context: Edward W. Brooke, who became the first African American popularly elected to the U.S. Senate in 1966, died at age 95. A Massachusetts Republican, Brooke was known for his independence, his work on key anti-poverty and civil rights legislation, and for sponsoring the Fair Housing Act of 1968. Despite his significant influence and bipartisan reputation, his political career ended after a scandal involving financial disclosures during his divorce. Honored with the Presidential Medal of Freedom and Congressional Gold Medal, Brooke is remembered as a pioneering figure who helped shape civil rights and housing policies and inspired future generations of African American leaders.

42316_42316.caption: In this file photo depart a train at the Rhode Island Avenue Metro station on May 26 2016 Falling debris caused officials to shut down the station for structural inspections
42316_42316.article_context: The Rhode Island Avenue Metro station in Washington, D.C. reopened after being closed due to falling concrete from the ceiling. Metro engineers inspected and repaired the station, determining there were no immediate structural dangers but identifying loose concrete caused by environmental deterioration. Debris-catching netting was installed as a precaution, and officials plan to conduct further inspections to address the issue long-term.

42331_42331.caption: School integration at the Barnard School in Washington DC in 1955 OHalloran Thomas J photographer the Library of Congress
42331_42331.article_context: After court-ordered busing ended in Charlotte-Mecklenburg in the early 2000s, schools in the district quickly resegregated along racial and economic lines, leading to widened academic achievement gaps and an increase in crime among students, particularly minority boys. Recent studies have found that concentrated segregation in schools fosters criminal networks among neighborhood peers, amplifying negative influences. While efforts such as extra spending and programs have improved test scores somewhat, they have not significantly reduced crime rates. The research underscores the harmful consequences of school segregation, and even as the Charlotte-Mecklenburg school board considers addressing these inequities, progress has been slow due to divided public opinion.

39544_39544.caption: The wife of Turkish soldier Mehmet Yavuz Nane cries over her husband body during the burial ceremony on July 24 2015 in Gaziantep
39544_39544.article_context: Turkey carried out its first airstrikes against Islamic State targets in Syria, marking a significant escalation in its involvement in the conflict. This move follows Turkey's decision to allow the United States and coalition forces to launch airstrikes from Turkish bases, notably Incirlik, aiming to strengthen joint efforts against the militants. The airstrikes and subsequent nationwide security raids were prompted by increasing attacks and threats from the Islamic State along the Turkish border and inside Turkey, including a deadly suicide bombing in Suruc. Turkish leaders signaled that these operations would continue, with further cooperation in intelligence sharing and military coordination with the U.S. and its allies likely.

40049_40049.caption: The FBI seeks help identifying this man wanted in three robberies
40049_40049.article_context: The FBI has released surveillance photos of a man wanted for three bank robberies in Washington, D.C., and Maryland that occurred in January and March. The suspect, described as a Black male between 25 and 30 years old and 5-foot-7 to 5-foot-9 tall, allegedly passed notes to bank tellers demanding money and suggesting he was armed. The FBI is offering a $5,000 reward for information leading to his arrest and is soliciting tips from the public through their website.

40562_40562.caption: Opposition Labour party leader Ed Miliband and his wife Justine Thornton arrive at the party headquarters in London
40562_40562.article_context: During Britain's divisive general election campaign, immigrants have felt increasingly scapegoated by politicians and the media, accused of causing issues such as strains on public services. In response, a crowdfunded 'I am an immigrant' poster campaign was launched nationwide to highlight immigrants’ positive contributions. Immigration is one of the top election issues, with parties such as the Conservatives and UKIP promising stricter policies, while Labour admits past mistakes but avoids setting strict targets. Despite being targeted politically, immigrants also represent a significant voting bloc, prompting some to push back against negative stereotypes and advocate for their role in British society.

443659_443659.caption: This week the California Fish and Game Commission banned prize hunts for coyotes as well other nongame animals such as beavers and bobcats
443659_443659.article_context: This week saw a range of significant environmental events and wildlife news around the world. Scientists identified the humpback whales in the Arabian Sea as the most genetically distinct and isolated population globally. In California, record-breaking rainfall brought drought relief, while the California Fish and Game Commission banned prize hunts for certain non-game animals, including coyotes and bobcats. In China, drought and damming led to the complete drying of Poyang Lake, resulting in the death of endangered Yangtze finless porpoises. Conservation efforts included a major rat eradication project on South Georgia island to protect bird populations. Additionally, protests occurred in Hong Kong against the city’s legal ivory trade, which activists claim enables smuggling of illegally poached ivory.

47669_47669.caption: Supporters of deposed Egyptian President Mohammed Morsi take shelter inside a construction site during a violent crackdown by Egyptian Security Forces in Cairo
47669_47669.article_context: Egypt experienced its deadliest day since the 2011 uprising when security forces stormed two protest camps in Cairo, killing at least 421 people, mainly supporters of ousted president Mohamed Morsi. The military-backed interim government declared a state of emergency following the widespread violence and mass arrests of Muslim Brotherhood members. Vice President Mohamed ElBaradei resigned in protest over the crackdown, while the United States and international community condemned the actions and urged a peaceful resolution. The clashes and sectarian attacks, including the burning of churches, further undermined hopes for a return to democracy and signaled a deepening political crisis in Egypt.

50889_50889.caption: Raechel Richards is embraced by her late husband s cousin Andrew Savant
50889_50889.article_context: Rob Richards, a Marine Corps sniper whose military career ended after a viral video showed him and others urinating on Taliban corpses in Afghanistan, was buried with honors at Arlington National Cemetery after dying at age 28 from an accidental painkiller overdose. Once praised for his combat achievements but later court-martialed and vilified for the incident, Richards struggled with the aftermath, including depression and addiction, after leaving the military. His burial became a reflection on the moral ambiguity of war, the psychological toll on soldiers, and the complexities of how such incidents shape both public perception and personal identity.

39847_39847.caption: In the late 1970s a Rutgers student who had been drinking fell out of the bleachers at a football game and was paralyzed Today two campuses of the New Jersey university offer sober housing
39847_39847.article_context: Colleges across the U.S. are increasingly providing 'sober dorms' and recovery programs to support students recovering from alcohol and drug addiction, a trend driven by rising substance abuse and dropout rates. Pioneered by Rutgers University, which began sober housing in the 1980s, these dorms offer substance-free environments, counseling, and community activities, helping students remain sober and succeed academically. Recent legislation in New Jersey requires all state colleges to offer sober housing, and similar programs are expanding to other universities. Experts emphasize these programs are not treatment, but provide ongoing support for students already in recovery, which has been shown to significantly reduce relapse rates compared to the general population.

43681_43681.caption: A child stands in the street after a Syrian government artillery shell destroyed his family home in the Shaar neighborhood of the northern city of Aleppo
43681_43681.article_context: Growing discontent and internal tensions among Syria’s Alawite minority, President Bashar al-Assad’s main base of support, are posing new challenges to his regime amid an ongoing rebellion. Recent incidents, including a violent shootout between Assad family members in their hometown of Qardaha and the detention of a prominent Alawite dissident, highlight fractures within the community. While most Alawites still support Assad out of fear for their safety should the Sunni-led opposition prevail, there is increasing frustration over rising death tolls and perceptions that Assad is exploiting Alawite fears for his own survival. Despite these tensions, most Alawites remain reluctant to support the opposition, seeing their fate tied to the regime in the face of sectarian threats.

42679_42679.caption: Russian gay right activists kiss during a protest near the State Duma Russia s lower parliament chamber in Moscow The State Duma was set to debate a bill that would introduce sanctions for providing minors with information on homosexuality but postponed the debate until next month
42679_42679.article_context: Chinese journalists protested government censorship following the alteration of a Southern Weekly New Year's editorial, which had originally advocated for constitutional reforms. Instead of a threatened mass strike, journalists quietly expressed defiance through subtle articles and social media posts, and held limited public protests. Police eventually cracked down on demonstrators, and publishers faced intense pressure from propaganda officials, including threats of dissolution. Despite hopes that new leader Xi Jinping might bring media reforms, most journalists refrained from major action to avoid personal and professional risks, although the incident prompted wider public discussion about freedom of speech in China.

48545_48545.caption: Mitt and Ann Romney attend a campaign rally in Apopka Fla
48545_48545.article_context: The vice presidential debate between Joe Biden and Paul Ryan is seen as pivotal in the 2012 campaign, following Mitt Romney's strong performance against President Obama in the previous presidential debate. Biden faces pressure to defend the Obama administration and regain momentum, while Ryan aims to capitalize on Romney’s gains and reinforce the Republican ticket. Polls show narrowing margins in key battleground states, making this debate especially consequential. Both candidates, regarded as substantive political players, have distinct strengths and vulnerabilities that could influence public perception and shift the trajectory of the race ahead of the next presidential debate.

43044_43044.caption: Protesters attempt to intimidate riot police in downtown Mexico City Protests against Mexico s newly swornin President Enrique Pena Nieto began early Saturday morning with violent confrontations in the streets and protest speeches from opposition parties inside the country s National Congress Protesters continued through the afternoon vandalizing downtown businesses smashing storefront glass windows and setting office furniture ablaze
43044_43044.article_context: Army Private Bradley Manning, accused of leaking hundreds of thousands of classified documents to WikiLeaks, is expected to testify in court for the first time as part of his legal team's effort to challenge the legality of his pre-trial confinement. Manning's attorney argues that Manning was unlawfully subjected to harsh conditions, including prolonged solitary confinement at Marine Corps Base Quantico, despite recommendations to ease those restrictions. The court proceedings aim to address these allegations of mistreatment, potentially impacting the charges or sentence Manning faces, which could include life in prison if convicted. The hearing includes testimony from military officials about Manning's confinement and mental health during detention.

46140_46140.caption: Capriles waves to supporters during a campaign rally in Barinas Venezuela Recent polls put Capriles roughly even with President Hugo Chavez who has been in power for 14 years
46140_46140.article_context: Venezuela's President Hugo Chavez, weakened by illness after 14 years in power, faces an unusually strong challenge in the upcoming presidential election from Henrique Capriles, a charismatic opposition leader who has united critics and capitalized on public frustration with crime, economic issues, and declining infrastructure. Polls are mixed, showing either a Chavez lead or a tight race, reflecting deep division in the country. The outcome has significant regional and global implications due to Venezuela's oil reserves and Chavez's anti-U.S. stance. Many Venezuelans are calling for change, but Chavez maintains strong support among the poor, bolstered by state-run media and social programs.

53579_53579.caption: Obama Fight against terrorism is not between America and Islam
53579_53579.article_context: President Obama delivered a rare Oval Office address in the aftermath of the San Bernardino attack to reassure a fearful public about the fight against terrorism, particularly the Islamic State. He reiterated his existing strategy of targeted airstrikes, intelligence sharing, and training local forces, avoiding major shifts or new initiatives. Obama cautioned against divisive rhetoric toward Muslims and calls for religious tests for refugees, arguing such moves betray American values and play into terrorist propaganda. Acknowledging criticism and doubts about the effectiveness of his approach, Obama urged patience and unity, emphasizing resilience and the dangers of overreacting out of fear.

452457_452457.caption: David Cameron in Shanghai I believe in marriage I believe marriage should be recognised in the tax system
452457_452457.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron announced that a new transferable marriage tax allowance will be introduced in the forthcoming autumn statement, marking the first step towards recognizing marriage in the UK tax system. Despite Chancellor George Osborne's skepticism about the allowance, Cameron emphasized his commitment to expanding support for married couples and raising the personal tax allowance for low-income earners, rather than offering tax relief for middle-income households. Cameron also underscored his strong working relationship with Osborne and prioritized deficit reduction over broader tax cuts, emphasizing fiscal responsibility alongside his support for lower taxes.

39289_39289.caption: Attorney Steven D Benjamin left and former executive mansion chef Todd Schneider arrive at court in Richmond for a Thursday pretrial hearing Circuit Judge Margaret Spencer deferred until May 14 a motion to dismiss the fourcount indictment
39289_39289.article_context: A Richmond judge has recused Attorney General Ken Cuccinelli's office from prosecuting former Virginia governor's mansion chef Todd Schneider, assigning a Norfolk prosecutor to handle Schneider's embezzlement case. Schneider's attorney asserts Schneider is a whistleblower who reported to authorities alleged wrongdoing by Governor Robert McDonnell and his wife, involving undisclosed gifts from businessman Jonnie Williams. Cuccinelli, also a recipient of Williams’s gifts, faced criticism for not pursuing Schneider's claims, leading to concerns over ethical conflicts. The case has drawn political attention and protest, with further hearings scheduled to address dismissal motions.

44232_44232.caption: Jame Cook 5 with his father Jumaane Cook holds a sign alongside supporters of the Affordable Care Act during a rally outside the Supreme Court before a hearing on the law on March 4
44232_44232.article_context: The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in favor of the Obama administration in King v. Burwell, upholding the Affordable Care Act's provision of subsidies to people purchasing health insurance on federal exchanges. The case posed a major threat to Obamacare, as a ruling against the government could have ended financial assistance for millions of Americans and destabilized insurance markets. The decision ensures that subsidies remain available in all states, regardless of whether they established their own exchanges. Republican leaders criticized the decision but are divided on how to proceed, while the ACA remains secure for now, with future changes possible depending on the outcome of upcoming elections.

42265_42265.caption: In the Central African Republic town of Obo children cheer a convoy of troops from the Central African Republic Uganda and the United States collaborating in the hunt for Joseph Kony
42265_42265.article_context: Ugandan and American troops have suspended their joint search for Joseph Kony, the leader of the Lord’s Resistance Army, due to political turmoil in the Central African Republic, where Kony and his group are believed to be hiding. The withdrawal comes after rebel groups overthrew the friendly government in the country and refused cooperation with foreign troops. While U.S. forces will remain on standby in the region, the suspension of operations has raised fears among human rights groups that Kony may exploit the situation to regroup and resume attacks. The U.S. also announced a $5 million reward for information leading to Kony’s capture, reaffirming their commitment to ending the LRA’s activities despite the setback.

47598_47598.caption: Kim Chongin center interim leader of the main opposition Minjoo Party of Korea marks a winning candidate for the parliamentary election in Seoul South Korea Wednesday
47598_47598.article_context: South Korea's ruling Saenuri Party suffered a surprising defeat in the recent general election, losing its parliamentary majority for the first time in 16 years. The opposition Minjoo Party narrowly won more seats, while the new People’s Party emerged as a significant third force. As a result, President Park Geun-hye’s legislative agenda faces serious obstacles, and her party leader resigned following the loss. The election was driven mainly by concerns over the weak economy rather than tensions with North Korea, marking a shift toward political stalemate ahead of next year’s presidential election.

39165_39165.caption: Ryan Murphy of the United States wins gold in the 100 meter backstroke
39165_39165.article_context: A conflict erupted at the Rio Olympics after Australian swimmer Mack Horton called Chinese competitor Sun Yang a 'drug cheat,' referencing Sun's past doping suspension. The remarks sparked outrage among Chinese netizens and drew strong rebukes from Chinese swimming officials and state media, with demands for an apology and nationalistic criticism of Australia. The dispute became a major topic online in China, highlighting tensions over sportsmanship and national pride during the Games.

469261_469261.caption: The Guardian Live EU referendum debate at the London Palladium
469261_469261.article_context: At a Guardian-hosted EU referendum debate in London, Labour’s Alan Johnson stated that Scots could be justified in seeking independence if the UK left the EU contrary to a pro-EU vote in Scotland, highlighting risks to UK unity posed by Brexit. The debate featured sharp exchanges between Nick Clegg, arguing for 'remain,' and Ukip’s Nigel Farage, advocating 'leave,' who dismissed concerns about the threat to UK unity and warned of rising support for Brexit in Scotland. Topics such as security, EU expansion, and immigration were hotly contested, with both sides criticizing each other's positions amid a vocal audience.

42593_42593.caption: A displaced Iraqi child who fled from violence by Islamic State militants in Mosul sits with her family outside their tent at Baherka refugee camp in Irbil
42593_42593.article_context: The House approved President Obama's plan to train and equip moderate Syrian rebels to combat the Islamic State, despite significant skepticism from both parties about the strategy's effectiveness. The vote, part of a spending bill to keep the government running, marked Congress's support for expanded U.S. involvement in Iraq and Syria, though many lawmakers expressed concern over a lack of clear strategy and the risk of prolonged conflict. Obama reiterated that no U.S. ground troops would be sent, and both Democratic and Republican legislators indicated a broader debate over military authorization would occur after the midterm elections. The Senate is expected to vote on the measure next, but divisions persist regarding the scope and duration of U.S. engagement in the region.

40834_40834.caption: A diver searches for evidence in the San Bernardino Calif shooting massacre that may have been thrown into Seccombe Lake Syed Farook and his wife Tashfeen Malik killed 14 people and injured 21 at the Inland Regional Center
40834_40834.article_context: The FBI announced that Syed Rizwan Farook and his wife, Tashfeen Malik, who killed 14 people and wounded 21 in a mass shooting at a San Bernardino office party, had been radicalized followers of a violent strain of Islam for some time. Investigators are still unsure whether the couple was radicalized independently or with outside help, and have found no evidence the attack was planned with overseas involvement. Malik had pledged allegiance to ISIS online, but ISIS has not directly claimed responsibility. A former neighbor, Enrique Marquez, legally bought the assault rifles used in the attack and supplied them to Farook. Authorities also discovered materials for homemade bombs at the couple’s home. The attack has prompted renewed debates about terrorism and gun control in the United States.

39871_39871.caption: The casket of Michael Brown is seen before the funeral
39871_39871.article_context: In the wake of the shooting of unarmed teenager Michael Brown in Ferguson, Missouri, there has been a noticeable shift in the mainstream feminist conversation, with white feminists increasingly addressing issues of race and police violence. This marks a contrast to previous priorities in feminist activism, which often centered on gender while sidelining race, and highlights longstanding tensions between white and black women in the movement. Black feminist scholars note that black women have always experienced intertwined struggles related to race and gender, while historically, the feminist movement neglected racial justice issues. The response to Ferguson, along with recent debates on immigration reform as a women's issue, signals a push toward a more intersectional approach within feminism that addresses both racial and gender-based discrimination.

461192_461192.caption: George Osborne is under pressure to change course as the UK hovers on the brink of a tripledip recession
461192_461192.article_context: A new poll reveals that most Britons now believe the government's austerity measures are damaging the economy rather than promoting recovery, increasing pressure on Chancellor George Osborne ahead of his upcoming budget. Cabinet divisions and criticism from the government's financial watchdog have added to uncertainty as the UK faces the risk of a triple-dip recession. The poll also shows declining support for the coalition parties, with Nigel Farage's UKIP gaining ground, and internal tensions among Conservatives and Liberal Democrats over the government's economic strategy. Meanwhile, Labour is intensifying calls for action to stimulate growth, and seat projections suggest the Tories could lose numerous seats to Labour if a general election were held now.

46060_46060.caption: FBI Director James Comey A new report commissioned by Congress highlights the bureau s post911 successes and limitations
46060_46060.article_context: A comprehensive report commissioned by Congress has found that while the FBI has significantly improved its counterterrorism capabilities and intelligence sharing since the September 11 attacks, it still faces major challenges. The report praised enhanced collaboration with the CIA and progress in intelligence gathering but highlighted weaknesses in informant development, intelligence analysis, and adaptation to new threats such as cyberterrorism. The report also noted leadership challenges and slow interagency cooperation with the Department of Justice's National Security Division. FBI Director James Comey acknowledged both successes and ongoing areas for improvement, with the review intended to guide future reforms.

42135_42135.caption: Bahayi stands guard on the roof of her house with a loaded gun after recent threats of burglary
42135_42135.article_context: Sara Bahayi has become Afghanistan’s first female taxi driver, challenging societal norms in a highly patriarchal country where women face significant discrimination and violence. Despite frequent harassment and threats, Bahayi continues to drive, supporting her family and inspiring other women to gain economic independence. Her presence offers a safe transportation option for local women and serves as a powerful symbol of resilience and progress. Bahayi’s determination has motivated several women to learn to drive, and she plans to establish Afghanistan’s first female-owned car dealership, further promoting women’s empowerment.

460385_460385.caption: Following the denial Jeremy Corbyn released a statement confirming that he did meet Dyab Abou Jahjah in 2009
460385_460385.article_context: Jeremy Corbyn, Labour leadership contender, admitted meeting Lebanese activist Dyab Abou Jahjah, who was later banned from the UK for extremism, after initially denying knowledge of him. The controversy arose when a photograph circulated showing the two sharing a platform at a 2009 event. Corbyn clarified that meeting someone did not mean endorsing their views. The incident led to renewed scrutiny of Corbyn’s past associations, including alleged links to individuals accused of antisemitism. Corbyn rejected any suggestion that he held racist or antisemitic beliefs, stating his consistent opposition to all forms of racism and his belief in dialogue for peace in the Middle East.

40672_40672.caption: CHARLESTON SC JUNE 27 A program with a cover photograph of Cynthia Hurd 54 is handed out before her funeral at the Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church where she was killed along with eight others in a mass shooting at the church on June 27 2015 in Charleston South Carolina
40672_40672.article_context: Over 800 mourners gathered at Emanuel AME Church in Charleston to honor Cynthia Hurd, a beloved librarian killed alongside eight others during a racially-motivated shooting at a Bible study. Speakers at her funeral praised Hurd's lifelong commitment to her community and her positive impact on local children and families. The service also reflected the city's collective grief and efforts at racial unity in the aftermath of the tragedy, as victims' families declared forgiveness and people of all races offered support. Hurd's funeral was one of several held for the victims, highlighting both personal loss and the broader societal response to the attack.

447908_447908.caption: Philip Hammond says the government will look again at proposals to cut the number of coastguard stations
447908_447908.article_context: Transport Secretary Philip Hammond has announced that the government is reconsidering its controversial plan to reduce the number of UK coastguard stations from 18 to eight, after facing strong opposition from coastal communities and some MPs. While the government is expected to proceed with shutting some stations, the final scale of the reductions may be less severe than originally proposed. Hammond stated that the consultation process is ongoing and a final decision, aimed at modernizing and improving the resilience of coastguard operations, will be announced before the summer recess. The process has created uncertainty among coastguard staff, and opposition figures have called for the plan to be abandoned altogether.

451299_451299.caption: A bearded seal rests on ice off the coast of Alaska These seals were protected until July 2014 when a judge ruled that projections of sea ice changes were based on speculation
451299_451299.article_context: Federal wildlife officials have decided to withdraw proposed protections for the wolverine, reversing earlier plans due to uncertainty over how climate change will affect the species’ snowy habitat. The decision, made by US Fish and Wildlife Service director Dan Ashe, goes against the recommendations of agency scientists and reflects doubts about localized climate predictions. Wildlife advocates attribute the reversal to pressure from western states that opposed federal protections and plan to sue the agency. The move ends proposals to reintroduce wolverines to former habitats in the southern Rockies, and signals broader challenges for protecting climate-sensitive species amid scientific uncertainty.

48497_48497.caption: By comparison these are mussel larvae hatched in corrosive waters An Oregon State University study showed that changing ocean chemistry leads to an odd shape shell deformities and high mortality
48497_48497.article_context: Ocean acidification, driven by human-generated carbon emissions, has become a major concern for scientists and coastal communities, particularly those dependent on fishing. Increased acidity is disrupting marine ecosystems, harming shellfish, corals, and key species at the base of the food web. Research shows impacts vary by region and species, with some shellfish hatcheries suffering production losses while others, like purple sea urchins, show signs of adaptation. Efforts by NOAA and local authorities include monitoring ocean pH, investigating affected species, and developing strategies to help industries adapt, but the broader solution of reducing carbon emissions remains challenging. The phenomenon threatens fisheries, aquaculture, and the livelihoods tied to healthy oceans.

42171_42171.caption: Football players to face disciplinary hearing after ref attack
42171_42171.article_context: Two Texas high school football players from John Jay High School were suspended and ejected from a game after deliberately targeting and hitting a referee during play. The incident, which was captured on video, has prompted the school district to consider further disciplinary action, including possible criminal charges. The team's coach publicly apologized for the event, which has jeopardized the players' football careers and sparked widespread condemnation.

449996_449996.caption: Tim Farron Cameron is launching an allout assault on social and affordable housing
449996_449996.article_context: Liberal Democrat leader Tim Farron has criticized David Cameron's government for plans to extend the right to buy scheme to housing association properties, which would be funded by forcing the sale of council houses. Farron and other Lib Dem leaders warn that this policy threatens the future of social and affordable housing, potentially destroying decades of progress and worsening the housing shortage for vulnerable communities. The Local Government Association and several local government leaders have also condemned the deal, calling it a reckless move that could create a national emergency by reducing the availability of genuinely affordable homes.

43946_43946.caption: Morsi s supporters clash with opponents outside the presidential palace in Cairo Wednesday s clashes began when thousands of Islamist Morsi supporters descended on the area around the palace where about 300 of his opponents were staging a sitin
43946_43946.article_context: Violent clashes erupted in Egypt between supporters of President Mohamed Morsi and opposition protesters outside the presidential palace, deepening the country’s political crisis. The conflict was sparked by Morsi’s recent decree granting himself sweeping powers and pushing a controversial draft constitution toward a referendum, angering a broad coalition of liberals, secularists, and former regime loyalists. Several presidential advisers resigned over the turmoil, while opposition leaders vowed to continue protesting until Morsi backs down. The situation raised concerns about possible military intervention, given the military’s autonomy in the new constitution and its historic role in Egyptian politics. Meanwhile, international calls, including from the U.S., urged dialogue to avoid further violence and protect democratic principles.

44193_44193.caption: Defense attorney Don West holds the Arizona Iced Tea can that Martin was carrying the night he was shot during testimony in Seminole County Circuit Court
44193_44193.article_context: The acquittal of George Zimmerman in the shooting of Trayvon Martin has underscored a sharp racial divide in American society, with polls showing that most African Americans disapproved of the verdict while a slim majority of whites supported it. The case intensified national debates on race, profiling, and the criminal justice system, with activists and Martin's family urging federal civil rights charges and reforms to gun laws. President Obama addressed the racial implications and shared personal experiences of racial bias, which resonated with Black Americans but was criticized by some whites for politicizing the case. The contrasting views reflect long-standing differences in how Black and white Americans perceive justice and race in America.

40502_40502.caption: Barry greets supporters and answers questions at a Days Inn parking lot in Johnstown Pa after his release from a federal prison Barry had been sentenced to six months in prison
40502_40502.article_context: The article reflects on the life and legacy of Marion Barry, the influential and controversial former mayor of Washington, D.C. Barry rose to prominence through civil rights activism and became a transformative political figure, empowering the black middle class and expanding opportunities in the city. Despite early successes, his administration was marred by corruption, personal scandals, and drug addiction, culminating in his arrest and imprisonment. Barry later returned to public life as a councilmember, maintaining his connection with the community even as his influence waned. The story details both his accomplishments and enduring flaws, portraying him as a complex and legendary figure in D.C. history.

40227_40227.caption: Activists react outside the court complex after the sentencing Dozens cheered when the verdict was announced
40227_40227.article_context: An Indian court convicted four men for the brutal gang rape and murder of a 23-year-old female student in New Delhi, an incident that drew global outrage and triggered widespread protests across India. The attack, which occurred on a private bus in December, led to the victim's death after extensive injuries. The case brought national attention to the issue of sexual violence against women and prompted the introduction of stricter laws. The convicted men, who came from impoverished backgrounds, were set to be sentenced, with the victim's family calling for the death penalty. A sixth assailant, a minor at the time, was previously sentenced to three years in a detention facility.

39433_39433.caption: A police crime lab van is seen in 1983 at the hotel where Vernon Evans Jr killed two people
39433_39433.article_context: Maryland currently has five men on death row, including Vernon Lee Evans Jr., who was sentenced nearly 30 years ago for a double murder related to a drug case. Despite death sentences, no one has been executed in Maryland since 2005 due to a de facto moratorium and lengthy appeals. The state is now considering abolishing the death penalty, following Governor O’Malley's proposal, which would affect only future cases. The article highlights the prolonged impact of capital punishment on victims’ families, inmates, and the justice system, questioning the practicality of maintaining the death penalty without enforcement.

43548_43548.caption: A neighbor who declined to give his name said the tires were stolen from Miriam Carey s car in the late spring or early summer and Carey was somewhat upset at apartment officials about it because of what she perceived as a lack of security The neighbor took this photograph
43548_43548.article_context: Miriam Carey, a 34-year-old woman from Connecticut, led police on a car chase from the White House to the U.S. Capitol before being shot and killed by officers while driving in reverse near a guard house. Carey allegedly tried to ram a barricade at the White House and struck a Secret Service agent during the chase, with her young daughter unharmed in the car. Authorities found various personal items in her vehicle but have not disclosed motivations for her actions, though it is suggested she may have struggled with mental illness. The incident has raised questions about police protocols on firing at moving vehicles.

47762_47762.caption: Morsi supporters attend a rally before breaking the daily Ramadan fast in Cairo The Islamic holy month during which Muslims fast from dawn to dusk has reduced the violence seen in the previous week
47762_47762.article_context: After Egypt's military ousted Islamist President Mohamed Morsi, liberal and secularist groups—previously weakened by internal divisions—see an opportunity to unite and reshape the country's future. Celebrating the collapse of the Muslim Brotherhood’s government, these groups hope to avoid past mistakes by prioritizing a new constitution and consolidating their leadership. However, their path forward is uncertain, facing competition from the military, members of the former Mubarak regime, and resilient Islamist factions. Meanwhile, Morsi and several Brotherhood leaders have been detained, but protests and clashes continue, underscoring the volatile and unpredictable nature of Egyptian politics.

40973_40973.caption: Israeli coalition leader Shimon Peres makes a speech before a voting session at the Knesset in Jerusalem Israel s divided parliament ratified Prime Minister Ariel Sharon s Gaza withdrawal plan a pivotal step toward the first evacuation of settlers from occupied territory Palestinians want for a state
40973_40973.article_context: Shimon Peres, a central figure in Israeli politics and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, died in Tel Aviv at age 93 due to complications from a stroke. Over his long career, Peres held almost every major government position, played a key role in building Israel’s military and nuclear capabilities, and championed the 1993 Oslo peace accords with the Palestinians. Though he was often seen as unpopular with voters and left a complex legacy, Peres remained influential in promoting both security and peace efforts, and later served as Israel’s president, gaining international recognition for his commitment to peace.

458759_458759.caption: A proposed pipeline to carry tar sands oil from Canada to the US has ignited protests on climate change grounds
458759_458759.article_context: Naomi Oreskes, a Harvard science historian, highlights Florida's ban prohibiting state employees from using terms like 'climate change' as a stark example of political resistance to scientific consensus, despite overwhelming evidence and the state's vulnerability to rising seas. The release of the documentary 'Merchants of Doubt,' based on Oreskes’s book, exposes how industry-funded think tanks employ tactics similar to those once used in tobacco and asbestos debates to delay acceptance of climate science by sowing public doubt. The article underscores a persistent pattern in US politics where ideological and economic interests undermine scientific findings, with scientists often harassed and discredited for their work. Oreskes argues that such resistance is driven by a distorted view of freedom tied to opposition to regulation, a stance that ultimately risks more severe government intervention when climate impacts worsen. Additionally, the media's insistence on 'balance' further muddles public understanding, while parallels are drawn to other powerful documentaries that have shaped public discourse on major political and environmental issues.

455355_455355.caption: Vince Cable thinks the far left see the EU as a capitalist club
455355_455355.article_context: Former Liberal Democrat business secretary Vince Cable warned that politicians may underestimate the strength of support for leaving the EU ahead of the upcoming referendum. Speaking at the Lib Dem conference, Cable noted rising Euroscepticism on both the right and left and cautioned that the margin of victory for staying in the EU could be much closer than expected. He stressed the importance of the Lib Dems maintaining their pro-EU stance and suggested cooperation with centre-left MPs to counter Conservative influence. Meanwhile, negotiations over Britain’s relationship with the EU are ongoing, with uncertainty over whether proposed changes will require treaty amendments before the referendum.

448090_448090.caption: The dossier is published by Vote Leave who are campaigning for Britain to exit the European Union
448090_448090.article_context: Vote Leave published a dossier detailing murders and rapes committed by EU nationals in the UK, aiming to highlight border security concerns ahead of the Brexit referendum. The move was criticized by Remain campaigners and legal experts as 'scaremongering' and accused of exploiting sensitive cases for political purposes. The Remain side emphasized the benefits of EU membership for security and justice cooperation, while also warning that Brexit could harm young people's futures. The incident deepened tensions between the campaigns, with both sides accusing each other of using fear tactics to influence voters.

40409_40409.caption: Opponents of Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi prepare to burn an Israeli flag during a protest outside the Defense Ministry in Cairo Tens of thousands of backers and opponents of Egypt s Islamist president held competing rallies in the capital and new clashes erupted between the two sides in the country s second largest city Alexandria in a prelude to massive nationwide protests planned by the opposition this weekend
40409_40409.article_context: Andrew D. Pochter, a 21-year-old American student from Maryland, was killed while observing anti-government protests in Alexandria, Egypt. Pochter, who was in Egypt teaching English to children and improving his Arabic, was stabbed by a protester and died alongside two others during the demonstrations. Known for his passion for Middle Eastern culture and peace efforts, Pochter was active in various campus organizations and planned to continue working and studying in the region. His death has drawn condolences from U.S. officials and highlights the dangers present in Egypt during ongoing political unrest.

50519_50519.caption: Supporters listen to Ted Cruz speak during the Election Night Watch Party at Iowa State Fair grounds in Des Moines
50519_50519.article_context: Ted Cruz won the Iowa Republican caucuses by securing strong support from very conservative and evangelical voters, key groups that made up a large share of the electorate. Donald Trump underperformed among new voters and late-deciding participants, while Marco Rubio made a strong showing with those who chose in the final week. Record turnout saw many first-time caucus-goers, but these new voters did not overwhelmingly favor Trump as expected. Overall, Cruz's appeal to the party's most conservative and religious segments delivered his victory, while Trump and Rubio split support among other voter groups.

54272_54272.caption: Students race to escape The attack began around 530 am Kenya Police Chief Joseph Boinet said according to news service Agence FrancePresse
54272_54272.article_context: On April 2, 2015, al-Shabab militants attacked Garissa University College in eastern Kenya, killing at least 147 people in one of the deadliest terror attacks in the country's history. The gunmen stormed dormitories, shooting and taking hostages, primarily targeting Christians while sparing Muslims. The siege lasted 15 hours before security forces killed the four attackers. The event highlighted ongoing security threats from al-Shabab, whose leaders have faced U.S. drone strikes, and underscored Kenya’s vulnerability despite previous warnings and its prominent role in regional anti-terror operations.

455423_455423.caption: Tarique Ghaffur accuses Metropolitan police of discriminating against him
455423_455423.article_context: Assistant commissioner Tarique Ghaffur, one of the most senior Asian officers in the Metropolitan police, has publicly accused the Met and its commissioner, Sir Ian Blair, of longstanding racial and religious discrimination that allegedly sidelined him, particularly in his role overseeing Olympic security. Ghaffur has filed an employment tribunal claim, seeking substantial damages, while deputy commissioner Sir Paul Stephenson and others have strongly denied the allegations and vowed to challenge them. The dispute has highlighted ongoing concerns about racism within the Met, echoing previous cases and inquiries into institutional discrimination.

40440_40440.caption: Special Police Officers or SPOs travel as part of a convoy of paramilitary forces in Chhattisgarh state in 2008
40440_40440.article_context: An investigation by India’s Central Bureau of Investigation has found that Indian security forces, not Maoist rebels as previously claimed, burned the village of Tarmetla and nearby areas in Chhattisgarh in 2011. The report charges specific police and paramilitary personnel with crimes such as arson and unlawful violence, following incidents where villagers were driven out, homes and granaries were destroyed, and several people were killed or assaulted. This marks a rare and significant acknowledgment of abuses by Indian security forces in their fight against Maoist insurgents, vindicating long-standing accusations from locals and activists regarding collective punishment against the indigenous population.

454899_454899.caption: It wasn t meant to be like this The PM had breezed into the committee room as if he was expecting his usual easy ride
454899_454899.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron faced unusually tough questioning from the Commons liaison committee, chaired by Conservative Andrew Tyrie, who pushed Cameron on his government’s lack of accountability and transparency regarding foreign policy and drone strikes. Cameron grew visibly frustrated during the session, struggling to answer pointed queries about the legitimacy of actions in Syria and Libya, the legality of drone operations, and committee oversight. The exchange marked a shift from previous, more relaxed committee proceedings, highlighting Tyrie’s determination to hold the prime minister to account in the absence of effective opposition from the Labour party.

42518_42518.caption: A Yemeni protester flashes the victory sign during a demonstration Monday in Sanaa against the Shiite Houthi rebels who have overrun the capital
42518_42518.article_context: Yemeni activists who led the 2011 Arab Spring protests, which overthrew President Ali Abdullah Saleh, are now deeply disillusioned as the country has collapsed into chaos and looming civil war. The hope for democracy and reform has faded, replaced by corruption, violence, and the rise of extremist groups after Houthi rebels ousted the government and dissolved parliament. Many activists have emigrated, while those remaining feel marginalized and fear that ongoing violence may push more youths toward extremism. Despite continued protests, activists like Faizah al-Sulimani reflect on the sacrifices made, questioning whether their struggle was in vain, as former leaders remain influential and the promised change has not materialized.

44237_44237.caption: Rep Chu and NEA Voto Latino presidents talk immigration at DNC
44237_44237.article_context: During the Democratic National Convention in Philadelphia, The Washington Post hosted a series of live events, panel discussions, and interviews with politicians, policymakers, and experts on major issues such as criminal justice reform, energy policy, health care, women's leadership, and immigration. Notable appearances included Gov. Jerry Brown, House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi, Sen. Chris Murphy, and campaign staff from Hillary Clinton. The events offered insights into the Democratic Party's platform and allowed for in-depth conversations about key challenges facing the nation, while Washington Post journalists provided behind-the-scenes perspectives on political reporting and coverage.

40133_40133.caption: People from the area wait outside the venue to see Clinton as she leaves the political meeting hosted at a Beaverdale home
40133_40133.article_context: Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign raised $47 million in its first quarter, but has already spent nearly $19 million — about 40% of its haul — assembling a large and sophisticated political operation with over 400 staff members, extensive polling, and top consultants. The campaign is rapidly expanding its infrastructure to prepare for both a competitive Democratic primary and a tough general election battle. Despite promoting an image of frugality, Clinton's team has faced scrutiny over high expenditures and questions about whether fundraising can keep pace with spending, especially since most contributions have come from donors who have already maxed out their legal limits. The campaign has made major investments in digital outreach, polling, and event production, aiming to create a robust organization reminiscent of successful strategies used by Obama’s 2012 campaign, while also adjusting tactics from her 2008 run.

469448_469448.caption: The American statistician Nate Silver has given his prediction for the UK general election
469448_469448.article_context: Nate Silver, known for his accurate US election forecasts, predicts a highly uncertain and complex outcome for the UK general election, with his model showing no party winning an outright majority. Silver's projections suggest the Conservatives will have a slight lead in seats over Labour, but a coalition of at least three parties would be needed to form a government, raising the possibility of a 'rainbow coalition.' The close polling, volatile support for minor parties like Ukip, and widespread tactical voting contribute to the unpredictability. Silver acknowledges the challenges in forecasting UK elections compared to the US, emphasizing there is still considerable ambiguity about which party will be able to form a government after the election.

42365_42365.caption: Members of GIPN and RAID French police special forces are pictured in Corcy near VillersCotterets where two suspects were reported to have been seen
42365_42365.article_context: The article recounts the traumatic experiences of several Parisians during the January 2015 terrorist attacks in Paris, where brothers Chérif and Said Kouachi killed staff at the satirical newspaper Charlie Hebdo, and their accomplice Amedy Coulibaly murdered hostages at a kosher supermarket. The attacks left 17 dead and shocked France, sparking intense debates about free speech, integration, and extremism among French Muslims. Survivors and acquaintances of the attackers reflect on the sociocultural challenges faced by immigrant communities and the deep divisions these events exposed. A national vigil followed, with many rallying around the phrase 'Je suis Charlie' as a stand for free expression and unity.

42672_42672.caption: Turkish nationalists burn a rainbow flag during a rally staged by the LGBT community in Istanbul on June 19
42672_42672.article_context: Although homosexuality is technically legal in Turkey, LGBT activists highlight increasing threats and discrimination, particularly under the country’s conservative government. Istanbul’s annual gay-pride parade was canceled for the first time since 2003, with officials citing security concerns following recent attacks, but organizers accuse the government of silencing dissent. Despite some past progress, including wider acceptance and representation, LGBT individuals continue to face harassment, violence, and lack of legal protections, with many cases of attacks going uninvestigated. Activists warn that the climate is worsening, and the government has failed to support or protect the LGBT community as conservative attitudes dominate society.

46731_46731.caption: Israeli security forces detain Palestinian men in the West Bank village of Beit Sahur during an operation to locate the three teenagers
46731_46731.article_context: Israeli authorities confirmed the discovery of the bodies of three kidnapped Israeli teenagers in the West Bank, who were abducted earlier in June. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blamed the Islamist group Hamas for the killings and vowed punitive action, although specifics have not yet been determined. The incident has heightened Israeli-Palestinian tensions, prompting extensive Israeli military operations and escalating violence with Gaza, including airstrikes and rocket fire.
