His and his wife Sarah's activism led to the passage of the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act in 1993, which mandated federal background checks for handgun buyers. Brady’s perseverance and public service made him a symbol of the gun-control movement, earning him national honors and recognition for his contributions.

46537_46537.caption: An intense Xclass solar flare occurred on Wednesday afternoon originating from Active Region 2158 This is the second solar flare in two days from AR2158 and the associated magnetic cloud could provide an intense aurora shows on Thursday and Friday
46537_46537.article_context: This week, two significant solar flares erupted from a sunspot region aimed almost directly at Earth, including an X1.6-class flare — the strongest type — prompting NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center to issue geomagnetic storm watches for Friday and Saturday. The expected storms, classified as G2 and G3, are predicted to impact high frequency radio transmissions but are not expected to cause major disruptions to power grids or satellites. Northern U.S. states may see enhanced aurora displays, and forecasters noted the unusual positioning of the sunspot group, though Earth will only receive a partial impact from the solar ejections.

442475_442475.caption: 19 June An environmentalist embraces a globe at the entrance of the Brazil Pavilion More than 50000 policymakers environmentalists and business leaders from around the world are meeting in Rio de Janeiro this week marking the 20year anniversary of the landmark Earth summit that paved the way for the Kyoto agreement on greenhouse gases
442475_442475.article_context: On 19 June, world leaders, policymakers, and activists gathered in Rio de Janeiro for the UN Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20), marking the 20th anniversary of the landmark Earth Summit. The event featured environmental art displays, protests by indigenous groups and activists against issues like resource waste, hunger, and military spending, as well as political actions regarding climate change and emissions reduction. Negotiators reached a draft agreement to be reviewed by summit leaders, while parallel civil society events highlighted demands for sustainable solutions and social justice.

444124_444124.caption: Offsetting needs a world with strong emissions targets set
444124_444124.article_context: The article argues that carbon offsetting, especially through mechanisms like the UN's Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), is a crucial first step in addressing collective climate inaction, challenging critics who claim offsetting is ineffective. The CDM has facilitated significant emission reductions, channeled billions into technology for developing countries, and set technical standards for global emissions management. Offsetting provides cost-effective emission reductions, builds broader support for climate policy, and familiarizes countries with emission reduction practices, thus paving the way for more ambitious climate action. While the CDM is not without flaws—such as some negative social impacts and a need for stricter evaluation—it remains essential for enabling global cooperation and laying the groundwork for stronger future climate commitments.

40596_40596.caption: The stabbing at a Brookland Metro bus waiting area comes amid a spate of violent crimes in or near Metro stations
40596_40596.article_context: A 15-year-old boy was stabbed in the bus waiting area of the Brookland Metro stop in Northeast Washington, with a 17-year-old suspect arrested shortly after the attack. The victim's injuries are not life-threatening. This incident follows recent violent crimes at Metro stations, including the fatal stabbing of a 24-year-old man aboard a train at the NoMa-Gallaudet U Street stop, for which a suspect has also been arrested.

447363_447363.caption: Proindependence voters from the Western Isles of Lewis and Bute march down Edinburgh s Royal Mile to protest against Scotland s independence referendum results blaming scaremongering by the BBC
447363_447363.article_context: Following Scotland’s independence referendum, supporters of the pro-independence ‘yes’ campaign gathered in cities like Edinburgh and Glasgow, some displaying defiance and others showing signs of disappointment and dejection at the results. Pro-independence protesters attributed their defeat partly to media influence and criticized the BBC for alleged scaremongering. These events were marked by public marches, emotional scenes, and damaged campaign materials, highlighting the deep divisions and strong feelings surrounding the referendum outcome.

43033_43033.caption: The Rev Al Sharpton says Hands up do nt shoot during his speech at the rally
43033_43033.article_context: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Washington, D.C., for a 'Justice for All' march organized by Rev. Al Sharpton's National Action Network, calling attention to police violence against unarmed African American men. Family members of victims such as Eric Garner, Michael Brown, and Tamir Rice spoke at the rally, emphasizing unity and the need for ongoing activism. The march, which drew a diverse crowd, was one of many protests held nationwide in response to the deaths of black men at the hands of police and grand jury decisions not to indict officers involved. The events highlighted generational tensions within the movement and reflected a growing demand for systemic change and justice for all Americans.

45677_45677.caption: Mexico s Foreign Affairs Secretary Claudia Ruiz Massieu shown on Dec 15 called Trump ignorant and racist She said that Trump s assertion that Mexico would pay for a wall between the two countries is absurd
45677_45677.article_context: Latino Republicans are facing deep internal conflict over supporting Donald Trump in the presidential election, as Trump continues targeting prominent Hispanic figures and adopts harsh stances on immigration. The situation has led some Hispanic GOP members to abandon their roles, including the Republican National Committee's Hispanic media spokeswoman, Ruth Guerra. Trump’s rhetoric has exacerbated the GOP’s struggles to appeal to minority voters, with polling showing record-high unfavorable ratings among Hispanics. While GOP leaders warn of long-term consequences, the party’s efforts to reach out to Latino voters remain undermined by Trump’s tone and policies.

452543_452543.caption: Tewkesbury in Gloucestershire surrounded by water during the 2007 floods
452543_452543.article_context: A National Audit Office report warns that over two-thirds of UK councils feel unprepared to handle increasing flood risks, with a national funding gap of over £100 million and difficulties in recruiting qualified staff. Although the government has shifted more responsibility for flood management to local authorities, only 30% feel they have the necessary expertise. Budget cuts, staff shortages, and unclear guidance from central departments pose further challenges, while climate change is expected to exacerbate flood risks. The government is encouraging more private sector funding to address the shortfall, but contributions remain low. Critics say current reforms may not fulfill their goals if these issues persist.

51119_51119.caption: A truck used by some of the protest s leaders during the demonstration stands abandoned and damaged after the explosion
51119_51119.article_context: At least 80 people were killed and over 230 injured in Kabul when suicide bombers attacked a peaceful protest mainly attended by the Shiite Hazara minority. The Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack, which is believed to be the group’s first major strike in an Afghan urban area and appears to deliberately target the Hazara community. The bombing occurred during a demonstration over government power line plans, and came despite security measures. Both Afghan and international leaders condemned the assault, which highlights escalating violence and sectarian tensions in Afghanistan.

42836_42836.caption: Young boys pick through the ruins of a recently bombed building gathering books from the wreckage in Jabaliya Refugee Camp in Gaza on Nov 28 2012
42836_42836.article_context: Support for Hamas in Gaza, once strong after its recent armed confrontation with Israel, is showing signs of decline as Gazans question the real gains of the conflict. While older generations view the battle as a victory, younger Gazans and women express skepticism about Hamas's achievements, focusing on the ongoing hardships and losses rather than perceived victories. Since seizing control from Fatah five years ago, Hamas has imposed strict Islamist rules, which many residents resent. Although Hamas’s use of longer-range rockets has boosted morale for some, internal divisions and war fatigue are evident. The group's reliance on support from Iran and its military strategy are contrasted by the approach of Fatah, which recently achieved recognition for a Palestinian state at the United Nations. Growing disillusionment among residents suggests that Hamas’s political gains from the conflict may be short-lived.

43339_43339.caption: An ultraOrthodox Jewish man prays as Israeli rescue workers clean the scene of attack
43339_43339.article_context: Four worshippers, including three Americans and one Briton, were killed in a Jerusalem synagogue attack during morning prayers by Palestinian assailants. Among those killed was Rabbi Mosheh Twersky, a prominent figure from a distinguished Orthodox Jewish family. The attack deeply affected the American and British Jewish communities, prompting calls for mourning and prayers across synagogues in the United States and Israel. The incident brought international attention to the ongoing Middle East violence and its impact on Jewish communities worldwide.

44251_44251.caption: Police officers at the SpringfieldBranson National Airport noticed a sharp decline in complaints after they started wearing body cameras
44251_44251.article_context: The Springfield-Branson National Airport police force in Missouri has seen a significant drop in traveler complaints since officers began wearing body cameras, suggesting the technology may improve relations between the public and police. This local success has influenced national conversations, especially following high-profile incidents of police violence and government proposals to subsidize body cams for police forces across the country. Evidence from other cities, like Rialto, California, also shows declines in complaints and use of force. As major police departments in cities like New York, Washington, and Los Angeles begin pilot programs and purchases, experts predict body cameras will become standard equipment for law enforcement nationwide, despite concerns about cost, privacy, and logistics.

47955_47955.caption: An elderly man fills out his ballot in Orane before casting it with the mobile Ukrainian election committee
47955_47955.article_context: Petro Poroshenko, a billionaire chocolate tycoon, claimed victory in Ukraine’s presidential election, securing over 55 percent of the vote according to exit polls. He takes office after the ouster of pro-Kremlin Viktor Yanukovych and faces major challenges, including ongoing violence in the separatist east, Russia’s annexation of Crimea, and strained relations between Russia and the West. Many citizens in eastern Ukraine were unable to vote due to unrest and separatist disruptions. Poroshenko has pledged to restore peace and unite Ukraine, pursue closer ties with the European Union, and hold new parliamentary elections. The final voter turnout was estimated at around 60 percent.

44755_44755.caption: An antigovernment protester runs away from a burning container in Istanbul s Taksim Square
44755_44755.article_context: Mass anti-government protests have erupted across Turkey, sparked by a police crackdown on a peaceful environmental demonstration in Istanbul on May 31. The unrest quickly expanded nationwide, with protesters voicing diverse grievances such as threats to personal freedoms, religious conservatism under Prime Minister Erdogan, and his foreign policy toward Syria. Erdogan has dismissed protesters as 'anarchists and terrorists,' while maintaining strong support among conservative voters. Demonstrations have been widespread and varied in nature, uniting people primarily in opposition to perceived erosion of liberties, but also reflecting regional issues. The crisis marks one of the most serious challenges to Erdogan's decade in power, with analysts suggesting he must address a broad range of concerns to restore stability.

39481_39481.caption: Unionized federal employees protest the government shutdown outside the McNamara Federal Building in Detroit
39481_39481.article_context: After a 16-day government shutdown and near default, Congress voted to reopen the government and raise the debt ceiling, with President Obama signing the bill immediately after its passage. The deal, brokered by Senate leaders Harry Reid and Mitch McConnell, brought furloughed federal employees back to work and temporarily suspended the debt limit until February 7, while funding agencies through January 15. The shutdown, rooted in a failed Republican attempt to undermine Obamacare, ultimately damaged GOP popularity and left its leadership divided. With the crisis resolved for now, both parties face renewed budget negotiations and the possibility of more fiscal standoffs in the months ahead.

42058_42058.caption: A man comforts his son who was injured during the school attack at Lady Reading Hospital in Peshawar
42058_42058.article_context: A Taliban assault on an army-run school in Peshawar, Pakistan, resulted in the deaths of at least 141 students and teachers, sparking nationwide and international outrage. The attack, carried out as retaliation for a recent Pakistani military offensive against Taliban strongholds, targeted primarily children and was widely condemned across Pakistan’s political, religious, and even militant circles. The unprecedented brutality of the massacre led to calls for national unity and stronger action against terrorism, though analysts noted ongoing ambivalence within Pakistan's leadership toward confronting militant groups. The Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility and framed the attack as revenge, highlighting the continuing struggle between militants and the military.

458020_458020.caption: Leonardo DiCaprio speaks at the opening of the United Nations Climate Summit 2014 September 23 2014 at the United Nations in New York
458020_458020.article_context: At a UN climate summit, actor Leonardo DiCaprio addressed world leaders, urging decisive action to combat climate change. He highlighted the severity of recent climate events and scientific consensus, stressing that the issue surpasses individual choices and requires large-scale government and industry intervention. DiCaprio called for putting a price on carbon emissions, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and investing in renewable energy, framing climate action as a moral duty and an urgent challenge for humanity.

41179_41179.caption: A Baltimore sheriff s officer asks protesters in front of the courthouse to move
41179_41179.article_context: In the trial of Baltimore police officer William G. Porter, who is the first of six officers charged in the arrest and death of Freddie Gray, defense attorneys Gary Proctor and Joe Murtha are using their experience and distinct courtroom styles to convince jurors of Porter’s good intentions and difficult circumstances. The trial, which has drawn national attention to issues of police conduct, focuses on the facts and seeks to provide Porter a fair trial rather than addressing broader social justice concerns. Both lawyers have notable backgrounds in high-profile cases and are working to present Porter as a credible, relatable defendant, hoping to persuade jurors to view his actions sympathetically during a complex and widely watched legal proceeding.

463954_463954.caption: Ban Kimoon the UN secretary general insisted progress was being made in the lead up to the Rio20 Earth summit
463954_463954.article_context: UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon expressed cautious optimism that the upcoming Rio+20 Earth summit could deliver a significant plan for global sustainable development, despite concerns over slow negotiations, absent world leaders, and the summit’s uncertain prospects. Ban highlighted progress in preparatory talks but acknowledged that many divisions remain on key issues such as defining a 'green economy' and financial burden-sharing. While a binding treaty is unlikely, he emphasized the potential for nations to agree on new sustainable development goals to complement existing UN poverty targets, framing the summit as the start of a shift toward more sustainable growth.

444833_444833.caption: A mother and baby The Tories would allow parents to divide up maternity leave between them
444833_444833.article_context: David Cameron has proposed making parental leave more flexible, allowing mothers and fathers to share time off with their newborns or take leave together, instead of the current rules requiring mothers to take the initial 26 weeks. The Tory plan, unveiled ahead of their spring conference in Gateshead, would let parents divide up 52 weeks of leave as they prefer after the first 14 weeks, aiming to make Britain more family-friendly and tackle the gender pay gap. The proposal drew criticism from Labour’s John Hutton, who argued the Tories were out of touch with working families and lacked credibility on family policies. This policy announcement coincides with the Conservatives’ efforts to boost their profile during their two-day conference.

463371_463371.caption: Sending undercover reporters to try to expose alleged discontent among Liberal Democrat ministers breached rules against the use of subterfuge by newspapers the PCC has ruled
463371_463371.article_context: The Press Complaints Commission reprimanded the Daily Telegraph for using undercover reporters and secret recordings to obtain stories about Liberal Democrat ministers, including Vince Cable. The PCC ruled that the paper's methods were unjustified and disproportionately intrusive, citing a lack of sufficient public interest. This decision followed complaints from ministers and the public, affirming that confidential conversations between MPs and constituents must be respected. The ruling vindicated Liberal Democrats who argued the operation breached trust, and the PCC announced plans to issue more guidance on subterfuge in journalism. While the Telegraph accepted the decision, its editor warned of negative implications for investigative reporting.

43274_43274.caption: Gen Sher Mohammad Karimi and other Afghan officials visit Helmand province s Sangin district Saturday The Afghan army has been battling a dayslong Taliban offensive in the area
43274_43274.article_context: The Taliban has launched a major offensive in Afghanistan's Helmand province, gathering over a thousand fighters in its largest attempt this year to retake ground as U.S. forces withdraw. The attack has focused on Sangin district, a strategic area long contested by insurgents, resulting in dozens of deaths and thousands displaced. Afghan security forces have struggled but claim to be regaining control, while the Taliban asserts substantial gains. The clashes highlight both the Taliban’s continued strength and challenges facing Afghanistan’s security forces as international support wanes.

42958_42958.caption: An EU flag flies over Independence Square in Kiev A poster of jailed former prime minister Yulia Tymoshenko is also seen on the metal base of a destroyed Christmas tree in the capital city
42958_42958.article_context: Ukrainian riot police moved against protestors occupying Kiev's Independence Square but withdrew after partially dismantling barricades, leaving the demonstrators in control. The police action, which led to several injuries, was met with strong condemnation from opposition leaders and Western officials. The protests began after President Yanukovych rejected a trade deal with the European Union in favor of closer ties with Russia, sparking widespread opposition. Both sides remain entrenched, with international leaders urging a peaceful resolution and negotiations.

39621_39621.caption: Destruction caused by a flash flood along Main Street
39621_39621.article_context: After a devastating flood in Ellicott City, Maryland that killed two people and caused tens of millions in damage to the historic downtown, local and federal officials have vowed to support the city's recovery and rebuilding efforts. County Executive Allan Kittleman assured residents and business owners that reconstruction will take months or years, and Senator Barbara Mikulski pledged to expedite federal emergency aid. The community has come together, with volunteers helping clean up and officials offering guidance and comfort, while assessments of damage and distribution of grants are underway.

454538_454538.caption: Tasmanian devils are facing a real extinction threat Tumours are the hereandnow threat and climate change is the next big threat
454538_454538.article_context: New research shows that Tasmanian devils’ low genetic diversity and historical population declines were primarily caused by climate change, not by hunting or the spread of facial tumour disease. Analysis of the largest genetic dataset for the species found two major population decreases in the past 50,000 years that substantially reduced gene diversity, linked to periods of colder and drier climate. While bounty hunting and disease have impacted the species, climate change remains the biggest long-term threat. Conservation efforts, such as creating 'insurance' populations, are vital due to the animals' limited genetic diversity, which makes them more vulnerable to disease and further environmental changes.

457775_457775.caption: A water stress map of the world released by Greenpeace showing distribution of coal plants and areas of heavy water use
457775_457775.article_context: A Greenpeace-commissioned report reveals that coal power plants currently use enough water to supply a billion people, and water use could almost double if all planned plants are built. Nearly half of new coal plants are projected to be built in areas already experiencing high water stress, especially in China, India, and Turkey. The report highlights the severe impact of coal on both water resources and climate, urging governments to halt coal expansion in water-stressed regions, phase out old and inefficient plants, and transition to renewable energy sources to save water and meet climate commitments.

47617_47617.caption: Turkish rescue personnel help a wounded person
47617_47617.article_context: A suicide bombing by three suspected Islamic State militants at Istanbul's international airport killed at least 44 people and wounded more than 200, worsening an already bleak tourism season in Turkey. The attack follows a string of bombings in the country and has further discouraged tourists, causing a sharp decline in visitors, hotel occupancy, and sales for local shops. The economic impact is severe, with analysts predicting slowed growth and continued high inflation. While most tourists are staying away due to security concerns, a recent thaw in relations between Turkey and Russia may bring some Russian tourists back, offering a glimmer of hope for the struggling tourism sector.

453951_453951.caption: A dead baby Sumatran elephant found in a river in Serbajadi in east Aceh district near Leuser conservation area Sumatra island Indonesia Dozens of elephants have died after being poisoned in recent years
453951_453951.article_context: A major international report shows world leaders are failing to meet targets set in 2010 to slow biodiversity loss by 2020, with habitats continuing to be destroyed and overfishing persisting. Scientists warn that most of the Aichi targets—including halving habitat loss and expanding protected areas—are unlikely to be achieved, mirroring previous failures to meet biodiversity commitments. Despite some increased awareness and funding, experts call the lack of progress a troubling sign and urge governments to redouble efforts as officials from nearly 200 countries gather to address the crisis.

463466_463466.caption: Jimmy Carr is said to have used a legal taxavoidance scheme
463466_463466.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron publicly criticised comedian Jimmy Carr for using legal but aggressive tax avoidance schemes, calling his actions 'morally wrong' and unfair to the general public who pay their taxes. Carr reportedly sheltered millions through the Jersey-based K2 scheme, paying less tax than most citizens, while similar allegations emerged about Take That members using the Icebreaker scheme. The government promised to crack down on such avoidance through new legislation, and HMRC confirmed investigations into both schemes. Amidst wider controversy about tax avoidance involving celebrities and Tory donors, officials and opposition MPs called for tougher enforcement and fairness in the tax system.

49487_49487.caption: Supporters celebrate the results at Barbara Comstock s electionnight headquarters in Ashburn Va
49487_49487.article_context: John Vihstadt, a Republican running as an independent, won reelection to the Arlington County Board, defeating Democrat Alan Howze. Vihstadt's victory, attributed to his opposition to the expensive Columbia Pike streetcar project and his fiscally conservative stance, came despite Arlington's strong Democratic history. The streetcar project was a central issue, dividing voters and candidates. While the result does not change the board's overall support for the streetcar, it signals growing dissatisfaction among county residents with high-cost development projects. In other races, Barbara Kanninen won a School Board seat, and several bond measures for transportation, schools, and infrastructure were approved.

42943_42943.caption: Cruz Trump campaign run by Washington lobbyists
42943_42943.article_context: Supporters of Senator Ted Cruz outmaneuvered Donald Trump's campaign in Arizona, Missouri, and Virginia, securing key delegate positions for the Republican National Convention despite Trump winning those states' primaries. However, this may not affect Trump's chances of clinching the nomination, as he remains on track for the necessary 1,237 delegates, with upcoming primaries expected to boost his lead. The delegate gains by Cruz could result in a convention audience filled with his supporters, highlighting the organizational weaknesses in Trump's campaign. Tensions rose among Trump backers in Arizona, who claimed the delegate selection process was unfair. Meanwhile, Cruz continues to focus on securing loyal delegates as a contingency if Trump fails to win outright, whereas Trump’s advisers express confidence in his inevitable nomination.

447394_447394.caption: Poland s huge coalfired power station Elektrownia Belchatow which has been named as the biggest single polluter in the EU
447394_447394.article_context: Elektrownia Belchatow in Poland has been named the largest carbon emitter in the European Union, producing over 30 million tonnes of CO2 last year, and is set to expand its capacity by 20%. A report by Sandbag Climate Campaign highlights Belchatow and dozens of planned coal-fired plants across Europe as evidence that EU policies, particularly the Emissions Trading Scheme, are failing to deter heavily polluting investments. Environmental groups warn that these expansions undermine the EU’s credibility ahead of global climate talks and threaten its targets for carbon reduction. While some countries, like the UK, are linking new coal projects to carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology, widespread adoption and economic feasibility of CCS remain uncertain, leaving Europe’s emissions problem unresolved.

42608_42608.caption: A UN chemical weapons expert checks a fellow inspector after they ended their visit to the site of an alleged chemical weapons attack in the Ain Tarma neighborhood of Damascus
42608_42608.article_context: U.N. chemical weapons inspectors visited a Damascus suburb in Syria to investigate a suspected toxic gas attack that killed hundreds, despite coming under sniper fire en route. The alleged attack has intensified international calls for military intervention, with the U.S. and its Western allies considering action against the Syrian government even without U.N. approval. While the inspectors are gathering evidence on whether chemical weapons were used, they are not tasked with assigning responsibility. The incident has raised tensions and led to diplomatic meetings among top military officials from multiple countries to discuss possible responses, further increasing speculation about imminent military action.

459222_459222.caption: Jim Murphy in favour of autonomy for Scottish Labour
459222_459222.article_context: Jim Murphy has announced his candidacy for the leadership of the Scottish Labour party following Johann Lamont's unexpected resignation. Murphy, who played a key role in Labour's pro-union campaign during the Scottish independence referendum, is considered the frontrunner and pledges to unite the party and pursue the role of first minister. Neil Findlay and Sarah Boyack have also entered the race, with Findlay emphasizing social justice and party unity. The contest highlights calls for greater autonomy for Scottish Labour and a renewed focus on progressive policies in the post-referendum period.

451940_451940.caption: Thousands of wispy white webs are draped over trees and bushes I was stunned when I saw all the cobwebs it makes the park look really spooky said Hannah Atkin 23 from Cambridge At first I thought it was a frost or spider s webs but when I looked more closely I realised the trees were actually covered in webs which were full of tiny caterpillars It really gave me the creeps
451940_451940.article_context: A striking outbreak of ermine moth caterpillars has covered around 16 trees on Jesus Green in Cambridge with dense, silvery webs, leaving the trees stripped bare of leaves. The caterpillars create large communal webs as protection from birds and feed on the surrounding foliage, sometimes causing significant but generally temporary damage to plants and trees. Experts attribute this year's high numbers to a cold winter and spring reducing predator populations. Ermine moth outbreaks like this are unusual but have been recorded in other parts of the UK, and affected trees typically recover by the following year.

52933_52933.caption: White House counsel Kathryn Ruemmler plans to leave by the end of the year to return to private practice
52933_52933.article_context: White House Counsel Kathryn Ruemmler, a trusted advisor to President Obama, is stepping down at the end of the year to return to private practice in New York. Ruemmler has been a key member of Obama's administration since 2009, playing a central role in advising on legal matters and national security issues, as well as managing responses to major investigations like the IRS controversy and Benghazi attack. Her departure marks the exit of an influential and highly regarded legal figure in Obama's inner circle.

42191_42191.caption: A large crowd turned out for the campaign rally in Daytona Beach Fla
42191_42191.article_context: The vice presidential debate between Joe Biden and Paul Ryan is seen as unusually important, coming after Mitt Romney's strong performance in the first presidential debate that shifted momentum in his favor. For the Obama campaign, Biden's goal is to counter Romney's gains and defend the administration's record, while Ryan aims to capitalize on Romney's performance and reinforce the Republican ticket's momentum. Both candidates are experienced and influential figures in their parties, making the debate more significant than typical VP exchanges. Polls show Romney closing the gap nationally and in key battleground states, heightening the stakes. The debate's outcome could have major implications for the direction of the race ahead of the next presidential debate.

44320_44320.caption: A man places a rose at the Belgian Embassy in tribute to victims of Tuesday s attacks in Brussels in Berlin on Wednesday
44320_44320.article_context: Jewish communities in Belgium and France marked the holiday of Purim in contrasting ways following a deadly terrorist attack in Brussels. In Belgium, Jewish congregations canceled planned festivities and large gatherings out of safety concerns, choosing instead to hold quiet worship services. Conversely, Jews in Paris proceeded with public Purim celebrations, emphasizing resilience and solidarity in the face of terrorism, with even higher attendance than previous years. The events highlighted the ongoing threat of anti-Semitism in Europe and differing community responses to violence.

463794_463794.caption: The female Sumatran rhino which is estimated to be between four and five years old was safely captured in a pit trap in Kutai Barat in East Kalimantan on 12 March
463794_463794.article_context: Conservationists have successfully captured a female Sumatran rhino in Indonesian Borneo, marking the first physical contact with the species in the region in over 40 years. With fewer than 100 Sumatran rhinos left due to hunting and habitat loss, this event is considered highly significant for conservation efforts. The rhino, found in East Kalimantan, will be relocated to a sanctuary for protection, though officials remain cautious about sharing its precise location to prevent poaching. The discovery raises hopes for the survival of the critically endangered species, but experts caution that more data is needed to determine if the population is sufficient for breeding and long-term survival.

43706_43706.caption: The 25 cities targeted by the administration in its Obamacare push
43706_43706.article_context: The White House is focusing its efforts to promote the Affordable Care Act on 25 major cities across the country, targeting areas with the highest numbers of uninsured residents in states where the federal government operates the health insurance marketplace. This targeted approach aims to maximize sign-ups, especially among young adults, given that a large proportion of the nation's uninsured are concentrated in these locations.

56256_56256.caption: Imran Khan chief of TehrikeInsaf party gestures while speaking at a ceremony in Lahore Khan has opposed a Pakistani government decision to recognize Israel saying the country should not be recognized until Palestinians achieve a state
56256_56256.article_context: Imran Khan, a prominent Pakistani politician and former cricket star, has announced plans to lead a large protest rally into South Waziristan to oppose U.S. CIA drone strikes in Pakistan’s tribal areas. The planned march, which includes foreign antiwar activists, has drawn concerns from Pakistan’s military and local authorities due to security risks from Taliban insurgents and the volatile situation in the region. While Khan frames the event as a peaceful demonstration to highlight civilian casualties from drone attacks, critics accuse him of staging a dangerous publicity stunt. The rally underscores tensions between Pakistan’s civilian government, its powerful military, and the ongoing U.S. drone campaign, which continues despite widespread public opposition.

465285_465285.caption: Lord Lawson It s the government s job to decide what is to be done
465285_465285.article_context: Chancellor George Osborne announced a public consultation as part of the government's plan to reduce the £156bn fiscal deficit, inviting input from the public, civil society, and opposition parties on where spending cuts should fall. The initiative, which includes meetings across the UK and a website, aims to promote transparency and inclusivity ahead of the upcoming autumn spending review. However, former chancellor Lord Lawson and others criticized the consultation as a public relations tactic, arguing that ultimate decisions rest with the government and past consultations have often been ignored. The government insists it wants genuine engagement and has set up new accountability measures, including a star chamber and review groups, to scrutinize departmental budget plans.

41629_41629.caption: Law enforcement and other emergency personnel respond to the scene of a shooting at the Grand Theatre 16 in Lafayette
41629_41629.article_context: A shooting occurred at the Grand Theater in Lafayette, Louisiana, during a movie screening, causing chaos as patrons rushed to evacuate. Sirens sounded, police quickly responded, and several people were injured, including a woman shot in the leg. Law enforcement stormed the building and reports indicated multiple victims and that the suspect died by suicide. The incident left witnesses shocked and terrified as they fled the scene amid uncertainty about the situation inside and outside the theater.

49223_49223.caption: Refugees from Afghanistan and Syria are seen shortly after arriving on an inflatable boat on March 12 2016 in Mytelene Greece
49223_49223.article_context: The Syrian conflict began in 2011 when widespread protests against President Bashar al-Assad's regime were met with violent repression, igniting a civil war. Rebel forces captured key cities like Aleppo, challenging Assad's control, while a major 2013 chemical attack killed nearly 1,500 people and drew global outrage. The rise of the Islamic State further destabilized the region, as the group seized territory and declared a caliphate in parts of Syria. The war led to a massive humanitarian crisis, forcing over 11 million Syrians to flee their homes. Russian military intervention in 2015 strengthened Assad but complicated international efforts. Occasional cease-fires provided brief respite, but the conflict saw the decline of moderate opposition forces and the persistent dominance of extremists and the Assad regime.

42618_42618.caption: A view of the first round of government talks in Kiev Ukraine The discussions on Ukrainian national unity opened a day after Ukrainian troops suffered their single heaviest loss of life against separatists
42618_42618.article_context: Rinat Akhmetov, Ukraine's wealthiest businessman, deployed workers from his steel plants to help restore order in Mariupol and other eastern cities amid ongoing separatist unrest. This move brought a temporary calm to previously volatile areas and marked a significant intervention by Akhmetov, who holds major influence in the region. While some speculate that he acted out of self-interest to protect his business and political power, Akhmetov denied supporting separatists and advocated for a more decentralized Ukraine. The situation remains tense, with accusations of betrayal among pro-Russian activists and uncertainty about Akhmetov’s intentions for future involvement.

43117_43117.caption: What to expect from Uber Lyft and Capital Bikeshare during Metro repairs
43117_43117.article_context: In response to Metro's SafeTrack maintenance plan, which is expected to impact commuters citywide starting this weekend, Washington D.C. officials announced measures to ease congestion and provide alternative transit options. These include expanding rush-hour parking restrictions in bus corridors, allowing shared taxicab rides, increasing cycling access with a discounted $2 Capital Bikeshare option, and potentially extending Circulator bus hours. The city will also increase traffic control efforts and closely monitor conditions as SafeTrack causes significant disruptions to the Orange and Silver Metro lines for the next 10 months.

469881_469881.caption: David Miliband expressed his frustration at a lack of vision from the Labour leadership
469881_469881.article_context: David Miliband, the UK foreign secretary, acknowledges that voters are unclear about what Labour and Prime Minister Gordon Brown stand for after poor results in the European elections. Miliband admits he considered resigning alongside James Purnell but ultimately chose to stay and urges Labour ministers to prepare for a tough general election fight. He calls for the party to clearly articulate its values and direction, pushing for stronger leadership and a reset of political priorities. Miliband also voices support for electoral reform and criticizes unfocused political briefings, while Lord Mandelson warns of continued unrest within the Labour party over Brown's leadership.

43807_43807.caption: An ambulance carries the body of a victim
43807_43807.article_context: Gunmen linked to a splinter group of the Pakistani Taliban attacked Bacha Khan University in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 20 students and two teachers and wounding dozens more. The assault, occurring just over a year after the deadly Peshawar school massacre, has renewed fears about the security of educational institutions and the ongoing threat posed by Islamist militants in Pakistan. A teacher and armed guards helped limit the casualties by confronting the attackers, but the incident has highlighted concerns about the effectiveness of Pakistan’s anti-militancy operations and the ongoing vulnerability of students to terrorist violence.

56122_56122.caption: Palestinian family members of Mustafa Aslan 23 mourn his death at their family house north of Jerusalem Aslan was shot by the Israeli army during a raid while searching for the three missing teens
56122_56122.article_context: Israeli authorities confirmed that the bodies of three kidnapped Israeli teenagers were found near Hebron in the West Bank, following a large-scale search operation. Prime Minister Netanyahu accused Hamas of responsibility and vowed retaliation. Tensions have escalated, with increased violence between Israeli forces and militant groups in the Gaza Strip, including airstrikes and rocket attacks. The two main suspects, allegedly Hamas operatives, remain at large. Amid rising hostilities, international calls for restraint have been issued, but the situation remains volatile.

42641_42641.caption: Yazidi sect members rest at a school where they are taking shelter in the Kurdish city of Dahuk
42641_42641.article_context: Iraqi President Fouad Massoum appointed Haider al-Abadi as prime minister, sparking a political crisis as incumbent Nouri al-Maliki refused to step down, claiming the move was unconstitutional. The standoff raised concerns about Iraq’s stability amid ongoing conflict with Islamic State militants. Maliki deployed security forces around government buildings and challenged Abadi’s appointment legally, but lost support within his own political bloc and among international actors, including the U.S., which backed Abadi. Abadi now has 30 days to form a new, more inclusive government, aiming to help quell sectarian tensions and confront Islamist insurgents.

453209_453209.caption: George Galloway who denies the allegations
453209_453209.article_context: A complaint against former Respect MP George Galloway, alleging misuse of parliamentary funds and improper employment of his assistant for personal errands, has been referred to the police by the parliamentary standards authority. The allegations were made by Galloway's ex-assistant, who claims she spent more time on personal tasks than official duties during her tenure. Galloway has denied the accusations and criticized the investigation process, saying he was not informed or given a chance to respond before the case was passed to the Metropolitan Police.

41871_41871.caption: Drivers Al Stachura left and Gary Stoychoff fill up the tank of Americans for Prosperity s Obama s Failing Agenda Tour bus after a rally in front of the Iron Horse Barbeque restaurant in Paragould Ark AFP recruits thousands of volunteers for phone banks and neighborhood canvassing That s different from many of largest conservative political groups which spend their budgets almost exclusively on mass media
41871_41871.article_context: Americans for Prosperity (AFP), a conservative advocacy group funded by the Koch brothers, is spending nearly $1 million in Arkansas state legislative races, aiming to flip the legislature to Republican control for the first time since the Civil War. Despite Arkansas being a safe Republican state in national elections, AFP is focusing on local issues such as opposing tax increases and the implementation of a state health insurance exchange linked to Obamacare. This influx of outside money has intensified competition and spending in state races, prompting Democratic groups to boost their own efforts. AFP's campaign illustrates a growing trend of national interest groups targeting down-ballot races to influence state policy and governance.

39530_39530.caption: Brent Thompson of Dallas Area Rapid Transit another of the slain officers
39530_39530.article_context: During the Dallas police shooting, Mark Hughes was mistakenly identified as a suspect after the police tweeted his photo, prompting a nationwide manhunt. Hughes, who was legally carrying a rifle in accordance with Texas law, quickly surrendered his weapon to police and was questioned before being released. Despite his innocence, the viral photo led to Hughes receiving thousands of death threats, with lawyers and critics highlighting the dangerous consequences of misinformation spread on social media. This incident has drawn comparisons to similar cases where erroneous online speculation has endangered innocent people.

41815_41815.caption: The 73foot fishing vessel Kupreanof is shown here June 10 as it sinks off the coast of Alaska
41815_41815.article_context: The U.S. Coast Guard rescued four men from a sinking 73-foot fishing vessel off the coast of Alaska near Cross Sound and Yakutat Bay. The dramatic rescue, captured on video, shows the men abandoning their ship for a life raft before being hoisted to safety by an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Air Station Sitka. The vessel ultimately sank as the rescue was completed.

44180_44180.caption: Michael A Brown departs the US District Courthouse in Northwest Washington after pleading guilty to a misdemeanor electionlaw violation
44180_44180.article_context: A federal investigation into political corruption in Washington, D.C. has accelerated following former council member Michael A. Brown’s guilty plea to bribery charges. Brown admitted to accepting illegal campaign donations, linking his case to a broader scheme allegedly orchestrated by businessman Jeffrey E. Thompson and consultant Jeanne Clarke Harris, who secretly funneled funds to support several local campaigns, including that of Mayor Vincent C. Gray. The investigation has also reached council member Vincent B. Orange, who has provided documents to prosecutors regarding campaign donations tied to Thompson. While prosecutors have not charged Gray or Thompson, the probe is intensifying, with additional subpoenas and ongoing cooperation from involved parties. The unfolding case highlights systemic violations of D.C. campaign finance laws and continues to place scrutiny on local officials.

49067_49067.caption: Crowds cheer outside the White House
49067_49067.article_context: Army Gen. Raymond 'Tony' Thomas, head of U.S. Special Operations Command, strongly criticized the trend of special operations personnel writing books, participating in movies, and advising video games, saying it damages operational security and runs counter to the ethos of special ops. His remarks follow a high-profile case where Navy SEAL Matt Bissonnette had to forfeit profits from his book about the bin Laden raid for violating disclosure agreements. Thomas warned that this issue affects all branches of special operations, not just SEALs, and called for less publicity moving forward to protect the secrecy vital to their missions. These concerns are echoed by previous commanders, who caution against overexposing elite U.S. forces as their missions continue worldwide.

463924_463924.caption: Protesters stage a sitin as they take part in a demonstration by the Take the Flour Back group in Harpenden Hertfordshire on May 27 2012
463924_463924.article_context: UK Environment Secretary Owen Paterson delivered a speech endorsing the use of GM crops, continuing a long-standing trend of government support for genetically modified food from both current and previous administrations. Despite repeated appeals citing scientific evidence and potential benefits, public opinion in the UK remains strongly opposed to GM technology due to concerns about safety, corporate control, and the perceived unnaturalness of GM foods. Advocates face significant challenges, including media hostility and regulatory barriers, and are advised to rebuild the case for GM crops from the ground up to shift public perception.

43000_43000.caption: German Chancellor Angela Merkel delivers a government policy statement during a session of the German lower house of parliament in October 2012 Germany s GDP for 2011 was 36 trillion It is Europe s largest and healthiest economy and has played a critical role during the eurozone crisis
43000_43000.article_context: China’s official economic data—including trade figures, GDP, and measurements of income inequality—are facing increasing skepticism from global financial institutions and economists amid concerns over their accuracy and transparency. Observers question whether discrepancies are due to statistical challenges in a transitioning economy, deliberate manipulation by the government, or systemic issues in data collection and reporting. The lack of independent verification and disclosure of methodologies exacerbates doubts, with experts warning that unreliable data could lead to poor policy decisions within China and complicate global economic analysis. Despite these challenges, some believe that heightened international scrutiny may push Chinese authorities toward improvements in statistical reporting.

39507_39507.caption: At the Newseum in Washington a view of a memorial for journalists killed while reporting
39507_39507.article_context: In the aftermath of the Arab Spring, hopes for increased press freedom across the Middle East were quickly dashed as governments cracked down on independent journalism, especially in Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt. In Bahrain, peaceful protests were met with harsh repression, including arrests, torture, and legal action against journalists and bloggers, many of whom remain in prison or exile. Saudi Arabia and Egypt similarly tightened laws against dissent, using vague terrorism charges to target reporters and social media activists. State surveillance and censorship have increased, with social media no longer a safe outlet for critical voices, and many journalists have been forced underground or into other professions. Despite these challenges, some, like satirical Bahraini journalist Faisal Hayat, continue to try to report and comment on current events, risking further persecution.

445230_445230.caption: Lord Ashcroft admitted yesterday that he was a nondom who did not pay tax in Britain on his overseas earnings
445230_445230.article_context: Lord Mandelson has accused Conservative deputy chairman Lord Ashcroft of failing to meet the conditions required for his peerage, notably by retaining non-dom tax status despite promising to become a permanent UK resident and taxpayer in 2000. Calls for an independent inquiry into Ashcroft’s tax and residency status have intensified, with Labour alleging he used his wealth to influence elections in the Conservatives’ favor. The House of Lords appointments commission says it cannot investigate retrospectively due to lack of authority, while David Cameron is dismissing the controversy as irrelevant. Ashcroft has now stated he will relinquish his non-dom status to comply with new guidelines for peers.

42945_42945.caption: Delaware Attorney General Beau Biden center stands with other members of his Delaware Army National Guard unit during a deployment ceremony
42945_42945.article_context: Beau Biden, the eldest son of Vice President Joe Biden and former Delaware attorney general, died at age 46 after a prolonged battle with brain cancer. A prominent figure in state and national politics, Beau was seen as a leading candidate for Delaware governor before his illness. He was praised for his public service, military dedication—including service in Iraq—and devotion to family. His passing prompted statements of grief and tribute from both President Obama and Vice President Biden, who highlighted Beau’s character and the personal tragedies the Biden family has endured.

53491_53491.caption: Supporters of Mohamed Morsi attend a sitin near the Rabaa alAdawiya mosque in the Nasr City neighborhood of Cairo
53491_53491.article_context: Violent clashes erupted across Egypt after security forces raided two large camps of supporters of ousted president Mohamed Morsi, resulting in at least 421 deaths—the country's deadliest day since the 2011 uprising. The interim military-backed government declared a state of emergency, and Vice President Mohamed ElBaradei resigned in protest. Hundreds of Muslim Brotherhood members were arrested, and sectarian violence flared with several Christian churches set ablaze. The crackdown marks a return to authoritarian measures, raising international condemnation and concerns about Egypt's path toward democracy.

49448_49448.caption: Members of the Palestinian security forces wait in line to vote at a polling station in the West bank town of Ramallah on Oct 18 2012
49448_49448.article_context: Palestinians in the West Bank began voting in local elections for the first time in six years, with Hebron holding its first municipal vote in 37 years. Despite the historic occasion, many districts lack genuine competition due to uncontested seats and a boycott by Hamas, leaving Fatah expected to dominate. The elections occur amid ongoing political division between Fatah and Hamas, fiscal challenges, and widespread skepticism about the vote's fairness and impact, as some see it as a limited exercise that cannot address the broader demand for Palestinian statehood.

54033_54033.caption: There are 715 million square feet of vacant office space in the DC region much of it piled in office parks
54033_54033.article_context: Suburban office parks in the Washington, D.C. area are experiencing high vacancy rates and declining value, with millions of square feet sitting empty as major tenants like the National Institutes of Health and Marriott International relocate or downsize. This shift is driven by changing work preferences, such as telecommuting and a desire for urban, walkable environments, especially among younger workers. As a result, traditional office parks are becoming 'ghost towns,' symbolizing a broader trend away from car-dependent, isolated workspaces. Although some commercial leasing is up in mid-sized buildings and tech companies are reinventing the office park model in Silicon Valley, the overall appeal of suburban office parks is waning amid evolving workforce and market demands.

52790_52790.caption: Low pressure is going to intensify rapidly over the Northeast this weekend Translation It s going to get cold and it s going to get windy There also may be some snow I m sorry
52790_52790.article_context: A major weather shift is expected in the Northeast this weekend, with a strong cold front bringing cold temperatures, heavy rain, strong winds, and possible snowfall to the region. Parts of Massachusetts, Vermont, and Maine, already suffering from extreme drought, could receive three to four inches of rain. Temperatures will drop sharply, with brisk lows and wind gusts up to 50 mph in higher elevations. The New England mountains may see their first snowfall of the season, with some areas forecasted to receive up to a foot by Monday.

461072_461072.caption: Lord Glasman who has criticised Ed Miliband s leadership for having no strategy no narrative and little energy
461072_461072.article_context: Labour peer Maurice Glasman criticized Labour leader Ed Miliband in a New Statesman article for lacking strategy and energy, prompting a blunt response from John Prescott, who told Glasman to 'bugger off'. This public disagreement has intensified pressure on Miliband as the Labour Party struggles to reconnect with disaffected working-class voters. The article also discusses concerns about the influence of 'gurus' and personalized policy making in politics, questioning whether theoretical ideas from thinkers like Glasman can translate into practical solutions within the current political climate.

40821_40821.caption: Maria Angelica Alvarez 90 a resident of Loma de Cristobal says she worries about gang violence in her neighborhood
40821_40821.article_context: Medellin, once known as the world's murder capital during the height of drug violence in the 1990s, has seen an 80% drop in homicides and become a model for urban transformation through social investment and targeted policing. Despite improvements, violence remains a persistent problem, with fluctuating homicide rates and ongoing extortion and gang activity. Officials worry that these gains are fragile, as gang leaders still exert influence and fear inhibits community cooperation with authorities. The city's progress, built through new schools, public spaces, and infrastructure, faces challenges maintaining security and long-term stability.

451933_451933.caption: The web sometimes covers hundreds of caterpillars and the damage to plants and trees can be severe although they usually recover by the following year
451933_451933.article_context: Hundreds of trees on Jesus Green in Cambridge have been covered in striking cobweb-like webs created by the larvae of the bird-cherry ermine moth. This annual phenomenon, exacerbated this year by weather conditions that reduced predator populations, has led to entire avenues of trees and bushes being stripped bare as caterpillars feed on the leaves within their protective communal silvery webs. Although the damage can appear severe and spooky, experts note that most affected plants and trees typically recover by the following year.

445406_445406.caption: In July 2012 long residue oil was released into the atmosphere from a faulty roof at Essar s Stanlow refinery
445406_445406.article_context: Essar Oil Ltd, operator of the Stanlow oil refinery in Cheshire, has been fined nearly £500,000 after pleading guilty to breaching environmental permit conditions related to two major pollution incidents in 2012. One incident involved an oil tank failure that released oil residue over a large area, affecting local property and prompting significant clean-up efforts. The second incident saw five tonnes of oil enter the Manchester Ship Canal, forcing its temporary closure. The court stated the fine was intended to emphasize the importance of environmental protection, and Essar has since taken measures to improve its operations.

44605_44605.caption: Obama vows to reduce backlog for veterans benefits
44605_44605.article_context: On Veterans Day, President Obama and local officials held ceremonies across Washington, D.C. to honor veterans of America's wars, including a wreath-laying at the Tomb of the Unknowns at Arlington National Cemetery. Obama emphasized the nation's gratitude and pledged never to forget veterans' sacrifices. Mayor Vincent Gray and Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton also paid tribute at the African American Civil War Memorial, highlighting the service of Tuskegee Airmen and advocating for full federal representation for D.C. residents. Veterans and speakers stressed the continuing struggles faced by service members, including the lasting impact of war and the importance of expressing thanks for their service.

42026_42026.caption: A priest attaches a pin which was given to him by former Korean comfort women to the clothes of Pope Francis during the Mass
42026_42026.article_context: Pope Francis sent a message of goodwill to China while flying over its airspace en route to South Korea, marking a rare gesture amid historically strained relations between China and the Vatican. Despite some optimism in Chinese media, Chinese authorities blocked several Chinese Catholics from participating in the Pope’s events in South Korea. Meanwhile, North Korea fired rockets prior to Francis's arrival, signaling further regional tensions. The visit highlights ongoing disputes over religious freedom in China and the difficulties in fostering official diplomatic relations between China and the Vatican.

41965_41965.caption: Rep Darrell Issa RCalif the chairman of the House Oversight Committee questions Internal Revenue Service Commissioner John Koskinen as lawmakers continue their probe of whether tea party groups were improperly targeted for increased scrutiny by the IRS on Capitol Hill in Washington Monday June 23 2014
41965_41965.article_context: The Hatch Act, a law designed to prevent most federal employees from engaging in political activities at work, has recently been in the spotlight due to several high-profile investigations and accusations involving government officials, including former cabinet secretaries Hilda Solis and Kathleen Sebelius. The law, originally enacted in 1939, aims to separate government service from partisan politics and is enforced by the U.S. Office of Special Counsel. Recent violations have involved activities such as soliciting campaign donations and making political statements in an official capacity. As political communication moves increasingly online, more federal workers are being scrutinized for potential Hatch Act breaches, prompting ongoing investigations and debate about political activity limits for government employees.

446263_446263.caption: Behaviour Mammals The Charge by Eric Pierre Eric had been tracking Arctic wolves on Victoria Island Canada when his guide spotted a herd of muskoxen 3 miles away Approaching Eric could see that the herd was nervous probably because wolves were also on its trail He made a detour and stopped about half a mile away upwind Suddenly he realised that the herd was now running towards them oblivious of them I ve seen muskoxen run away says Eric I ve seen them react to a threat by forming a circle and I ve even seen a male charge But I ve never seen a herd spread out into a charging line like this I could hear the thundering of their hooves It was one of those situations where it really mattered that I made the right choice between technical accuracy aesthetics and security
446263_446263.article_context: A selection of winning images from the Wildlife Photographer of the Year awards highlights extraordinary encounters with nature, including Valter Binotto's secretive documentation of endangered Apollo butterflies in Italy, Paul Goldstein's dramatic shot of panicked flamingos at Kenya's Lake Nakuru, Eric Pierre's rare photograph of a charging muskox herd in the Canadian Arctic, and Joel Sartore's image of a mountain goat navigating a precarious ledge in Montana. Other notable photos include Louis-Marie Préau's underwater capture of a European beaver in France, Gregory Basco's artistic portrayal of a gray-headed chachalaca in Costa Rica, and Bob Keller's panoramic of a lichen-covered red alder grove in Oregon. These images showcase both the beauty and vulnerability of wildlife and wild places around the world.

41996_41996.caption: Cuban security forces arrive with Alan Gross outside the courthouse in Havana where he is to stand trial
41996_41996.article_context: The United States and Cuba announced the restoration of diplomatic relations after more than 50 years of hostility, following Cuba’s release of American aid worker Alan Gross. The historic move, enabled by 18 months of secret negotiations and the involvement of Pope Francis and Canada, will include reopening embassies, easing trade and travel restrictions, and reviewing Cuba’s status as a state sponsor of terrorism. The agreement also involved a prisoner swap, with three Cuban spies released in exchange for Gross and an unnamed U.S. intelligence asset held in Cuba. President Obama argued that the decades-long policy of isolation had failed, calling for a new approach, while the initiative drew both praise and sharp criticism from U.S. politicians. The shift is expected to have significant implications for U.S.-Latin American relations and is widely celebrated in Cuba.

41224_41224.caption: Prime Minister Shinzo Abe of Japan and President Obama at the Lincoln Memorial On the discussion agenda are a variety of economic security and global issues including the TransPacific Partnership and climate change
41224_41224.article_context: Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe’s state visit to Washington highlights deepening defense and economic ties between the U.S. and Japan, but is overshadowed by lingering tensions over Japan’s wartime past, particularly the issue of forced sexual slavery known as 'comfort women.' Abe’s ambiguous stance on historical reconciliation has alarmed neighboring countries, especially South Korea, prompting calls for a clear apology. While the visit includes new defense agreements and ongoing trade negotiations, U.S. officials remain wary that unresolved historical disputes may complicate regional diplomacy and efforts to counterbalance China’s influence in Asia.

460200_460200.caption: Signal crayfishWhy is it dangerous It s 30 years since the American signal crayfish was introduced into Britain for aquaculture purposes It is a fastgrowing aggressive and voracious species which has few natural predators once it reaches maturity It has had a huge impact on the ecosystems it has colonised so farMore information bitlyobservercrayfishWhere to report your sighting nonnativespeciesorgrecordingWhen to spot it All year
460200_460200.article_context: A range of invasive non-native species have become established across Britain, including the signal crayfish, grey squirrel, muntjac deer, ring-necked parakeet, red-eared terrapin, harlequin ladybird, horse-chestnut leaf-miner, rhododendron, floating pennywort, and Himalayan balsam. These species have caused significant ecological impacts, such as outcompeting or preying on native wildlife, damaging trees, altering watercourses, and threatening biodiversity. Authorities and organizations are monitoring and encouraging public reporting of sightings to track and manage their spread.

40889_40889.caption: Adye Sunday 25 who was abducted by the Lord s Resistance Army when she was 13 prepares food to sell at a center set up to help those who have left or fled the LRA in Gulu Uganda Adye Sunday who was forced to be among Joseph Kony s dozens of wives and says he s also the father of her two children is nt sure how she feels about the calls to kill or capture Kony
40889_40889.article_context: The joint Ugandan-American search for Joseph Kony, the infamous leader of the Lord’s Resistance Army responsible for mass abductions and atrocities, has been suspended due to political upheaval in the Central African Republic, where Kony is believed to be hiding. Recent rebel activity has led to the Central African Republic's government being overthrown, and cooperation with foreign troops halted. Although American and Ugandan forces will remain in the region for now, operations are on hold until stability returns, raising international concern that Kony and the weakened LRA may regroup and resume attacks. The US also announced a $5 million reward for information on Kony and two other LRA leaders, reaffirming its commitment to pursuing them despite the suspension.

40427_40427.caption: Duterte happy to slaughter drug addicts like Hitler massacred Jews
40427_40427.article_context: Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte defended the deaths of innocent people during his aggressive war on drugs, referring to them as 'collateral damage' rather than criminal acts or negligence. In a recent interview, he insisted that the killings were a result of law enforcement defending themselves and justified his harsh stance as necessary to combat the country's drug problems. Duterte dismissed criticism from international leaders and human rights groups, frequently responding with controversial and profane remarks. Over 3,000 people have died since the start of his campaign, and Duterte indicated that only some of the deaths will be investigated. He rejected the idea of focusing resources on rehabilitation, instead promoting fear as a deterrent to crime.

460191_460191.caption: RhododendronWhy Victorian plant explorers were constantly hunting for new species of rhododendron in the foothills of the Himalayas The pinkflowered species has since invaded many woods shading out native plants and hosting a fungus that kills some forestry and native treesMore information bitlyobserverrhodendronReport to nonnativespeciesorgrecordingWhen to spot it All year
460191_460191.article_context: Several invasive non-native species, including the American signal crayfish, grey squirrel, muntjac deer, ring-necked parakeet, red-eared terrapin, harlequin ladybird, horse-chestnut leaf-miner, rhododendron, floating pennywort, and Himalayan balsam, are spreading across Britain and raising concerns about their negative impacts on native wildlife and ecosystems. These species, introduced through human activity or accidental release, out-compete or harm native fauna and flora, causing ecological imbalance. Authorities and scientists are monitoring their effects and encouraging the public to report sightings to help manage their spread.

39189_39189.caption: Top US general says troops could be redeployed in Iraq
39189_39189.article_context: President Obama’s top national security advisers have recommended increasing U.S. military involvement in Iraq and Syria by placing a limited number of Special Operations forces on the ground and moving American advisers closer to combat zones, signaling concern over stalled progress against the Islamic State. These measures, which still require Obama’s approval, would mark a significant escalation but stop short of direct combat roles for U.S. troops. The recommendations reflect frustration with the current strategy and a push by Defense Secretary Ashton Carter for more aggressive options, following setbacks such as the fall of Ramadi. While the proposed changes focus mainly on bolstering local partner forces and targeting Islamic State resources, broader actions like no-fly zones were ruled out due to risks of direct conflict with Syrian, Russian, or Iranian forces. Similar discussions are ongoing for continued U.S. troop presence in Afghanistan, aiming to counter extremist groups despite persistent local instability.

49438_49438.caption: Former cricketer Imran Khan accompanied by his wife Jemima wipes his face during the funeral of Diana Princess of Wales at London s Westminster Abbey
49438_49438.article_context: Imran Khan, a popular Pakistani politician and former cricket star, plans to lead a large rally into South Waziristan to protest U.S. CIA drone strikes, which he says have caused civilian casualties. Despite winning significant public support for his anti-drone stance, Khan’s planned march faces obstacles from Pakistan’s military, which controls access to the volatile tribal area, and security concerns from both local authorities and the Pakistani Taliban. While the army claims the decision lies with the civilian government, the march has sparked debate over governance, security, and anti-American sentiment in Pakistan. Critics argue the rally is a risky publicity stunt, but Khan asserts it is meant to draw attention to the impact of drone attacks on civilians.

48856_48856.caption: Imran Khan a cricket legend and chairman of Pakistan s Movement for Justice party addresses supporters during a campaign stop in Murree
48856_48856.article_context: In the lead-up to Pakistan’s national elections, violent attacks—including deadly bombings—have targeted both liberal and Islamist politicians, resulting in at least 18 deaths on Tuesday and around 100 killed since April. The election, expected to be a landmark democratic transition, is described as the bloodiest in Pakistan’s history due to militant efforts—primarily by the Pakistani Taliban—to disrupt the democratic process and threaten voters. Security forces are being heavily deployed to protect polling stations. Despite the threats and violence, most parties are continuing their campaigns, and there is widespread public support for participating in the election as a path forward for democracy in Pakistan.

43113_43113.caption: Jonathan Butler center who went on a hunger strike to protest the treatment of African Americans on campus talks to Concerned Student 1950 supporters during the We Are Not Afraid march
43113_43113.article_context: At the University of Missouri, a wave of racial incidents and ongoing frustration among black students culminated in a campus movement that gained national attention, particularly following the 2014 shooting of Michael Brown in nearby Ferguson. Tensions peaked when graduate student Jonathan Butler began a hunger strike demanding the resignation of university president Tim Wolfe, citing the administration's lack of response to racial concerns. Approximately 30 black football players joined Butler's protest, pledging not to play or practice until Wolfe stepped down. Their involvement rapidly intensified pressure, and Wolfe resigned within days. The protest, driven by the activist group 'Concerned Student 1950,' highlighted systemic racism and spurred calls for increased minority representation and support on campus. Subsequently, the university appointed Michael A. Middleton, a black interim president, signaling a commitment to continued progress on racial issues.

462199_462199.caption: A Greenpeace activist dressed as a brinjal protests in Bangalore India
462199_462199.article_context: This week’s major news centered on India’s decision regarding the introduction of genetically modified aubergines, which sparked intense debate about environmental impact, food system control, and farmer support. Other key topics included positive reactions to Tesla’s Roadster Sport, highlighting the growth and missed opportunities in electric car technology, and the US government's approval of a national climate monitoring information service. Additionally, there was notable discussion on India’s large-scale investment in solar power as part of its National Solar Mission.

461468_461468.caption: Ieuan Wyn Jones outgoing leader of Plaid Cymru
461468_461468.article_context: Ieuan Wyn Jones, outgoing leader of Plaid Cymru, will use his final conference speech to urge the nationalist party to broaden its appeal and become more inclusive, targeting people who have never voted Plaid before. After disappointing election results and losing seats to the Conservatives, Jones criticizes Labour’s governance and argues Plaid must lead Wales’s continued journey toward greater autonomy and self-confidence. He reflects on Plaid’s achievements in coalition government, acknowledges shortcomings in communicating their successes, and calls for Wales to gain further powers and build national confidence.

43751_43751.caption: Syrians clear the rubble of a house that was destroyed in a government airstrike Saturday in Kal Jubrin on the outskirts of Aleppo
43751_43751.article_context: In Cambodia, large-scale land disputes have sparked public anger towards Chinese investors, who are involved in numerous redevelopment and infrastructure projects across the country. Most notably, thousands of residents in Phnom Penh's Boeung Kak Lake district faced eviction due to a Chinese-financed real estate development that transformed the city's biggest lake into a barren sand-filled area. Protests led by local activists such as Tep Vanny have drawn attention to forced evictions and inadequate compensation, resulting in international criticism and temporary suspension of World Bank lending to Cambodia. While Chinese investment has brought significant infrastructure improvements and jobs, it has also caused the displacement of hundreds of thousands, fueling social unrest and highlighting the tension between economic growth and human rights.

50322_50322.caption: Syrian President Bashar Assad shown on Aug 31 in Damascus is said to be confident that the US and its allies will soon seek his partnership in an international coalition against terrorism
50322_50322.article_context: Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, who recently declared victory in Syria’s civil war, faces growing challenges to his rule despite continued support from Iran and Russia. The U.S. has rejected Assad’s appeals for partnership against Islamic State militants, who have recently inflicted military defeats on the Syrian army and heightened discontent within Assad’s core Alawite base, many of whom are frustrated by ongoing losses and heavy casualties. While Assad still holds power and his opposition is divided, fatigue and resentment are rising among his supporters, and U.S. policy remains focused on backing moderate rebels rather than cooperating with his regime. The conflict appears to be entering a new and potentially more dangerous phase as both international and domestic pressures on Assad increase.

453114_453114.caption: The amendment to the energy bill would stop landlords from renting out homes that fell into the worst two bands of energy efficiency
453114_453114.article_context: The UK government has announced new measures requiring landlords to improve the energy efficiency of the country's least efficient rented homes, or face being banned from letting them out. An amendment to the energy bill will prevent landlords from renting properties in the two lowest energy efficiency bands (F and G) from 2018, impacting around 680,000 homes. From 2016, landlords must also accept reasonable requests from tenants for energy efficiency improvements, with funding available through the government's 'green deal' loan scheme. While campaigners welcomed the move, they argued implementation is too slow and criticized the bill for not offering stronger protections for tenants who request upgrades.

51123_51123.caption: Aid delivered to Yazidis hiding in Iraqi mountains
51123_51123.article_context: As Kurdish forces fought ISIS in northern Iraq, former Iraqi foreign minister Hoshyar Zebari discussed the crisis in an interview. He revealed that Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki was close to staging a coup to remain in power, but military and Shiite militia neutrality, along with Iranian support for the new government, eased tensions and improved prospects for political transition. Zebari praised U.S. airstrikes for halting ISIS advances and boosting Kurdish pesh merga morale. He emphasized urgent needs for more military aid and advisers, and stressed that defeating ISIS and forming a new government were immediate priorities, even as Kurdish aspirations for independence were set aside due to the existential threat posed by ISIS.

44337_44337.caption: A picture of Michael Brown can be seen in the lobby of Friendly Temple Missionary Baptist Church before his funeral
44337_44337.article_context: The aftermath of Michael Brown's shooting in Ferguson sparked a notable shift in the feminist movement, with white feminists beginning to address issues of race and police conduct more directly. This shift was observed by activists and scholars who noted that while black women have long viewed race and gender as inseparable, white feminists historically prioritized gender.
