The military, wary of escalating tensions and past coups, has urged a negotiated settlement to avoid further instability. While Sharif has signaled willingness to engage in dialogue, Khan refuses talks unless Sharif steps down. Despite some outbreaks of violence and disruptions in the capital, most other political and religious leaders, along with international actors, are calling for peaceful negotiations to resolve the standoff.

40046_40046.caption: Chavez supporters react to the announcement of his death outside his hospital in Caracas
40046_40046.article_context: The death of Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez evoked strong, divided reactions, with many poor Venezuelans mourning his passing due to the social welfare policies he championed, while exiles and critics celebrated the end of his autocratic rule. World leaders and Latin American presidents offered tributes, recognizing his role in promoting regional integration, while critics highlighted his economic mismanagement and concentration of power. Chavez's death marks a significant turning point for Venezuela and its allies, many of which relied heavily on subsidized oil, leaving the future uncertain. The country is set to hold new elections soon, as mandated by its constitution, with international statements calling for respect for democracy and human rights as Venezuela enters a new era.

471815_471815.caption: David Cameron has not submitted details of his plans for reform and repatriation of powers
471815_471815.article_context: EU leaders have decided not to discuss Britain's proposed EU referendum or its demands at Thursday's summit, expressing frustration at Prime Minister David Cameron's lack of clear, written negotiating demands. While Cameron seeks to renegotiate the UK's EU membership terms before holding an in/out referendum, negotiations have been slow as the UK has not specified its requirements. As a result, substantive talks are now expected to take place at the December summit, with the referendum likely pushed to the summer or autumn of next year. The discussions are expected to intensify in the coming months, moving from technical to higher-level political negotiations.

50943_50943.caption: Volodymyr Bilobrov 26 a truck driver has spent 98 days in Kiev s Independence Square
50943_50943.article_context: Pro-Russian activists in eastern Ukraine, particularly in Kharkiv and Donetsk, have posed significant challenges to the country’s new pro-Western government, staging large rallies, demanding regional autonomy, and engaging in violent clashes with pro-Kiev supporters. These confrontations have resulted in fatalities and injuries, prompting Russia to threaten intervention, citing the need to protect ethnic Russians. While pro-Moscow groups claim persecution by nationalist elements, local officials and police say such threats are exaggerated and much of the violence appears tied to local political interests and criminal groups. Despite divisions between pro-Russian and pro-Ukrainian citizens, local leaders like Kharkiv’s mayor now affirm the city’s status as part of Ukraine, reflecting complicated regional loyalties and the tense atmosphere following Russia’s annexation of Crimea.

56230_56230.caption: Civilians fleeing the siege of Fallujah face grim future
56230_56230.article_context: The battle for the Syrian city of Manbij has stretched into its second month, with U.S.-backed Syrian Democratic Forces encircling the city and fighting to push out Islamic State fighters. Despite significant gains, ISIS is fiercely holding onto a key cluster of reinforced concrete grain silos at the city's southern edge, using snipers, mines, and tunnels to resist advances. This stubborn defense has drawn comparisons to the Battle of Stalingrad, highlighting ISIS’s determination to retain strategic positions. The outcome is significant, as Manbij has served as a crucial hub for ISIS operations, and its liberation is being touted as evidence that the U.S. strategy in Syria is making progress.

43007_43007.caption: Rescued dogs from a South Korean dogmeat farm are transported to the United States to be adopted
43007_43007.article_context: More than 30 dogs bred for meat on an unlicensed farm in South Korea were rescued by Humane Society International and temporarily housed at a Rockville, Maryland shelter before continuing to no-kill shelters in North Carolina for adoption. The rescue is part of ongoing efforts by the organization to shut down dog farms in South Korea, where the dog meat industry is declining, and provide better futures for these animals. Since 2014, over 500 dogs have been relocated to new homes across the United States as a result of these campaigns.

461758_461758.caption: Alex Salmond addresses the SNP conference in Inverness The Scottish people will set the agenda for the future he said
461758_461758.article_context: Scottish First Minister Alex Salmond used his keynote speech at the SNP annual conference to assert that Scotland's future will not be dictated by Westminster, emphasizing that the Scottish people will determine their own constitutional fate. Salmond highlighted the SNP's historic election victory as a mandate for an upcoming independence referendum, pledging a campaign to endorse Scotland's Claim of Right. He criticized the UK government's Scotland bill as inadequate and accused Westminster of disrespecting Scottish interests, particularly regarding energy policy and North Sea oil revenues. Salmond reiterated the call for greater powers for Scotland and reaffirmed the SNP's commitment to allowing Scots to choose their own path, including the option of full independence.

451700_451700.caption: Mining lorries carry loads of tar sands in Alberta Canada One climate scientist warned that it would be game over for efforts to stop global warming if Canada s tar sands were fully exploited
451700_451700.article_context: The Church of England has divested £12 million from tar sands oil and thermal coal companies, marking its first investment restrictions due to climate change. This decision is part of a broader moral responsibility to protect vulnerable communities from global warming. The move, celebrated by environmental campaigners, sets new limits on investments and signals a shift towards a low-carbon economy. While the church continues to engage with oil and gas majors like Shell and BP, it makes clear that failure to achieve meaningful change could lead to further divestment. The announcement reflects a strengthened climate policy, aiming to lead institutional investors in addressing environmental and social justice concerns.

43105_43105.caption: New satellite images show objects about 1600 miles from Perth Australia The images mark the fourth set of data from satellites showing objects that may have come from the plane drifting in the remote waters of the southern Indian Ocean
43105_43105.article_context: The search for missing Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 continued into its fourth week, with increased international efforts involving planes and ships scanning a new search area in the Indian Ocean. Aircraft spotted floating objects that could be debris, but they have not yet been confirmed as related to the flight. The search area shifted northeast after new analysis indicated the plane traveled faster and likely ran out of fuel sooner. The teams are racing against time to locate the critical black box before its signals expire. Meanwhile, Chinese relatives of the passengers arrived in Malaysia seeking answers, expressing frustration with the investigation's progress.

53207_53207.caption: Ontheground reporting from Iraq as Kurdish forces fight the Islamic State
53207_53207.article_context: Kurdish peshmerga forces, backed by U.S.-led airstrikes and including Yazidi fighters, launched a major offensive to retake the northern Iraqi city of Sinjar from Islamic State militants. The assault began at dawn with about 7,500 fighters advancing in a three-pronged attack, aiming to cut the highway linking the Islamic State's territories in Iraq and Syria. The operation represents the largest Kurdish-led offensive against ISIS and is a critical effort to disrupt the group's supply lines. U.S. and British advisers are supporting the mission, while coalition airstrikes target militant positions. The offensive follows devastation in the Yazidi community after Sinjar's capture by ISIS in 2014, and success in Sinjar would be a significant blow to the militant group's regional control.

41829_41829.caption: Ramirez and Roa talk to termite inspector Rich Dooly right after he inspected their home Hundreds of toy figures are placed on a shelf as part of Ramirez s toy collection
41829_41829.article_context: The approval of same-sex marriage by popular vote in Maryland, Maine, and Washington is expected to provide an economic boost to the wedding industry in those states, as more same-sex couples will seek to hold weddings and related events locally. Maryland-based officiants and wedding service providers anticipate an increase in business, with some planning for significantly more ceremonies. However, some businesses focused exclusively on same-sex weddings have struggled due to smaller budgets and limited clientele, with at least one choosing to close despite the expanded market. The development is seen as both a milestone for gay rights and a potential new market for wedding-related services.

47957_47957.caption: NBCUniversal severed ties with Trump saying At NBC respect and dignity for all people are cornerstones of our values Due to the recent derogatory statements by Donald Trump regarding immigrants NBCUniversal is ending its business relationship with Mr Trump
47957_47957.article_context: Donald Trump, facing heavy criticism over his comments describing illegal immigrants as 'rapists' and criminals, asserted he will win the Latino vote in the 2016 presidential election. Despite backlash from businesses and celebrities—including chef Jose Andres canceling a restaurant deal and several organizations cutting ties with Trump—he claimed to have good relationships with legal immigrants working on his Washington hotel project, many of whom are from Central America. Protests and further criticism from various groups and officials continue to mount in response to his remarks.

54995_54995.caption: During the earthquake bricks fell from a building on Old Georgetown Road in Vienna Va smashing these vehicles
54995_54995.article_context: On August 23, 2011, a rare 5.8-magnitude earthquake struck the Washington, D.C. region, causing initial panic and widespread evacuations but resulting in few injuries and no fatalities. Notable damage occurred to major landmarks, including the Washington National Cathedral and the Washington Monument, both of which required extensive and costly repairs. The quake's epicenter was in Mineral, Virginia, which also suffered significant damage, including the destruction of its high school. Scientists have continued to study the unlikely event, which challenged assumptions about seismic activity in the region. While the earthquake left a physical and financial impact, its memory has largely faded, becoming more a subject of local anecdotes and humor than lasting trauma.

52575_52575.caption: Turkish soldiers stand guard as Syrian refugees carry their belongings at the border in Suruc Turkey late Saturday September 20 2014
52575_52575.article_context: The number of Syrian refugees fleeing to Turkey from Islamic State advances near the town of Kobane reached 100,000 in less than a week, with most being ethnic Kurds. Heavy fighting between Islamic State militants and Kurdish fighters has driven people from their homes, and Turkish authorities are preparing for an even larger influx. The Turkish government has closed some border crossings to prevent Kurdish fighters from crossing into Syria, leading to clashes with protesters at the border. The U.N. has called for increased international support as Turkey faces mounting humanitarian needs.

40780_40780.caption: A Romanian Cugir semiautomatic rifle with a large scope is shown inside the abandoned 1998 Honda Accord belonging Oscar OrtegaHernandez
40780_40780.article_context: Washington Post reporter Carol Leonnig won the Pulitzer Prize for national reporting after her months-long investigation revealed serious security lapses within the Secret Service, including incidents where armed individuals entered or approached the White House and failures in responding to attacks. Her coverage led to sweeping leadership changes at the agency, including the resignation of its director. Other notable Pulitzer winners included The New York Times for coverage of the Ebola crisis, the Los Angeles Times, The Post and Courier for reporting on domestic abuse, and others recognized for their work in criticism, photography, and investigative journalism.

44658_44658.caption: Washington taxi drivers park their cars on Pennsylvania Avenue to protest ridesharing services The onslaught of services such as Uber and Lyft has fostered a new spirit of cooperation in the taxi industry
44658_44658.article_context: Faced with the rapid growth of ride-share services like Uber and Lyft, traditional taxi companies and drivers in the Washington region are uniting in unprecedented ways to advocate for stricter regulations on their new competitors. Taxi drivers, cab companies, and unions are collaborating on lobbying efforts, legal challenges, and public protests, arguing that ride-share companies enjoy an unfair advantage by operating under fewer rules. Some regulatory victories have been achieved, such as a Maryland ruling requiring Uber to obtain a state permit, though other jurisdictions have allowed ride-shares more leeway. The taxi industry is also pushing to modernize by adopting new technologies and organizing drivers, while emphasizing the need for fair competition and improved working conditions as they adapt to a changing transportation landscape.

41941_41941.caption: Antigovernment protesters rest during a massive demonstration outside the presidential palace in Cairo
41941_41941.article_context: Supporters of Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, largely comprised of the Muslim Brotherhood, rallied near Cairo’s presidential palace, claiming a duty to defend both the building and Morsi himself from opposition protesters. Tensions between the two sides have led to violent clashes, with allegations of beatings and interrogations against opposition protesters by Morsi’s supporters. While the Brotherhood’s political party denies any use of violence, its members describe their actions as protecting the legitimacy of Egypt’s revolution and upcoming constitutional referendum. The group sees itself as the rightful guardian of Egypt’s democratic process, portraying opposition forces as being disruptive and linked to the old Mubarak regime.

40328_40328.caption: The coffin containing Nelson Mandela arrives in his home town of Qunu
40328_40328.article_context: During Nelson Mandela’s memorial service, a sign language interpreter named Thamsanqa Jantjie was exposed as a fake, drawing widespread criticism from the deaf community and professional interpreters. Jantjie, who admitted to suffering from schizophrenia and hearing voices, failed to convey any real sign language, instead making nonsensical gestures. It was later revealed he was hired by a company that has since disappeared and his qualifications were questionable. South African officials apologized and launched an investigation into the incident, which overshadowed the solemn tribute to Mandela and raised concerns about security and respect for the deaf community.

463335_463335.caption: A couple wades through the flooded town centre of Uckfield in East Sussex October 2000
463335_463335.article_context: The article discusses recent claims by Al Gore that scientists have clear proof of climate change causing extreme weather events, such as floods and droughts. The author, a climate scientist involved in event attribution studies, clarifies that while it is possible to estimate how human-driven climate change affects the probability of specific events, actual scientific analyses have only been conducted for a few cases, often with nuanced or uncertain results. Some extreme events have been linked to increased risk from human influence, while others have not, and in some cases risks have even been reduced. The article emphasizes that current scientific capabilities focus on quantifying changes in risk, not proving direct causation for individual events, and warns against overstating what the evidence shows.

41655_41655.caption: Mark Stephen Love escaped from handcuffs in the back of a police cruiser
41655_41655.article_context: Mark Stephen Love, a 24-year-old man, escaped from a police cruiser in Prince William County after being arrested for unauthorized use of a vehicle. Love managed to free one hand from his handcuffs and flee from the back seat of the patrol car, remaining at large for a day before being recaptured at a home in Woodbridge with the help of a K-9 unit and helicopter. He now faces multiple charges, including felony escape from custody, and is being held without bond pending a July hearing. The police department is conducting an internal review of the incident.

466215_466215.caption: MPs expenses the inquiry bill is the latest financial blow to the taxpayer from cleaning up the system that was operating at Westminster
466215_466215.article_context: The police investigation into abuses of parliamentary expenses has cost UK taxpayers over £840,000 so far, with up to 13 officers involved since the scandal emerged in 2009. Several former MPs and a peer have been convicted, and further cases are still being examined. The final cost could surpass £1 million, adding to the financial burden caused by the widespread misuse of the parliamentary expenses system. Despite attempts at reform, the expense of overseeing and processing MPs' claims remains high.

458258_458258.caption: Jack Straw argues that the bill introducing the referendum is being coupled unnecessarily with gerrymandering boundary changes
458258_458258.article_context: The Labour shadow cabinet has decided to oppose the government's bill that combines a referendum on the Alternative Vote (AV) system with constituency boundary changes and a reduction in the number of MPs. This move increases the likelihood that the coalition government could face defeat in Parliament over one of its key policies. Labour supports an AV referendum in principle but objects to the linking of voting reform with boundary changes, which they claim would unfairly benefit the Conservatives. Significant opposition also exists within the Conservative Party, particularly regarding the proposed date for the referendum coinciding with local elections. The situation has raised the prospect of a Tory-Labour alliance blocking the bill, potentially causing a significant setback for the coalition government.

55577_55577.caption: A fighter from the Sadik unit of Free Syrian Army s Tahrir al Sham brigade prepares to throw a hand grenade at Syrian soldiers in Mleha suburb of Damascus
55577_55577.article_context: A volunteer-run recovery center in Reyhanli, Turkey, near the Syrian border, is treating a growing number of Syrians who have been paralyzed by injuries from the ongoing civil war, many caused by snipers and explosions. While some patients recover and move on, those with severe spinal injuries—including children, women, and fighters—face prolonged stays due to lack of accessible housing and support. The center, funded by donations, has seen the number of paralyzed patients rise from three to 22 and regularly turns away new cases due to limited capacity. Most patients struggle with uncertainty about their future, separation from families, and limited prospects for reintegration, highlighting the long-term humanitarian challenges caused by the war.

40100_40100.caption: Bernie Sanders I will help Hillary Clinton become the next president
40100_40100.article_context: Bernie Sanders publicly endorsed Hillary Clinton at a rally in New Hampshire, pledging to support her bid for the presidency and emphasizing the importance of uniting to defeat Republican nominee Donald Trump. While both candidates expressed praise for each other and called for party unity, there were visible signs of lingering tensions among Sanders supporters. Sanders highlighted his continued commitment to progressive issues and acknowledged policy concessions Clinton had made to appeal to his base. Although Sanders will not formally exit the race before the Democratic convention, his endorsement marks a significant step toward party consolidation as the general election approaches.

42429_42429.caption: Vice President Biden kisses the head of University of Colorado sophomore Emma Beach in April after hearing her speak as part of the It s On Us campaign about sexual violence on campus
42429_42429.article_context: The Obama administration, led by President Obama and Vice President Biden, has undertaken a major effort to address sexual assault on college campuses through stricter federal oversight, advocacy campaigns, and changes in disciplinary procedures. Their approach includes withholding federal funds from institutions deemed insufficiently serious about tackling sexual misconduct and launching the nationwide 'It’s On Us' public-awareness initiative. These measures have led to increased reporting of campus sexual assaults and the adoption of less stringent evidentiary standards for adjudicating cases, sparking controversy and concerns over due process. The administration’s policy is rooted in civil rights protections under Title IX, with ongoing debates over the fairness and legal authority of federal guidance.

43937_43937.caption: People take part in a rally in Donetsk that marks the victory of the Dombass region against fascism in World War II
43937_43937.article_context: Fighting erupted near Donetsk airport in eastern Ukraine, violating the eight-day cease-fire, as Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of seeking to destroy Ukraine and called for NATO membership as a safeguard against further aggression. Despite sporadic cease-fire breaches, government forces still hold the airport while separatists control the city. Deaths were reported on both sides, and Russian humanitarian aid convoys continue entering the region. Tensions persist following Russia's annexation of Crimea, with Ukraine and Western allies accusing Moscow of backing pro-Russian rebels, though Russia denies direct involvement.

40709_40709.caption: LIBYA BENGHAZI March 2 2011 153056 The now destroyed nasser statue constructed in honor of the former egyptian president FROM THE BOOK LIBYAN SUGAR
40709_40709.article_context: In 2011, photographer Michael Christopher Brown left China to document the war in Libya, despite having no prior conflict experience. After breaking his camera, he used an iPhone to capture images of the conflict, an experience that deeply affected him and led to his book 'Libyan Sugar.' The book combines war photography and personal reflection, including Brown’s correspondence with loved ones and details about surviving a shrapnel injury in Misrata. Brown’s decision to document the war was influenced by his family’s history of military service and his identification with the values of the Arab Spring. While Brown survived, fellow journalists Tim Hetherington and Chris Hondros lost their lives in Libya.

45782_45782.caption: French police forces and forensic officers stand next to the truck involved in the attack
45782_45782.article_context: On Bastille Day in Nice, France, a truck plowed into a crowd celebrating the holiday, killing at least 84 people and injuring many others, including children. The driver, a French-Tunisian man known to police for petty crimes, also fired on the crowd before being shot dead by police. Authorities described the attack as a deliberate act of terrorism, and France extended its state of emergency while announcing three days of national mourning. The attack drew international condemnation and renewed concerns about terrorism in France and Europe, coming after several other major terror incidents in the region.

455965_455965.caption: Vince Cable has condemned multinational companies that use tax avoidance techniques
455965_455965.article_context: UK Business Secretary Vince Cable called Starbucks 'tax dodgers' and expressed understanding for consumer boycotts over the company's tax avoidance practices. Starbucks, along with Amazon and Google, faced criticism from parliament's public accounts committee and HMRC for using accounting tactics to pay minimal tax in Britain. The outcry has led Starbucks to arrange a meeting with HMRC regarding its tax bill, while other ministers and officials highlighted growing public pressure and consumer action as driving companies to address their tax affairs.

40493_40493.caption: Cuban President Raul Castro and President Obama shake hands as they head to the opening ceremony Summit of the Americas
40493_40493.article_context: President Obama and Cuban President Raúl Castro held a historic meeting during the Summit of the Americas in Panama, marking a symbolic end to over 50 years of official estrangement between the United States and Cuba. Both leaders expressed willingness to build a 'new relationship' and to reopen embassies in Havana and Washington, although concrete dates were not set. Obama emphasized honest discussion about differences, particularly on human rights, while Castro acknowledged disagreements but stressed patience. The encounter is viewed as a significant shift for U.S.-Latin American relations and a potential legacy achievement for Obama's presidency. The summit also featured strong speeches from regional leaders, including Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro, who criticized U.S. policies but called for dialogue.

465963_465963.caption: Shadow chancellor John McDonnell spoke out in his first newspaper interview since his controversial appointment
465963_465963.article_context: Newly appointed shadow chancellor John McDonnell sharply criticized George Osborne’s economic policies as 'immoral' for harming the poorest, and outlined a radical leftwing plan for the UK economy in his first major interview. McDonnell—backed by Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn—advocated for sweeping democratic involvement in Labour policymaking, including renationalising industries like railways and Royal Mail, and reassessing roles of key government institutions. He dismissed claims of being a 'deficit denier,' promising fiscal responsibility without targeting low or middle earners, and derided Osborne’s budget surplus plan. Despite internal changes, polls show the Conservatives maintain a lead over Labour and that public support for Corbyn’s leadership remains limited.

43838_43838.caption: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is seen on a screen as he addresses the media from the London embassy of Ecuador where he has beenfor some 312 years to avoid extradition to Sweden for questioning about alleged sexual offenses
43838_43838.article_context: A U.N. panel declared that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is being 'arbitrarily detained' in the Ecuadorian Embassy in London, a decision Assange hailed as a victory. However, the panel's opinion was not unanimous: one member, Vladimir Tochilovsky, dissented, arguing that Assange was not detained but was instead self-confining to avoid arrest and that his situation falls outside the panel's mandate. Tochilovsky’s dissent has been supported by several British legal experts, who view the majority decision as misguided. The panel’s finding is not legally binding but has generated significant debate about international law and human rights.

45250_45250.caption: As a naval officer during the Vietnam War Kerry
45250_45250.article_context: The Senate failed to pass an international treaty supporting the rights of the disabled, but the debate highlighted Senator John Kerry's diplomatic skills and vision, positioning him as a leading contender to succeed Hillary Clinton as Secretary of State. Kerry, who chairs the Foreign Relations Committee and is widely respected across party lines, is seen as a preferable choice over U.N. Ambassador Susan Rice, whose potential nomination has drawn criticism linked to the Benghazi incident. The White House is expected to announce Cabinet nominations soon, and Kerry's renewed commitment to the Senate has earned him bipartisan support, making him a strong candidate for a top diplomatic role.

42031_42031.caption: Paige Comstock Cunningham helped pioneer an approach to fighting abortion that emphasizes protecting women from harm You ca nt just focus on the child and not on the mother and her needs she says
42031_42031.article_context: The Supreme Court is set to hear its most significant abortion case in decades, focusing on a Texas law that imposes strict regulations on abortion clinics and doctors—requirements framed by antiabortion activists as measures to protect women’s health. This reflects a shift in antiabortion strategy from prioritizing fetal rights to emphasizing alleged harms abortion poses to women, a focus that has influenced laws enacted in numerous states. Abortion rights groups argue these regulations are unnecessary and intended to restrict access, noting abortion’s safety and criticizing what they see as a patronizing approach. While the Supreme Court debates whether scientific evidence must support such laws, the antiabortion movement is simultaneously renewing efforts centered on fetal rights. The outcome of the case could have major implications for abortion access nationwide.

442469_442469.caption: Local choir members wear Tshirts with Save Our Rhinos slogan perform during the World Wildlife Day celebration at the Kruger national park in Mpumalanga South Africa
442469_442469.article_context: Recent wildlife and environmental photographs highlight both the beauty and crisis facing global nature. Key events include the impact of climate change accelerating ecological catastrophes like beetle plagues in Honduras and coastal erosion in Costa Rica, the mass stranding of 337 sei whales in Chile, conservation efforts for endangered species in China, Sri Lanka and Mexico, and actions against illegal wildlife trade in Indonesia. The images also celebrate milestones such as the world’s oldest tracked bird, a Laysan albatross named Wisdom, returning to Hawaii to lay an egg and mark International Cheetah Day, while emphasizing ongoing threats to biodiversity worldwide.

41109_41109.caption: Police take a man into custody a block away from the early morning siege in the SaintDenis neighborhood
41109_41109.article_context: Abdelhamid Abaaoud, identified as the mastermind behind the Paris attacks, was killed in a police raid north of Paris. Abaaoud, a Belgian of Moroccan descent and senior Islamic State operative, had been able to move in and out of Europe undetected, highlighting serious security concerns. He had longstanding ties with several attackers from the Paris incident and was linked to multiple previous terror plots in Europe. French officials confirmed his death after a seven-hour siege, during which a woman also detonated a suicide device and eight others were arrested.

458680_458680.caption: Clayton ThomasMuller of the Indigenous Environmental Network at a protest outside the BP annual general meeting at the ExCel Centre in London
458680_458680.article_context: At BP's annual general meeting in London, activists protested against the company, accusing it of inadequately addressing the aftermath of the Gulf of Mexico oil spill and criticizing its use of the dispersant Corexit, which they say poses ongoing environmental and health risks. Protesters also condemned BP's involvement in Canadian tar sands mining, citing environmental destruction and violations of indigenous rights, and called for the company to withdraw from these operations. BP defended its record, citing significant spending on cleanup, compensation, and scientific research to mitigate future spills.

42461_42461.caption: Dick Van Dyke heads to the stage before introducing presidential candidate Bernie Sanders at a rally at Santa Monica High School on May 23
42461_42461.article_context: Dick Van Dyke, the 90-year-old Hollywood icon, spoke at a Bernie Sanders rally in Santa Barbara to urge older voters to support Sanders, highlighting his call for a return to stricter financial regulations like the Glass-Steagall Act. Van Dyke argued that older generations should back Sanders as he advocates policies reminiscent of the prosperous 1950s and 1960s, before deregulation allegedly led to economic instability. The event showed Van Dyke lending his celebrity influence to Sanders' campaign, emphasizing unity across age groups.

462514_462514.caption: Some of the 1000 water tanks being used to store contaminated water at the Fukushima Daiichi site
462514_462514.article_context: The manager of the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant admitted ongoing challenges in containing large amounts of radioactive water, with 6,000 workers focused on stabilizing the site nearly four years after the 2011 disaster. Efforts include building a frozen underground barrier and deploying a new water treatment system, though concerns about effectiveness remain. A major milestone was reached with the successful removal of all spent fuel assemblies from the damaged reactor No 4, but the process of extracting melted fuel from reactors 1, 2, and 3 remains unresolved due to high radiation and technical complexities. Full decommissioning and compensation for displaced residents are expected to take at least 40 years and cost around 10 trillion yen.

39860_39860.caption: Spectators observe as members of Provine High School s marching band participates in the Emmett Till Parade OMarching for Unity and Equality in Remembrance of Emmett Louis Till
39860_39860.article_context: Marking the 60th anniversary of Emmett Till’s lynching, relatives visited Money, Mississippi, where the teenager’s murder in 1955 became a galvanizing event in the civil rights movement. Today, the site of Till’s abduction and murder is neglected and largely forgotten, reflecting the broader decline and economic hardship facing the region. While some believe the sites should be preserved as historic monuments, others argue that such efforts do little to address the area’s poverty and ongoing issues. The visit coincided with renewed national debates about how to remember and reckon with painful aspects of American history, as Till's family retraced key locations in the case and mourned both their loss and the fading local memory of these pivotal events.

44380_44380.caption: Thaksin has carefully tried to cultivate a good relationship with the crown prince something that would play to his advantage after the succession
44380_44380.article_context: Thailand’s recent political turmoil and military coup are closely linked to concerns over royal succession, as the revered King Bhumibol’s declining health raises uncertainty about the country's future leadership. While the king has been a stabilizing force for decades, his less respected son, Crown Prince Vajiralongkorn, is set to succeed him, fueling anxiety among elites and rival political factions. The military, led by Gen. Prayuth Chan-ocha, seized power in the wake of protests against Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra, reflecting deep divisions tied to the influence of Yingluck’s brother, Thaksin Shinawatra. Strict laws preventing criticism of the monarchy create a secretive environment, making frank discussion of succession and the monarchy’s political role virtually impossible.

450436_450436.caption: Fishing vessels tracked using transponders Illegal vessels will often switch off their transponders and go dark making them impossible to track without the use of satellite radar
450436_450436.article_context: Satellite technology is now being used to track and combat illegal fishing in marine reserves such as Ascension Island, which historically have been difficult to police due to their remoteness and the tendency of pirate vessels to switch off tracking transponders. UK-funded initiatives using satellite radar can detect these 'dark targets,' allowing authorities to better enforce fishing bans and target their patrols. While the technology marks a major breakthrough for ocean protection and enables the monitoring of vast reserves, enforcement is ongoing and challenges remain, especially in prosecuting offenders and providing alternative funding for local communities that rely on fishing. Despite the expansion of marine protected areas—which now cover about 2% of the world’s oceans—many areas remain vulnerable, and experts call for more comprehensive protection and funding to ensure the survival of marine wildlife and ecosystems.

446906_446906.caption: Protesters throw a firebomb at the riot police in Keratea
446906_446906.article_context: For the past four months, residents of Keratea and nearby villages in southern Athens have staged nightly gatherings and protests to oppose government plans for a landfill in their area. The demonstrations have escalated into clashes with riot police, destruction of construction equipment, highway blockades, and the use of Molotov cocktails, with support from anarchist groups. Despite government and EU pressure to close illegal dumps and modernize waste management, locals argue the landfill threatens the environment, archaeological sites, and their quality of life. The conflict highlights ongoing tensions between local communities, authorities, and European waste disposal standards.

446335_446335.caption: Zac Goldsmith left and Sadiq Khan have been campaigning hard since they were selected as the Conservative and Labour candidates respectively
446335_446335.article_context: The official campaign for the London mayoral election begins, with voting set for 5 May alongside London Assembly elections. The main contenders are Labour's Sadiq Khan and Conservative Zac Goldsmith, with Khan currently the marginal favourite according to polls. The race is seen as a two-way contest, though candidates from the Lib Dems, Greens, Ukip, and Respect, including George Galloway, are also running. The outcome could impact national politics, particularly for Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn if the party performs poorly. The campaign emphasizes the personal backgrounds of Khan and Goldsmith, and is expected to be closely contested and scrutinized outside London. Candidates must meet strict nomination requirements to get on the ballot, and voters have until 18 April to register.

43043_43043.caption: Members of the Maidan selfdefense unit follow the coffin of fellow member Andryi Poznyak 25 who was killed in central Kiev
43043_43043.article_context: Pro-Russian activists in eastern Ukraine, especially in Kharkiv and Donetsk, have staged increasingly violent protests and clashes with pro-Ukrainian supporters, posing significant challenges to Ukraine’s new pro-Western government. Russia has threatened to intervene, citing the need to protect ethnic Russians, while accusations abound of Russian agents and mercenaries crossing the border to fuel unrest. Local politics, economic ties to Russia, and disputes over language and national identity have further deepened divisions. While some activists claim persecution by far-right Ukrainian nationalists, evidence of systematic violence is lacking, and many incidents appear linked to criminal factions rather than political motives. Despite these tensions, some city officials and residents maintain that Kharkiv remains fundamentally Ukrainian, illustrating the complex and divided loyalty in the region.

44173_44173.caption: Jillian Blenis of Boston reacts as she visits a makeshift memorial for the victims of Monday s bombings at the Boston Marathon on Boylston Street in Boston
44173_44173.article_context: Many victims of the Boston Marathon bombings suffered severe leg injuries because the bombs, packed with metal fragments like nails and ball bearings, detonated close to the ground. Doctors at multiple hospitals reported numerous traumatic amputations and are working to save as much of each patient's leg as possible. Tourniquets applied by first responders were critical in saving lives, and medical experts emphasize the importance of such equipment in emergency responses. The attacks resulted in long-term medical challenges for survivors, including multiple surgeries and physical rehabilitation.

39360_39360.caption: ProRussian militants wielding clubs attack a proUkrainian protester during a rally in the eastern city of Donetsk Ukrainian security forces looked on passively when the crowd was ambushed by dozens of armed young men who swung their whips and hurled molotov cocktails after blowing past hundreds of government security forces
39360_39360.article_context: Pro-Russian separatists in Donetsk, Ukraine, stormed the state prosecutor’s office, forcing riot police into a humiliating surrender as the crowd chanted and waved Russian and separatist flags. The violence underscored the Ukrainian government's struggle to maintain control and highlighted the weakness and demoralization of local security forces. In response to escalating unrest and Russian military pressure near the border, Ukraine reinstated compulsory military service. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin demanded that Ukraine withdraw its troops from the southeast and called for a national dialogue on constitutional reform, further deepening tensions as hopes for dialogue faded.

50891_50891.caption: In first city he visited as president Obama touts economy
50891_50891.article_context: President Obama visited Elkhart, Indiana to defend his administration’s economic record and criticize Republican policies as he took on a more active role in the 2016 campaign. He highlighted Elkhart’s recovery since the Great Recession as evidence of his policies’ effectiveness, countering Republican claims that his administration hindered growth. Obama attacked Republican and Donald Trump’s economic proposals, arguing they favor the wealthy and would increase the deficit, while urging support for trade and immigration reforms. Despite improvements, he acknowledged ongoing challenges in Elkhart’s economy. Obama called on voters to reject fear-based politics and continue the progress made during his presidency.

44318_44318.caption: Eric Justin Toth taught at the Beauvoir school in Washington seen here Toth was added to the FBI s most wanted list after Osama bin Laden s death The agency describes Toth as a crafty fugitive and child predator who will not stop until he is arrested typical for a pedophile He worked where he had access to kids ingratiated himself with families and got extended alone time with their children sometimes as a tutor Then he allegedly exploited children and took pictures of them for gratification
44318_44318.article_context: Eric Justin Toth, a former teacher at Beauvoir elementary school in Washington, D.C., was captured in Nicaragua after being recognized by an American tourist and placed under arrest by Nicaraguan authorities. Toth had been on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list for five years, accused of producing and possessing child pornography, including explicit images of young boys in his classroom. After eluding authorities by using aliases and faking his suicide, Toth was extradited to the United States, where he faces significant prison time if convicted. Additional charges are pending in Maryland, and authorities suspect there may be more victims.

41579_41579.caption: People participate in a service dedicated to Barry at the Temple of Praise while remembering the life of the former mayor of Washington Sunday Barry was a regular visitor to the church
41579_41579.article_context: Marion Barry, former mayor of Washington, D.C., was celebrated by many as a champion of the city’s poor and marginalized communities, especially African Americans. Despite personal scandals, including a 1990 drug arrest and recurring public controversies, Barry maintained strong support among residents in the city’s most underserved neighborhoods, largely due to his efforts to create economic opportunities for minorities, provide municipal jobs, and implement programs like summer youth employment. His career was marked by both resilience in the face of adversity and criticism for administrative dysfunction and patronage. Even after his mayoral terms ended and citywide influence diminished, he remained an important political figure in Ward 8, where constituents credited him with improving lives and embodying perseverance.

468698_468698.caption: I m not going to say anything that damages Labour because I think this government is terrible and I really want a Labour government back Alastair Campbell
468698_468698.article_context: Alastair Campbell, former Labour Party strategist, discusses his experience with political winning and losing, drawing comparisons between politics, sport, and business in his new book 'Winners and How They Succeed.' He emphasizes the importance of strategy, leadership, and teamwork in achieving success, admires figures like Vladimir Putin for their strategic clarity, but acknowledges that such single-mindedness is difficult in mature democracies. While Campbell supports Labour and refrains from criticizing current leader Ed Miliband directly, he suggests the party is not fully capitalizing on its talented members. The interview highlights tensions between the authoritarian traits often found in winners and the need for participatory politics, questioning whether the models of success in sport and business are appropriate for democratic leadership.

42094_42094.caption: Afternoon prayer in the Grimhojvej mosque in Aarhus The mosque s leaders deny allegations that it has recruited young men to fight in Syria Denmark has produced more foreign fighters per capita than almost anywhere else
42094_42094.article_context: Aarhus, Denmark has adopted a controversial, rehabilitation-based approach to returned Islamist fighters that contrasts with more punitive strategies seen elsewhere in Europe. Rather than imprisoning returnees like Talha, who fought in Syria, the city offers psychological counseling, education, and job assistance, aiming to reintegrate individuals and reduce extremism. Central to this effort is engagement with the Grimhojvej mosque, previously suspected of links to radicalization, which now participates in dialogue with authorities to discourage travel for jihad. While officials cite a sharp drop in the number of residents leaving to fight abroad as success, critics argue the policy is too lenient, fueling broader debates about integration, Islam, and security in Denmark and Europe.

52991_52991.caption: Shah Walliullah Adeeb governor of Badakhshan province in Afghanistan By seizing areas in Badakhshan he said of the Taliban they are trying to send a message that the national government is helpless
52991_52991.article_context: As the U.S. winds down its military presence in Afghanistan, the Taliban insurgency is evolving into a fragmented and regionally diverse force. In Badakhshan province in the north, the Taliban is comprised mostly of local non-Pashtun fighters and ex-mujahideen, allowing girls’ education and avoiding the ultra-violent tactics seen in southern regions. This local adaptation has enabled the Taliban to gain ground and establish control in areas previously untouched by their influence. The fragmentation of the movement has made the insurgency more complex and harder for the Afghan government to counter, and rising violence underscores Afghanistan’s continued instability following the drawdown of foreign troops.

464673_464673.caption: Yoko Ono attends the Yoko Ono s Imagine No Fracking Installation at ABC Home Carpet on April 19 2013 in New York City
464673_464673.article_context: New York became the first U.S. state with major shale gas reserves to ban fracking, primarily due to concerns over public health and environmental risks. The decision followed a six-year campaign supported by celebrities and grassroots groups, but was ultimately guided by a comprehensive health department report citing peer-reviewed scientific studies linking fracking to issues such as air and water pollution, increased illness, and birth defects. In contrast, the UK government continues to support fracking, downplaying health risks and relying on industry self-regulation and limited scientific review, despite criticism from public health experts who argue the available evidence is insufficient and the regulatory system inadequate.

41267_41267.caption: A man attaches a poster with a portrait of the President Viktor Yanukovych depicted as Adolph Hitler with a bullet hole in his head as the protesters block the Ukrainian Cabinet of the Ministers building in Kiev
41267_41267.article_context: Amid mass protests in Ukraine over President Yanukovych's refusal to sign an association agreement with the European Union and his pivot toward Russia, the U.S. has taken a cautious, measured approach. Secretary of State John Kerry made only mild public statements and skipped a planned visit to Kiev, reflecting concerns about antagonizing Russia, which is currently cooperating with the U.S. on other global issues. The Ukrainian government has faced opposition protests and allegations of police brutality, but a no-confidence vote against Yanukovych failed. While the U.S. continues to support Ukraine's European aspirations, it avoids direct involvement to maintain broader diplomatic relations with Russia.

45363_45363.caption: Internet startup employees work on their computers in Beijing this year Mobile device usage and ecommerce are in wide use in China and now the Communist Party wants to compile a social credit score based on citizens every activity
45363_45363.article_context: China is developing an ambitious social credit system that aims to collect vast amounts of data on its citizens and businesses, assigning them scores based on their political, commercial, and social behavior. The system intends to reward trustworthy actions and punish infractions, potentially affecting individuals’ access to loans, schools, travel, and other privileges. Pilot projects have already sparked public backlash due to concerns over privacy, subjectivity, and potential for abuse, with critics describing the initiative as a move toward a totalitarian surveillance state. While officials argue the system will promote sincerity and regulate the economy, experts warn of technological, political, and cybersecurity challenges, as well as the risk of increasing government control over personal lives.

48475_48475.caption: People spend time in Aleppo Public Park on the governmentheld side of the city left and the remains of a market in the rebelheld old city of Aleppo
48475_48475.article_context: Aleppo, Syria's largest city, is deeply divided by five years of conflict, with government-held areas experiencing relative normalcy and bustling public life, while rebel-held neighborhoods remain devastated and encircled. Russian airstrikes have recently strengthened pro-government forces, enabling further advances and improved conditions in government-controlled zones despite ongoing hardships like lack of electricity. A recent cease-fire has brought some respite, although violations persist and civilian suffering continues. Displaced residents have flocked to safer parts, but widespread destruction and uncertainty remain, with negotiations slowly beginning amid continued fighting.

47502_47502.caption: Former Florida governor Jeb Bush s likely 2016 campaign has already undergone a shakeup in staffing amid disappointing polling and other problems
47502_47502.article_context: Jeb Bush, just days before officially launching his presidential campaign, made a major staff shake-up by appointing Republican strategist Danny Diaz as campaign manager, replacing David Kochel, who will now focus on strategy for early-primary states. This change reflects concerns over Bush’s lagging poll numbers and challenges distinguishing himself in a crowded GOP field, despite significant fundraising. The restructuring comes ahead of Bush’s campaign kickoff and a foreign policy tour in Europe, signaling an effort to strengthen his operation and adapt to the evolving political landscape.

41677_41677.caption: Kim Jong Eun greets cheering North Korean soldiers during a visit to a military unit on a western island bordering South Korea
41677_41677.article_context: North Korea's nuclear test in February was shrouded in secrecy, with officials and experts noting unusually effective containment of radioactive emissions, which limited outsiders' ability to determine the type of bomb tested. This has fueled suspicions that North Korea has shifted to a weapon using highly enriched uranium, suggesting advances in its nuclear capabilities and providing a new pathway for bomb-making beyond its limited plutonium stockpile. The event heightened concerns about possible nuclear cooperation with Iran, as both countries have a history of missile collaboration and recent agreements for technical cooperation, though there is no direct evidence of nuclear partnership. The test has raised alarm among U.S. and South Korean officials about North Korea’s progress in its nuclear and missile programs.

41145_41145.caption: Dr Alex Yadao 73 is accused of running a cashonly operation out of his Prince William Co office pushing as many as 8000 pills each week
41145_41145.article_context: Dr. Alex Peralta Yadao, a physician in Fairfax County, was arrested for illegally selling prescription pain medications including Oxycontin and morphine. The alleged cash-only operation, conducted with Keith Edward Payne, led to multiple charges of drug distribution and prescription fraud against both men. Two of Yadao’s clients, Paul Mathew Philips and Bonnie Kay Philips, were also arrested and charged related to prescription fraud and possession. All four suspects are being held and are scheduled for court appearances in February 2012.

39698_39698.caption: Nafisa Nabizada sits in mourning at her home in Herat Her family paid 65000 ransom to kidnappers for her 9yearold son Ali Sena Nowruzee only to find that the boy was killed by the men who took him including a family bodyguard
39698_39698.article_context: Herat, Afghanistan, once considered a model city of prosperity and relative peace, has faced a dramatic surge in kidnappings targeting its middle class. The kidnapping and subsequent murder of nine-year-old Ali Sena Nowruzee—by his family's own bodyguard—sparked massive public outrage and protests, exposing growing lawlessness and lack of effective government response. Despite high-profile arrests and promises from Afghan President Hamid Karzai, the wave of abductions continues, threatening the stability, economic growth, and public confidence in Herat. The crisis has led residents to question whether efforts to reduce insurgency have inadvertently enabled organized criminal networks to flourish.

45876_45876.caption: From left Celine Balitran George Clooney Ellen DeGeneres and Anne Heche pose before the 1997 White House Correspondents Association Dinner DeGeneres had recently announced she was gay and she caught a significant amount of attention as she spent most of the evening in various states of attachment to Heche reported The Post s Marc Fisher
45876_45876.article_context: The White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner has evolved from a small, exclusive gathering for journalists into a major four-day celebrity-filled social event. Originally focused on fostering relationships between reporters and political sources, the dinner gained nationwide attention in the late 1980s when high-profile guests became the main attraction. Over the years, celebrities and media stars have come to dominate the event, overshadowing its original journalistic purpose and sparking criticism about its focus on fame rather than press professionalism. Despite debates over its meaning and relevance, the dinner remains a showcase for the intersection of politics, media, and celebrity culture.

42009_42009.caption: Senior military officials at the Pentagon and officers in command positions in the services have opposed a Senate proposal to strip commanders of the power to decide which sexualassault complaints are taken forward to trial
42009_42009.article_context: A new Defense Department report shows an 8% increase in the number of U.S. troops reporting sexual assault in the past year, with 5,983 cases filed. While actual estimates of unwanted sexual contact declined from previous years, more victims are coming forward, with 24% filing reports compared to 11% two years ago. The data has intensified a Congressional debate over military justice reform, including whether commanders should retain authority over prosecuting sex crimes. The report also reveals that 62% of those who reported assaults faced retaliation, highlighting ongoing concerns within the armed forces. Some lawmakers, such as Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, are pushing for stricter reforms, but proposed changes have so far failed to pass the Senate.

44043_44043.caption: George HW Bush is out of the hospital after over two months of treatment
44043_44043.article_context: Former president George H.W. Bush has been released from a Houston hospital after receiving treatment since November for a severe, bronchitis-like cough and a persistent fever. Although his condition at one point required intensive care, doctors said his illness was never life-threatening. Bush expressed gratitude to the hospital staff and supporters, and will continue physical therapy at home without any special medication.

473073_473073.caption: Nat Rothschild has lost his libel action against the Daily Mail
473073_473073.article_context: A London High Court dismissed financier Nat Rothschild's libel claim against the Daily Mail, which had described him as a 'puppet master' orchestrating a controversial 2005 trip to Russia with Lord Mandelson and billionaire Oleg Deripaska. The newspaper alleged the trip exposed Mandelson, then EU trade commissioner, to accusations of conflict of interest, though it withdrew some claims about his involvement in an aluminium deal. The judge ruled that Rothschild's actions could reasonably lead to suspicions of impropriety, despite no evidence Mandelson engaged in improper discussions. Rothschild expressed disappointment at the ruling and intends to appeal.

41735_41735.caption: An emergency responder near the scene of the attack
41735_41735.article_context: A 17-year-old Afghan refugee attacked passengers on a German train with an ax, injuring at least five people before being shot and killed by police in Bavaria. The assailant reportedly shouted 'Allahu Akhbar' during the incident, but authorities have not confirmed if it was an act of terrorism and are investigating the motives. The attack heightened security concerns in Germany, coming shortly after a deadly assault in Nice, France.

42010_42010.caption: Obama in Ore Words wo nt bring their loved ones back
42010_42010.article_context: Despite the perception that gun owners are either strongly pro-gun or anti-gun, most actually support measures like universal background checks and other restrictions. However, their voices are largely absent from national debates, which tend to be dominated by the NRA and anti-gun groups. Polls indicate a majority of gun owners support certain regulations, but those who advocate for moderate reforms are often marginalized or face backlash from gun rights organizations. New efforts, such as nonprofit groups like Evolve, aim to create a middle ground and focus on gun safety, but they face challenges due to funding disparities and entrenched opposition from powerful lobbying groups like the NRA.

43306_43306.caption: Osman Sesay 28 has been charged with firstdegree murder in the death of his girlfriend s 1yearold son
43306_43306.article_context: Osman Sesay, a 28-year-old Riverdale man, has been arrested and charged with first-degree murder and child abuse after his girlfriend’s 1-year-old son, Ahmed Jalloh, died from multiple blunt-force injuries. Police reported that the child was left in Sesay’s care on August 1, and was later found unresponsive and pronounced dead at a hospital. An autopsy determined the death was a homicide, and Sesay has been held without bond.

43598_43598.caption: Siamak Namazi an Iranian American businessman arrested in October is shown in May 2012
43598_43598.article_context: Reza 'Robin' Shahini, a U.S.-Iranian dual national, was arrested in Iran while visiting his ailing mother, becoming the fourth dual national detained in the country in five months. His arrest, among others involving citizens from the U.S., UK, France, and Canada, reflects a pattern of Iranian hard-liners targeting ordinary dual nationals in an apparent attempt to discourage engagement with the West and undermine President Rouhani’s outreach to the Iranian diaspora. These detentions have increased concern among expatriate communities, as Western governments warn of ongoing risks and their limited ability to assist detained citizens.

49674_49674.caption: Sydney s French community gathers for a moment of silence to coincide with the national moment of silence observation in France
49674_49674.article_context: French authorities launched a massive manhunt for brothers Said and Chérif Kouachi, suspected Islamist extremists believed to be responsible for a deadly attack on the Paris offices of the satirical newspaper Charlie Hebdo that left 12 dead and 11 wounded. Said Kouachi is known to have traveled to Yemen in 2011 to connect with al-Qaeda affiliates, raising concerns about their training and motives. As security forces searched rural areas near Paris, France remained on high alert with fears of more attacks and rising social tensions, including anti-Muslim incidents and political strife. The attack has fueled debate about security lapses and immigration in France and across Europe, with far-right groups attempting to leverage the tragedy for political gain, while many citizens and leaders called for unity in the face of terror.

52172_52172.caption: Though small in scale the event was indicative of the anger in places like Pakistan which has tough blasphemy laws
52172_52172.article_context: In Peshawar, Pakistan, a small group of religious and political activists held a memorial service honoring the Kouachi brothers, the gunmen responsible for the Charlie Hebdo attack in Paris that left 12 dead. The event, featuring speeches and prayers, reflected the deep religious sensitivities around depictions of the Prophet Muhammad and Pakistan’s strict anti-blasphemy laws. While the ceremony only drew limited local participation, it was part of a broader regional reaction, with similar rallies held in Afghanistan, highlighting ongoing tensions surrounding free speech and blasphemy in the region.

41265_41265.caption: AntiSyrian regime protesters hold banners and chant slogans during a demonstration in the neighborhood of Bustan AlQasr in Aleppo
41265_41265.article_context: The Obama administration is considering a policy shift that would provide direct non-lethal aid, such as body armor, armored vehicles, and possibly military training, to Syrian rebels for the first time in the two-year-old conflict. The move, which stops short of supplying weapons, is being discussed in high-level meetings with U.S. allies in Europe and the Middle East, as the U.S. and its partners seek ways to break a prolonged stalemate and respond to mounting rebel criticism of insufficient support. This development comes as both Western and Arab countries increasingly acknowledge the unlikelihood of a negotiated settlement with President Bashar al-Assad and the growing influence of militant groups among the opposition. The European Union also moved to ease restrictions, allowing member states to provide more non-lethal military assistance to the rebels.

51273_51273.caption: Akeel Yahya Mohammed left and Luay Abdul Sabar pass the time at alRahbi park in Adhamiyah neighborhood They said they can remember when the nowrenovated park was used by alQaedalinked Sunni insurgents as an execution ground during the sectarian conflict of 20062007 Now they say they spend their evenings there talking about anything but politics
51273_51273.article_context: Sectarian killings have resurged in Baghdad amid the ongoing war in northern Iraq, with recent incidents recalling the brutal civil war of 2005-2007. Sunni civilians are being targeted in largely Shiite neighborhoods, heightening fears of Shiite retaliation as Shiite militias mobilize in response to the advance of the Islamic State. While Shiites see these militias as essential protection, Sunnis feel increasingly vulnerable and powerless under the Shiite-dominated security forces and government, lacking both weapons and trust in authorities. Tensions and polarization threaten to trigger renewed large-scale sectarian violence in the capital.

442293_442293.caption: Yvette Cooper called the abuse and rape threats directed at Caroline CriadoPerez on Twitter disgraceful
442293_442293.article_context: After feminist campaigner Caroline Criado-Perez received a barrage of rape and death threats on Twitter following her successful push for a woman to be featured on a banknote, Shadow Home Secretary Yvette Cooper criticized Twitter’s inadequate response to the abuse. Cooper called for the platform to implement easier methods for users to report abuse and to review its policies on handling threatening behavior. Thousands signed a petition demanding a one-click report button, and concerns rose about social media platforms’ responsibility to protect users. Twitter stated it was working on simplifying its reporting process, but campaigners and MPs urged more substantial action and accountability in tackling online abuse.

41216_41216.caption: Mexican Marines patrolling the beach run to avoid a wave in Acapulco The Mexican beach destination has long struggled with drug violence and gang warfare
41216_41216.article_context: Acapulco, once a glamorous international tourist destination, is now marked by heavy military and police presence due to persistent drug violence and organized crime. Despite recent security concerns and high-profile tragedies like the disappearance of 43 students nearby, domestic tourism to Acapulco is rebounding, with tens of thousands of Mexican visitors flocking to the city for holidays and events, while international tourism remains low. The city's authorities and business owners are working to maintain safety in tourist areas and boost visits, but the transformation from luxury hotspot to a primarily Mexican getaway underscores ongoing struggles with violence, protests, and public perceptions.

461279_461279.caption: The number of siberian tigers has fallen 40 in five years
461279_461279.article_context: A mysterious disease is threatening the survival of the endangered Siberian tiger, resulting in abnormal behavior and deaths among collared tigers monitored by conservationists in Russia. The most recent case involved a tigress named Galya who was shot after becoming a danger to people, and her cubs were also found dead. Scientists suspect a neurological illness that impairs hunting abilities and may be spreading through the Amur tiger population, risking an epidemic. With already declining tiger numbers due to poaching and habitat loss, experts warn that this new threat could push the species to extinction. Conservation strategies are now being updated to address disease control, including vaccination, ahead of a global Tiger Summit.

51192_51192.caption: The kink in the track where a Green Line train derailed on Friday
51192_51192.article_context: Metro has fully restored Green Line service between Fort Totten and Prince George’s Plaza after repairing track damage caused by extreme heat and a derailment near West Hyattsville. Heat restrictions on all lines have been lifted following cooler temperatures and rainfall. Repair crews replaced a 1,000-foot section of rail and removed three derailed train cars, while shuttle buses assisted passengers during the closure. Metro officials are investigating inspection procedures and plan to enhance track safety with new high-tech equipment set to be operational by autumn.

49234_49234.caption: An arts group wants to develop the former trolley station under Dupont Circle seen here in 2010 into a public arts and space
49234_49234.article_context: The Arts Coalition for the Dupont Underground, a nonprofit group, has signed a five-year lease with Washington, D.C. to revamp the long-abandoned trolley station beneath Dupont Circle into a unique underground venue for art exhibits, cultural events, and pop-up shops and restaurants. The coalition will pay $30,000 annually with no financial support from the city, relying instead on fundraising efforts to bring the 75,000-square-foot space up to code and ready for public use. This initiative aims to draw crowds for diverse events and test the financial viability of such a cultural hub, emphasizing flexible, rotating programming and retaining the site’s industrial character.

48597_48597.caption: Outgoing House Majority Leader Eric Cantor talks about his defeat at a news conference June 11
48597_48597.article_context: Eric Cantor, the outgoing House Majority Leader, suffered a surprising defeat in his primary race against underdog Dave Brat, despite significantly outspending his opponent. The article highlights Cantor's history of poor vote-counting, referencing his inaccurate 2010 prediction that House Democrats lacked enough votes to pass Obamacare—a bill that ultimately did pass. Cantor’s overconfidence and miscalculations are underscored as key factors in both his legislative and electoral defeats.

453827_453827.caption: Michael Gove If it is right then it means that the Conservatives have clearly won this election and Labour have clearly lost it
453827_453827.article_context: As early election results suggested the Conservative Party was close to securing a parliamentary majority, David Cameron announced he would aim to govern in the national interest and unify the country. With Labour figures largely conceding defeat, exit polls showed the Tories outperforming expectations and the Liberal Democrats suffering major losses. Cameron and his party, emboldened by the results, prepared to govern alone rather than seek coalition partners, while senior Conservatives emphasized the need for strong and stable leadership. Cameron also indicated a willingness to reach out to the Scottish National Party by proposing further devolution of powers to Scotland.

40487_40487.caption: Regulators announced Thursday that Wells Fargo is being fined 185 million for illegally opening millions of unauthorized accounts for their customers to meet aggressive sales goals
40487_40487.article_context: Wells Fargo announced it will eliminate sales goals for its retail banking staff after a federal investigation revealed that the pressure to meet these targets led thousands of employees to create fake accounts without customers' consent. The move comes after the bank was fined $185 million and fired 5,300 workers involved in the fraudulent scheme. CEO John Stumpf stated the change aims to restore customer trust and refocus on customer needs, with the sales goals set to end on January 1. The scandal centered on Wells Fargo's aggressive 'cross-selling' practices, which have also been temporarily scaled back in response to customer concerns.

449273_449273.caption: Crispin Blunt the former justice minister said cabinet ministers opposed to a third runway at Heathrow airport should recuse themselves over the commission s findings
449273_449273.article_context: A group of senior Conservative MPs, led by Crispin Blunt, has warned Prime Minister David Cameron against allowing cabinet ministers with constituency interests near Heathrow—such as Boris Johnson, Justine Greening, Theresa May, and Philip Hammond—to influence the government's response to the Airports Commission’s upcoming findings on airport expansion. The Gatwick-area MPs argue that Heathrow is the better site for a new runway due to superior infrastructure and economic advantages, and fear a political compromise could see Gatwick selected for expansion. The group is pressing for an impartial government assessment and that ministers with personal interests recuse themselves from decision-making, emphasizing national interest over party politics.

46811_46811.caption: Trump I understand the world much better than Obama
46811_46811.article_context: A leaked internal memo reveals growing frustration within Donald Trump’s presidential campaign, with senior adviser Barry Bennett urging staff to ignore critics amid a turbulent week marked by the campaign manager’s battery charge and increasing negative media coverage. Bennett criticized both the media and Republican establishment for their attacks, emphasizing that such criticism only strengthens Trump’s support among voters. Trump and his advisers dismissed claims that the week had been the worst for the campaign, arguing that establishment backlash was expected and should not influence their strategy.

43375_43375.caption: Galveston Police Sgt Cody Cazalas points out Durst as a videotape is played during testimony in the New York real estate heir s murder trial
43375_43375.article_context: Robert Durst, a wealthy New York real-estate heir suspected in three deaths, was arrested by the FBI in New Orleans soon after HBO aired the finale of 'The Jinx,' a documentary series about him. The arrest came after filmmaker Andrew Jarecki gave authorities audio months earlier in which Durst, unaware he was being recorded, appeared to confess by saying 'Killed them all, of course.' The admissibility of this audio as a confession remains uncertain. Jarecki also provided authorities with a critical letter linked to one of the victims, Susan Berman, which further implicated Durst. The documentary and its revelations prompted renewed law enforcement action against Durst.

449184_449184.caption: India s prime minister Narendra Modi has said his commitment to renewable energy is not aimed at impressing the world following international pressure to cut greenhouse gas emissions
449184_449184.article_context: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi reiterated his commitment to global climate action but did not confirm whether India would set an emissions peak this year. In a Time magazine interview, Modi emphasized India’s leadership potential and highlighted ambitious renewable energy targets, aiming for 175GW from green sources. While India remains the world’s fourth-largest emitter and its emissions are projected to rise, Modi pointed to initiatives like increased mass transit, cleaner cooking fuels, and river cleanup as evidence of environmental stewardship. He also urged the global community to adopt more sustainable, less consumer-driven lifestyles to reduce environmental impact.

39851_39851.caption: Members of Westboro Baptist Church protest near Woodrow Wilson High Westboro also picketed the city s Capital Pride Parade on Saturday and is planning to protest a number of other Washington institutions including the Supreme Court the White House and Congress that the church believes have been too supportive of samesex marriage
39851_39851.article_context: Members of the Westboro Baptist Church held a small anti-gay protest at Wilson High School in Washington, D.C., targeting the school’s annual Pride Day and its principal, Pete Cahall, who recently came out as gay. In response, hundreds of students, parents, and community members organized a peaceful counterprotest that far outnumbered the Westboro group, advocating for acceptance and LGBTQ rights. The demonstration drew widespread community and political support, reflecting strong solidarity for inclusion at the school. The school community emphasized that the event was about promoting love and acceptance, and student organizers vowed to continue fighting homophobia beyond this single event.

42699_42699.caption: A sketch artist s rendition of the scene inside the federal courthouse with Judge George OToole and jurors during the verdict deliberation of Dzhokhar Tsarnaev s trial in Boston
42699_42699.article_context: Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was found guilty on all 30 counts in the Boston Marathon bombing trial, including charges that carry the death penalty. Evidence, including video footage and witness testimony, overwhelmingly proved his involvement in the 2013 attack that killed three people, wounded over 260, and included the murder of an MIT police officer. The jury will next decide whether Tsarnaev receives life in prison or the death penalty. Prosecutors characterized the bombing as a calculated act of terrorism, with Tsarnaev and his brother acting together out of radical motives. The verdict comes nearly two years after the bombing and has brought some closure to victims and the city of Boston.

43642_43642.caption: Harold MacMillan poses with his wife in January 1957 The queen asked MacMillan to form a new government when Eden resigned because of ill health
43642_43642.article_context: Theresa May became Queen Elizabeth II's 13th British prime minister after David Cameron formally resigned following the political upheaval triggered by the EU referendum. The queen, who has remained a constant presence above the political fray since her accession in 1952, plays a key but politically neutral role in the transfer of power. The monarch holds private, weekly meetings with her prime ministers to discuss state matters, though the contents of these discussions remain confidential. Given the average tenure of British prime ministers and the queen's good health, it is likely that May will not be the queen's last prime minister.

45612_45612.caption: As a Virginia delegate Taeb has personal ties to VP nominee Tim Kaine
45612_45612.article_context: Yasmine Taeb, a newly elected Democratic National Committee member and Sanders delegate from Virginia, attended the Democratic National Convention navigating the tension between supporting her progressive base and promoting party unity after Hillary Clinton secured the nomination. Despite disagreeing with some establishment positions, such as Nancy Pelosi's stance on gun control, Taeb tried to bridge gaps within her delegation, especially by highlighting Senator Tim Kaine’s policies to persuade Sanders supporters to back the Clinton-Kaine ticket. Conflicts arose within the delegation, including protests against a corporate-sponsored event, reflecting the broader challenge of uniting progressive and establishment Democrats as the party moved forward with Clinton as the nominee.

42464_42464.caption: Army Staff Sgt Adam S Thomas was killed in Afghanistan Oct 4
42464_42464.article_context: Staff Sgt. Adam S. Thomas, a Green Beret from Maryland assigned to the Army’s 10th Special Forces Group, was killed by an improvised explosive device during a counterterrorism operation against the Islamic State in eastern Afghanistan’s Nangarhar province. The operation was part of broader U.S.-Afghan efforts to combat ISIS in the region. Thomas’s death marks the third U.S. combat fatality in Afghanistan this year.
